title: Proof of concept: fused stages 4-7 in WGSL and a pinned LibRaw decode
outcome: WGSL kernel within 8.1e-6 of the CPU reference on nine settings sets (llvmpipe), its 1 % gain twin at 2.2e-3 or more; LibRaw decode doubles every channel mean at +1 EV on three roll #8 NEFs (ratio 2.0000).

title: Repository rules, task log and CI on macOS and Windows
outcome: CLAUDE.md with the hard and comment rules, docs/tasks.json, CI building the workspace and running the render checks; first run green on macos-latest and windows-latest.

title: Vendor LibRaw 0.22.2 and build it from source on every platform
detail: LibRaw 0.21 from the system knows no Nikon Z f: identity rgb_cam, zero cam_xyz, so roll #8 decoded as raw camera RGB.
outcome: LibRaw 0.22.2 vendored and compiled by build.rs with cc, pkg-config dropped. Z f now gets its matrix (cam_xyz non-zero); linearity test 2.0000 at +1 EV on three roll #8 frames; against the Swift decode a 3x3 fit is near-diagonal (scale about 2.7, median error 0.3 to 0.9 % on DSC_6448), so no channel swap or clipping.

title: Phone link: scanner remote over Noise, LocalSend import, phone FFI
detail: Crates oni-link, oni-localsend, oni-link-ffi and oni-link-demo for ONI Mobile; the desktop drives Host, HostEvents and publish.
outcome: Four crates, 44 tests with twins that fail when a guard is removed (stranger key, reused pairing code, revoked phone, lying sha256, wrong size, traversal, wrong pinned fingerprint), green on macOS and Windows CI. Loopback bench 0.08 ms median, 0.31 ms p99 per press. The FFI was built for iOS and linked into ONI Mobile, which launched in the iOS simulator on the reference Mac.

title: Move the vendored LibRaw version note out of the include path
detail: macOS clang found libraw/VERSION for #include <version> on a case-insensitive disk and parsed it as C++.
outcome: Note moved to crates/oni-decode/LIBRAW_VERSION; Linux build passes; macOS verified by CI on the next run.

title: Bring the ported core crates into the workspace
detail: oni-settings, oni-render (replacing the smaller one), oni-graph, oni-colour, oni-export, oni-library and the Slint proof of concept, ported from the Swift app as standalone packages.
outcome: Seven crates in crates/ (oni-settings, oni-render replacing the smaller copy it contains, oni-graph, oni-colour, oni-export, oni-library, oni-ui-poc) plus oni-fixtures; PaperCorrection kept in oni-settings only and ExifMetadata in place of oni-export's Metadata; Graph::from_device and Gpu::from_device, the shared-device check with its twin. On Linux with lavapipe: build, clippy --all-targets (0 warnings) and cargo test --release --workspace pass, 233 tests in the moved crates with roll #8, the Lumix files and the Swift dumps present; with every folder absent and ONI_SKIP_HEAVY set, as CI runs, 233 pass and 22 checks print SKIPPED, the kernels judged on a stand-in negative; with no Vulkan driver the GPU checks skip. macOS and Windows not verified here: left to the CI run of this push. oni-decode's linearity check still fails without a RAW, so CI excludes it.

title: Hold the graph checks at the spread Metal measures
detail: On macos-latest the Lanczos enlargement lands 2.2e-5 from its scalar reference, past the 1e-5 set on lavapipe.
outcome: oni-graph tolerance 1e-4 with the measured spreads in its comment; the softened-source twin now printed, 1.4e-3 to 3.9e-3 on roll #8, and every graph check passes on lavapipe. CI run 20 green on macos-latest (build, core and phone link checks); windows-latest still running when this was written. CI now passes --no-fail-fast.

title: Decode on the Swift app's definition: 5000 K balance, baseline exposure, concurrent decodes
detail: LibRaw balanced on the camera's pre_mul (D65) and normalised on its largest multiplier: roll #8 sat 1.3 to 1.6 stops under CIRAWFilter, channel ratios apart. LIBRAW_NOTHREADS shared the bit reader between decodes, so two at once corrupted each other.
outcome: Balance moved from the camera's pre_mul (D65) to 5000 K Planckian from cam_xyz, Bradford to D65, scale anchored on the most sensitive channel, plus 0.48 stop default baseline. Against CIRAWFilter dumps (10 roll #8 NEFs, 2 S1R RW2s, box-reduced on the measured crop): Swift/Rust mean ratio went from R 2.43 G 2.55 B 2.98 (NEF) and 2.85 3.05 3.17 (RW2) to 1.04 0.98 0.92 and 1.02 0.98 0.82; median relative error from 0.59 0.61 0.67 to 0.04 0.02 0.09 (NEF) and 0.65 0.67 0.68 to 0.02 0.02 0.24 (RW2); luminance within 0.03 stop on every checked frame. Planckian beat D50 on the neutral extrapolated through a 3x3 fit. LibRaw built without LIBRAW_NOTHREADS: two concurrent NEF decodes equal sequential ones bit for bit, and the same test fails with 'data corrupted' when the define is restored. Linearity ratio 2.0000 on NEF and RW2; cargo test and clippy clean on Linux only, macOS and Windows left to CI. Workspace tests rerun on the new decode: all pass; the roll #8 kernel check's clip twin now sits under each region's own brightest channel and its coverage guard is a mean over the centres, two frames by default, ONI_FULL_ROLL=1 for all ten (passes both ways). Linux only; macOS and Windows on CI.

title: Make the phone FFI's Kotlin bindings compile
detail: UniFFI's Kotlin RemoteSession implements AutoCloseable, whose close() collides with an exported close(); a Kotlin exception field named message collides with Throwable.message.
outcome: hang_up and Failed { reason } exported. Verified: the generated Kotlin compiles on the JVM and, against oni-link-demo's host, pairs, presses, receives screens through the listener, sends a 300 kB file, reconnects with the stored key, and a stranger key is refused; cargo test -p oni-link-ffi passes.

title: Port the editing model: store, commands, history, propagation
detail: A headless crate oni-core over oni-settings and oni-library: the open frame's store, commands with relative steps, undo with coalescing, copy and paste, presets per row, roll-wide gestures, the automatic balance key behind a measuring trait, and oni-link's Host wired to the store.
outcome: New crate oni-core. EditorStore holds the open frame, writes once per command and reports a FieldSet (one bit per PipelineSettings field) through Applied and take_changes; Command has Set/Step on scalar Knobs clamped to the panes' ranges, Write for structured edits, Mode, Reset (the bar's: geometry, flat-field, dye family and roll kept) and the scanner keys, From<oni_link::Command> so the wire's type maps unchanged. History ported with Swift's 0.4 s coalescing, 200-step limit and companions; hold/release records a drag as one step. A hand edit of a Roll Settings field writes every frame naming the same RollReference id as part of that step; paste carries LookSettings whole, paste to roll attaches the roll to the open frame's step; Parameters.all rows, presets file format, reset/imported/unconverted, the ONI Trash through oni-library, the balance key through a Measure trait (applied, dosed, Each/Average), oni-link Host wired by link::Link and link::drive. Checks, 35 tests each with a twin: the field placement check reads the 42 names off PipelineSettings' own Deserialize and refuses a field placed in none or two families; on the 38 roll #8 sidecars copied to a temp folder, every sidecar rewrites to its own bytes, a Roll Settings gain moves all 38 files as one step and undo/redo give back the exact bytes, a 12-notch drag is one step and one roll write, paste moves only Look fields and gallery undo restores the bytes, paste to roll is one editor undo over the roll, the balance key reads nothing until pressed and one undo takes back three frames, trash marks the sidecar and leaves the original file; a real Host and Remote on loopback edit the store and undo back to the opened settings. Left: share codes (zlib), retiring shipped presets, the RGB-pass split in Reset to Default, fitting a pasted crop inside the image, JournalEdits, Prepare the Roll and RollDraft steps, measuring a roll (RollReference.combined), and any renderer behind Measure. cargo test -p oni-core and clippy clean on Linux only.

title: Desktop app shell in Slint: window, panel, toolbar, gallery, canvas
detail: crates/oni-app, binary oni, after docs/ui-spec.md and the oni-ui-poc proof of concept: the Swift app's window copied identically (bar in three zones, panel with tabs, canvas card, gallery, archive tree, menus and keys), design tokens generated from DSTokens.swift, the store behind a trait answered by oni-core's EditorStore, renders through a Renderer trait and one WGSL display kernel.
outcome: Built crates/oni-app (binary oni): the bar, the panel with the Color tab bound to oni-core's EditorStore (one store write per notch, a drag is one undo step, a block reset is one write), the Roll tab, a canvas fed by a latest-value render slot through a Renderer trait, a WGSL Rec.2020 to sRGB/P3 display kernel with dither, the virtualised gallery (GalleryLayout port), the archive tree, labels and keys, tokens generated by oni-tokens from DSTokens.swift. Verified headless with Slint's software renderer on a hard-linked mirror of roll #8: first render, a 12-notch Exposure drag, Control+Z undoing it whole, double-click reset, Control+G to the gallery, ten thumbnails read, digit labels written to the mirror's sidecars and refused while a text field holds the focus, originals' stamps unchanged; the display kernel matches its CPU reference within one level on lavapipe; each numeric test has a twin. Not verified: a real window (no X11 here), so the GPU canvas import, real pointer drags and the macOS command key are untested. Stubbed: the renderer is oni-render's stage 4-7 stand-in, which refuses the Scanner face (5 of roll #8's 10 frames render nothing) and the positive mode; every file is treated as a mosaic; curves, Auto White Balance, the brush, the film and dye pickers and most menu actions answer that they are not in this build; the description field is not saved.

title: Run CI by hand only
detail: The GitHub account's free Actions minutes are used up; further runs are billed.
outcome: ci.yml triggers on workflow_dispatch only and runs Windows only; the six running or queued runs were cancelled. macOS checks run on the owner's Mac.

title: Prepare the repository to be public
detail: Public repositories get GitHub Actions for free.
outcome: History audited: no key, token, private image or RAW; the only personal datum is the owner's commit email on two GitHub merges, already public on the releases repository. LICENSE (GPL-3.0) and a README added. The repository went public on the owner's word; Windows CI runs on every push.

title: Port Pipeline.apply: the whole chain from settings to the working-space image
detail: A crate oni-pipeline building, on oni-graph and oni-render's kernels, every stage Pipeline.apply runs, in Swift's order, from PipelineSettings.
outcome: New crate oni-pipeline: Pipeline::image and render build Pipeline.apply as one render-graph recipe from PipelineSettings, in Swift's order: capture stops, flat-field (shipped Valoi mask or a caller's), orientation, rotation and crop, dust corrections (patches supplied by the caller), stages 4-7 for negative, positive and monochrome, curves, spectrogram, the points', the hand's and Chrome's saturation curves, vignette, chroma denoise and sharpening (joint or around Texture, dosed by full_width), Texture, monochrome luma, output clip, a sheet's ground; the Scanner face's Frontier table with its warmth looks and the ONI machine (Pro on a resting Lighting, the clicks as gains, OniLook's cube). oni-graph gained auxiliary inputs with shared prefixes run once; oni-render's kernels became bodies shared with the graph, plus Gaussian, affine, orientation and stroke-mask built-ins with CPU references. Verified: 18 unit tests; tests/stages.rs runs every stage on lavapipe against its CPU reference (worst 7.5e-6) with a failing twin each, and six settings families render finite with a region equal to the cut of the whole; tests/roll8.rs feeds the Swift decode dumps of DSC_6432 and DSC_6448 with their sidecars (perPixelOnly) and lands on the Swift renders at mean 1.3e-4 and 1.4e-4, p99 3.7e-4; with ONI_FULL_ROLL=1 all 38 frames pass, worst mean 1.04e-3 and p99 2.5e-3 on Scanner frames, every twin (channels swapped, print bypassed, other machine, clicks or capture stops ignored) failing by at least 6e-3 of mean. LibRaw's own decode, reduced by the pipeline's Lanczos, sits 0.025 to 0.068 of mean from the Swift render on the 10 NEFs present: the decoder's move, bounded and not compared for parity. Not verified against Swift: rotation, crop, flat-field, corrections, curves, vignette, Texture and detail, because no roll #8 sidecar uses them; their kernels are checked only against the CPU references.

title: Roll checks count only the frames they test
detail: On the owner's Mac, Roll #8 holds 38 NEFs and a contact sheet's sidecar, and Negs holds 13 sidecars: seven checks failed on folder counts.
outcome: Checks read NEF and RW2 sidecars only, the Lumix check its two calibration frames, the library its ten oracle frames, the render check at least its frames. The four targets pass on the cloud's subset; the Mac rerun is the check on the full folders.

title: Render the app's canvas through the real pipeline
detail: oni-app renders through oni-pipeline on one wgpu device shared with the display kernel and Slint; a decode router sorts files on their bytes; thumbnails use the same pipeline. Also: the pipeline's roll check judges every frame and skips a frame whose sidecar is newer than its reference dump.
outcome: oni-app renders through oni-pipeline (Pipeline::render on oni-graph) instead of the stages 4-7 stand-in: main opens one wgpu device and hands it to Slint's femtovg-wgpu renderer (WGPUConfiguration::Manual), the graph (Graph::from_device) and the display kernel; the render slot keeps one job in flight and one waiting. A frame is decoded once on a thread, uploaded, reduced by the graph's Lanczos to the 2000 px preview with its two outer rows rebuilt from the third (rebuildingEdge), materialised and kept on the GPU (the open frame plus the last four previews); each notch renders the preview with full_width set. Thumbnails render the same preview through the pipeline at 480 px, so Scanner-face and positive frames draw. Decode router in oni-decode (route, decodes_via_mosaic, container): bytes first (CFA or Photometric 32803 to LibRaw, LinearRaw TIFF/DNG to a port of ContainerRead with its table, black, white and comb-mean reduced read), the RAW extension only when the bytes claim nothing, as the Swift app does; the store's sidecar migration uses the same routing. Refused with a status, not approximated: plain images (JPEG, PNG, RGB TIFF, the ImageIO branch and its source encoding), a linear scan whose sidecar says primariesConverted, RGB pass triplets; dust patches and custom flat-field masks are not supplied (the pipeline leaves them out), full-resolution regions are not rendered yet, lens correction for corrected frames has no LibRaw equivalent. On the GPU path the worker no longer encodes the canvas on the CPU (the histogram reads a quarter sample); the software path encodes on every core. oni-app no longer depends on oni-render; it keeps oni-ui-poc for the keycap, spring and track modules only. The pipeline's roll check judges every frame before failing and skips, with a printed line, a frame whose sidecar is newer than its reference dump (ONI_REFERENCE_FRESH=1 trusts copies without dates, as the cloud's are). Verified on llvmpipe (4 cores): oni-app 24 unit tests (engine inverts a negative, keeps a positive in order; edge rebuild; parallel encode equals the reference; LRU) and the headless test on a hard-link mirror of roll #8: first render 7.0 s from opening, a notch 0.4 to 0.6 s (pipeline about 0.48 s on the software GPU, the first render 3.7 s with shader compilation), 10 of 10 thumbnails in 29.5 s, 5 of them on the Scanner face, a Scanner-face frame opened in 4.5 s. oni-decode 9 unit tests (synthetic LinearRaw TIFF read through its table, the branch from the bytes, the comb mean) and its RAW checks; oni-pipeline roll check with ONI_FULL_ROLL=1 ONI_REFERENCE_FRESH=1: 38 frames judged, worst mean 1.04e-3. cargo build --release -p oni-app produces oni. Not verified: Metal or DirectX, the femtovg-wgpu canvas on a shared device, a real linear DNG scan (none on hand).

title: Windows CI on every push again
detail: The repository is public, so Actions minutes are free: push and pull_request triggers return beside workflow_dispatch, the matrix stays Windows only.
outcome: ci.yml runs on push, pull_request and workflow_dispatch, Windows only; the YAML was read back, no run was started or awaited.

title: The app logs its GPU and its render times
detail: At startup the wgpu adapter and Slint's renderer; per render its job (notch, thumbnail, open), pipeline and end-to-end times; every 120 notch renders and on exit the notch centiles (p50, p99, worst gap, frames past 8.3 ms); ONI_BENCH=1 scripts a 60-notch Exposure drag and quits. To stderr and <support>/Logs/oni.log.
outcome: timing.rs: support folder (ONI_SUPPORT, else ~/Library/Application Support/Open Negative Initiative, %APPDATA% or XDG), log lines stamped in seconds to stderr and <support>/Logs/oni.log, Notches with Swift's FrameRate centiles (sample at count x q) on end-to-end latency and on the gaps between notch frames under 1 s. Jobs carry their kind and ask time; the render thread times the pipeline; a notch ends when the CPU bytes are set or the display kernel has written the texture; an open is timed from open_photo, decode included; thumbnails are timed on their own thread. main logs the adapter (name, backend, type, driver) and the Slint backend, the rendering notifier logs the API it set up, or the software renderer when it refuses notifiers. bench.rs drives press, 60 drags of 2 pt on a 300 pt track every 8.3 ms, release, waits for the last revision on the canvas, undoes, flushes and reports. Verified on llvmpipe: unit tests (centiles with a twin under the budget, idle rest not a gap with a 20 ms twin, the 120-render report window); the headless test on roll #8 ran the bench: 4 notch renders, end to end p50 574 ms, p99 866 ms, worst gap 525 ms, Exposure back at its value, revision moved by at least two. Not run on the Mac: Metal timings, the femtovg-wgpu notifier line, the file on disk there.

title: Pair the phone from the desktop: the QR code
detail: File > Pair Phone… starts oni-link's Host on the local network on its own thread, shows the pairing QR code in a sheet, and drives the store once paired: the phone's scanner keys step the open frame, State is published after every change, Walk opens and selects the neighbour frame.
outcome: phone.rs: the desktop's key made once in <support>/Link/host.key, trusted phones in <support>/Link/trusted.txt, the Host on a 'phone link' thread with a current-thread tokio runtime, listening on 0.0.0.0:53318 (any free port when taken), stopped and joined on drop; the QR code drawn from the URI (8 px modules, 4-module margin) for a Slint image. The pairing code carries the address of the interface that routes outward and the bound port. app.rs: File > Pair Phone… shows the sheet (pairing.slint: scrim, panel card, Enriqueta title, the code on white, status, DONE; DONE, the scrim or Escape close it and spend the code); each Host event is applied on the interface thread through Link::handle on the EditorStore (Store::editor), then the window publishes; every publish refreshes the phone's screen with the open frame's place in its group; Walk opens and selects the neighbour, stopping at the ends. A launch with a trusted phone starts the Host without opening a pairing window. Verified on llvmpipe: unit tests (the QR finder and margin with a light-ring twin, a trusted key written once, the host key kept across starts) and tests/phone.rs on the headless window: the sheet's URI pairs a loopback Remote (its addresses, then 127.0.0.1 on its port), the first screen reads frame 1 of 2, Step D +3 moves the store's scanner.d by 3 and the phone reads it, the phone's undo returns it, Walk +1 opens and selects B, a second walk stops at the end, and after DONE a second phone on the same code is refused while the first stays connected. Screenshot of the sheet read back. Not tried with the Android phone or through the macOS firewall prompt.

title: Clicking a photo in the library list crashes the app
detail: row_clicked kept an `if let` scrutinee's RefCell borrow alive through a block that borrowed mutably; the panic happens inside winit's mouse_up, which cannot unwind, so the app aborts.
outcome: row_clicked binds the index before borrowing mutably. Grepped oni-app for borrows living across a mutable borrow or a Slint setter: publish_bar, publish_tree, publish_tiles, publish's block markers and the gallery scroll now read the state first, then set properties. The headless test on roll #8 clicks DSC_6440's list row (opens it, selects its tile) then a tile (moves the selection): passes in 52 s on llvmpipe; with the old row_clicked restored it panics with 'RefCell already borrowed' at app.rs:637. Not run on the Mac.

title: The interface stands on a strict design system
detail: Simple flat buttons in place of the keycap chrome; every screen of crates/oni-app/ui built only from ui/ds components and semantic tokens grouped over the generated Swift tokens; a check refusing any literal length, colour, duration, font or styled primitive outside ui/ds; a catalogue window (oni --catalogue) showing every component in each variant and state.
outcome: ui/ds: tokens.slint stays generated by oni-tokens; theme.slint groups it semantically (Colour, Space, Radius, Stroke, Type, State, Motion, and ButtonStyle, SliderStyle, SectionStyle, TabsStyle, ToggleStyle, FieldStyle, RowStyle, TileStyle, SheetStyle, MenuStyle, TipStyle, PlotStyle, CardStyle, StatusStyle, ShellStyle), the only literals being the channel hues, medal foils, tooltip ground, strong weight, tooltip delay and width, menu width and pairing code side; base/controls/containers/collections.slint hold the components behind one door, ds.slint. Buttons are flat rounded rects (plain, accent, caution, destructive; on; disabled; small), the slider a flat rail with a flat knob, the tabs a segmented control, the toggle a switch. Every screen (bar, panel, Roll/Crop/Color/Details panes, canvas card, gallery, tree, info column, pairing sheet, window and tooltip) is rebuilt from them; the keycap rasters (caps.rs) and the oni-ui-poc dependency are removed, motion.rs and track.rs moved into oni-app, Options.scale dropped. src/strict.rs + tests/design_system.rs refuse outside ui/ds any non-zero length, duration or angle literal, colour literal (hex, rgb/hsl, gradients, Colors., named colours), typography or styling property, numeric opacity, Text/TextInput/Image/PopupWindow/Path/Window and std-widgets imports; seventeen planted values in a copy of panel.slint each fail with the right rule, the same plants inside ui/ds pass, and comments, strings and 0px pass. ALLOW is empty. oni --catalogue or ONI_CATALOGUE=1 opens the catalogue (every component in each variant and forced hover/pressed state). Verified on llvmpipe: lib tests, design_system, catalogue, headless (roll #8 drag, undo, double click, gallery, labels, list row, Scanner face, bench) and phone pass; screenshots of the editor, gallery, pairing sheet and catalogue read back. Not seen on a Mac screen.

title: Resizing the window crashes the app
detail: Slint's surface configure waits for the shared device to go idle and wgpu reports a validation error when another thread submitted meanwhile; the default handler panics. Errors are logged instead, and the render thread's submissions stay off the reconfigure.
outcome: render.rs: Shared is the engine behind a gate; the interface thread closes it on Resized and ScaleFactorChanged (main.rs, winit window-event hook) and waits for the render and thumbnail threads to leave, so nothing submits while Slint's Surface::configure waits for the device to go idle; it reopens on the next event-loop turn. Device::open logs uncaptured wgpu errors to the log instead of panicking. ONI_BENCH=resize resizes the window between 1100x712 and 900x600 on every notch of the bench drag. On the Mac (Apple M2 Max, Metal): before, 3 of 3 runs aborted with 'In Surface::configure: Failed to wait for GPU to come idle'; after, 5 of 5 runs and 5 more on the final build finished, no wgpu error logged, no panic.

title: A drag shows one frame per display refresh
detail: A dragged value reaches the settings once per display frame (1/120 s), and the notch path drops its waste: no CPU readback, no per-frame buffer upload on the interface thread, a stale notch superseded rather than queued. Target: gap p99 at or under 8.3 ms.
outcome: Measured on the Mac (Apple M2 Max, Metal, 120 Hz main screen), ONI_BENCH=1 on DSC_6432: before, 16-18 of 60 notches rendered, end to end p50 26 ms, gap p50 37-38 ms, p99 47-50 ms; a notch was 5 ms of GPU, 3-9 ms of readback, 3.7 ms of CPU histogram, 5 ms of upload on the interface thread, behind a 30 Hz hand-off. Done: the hand-off is one write per display frame (track.rs, 1/120 s); a notch's render stays on the GPU (materialised, read by the display kernel as a texture); the histogram is counted on the GPU on the pulse; the preview is reduced once to the canvas's device pixels (808 px on the default window); no rendering notifier, whose pre-flush emptied femtovg's pipeline cache and cost 8 ms of the interface thread per frame. After: 47 of 60 notches rendered, the rest superseded in the slot; encode p50 0.4-8 ms; gap p50 8.3-8.5 ms, p99 8.6-30 ms across six runs (ONI_BENCH=1 and settled). Open: p99 under 8.3 ms in every run; 'past 8.3 ms' counts vsync jitter of tenths of a millisecond, and the bench's 8.33 ms timer beats against the display link.

title: Inventory the Swift app's features against the port
detail: docs/parity/: every user-facing feature, hidden constant, interaction rule and codec migration of the Swift app, each with its Swift and Rust file, a status and the Rust test that proves it; every Swift self-check against its Rust twin; which pipeline branches the Swift comparison reaches.
outcome: docs/parity/ holds README.md (statuses, counts, values that differ, the ten largest gaps), editor.md, archive.md, export-colour.md, other.md, hidden.md and checks.md. 447 Swift rows: 121 done, 147 partial, 179 missing, 193 with a proving Rust test; 5 port-only rows. Of 162 Swift self-checks, 54 have a Rust twin, 26 a partial one, 82 none. Of 33 pipeline branches, 10 are reached by the Rust-vs-Swift render test and 23 are not. Read from the Swift and Rust code, not run: every cited Rust test name and file was checked to exist by script; no cargo build.

title: Scroll every surface by the wheel only; dragging stays on the sliders and the image
outcome: The design system's Scroller and ListView set mouse-drag-pan-enabled false; the panel panes and the catalogue use them and the strict check refuses a raw Flickable or ScrollView (planted twin added). tests/scroll.rs drags the catalogue page and asserts it stays put while the wheel scrolls it; with the flag turned back on the same test fails. The library ListView is covered by the component, not by a drag test. oni-app suite green on llvmpipe.

title: Open an archive as the Swift app does
detail: Open Folder… and the ADD FOLDER key, the folder remembered across launches, the SQLite index as a disposable cache, thumbnails at 320 px in a durable folder named by fingerprint, Read the Folders Again and Recheck Originals.
outcome: The app launches on the gallery and opens a folder through the system picker (⌘O), a dropped file opening its folder then itself; the folder is remembered in preferences.json and read behind on its own thread into the SQLite index in the caches, a second read reading no file again; a folder reached through a link (/tmp on macOS) reads on its real path, tested with a symlink on Linux, not yet on the Mac. Thumbnails are 320 px JPEGs at 0.6 named by fingerprint in Thumbnails/, drawn only when absent, read back from the disk latest first, and drawn again 2 s after an edit's sidecar write or the photo's opening. Verified by oni-app/tests/archive.rs (picker, index, preference, files written once, a removed file redrawn alone, the 400 ms write and the 2 s redraw each with a twin) and the library.rs read and link tests, headless on linear TIFFs. Not done: several roots at once, the navigator, the embedded scan shown for an unconverted frame.

title: Measure behind the automatic keys: blocks, Classic's two steps, Auto White Balance and the pipette
detail: oni-measure: Pipeline.reading's one door (render before the levels, measuring, clamped, the measurement windows, 19 px blocks), AutoLevels' two steps, FilterBalance's Newton on Temperature and Tint, the pipette's disc, AutomaticKey's sheet branch; the app's Auto White Balance key wired to it.
outcome: oni-measure ports Pipeline.reading (render before the levels, measuring, clamped, the measurement windows, 933/48 px blocks with 8 % tails), AutoLevels' two steps, FilterBalance's Newton (p = 6, 480 px, 8 iterations), the pipette and AutomaticKey's sheet branch; the app's Auto White Balance key reads every target off the interface thread and lands as one undo step. Tests (all green on lavapipe): tests/blocks.rs 5, auto_levels.rs 7, pipette.rs 4, filter_balance.rs 2 (GPU), 10 unit tests, each claim with a twin. Against Swift on roll #8's decode dumps (1000 px, Swift measured at 1400): Auto White Balance lands within 0.0053 stop of the filters written on DSC_6446 (Pro) and 0.0122 on DSC_6464 (Scanner), the other frame's press and red-blue swapped as twins; a second press moves the gains 0.0027 st and the ends 0.0002; the pipette drifts 0 under moved windows, 0.084 when read after the levels. oni-app/tests/auto_balance.rs presses the key on DSC_6432 in the headless window (LibRaw decode): the filters land at 0.67 of the press and one undo restores the settings whole. Not run on the Mac; no Each or Average dialog, a selection balances each frame; dust patches and custom flat-field masks are not read (Inputs::default); the harness for Swift's own 1400 px copies (ONI_SWIFT_MEASURE) skips until the Mac writes measure.json.

title: Port the Swift self-checks whose behaviour lives in the core crates
detail: docs/parity/checks.md: every none or partial check in oni-settings, oni-library, oni-colour, oni-export, oni-decode, oni-graph, oni-render and oni-core outside measurement becomes a Rust test with the Swift check's adversarial values and a twin that fails by construction.
outcome: Thirty-six Rust tests port the Swift self-checks, each with its adversarial values and a twin that fails by construction: oni-settings 7, oni-core 10, oni-library 8, oni-pipeline 9, oni-decode 2, oni-colour 1 (tests/swift_checks.rs in each), plus oni-settings/src/axis.rs for the histogram overshoot: thirty-seven in all. checks.md now reads 72 twin, 15 partial, 75 none of 162; the rows left say why (oni-app, the measurement wave, or no Rust code). Verified: cargo test --release on oni-settings, oni-core, oni-library, oni-decode, oni-colour and the oni-pipeline swift_checks with ONI_SKIP_HEAVY=1, and the heavy RAW checks (density migration, chroma and sharpening tracks) run on roll #8 and the Lumix S1R frames on lavapipe.

title: Wire the gestures the core already implements, and the menus as Swift titles them
detail: Copy, paste, paste to roll, framing copy and paste, film type, trash, reset to default, the gallery history; every menu item and shortcut of EditorCommands whose behaviour exists in the core, with Swift's titles, enabled states and undo titles.
outcome: The menu bar carries Swift's titles, shortcuts and live rules (EditorScene+Menus.swift), bare keys yielding to a focused field; copy and paste settings, paste to roll with its reach, framing copy and paste on the selection (the open frame fitted), film type, Move to ONI Trash, Reset to Imported State, ⌘K, mirror, the filter cycle, Show the Selected Photo and New Roll from Selection go through the core as one gallery step each, another roll's look asking on the Another Roll sheet, and the gallery's ⌘Z names its step. Verified by oni-app/tests/gestures.rs headless (titles in both modes, Escape then Return on the sheet, undo and redo titles, trash marked never moved, New Roll moved in and walked back, each with a twin). Not done: Restore (no ONI Trash view), Ungroup (no film gesture in the core); items of features absent from this build stay dark.

title: Align the values that differ from Swift
detail: Sidecar write delay 400 ms, a block reset landing on the current mode's rest, Dye Separation reset clearing family and by-hand, the system's double-click interval, the Roll tab block order, straighten re-fitting the crop.

Verified by store.rs and fields.rs tests with twins and the archive.rs write-delay check. Straighten's re-fit landed with the geometry work (#43), not here.

title: Measure a roll's reference: each frame's Classic, the roll combined, the base pick
detail: RollReference.measured and combined (gains on the median, the most extreme frame dropped from three up, a picked base as every black, the median only when every frame has one), Prepare the Roll's start settings and measureRoll without its sheet, EditorScene.base.
outcome: oni-measure/src/roll.rs ports RollReference.measured, combined, the Prepare the Roll start settings, measureRoll without its sheet and EditorScene.base. tests/roll.rs (5) ports RollReference.selfCheck's combining claims and the colour factor's 0.63 with twins. Against Swift: the reference recomputed from the 38 Swift decode dumps lands within 0.0096 stop (gains), 0.0070 (white) and 0.0019 (median) of the one every roll #8 sidecar carries; red and blue swapped on every frame part it by 2.50 stop and 0.12, the twin. No Prepare the Roll surface calls it yet; contact sheets, RGB passes and CaptureExposure's EXIF reading are not ported; the base pick is not recorded in the sidecars, so it was given back from the stored base.

title: Parity bugs the ported Swift self-checks found in the core crates
detail: Each failing port is a Rust departure from the Swift code, fixed to match it.
outcome: Five departures fixed to match Swift: presets::default_name and presets::decode trimmed line breaks where Swift trims .whitespaces only (Propagation.swift:209-211, 476); presets::save failed when a stale same-id file could not be removed where Swift ignores it with try? (Propagation.swift:417); oni-decode had no isLowPrecision or bitsPerSample (RawDecode.swift:400, ContainerRead.swift:198), now is_low_precision and container::bits_per_sample; plain::read dropped a TIFF's embedded profile when it outweighed the pixels (598 bytes over a 4 x 1 frame), because the image crate caps a tag at the pixel byte count, so a tagged file read as undeclared where ImageIO reads its profile (SourceEncoding+Checks.swift:90-91), now read with a decoder on default limits. Each is held by its ported check and that check's twin.

title: Export is a mode of the card: targets, rows, previews, panel and the export pipeline in the app
outcome: Export is a mode of the card (export_card.rs, ui/export.slint): the target is the selection else the open photo, counted in the menu, the bar's key, the card's key and the context label; one line per photo with its proofed preview and EXIF fields kept in the sidecar; presets, format, compression, quality, size, HDR; the estimate; Save or a folder with the clash dialog; the full render unproofed with the canvas's masks and patches, written by oni-export with only ONI's metadata, noted in the journal. Verified by tests/export_window.rs on roll #8 (TIFF 16 read back: size, ZIP, ICC, no scan tags with the NEF as twin, pixels within 0.0076 of the canvas, the swapped-channel twin failing; a batch with its clash and Cancel twin) and the export.rs unit tests, run through the wrapper.

title: Colour management in the app: spaces, profiles, the canvas proof, the paper proof and Paper Correction

The space staging animation is not ported.

title: The manual curves editor and its point rules
detail: Curves editor as a DS plot: natural cubic spline, a press takes the nearest point or adds one, a double-click removes it, drag limits, per channel tabs, one history step per drag through the hand's cadence.
outcome: oni-app/src/editors: curve.rs (CurveEditorView: press takes the nearest point within 14 pt to the pointer, else adds one and drags the first within 0.01 in x; a double click removes the disc under it at the second release; Curve.add/move_point/remove in oni-settings hold the 0.001 margin, the square and the two ends), mod.rs Gestures (one store.hold per press, writes through track::Hand at HAND_INTERVAL with a trailing timer, store.release at the end; Scanner face edits land in scanner_finish), shell.rs (Slint glue; the plot redraws from the hand on every event, the store is published only when written). DS: ui/ds/plots.slint (Plot, LevelsTrack, TrackKnob, PlotReadouts, AxisCaptions), the curves block in panel.slint with its reset, lit tabs and fold. Checked on llvmpipe with the shared-target wrapper: 34 editors unit tests with twins (exact point written, writes per hand interval, one undo per press, double click within and past 500 ms, each channel alone, the Scanner face keeping Pro's curves) and tests/editors.rs, which drags a point on the Curves plot with pointer events in the headless window: the dot follows each move ahead of the store, 30 fast moves give at most one write per interval plus the ends, the point lands at (0.5, 0.7), one Edit > Undo takes it back, a folded plot takes no press. oni-settings and oni-app suites green (ONI_SKIP_HEAVY=1). Gap: drawn over the output histogram, where Swift draws the manual curves' input with the channel in focus. Not seen on a Mac screen.

title: Levels, spectrogram and saturation curve editors, and the print curve overlay
detail: Per-channel levels track and handles, the spectrogram wheel with its band sliders, the saturation curve, the print curve drawn over the histogram; every hidden rule of LevelsView, SpectrogramPanel, SaturationCurveView and PrintCurveView.
outcome: Levels (levels.rs, LevelsView): five handles on the track sharing the histogram's inset, the median on its own travel, one write path for drag and scroll, a double click resetting the handle alone, presses caught front to back within the grab, scroll along the track moving the handle under the pointer else the nearest; readouts as densities to three decimals; the block resets R, G, B to the roll's window or the bare axis. Spectrogram (spectrogram.rs, SpectrogramPanel and SpectrogramBands): grabbed never jumped, a press alone selects and focuses, arrows step 2 % of the axis, Tab and Option-Tab walk the wheel while it holds the focus, a double click resets the point's own axes; eight swatch tabs (Tabs gained swatches) and the Hue, Saturation, Luminance sliders with their spectra and double click to zero. Saturation curve (saturation.rs): laid on linear light, a press takes the point under it or the closest along the light, a double click lays it on 0.5 from the points before its first press. Print curve (print.rs): the moved channels, the RGB curve and its dashed mirror over the main histogram on the Color tab. Grade blocks hidden in monochrome. Checked on llvmpipe: unit tests with twins port LevelsView.selfCheck and SpectrogramPanel.selfCheck; tests/editors.rs drags the white levels handle 40 pt (it moves by the travel, the others stay, one undo), presses the wheel and steps it with the up arrow (an unfocused wheel ignored it), and a monochrome store lays out no wheel. Screenshots of the three panes read back. Gaps: the levels histogram (Plots.levels) is not filled yet, no 8-bit badge, not hidden on the Scanner face (no face panel yet), the band sliders do not spring on outside changes, a press on a non-focusable surface does not unlight the wheel, no swatch tooltip. Not seen on a Mac screen.

title: The canvas as Swift's: zoom, pan, full-resolution regions, compare, screen gamut
detail: Viewport.swift and CanvasNavigation.swift ported: the zoom ladder, fit and the 100 % toggle on double-click, wheel and pinch zoom about the pointer, trackpad and drag pan, the clamp; past the preview's ratio the visible region renders at full resolution; Compare Before/After with its split; the screen gamut stripes.
outcome: viewport.rs ports Viewport and CanvasEvents (the ladder, fit, the 100 % toggle landing on its number, zoom about the pointer, the clamp, needsFullResolution on the nominal 24 Mpx budget, the wheel's 1.10 a notch and the trackpad's 1.0025 a point). The canvas's TouchArea pans on a drag and toggles 100 % on a double click, the wheel zooms, a precise delta pans unless ⌘, Slint's ScaleRotateGestureHandler zooms about the pinch; ⌘− / ⌘+ walk the ladder in the editor; the status line reads the zoom label. A render covers only the visible region, from the preview reduced once to the scale shown, or past its ratio once the view has settled 150 ms from the frame decoded again at full resolution. Compare Before/After renders the bar's reset frame with the dust kept on the same view, kept while its settings and the view hold, beside a split guide Slint draws. The screen gamut stripes are laid by the display kernel, nine drawable pixels a period, the canvas encoded again thirty times a second while on, ⇧⌘Y. Checks: seven Viewport tests with twins, a GPU view test (100 % reads the canvas's pixels only from the full frame, unsettled stays on a stretched preview, fitted reads the whole preview), the zebra against its CPU reference with a phase twin; on the Mac ONI_BENCH=zoom reached full resolution 1155 ms after the double click and rendered 60 of 60 pan steps (gap p50 9.0 ms), ONI_BENCH=compare rendered one before over a 60-notch drag. Not done: the zoom bubble in the bar, the region cache's 30 % margin (each pan step renders the visible region again), the split's haptic ticker; pinch and wheel not tried by hand.

title: Dust patches and custom flat-field masks reach the render
detail: The pipeline's Inputs carry the frame's dust patches and its custom flat-field mask, loaded as Swift loads them, on the canvas, the thumbnails and the export.
outcome: flat_fields.rs reads the custom masks the Swift app keeps in the support folder (masks.json, <id>.tiff in half or single float) with their peaks and passes flag; the engine uploads a frame's mask once per id and hands it to the pipeline on the canvas and the thumbnails. patches.rs finds and writes each correction's patch in Caches/Open Negative Initiative/Corrections/<id>.tiff; heal.rs ports CorrectionRenderer.generate on the CPU in Core Image's frame (coarse 8 px then fine 1 px search with the ring's hole left out, the parabolic refine, the tone field's base and slopes); as a frame with strokes opens, each correction without a patch is generated in turn on the full-resolution frame framed with the others healed, and the cache is purged at quit, as Swift's. Checks: a custom mask divides a flat frame and a gone id leaves the stage out; the Swift app's three masks on this Mac read whole; a cached patch heals its stroke's centre and not the frame's corner; the search finds a block copied 288 px left and 168 px down on smoothed noise and the patch carries its pixels; the tone field lifts a copy by the step between halves. On the Mac: a roll #8 frame given a stroke had its patch generated 1.1 s after opening, decode included. Not ported: the export's inputs (export.rs passes none), Load… and Use This Photo as Flat-Field, the fallback flag and the source markers.

title: Presets in the app: deck, save sheet, editor, apply, share code, import, menu list

Checked by oni-app/tests/presets.rs on the headless window and ONI_BENCH=presets in the real one. Left: the deck's fade mask at its ends.

title: Scanner face: the face switch, the Lab keypad and its machines
detail: The Pro/Scanner tab bar and Scanner Emulator menu item, the ONI and Frontier machine picker, the Density, Color and Look keypad blocks with their step and reset keys, the Lab screen, Esc and the walk keys; the desktop keypad and the phone drive the same commands.

The Color tab on the Scanner face shows the Machine tabs, Density/Color/Look keypads and Effects step keys, built as ui/ds Key, KeyRow, Keypad and LabScreen; the plot band is the Lab screen; Dye Separation is hidden; Esc leaves the Lab, bare arrows walk, Space goes to the gallery. The window test checks Effects keys leave Pro's Contrast and a Pro step leaves the Scanner's.

title: The image at a steady 30 fps while a value slides, the interface at the display's rate
detail: The store write and render follow DS.Motion.recomputedInterval (1/30 s) while the knob and its label follow every event; a render never queues; memory stays flat over a long drag. ONI_BENCH=long drags for ten seconds and reports the image's cadence; a notch is timed from the hand's move.
outcome: track.rs: HAND_INTERVAL is 1/30 s again, commented as the image's cadence; the knob and readout are set on every drag event. A notch is timed from the drag event whose value it shows (Slide.moved_at). timing.rs: Notches::cadence counts the gaps within 5 ms of 33.3 ms and past 50 ms. bench.rs: ONI_BENCH=long waits for every thumbnail, then drags Exposure 0.1 pt a notch at 120 Hz for ten seconds. On the Mac (Apple M2 Max, Metal; the one screen connected runs at 75 Hz), ten-second drag on DSC_6432, at 1/120 s: 937 renders, gap p50 8.7 ms, p99 13.4 ms; event to canvas encode p50 0.5 ms, p99 6.8 ms; footprint 1100-1115 MB, graphics 253-262 MB. At 1/30 s, three runs: 247-249 renders, gap mean 33.4-33.5 ms, p50 33.3-33.5 ms, p99 39.5-40.8 ms, worst 40.2-42.1 ms, 226-237 of 246-248 within 5 ms of 33.3 ms, none past 50 ms; event to encode p50 5.4-6.7 ms, p99 13.3-14.1 ms (the wait for the hand-off); footprint 1109-1111 MB, graphics 258-260 MB, flat over the drag. Interface with SLINT_DEBUG_PERFORMANCE=refresh_full_speed: 75 fps every second of the drag, the display's ceiling; the interface thread idle 79 % of the time, about 2.8 ms of work a frame. Not measured: an uncapped rate (Slint sets AutoVsync and drives frames from the display link), per-frame times and present latency (no frame hook without the rendering notifier, which recompiles femtovg's pipelines).

title: Geometry as Swift's: the crop frame, ratios, rotate, mirror, straighten, the measuring window
detail: Geometry.swift's model ported (mirror, rotate, adopt, the measuring window, fitCropInsideImage, straightened, applyRatio, normaliseCrop); the Crop tab's keys bound; the crop frame and the measuring window on the canvas with their handles, constrained as CropOverlay does; the canvas uncropped while framing; framing copy and paste.
outcome: oni-settings/src/geometry.rs ports Geometry's model: mirror and mirror_vertically with the frame, rotate (the crop and window turned, the ratio applied again, the fit), adopt, measure_window_in_crop, propose_measure_window, oriented_size, cropped_pixel_size, rotated_bounding_size, fit_crop_inside_image, straightened, apply_ratio about an anchor with the floor carried, normalise_crop, pixel_label, straighten_scale. The Crop tab's keys write through the store: Copy, Paste, Paste to Roll framing, the ratio tabs and Vertical (remembered and adopted by the next frame as its Crop tab opens), Straighten re-fitted from the gesture's own frame (160 ms idle), Rotate 90° clockwise (three quarters), both mirrors, the Measuring Window keys, the kept pixels. The canvas, while the Crop tab is open, renders the frame uncropped and a crop move renders nothing; FrameOverlay draws the crop frame (scrim, thirds, brackets, edge bars, body) and the measuring window, each handle's move constrained as CropOverlay does, one undo step a gesture. Checks: five geometry tests and three overlay tests with twins; ONI_BENCH=crop on the Mac: 1:1 cut a 6064 × 4039 frame to 4039 × 4039, rotation and mirror kept it, the bottom-right corner dragged in held the top-left, straightening refitted it, six undos returned the starting geometry. Not done: Paste fitting frames other than the open one, the live size badge, the off-view arrow, Esc cancelling a drag, the crop-first warning before Auto White Balance.

title: De-dust as Swift's: the brush, the strokes, the patches, the list
detail: The De-dust tab and mode, the brush and its keys, strokes painted on the canvas, each patch generated and laid, the corrections list with removal, the generating note and the fallback warning, Space's hand tool.
outcome: The bar's key and the menu enter and leave the hidden De-dust pane (pane 4), leaving onto the panel the hand was in, never the crop. The brush runs 4 to 120 px (12 by default), [ and ] step it by four in De-dust, a double press resets the slider. The painting layer draws the brush's disc and the live stroke; a stroke of two points at least on the picture becomes a correction at the brush's radius, its patch generated by heal.rs as the frame's others; each correction draws its ring and number; the rows read Correction N, Generating… while its patch is pending, a help mark when the search fell back; Remove discards the correction, its cached patch and the engine's copy. Check: ONI_BENCH=dedust on the Mac entered De-dust, set the brush to 20 px with two keys, painted a nine-point stroke, had its patch 2.0 s later, removed it with its patch and left the tool, the sidecar back to what it was. Not done: Space's hand tool (no key release reaches the app), the dashed line to the patch's source and the source shape.

title: The canvas's leftovers: the zoom bubble, Space's hand, the patch's source, the crop's size badge
detail: The zoom bubble above the canvas with the ladder's keys, Space held in De-dust panning instead of painting, the line from each correction to its source and the copied stroke, the kept size above the crop frame while a handle is held, and what else the editor's parity lists missing on the canvas, Crop and De-dust. title: Every render branch against Swift's own render
detail: The Swift app's render path driven from its sources (built apart, the Swift repository untouched) on adversarial settings for every branch, on a roll #8 frame and a Negs RW2 decoded by Swift; the Rust pipeline on the same decoded input and settings, compared per branch; each branch that differs fixed. Per branch, on the Swift decode: 23 settings sets (21 per pixel, sharpening, chroma denoise and texture through a probe build of a copy of the Swift sources) on two frames, every one within mean 4.4e-4 and p99 2.5e-3 of Swift; the one departure, a vertical crop one pixel wide, was the test's grid (LibRaw's width for Swift's ImageIO one). Balance strength and paper correction left the list: neither is a render branch. Extended through a probe build to the branches `--render` cannot reach: decodes outside LibRaw, RGB passes, dust patches generated, reduced, placed and feathered, and exports; each departure fixed in the port (area averages inside the image, Core Image's anchored Lanczos, the stroke mask's gamma, alpha carried to the file and the canvas, the maker's crop on a RAW, ImageIO's TIFF tags), the rest named open in hidden.md.

title: The editors' leftovers: the 8-bit badge, the wheel's focus release, sprung knobs, swatch names, the deferred step
detail: The 8-bit source badge under Per-Channel Levels, a press outside the spectrogram releasing its lit point, the band sliders' and levels' knobs springing on a change from elsewhere, the swatch tabs' names in a tooltip, and the step closed 150 ms after the hand lifts as Swift records it. Per-Channel Levels hidden on the Scanner face once that face's panel lands.
outcome: EditorStore gained a deferred release (release_deferred, defer, settle_if_due, SETTLE_DELAY 0.15 s): a step is recorded 150 ms after the last change, an unheld change moves it on, a hold or an open records it; every editor press, key, scroll notch and reset takes it, so a curve double click whose second press lands inside the delay is one step with the first press's move, and an undo inside the delay takes the step before it, as Swift's deferred task does. The panel's sliders still record at release. A left press anywhere off the wheel releases its focus through the winit press hook in main.rs (headless, the test calls the function the hook calls; the hook itself is not exercised). The levels handles and band sliders spring with Motion.settle, placed under the hand, while scrolled and on a photo opened (editors/sprung.rs). Swatch tabs give their band's name in the tooltip. WarningBadge (DSBadge warning capsule) under Per-Channel Levels on oni_decode::is_low_precision; the block hidden on the Scanner face, read from EditorStore.scanner_face. Verified by oni-core store tests a_press_within_the_settle_delay_joins_the_step_before_it and an_unheld_change_moves_the_waiting_step_on_and_a_plain_release_records_it with twins, editors unit tests (focus release, notches in and out of the delay, the double click in and out of the delay), sprung.rs tests with twins, and the window test, which double-clicks a point in and out of the delay, watches a levels handle spring back on undo, presses on and off the wheel, hovers the first swatch, opens an 8-bit LinearRaw scan and switches a frame opened from the archive to the Scanner face. oni-core, oni-settings and oni-app suites pass with ONI_SKIP_HEAVY=1.

title: The levels' and curves' input histograms
detail: The levels plot over the levels' input histogram (UI/SettingsPane.swift:157-171) and the curves over the manual curves' input histogram with the channel in focus (Scene/EditorScene+Panel.swift:139, UI/CurveEditorView.swift:113-117), computed on the GPU at the image's cadence like the main histogram, filling Plots.levels and the curves' input. Read in the render thread after a render, at most once an image interval and always on the last job of a burst, on `Negative.measure` (1400 px) or `measureSmall` (0.35 of it) under the hand, through oni-measure's reader; drawn as `HistogramTraces` with each editor's channel in focus.

title: The scan as the file holds it for a frame not yet converted, in the gallery and the editor's column
detail: Thumbnails.produce: a frame whose sidecar is missing or equals Parameters.unconverted shows Thumbnails.scan, the file's embedded preview (ImageIO's FromImageIfAbsent) at 320 px, never the pipeline's render.
outcome: A frame whose settings equal Parameters.unconverted shows the scan as the file holds it (Thumbnails.produce/scan): a RAW its embedded preview read through LibRaw's unpack_thumb, never demosaiced, decoded at an eighth by the JPEG's IDCT, turned by the frame's flip and averaged to 320 px; any other file its own pixels read at 320. A RAW carrying no preview falls back on the render. Ten unconverted NEFs of roll #8, release: about 53 ms a tile against 360 ms at half size and 1 s whole. Checks: the flips turn the preview as a decode is turned, with a twin; a NEF's preview reads as a JPEG and a portrait copy reads flip 6 (ONI_RAW_DIR); the reduction averages each half, its twin keeping a small image; fresh settings read as unconverted and an edit as converted. favourites.rs and flat_fields.rs keep their checks in files of their own, under the 400-line ceiling.

title: Several archive folders and the navigator: favourites, the disk's folders, what is remembered across launches
detail: FolderNavigation and Navigator: Computer (home and volumes), the base and its parent, favourites seeded once from roots.json and kept in favourites.json, a click unfolding and a double click opening, the base, the favourites view and the unfolded rows remembered.
outcome: oni-library navigator.rs (Computer, children, clicked, Navigation) with twins of Navigator.selfCheck and FolderNavigation.selfCheck; app/navigator.rs and navigator.slint: Computer read again as volumes come and go, listings off the interface thread, the click count kept as AppKit's, favourites starred and viewed alone, the favourites surveyed behind the opened folder for their rolls, Parent and the pill's folders above, the folder menu (Open, the favourite, Rename… in place, Make a Roll and Back to a Folder, New Folder Inside, Show in Finder), the open photo's folder revealed beside it at a remembered height, RootWelcome and RootsCatchUp, the ONI Trash's rows under Computer, navigatorBase/FavouritesOnly/Unfolded/EditorHeight and rootsCatchUpShown kept; preferences now read the file again before each write. tests/navigator.rs drives it all on a disk of its own, through a relaunch. Left: the favourites' photos reach the index only when opened; SidebarKeys; a roll row's stock icon.

title: New Roll asks for its folder's name, and menu items for features absent from the build stay dark
detail: rollFolder(from:) sets renameRequest on the new folder, answered by the column's rename field and renameFolder; every menu item reads a live flag computed as menuState does, false for an action this build does not carry. The request waits for the archive's column beside the photo and names the row in place (#81).

title: Carry the project's decisions, targets and research into the repository for terminal sessions
detail: CLAUDE.md gains the goal, definition of done, performance targets, interface rules, working loop and roadmap; docs/research holds the performance and Frontier notes; CLAUDE.local.md is ignored.
outcome: CLAUDE.md extended, docs/research/ added with its README, .gitignore ignores CLAUDE.local.md. Checked: tasks.json parses, no private detail in the diff (grep for email, user paths, machine names).

title: Editing crashed; a gallery double-click and the sidebar's selection
detail: The canvas's resize under an open frame read the full size through a borrow its own scrutinee held while it wrote the viewport: RefCell already borrowed at app.rs:3428, every time the editor opened (the canvas resizes). Fixed by binding the read first; reproduced in the real window by ONI_BENCH=resize, which panics without the fix and passes with it. The gallery's double-click and the selection shared with the sidebar land from the gallery session. The tree lights a photo row for the gallery's selection or its ring (`TreeEngine.marked`), relit in place on each pick; every load designates the frame (selection, cursor, ring) as Swift's `load` does; the ground clears the ring with the selection; a click under the last row reaches no gesture, as Swift's document ends with its cells.
outcome: ONI_BENCH=flows in the real window: three frames clicked once (lit alone in the grid and the sidebar), double-clicked open, edited through resizes, back in the gallery still lit, a click under the rows changing nothing; no failure. The gallery test's ring twin fails when the tree drops the ring.

title: Wire what the core already does: Reset to Default…, Ungroup, Join the Roll, Roll of the N, Each or Average
detail: Reset to Default… from the menu and the cell menu (reach read off the main thread, Swift's confirm, one gallery step); Ungroup in the Rolls menu with its title and rule; the Measured Roll block's count, warnings, Join the N and Roll of the N; Auto White Balance over a selection asking Each or Average, with its progress on the key and the others' thumbnails redrawn; Prepare the Roll and the contact sheet kept dark until they exist. Any new state of the open frame now arms its sidecar write, a slider's or not.
outcome: oni-app/tests/rolls.rs drives every gesture on the headless window, each with a twin; it found the open frame's reset never written, as no slider had moved. ONI_BENCH=flows and presets pass in the real window.

title: The Roll tab's settings blocks: Source Encoding, Source Balance, the dye families, the flat-field's toggle, mask and sliders
detail: SettingsPane's blocks in Swift's drawn order: the flat-field's toggle, gear, mask picker, Amount, Temperature and Tint, Apply to Selection; Source Encoding for a plain file naming no profile, its pick reading the file again (redecode on any new reading, undo included); Source Balance's three gains named by the mode's ends and reset to the roll's stops; the dye family tabs; Balance Strength hidden with Dye Separation. Swift's gear glyph is brought into the design system.
outcome: oni-app/tests/roll_tab.rs drives each block on the headless window with its twins; the block-order check caught a first reorder that broke Swift's (Density Ceiling and the levels belong to manualBalance).

title: Prepare the Roll: its five steps, its draft in the sidecars, the measure off the interface thread landed as one gallery step
detail: The .roll mode from the Rolls menu, the gallery's PREPARE ROLL and the Roll tab's key, one frame bringing its folder's own roll (the rest said left out); the panel's Film, Flat-Field, Base, Flags and Window steps with Swift's words, NEXT, SKIP, Back, Cancel and Esc, the bar's step keys and lamps; the frame card in its scan's shape with the measuring window, the flags' sheet, the base's unturned scan with its ring and loupe; the roll's previews rendered at rest on its film and flat-field on a graph of their own; the draft written in every sidecar and resumed; MEASURE N FRAMES read off the interface thread with progress and Stop, landed by the store as one gallery step, then the editor; a frame never measured opened in the editor asks for its roll (requireRoll, on in the app, off for the window checks). Left dark: the contact sheet, a frame taken as a mask and Load…, RGB passes' grouping and registration, tutorial videos.
outcome: oni-app/tests/prepare.rs walks the whole flow on the headless window through pointer events and the globals, with twins; it found synthetic frames with one flat channel have no ends to measure, so the check's frames ramp every channel. ONI_BENCH=prepare on roll #8's test copy: 38 frames read in 0.1 s, the base's scan in 2.3 s, 37 frames measured and landed in 52 s, undone to the same settings.

title: The flat-field mask library: Use This Photo as Flat-Field, Load…, Rename, Folder, moving a photo out, the sliders remembered
detail: CustomFlatFields.load decodes the file off the interface thread through the photographs' own path (LibRaw, the preview's side, the edge rebuilt) and keeps it as a half-float TIFF in working light under the first 8 bytes of its SHA-256, a triplet's pass names included; rename, forget and isMaskSource as Swift's. The Roll tab's keys are wired with Setting… and Loading…, the notices No Mask Set and No Mask Loaded, Move This Photo Out of the Library? (Library.moveOut into FlatField Presets, the neighbour opened under the same flat-field), a design-system sheet with a field for Rename This Flat-Field Mask, and Folder. The three sliders are kept per machine under flatFieldSliders on a hand's edit and laid on a frame never dialled as it opens, the history starting there. A mask missing from the render cache is asked again, so a mask loaded later reaches the frames naming it.
outcome: oni-app/tests/masks.rs drives Load…, the refused file, Rename by Return, Folder, the sliders kept and not kept by an undo, Use This Photo with Keep in Library then Move Out on temporary files; unit twins for the id, the triplet's id, the source test, the move under a free name, the remembered sliders and the adjusted opening.

title: The open frame's last settings written when the app quits, and a failed write asked about first
detail: QuitGuard: the window's close writes the open frame's sidecar at once instead of losing the last 400 ms; a write that fails raises Swift's alert, Cancel the default so Return never discards the work; a quit that never asks the window to close still writes after the event loop.
outcome: oni-app/tests/quit.rs: a drag then a close writes the value at once (twin: not yet written before the close); a locked folder makes the close ask, and Return keeps the app open.

title: Small parity gaps: the grid size and muted clicks remembered, Show in Finder on the whole scope, Chroma Denoise hidden in monochrome
detail: `galleryColumns` and `soundMuted` kept under Swift's @AppStorage keys and read at launch; Show in Finder selects every photo of its scope in one viewer (NSWorkspace.activateFileViewerSelecting); the Details tab hides Chroma Denoise on a monochrome frame.
outcome: oni-app/tests/session.rs checks two sessions and a fresh support folder as twin; the Roll tab test checks the monochrome flag the Details tab reads.

title: The Help menu: Console, What's New and its seals, the welcome sheet, Report a Bug with its sealed log
detail: The console window polling the session's log with Copy and Reveal; What's New's six notes as seals on their headings, read on hover and kept until the app quits, Show What's New Again; the welcome sheet once per edition (welcomeSeen 1.2.1) with Website and Feedback; Report a Bug sealing the log to the maintainers' X25519 key (HKDF-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305, raw deflate, cut from its oldest lines to 58 000 characters) and posting it to the site's /report; Show My Year on Film dark until it exists.
outcome: oni-app/tests/help.rs over two sessions with an injected reporter (refusal twin); report.rs seals opened by CryptoKit and CryptoKit's opened by Rust (tools/seal_cross.swift, ONI_SEAL_CROSS); ONI_BENCH=console shows the log in the real window.

title: The contact sheet: New Contact Sheet, the sheet Prepare the Roll lays, its sidecar and reference, detail off on a sheet
detail: ContactSheet's grid ported (six to a row, gap 0.04, the 2^24 pixel cap, the roll's tile derived from it, the median aspect, frames fitted, row 0 on top, each frame's window laid as the sheet's reads); New Contact Sheet over the selection in gallery order, live on canMakeSheet with sheetTitle on the menu and both bar keys, refused on a roll never measured, counted per frame then Writing the file, Adding it to the library, Opening it; the file a 16-bit uncompressed TIFF in linear Rec. 2020 beside the first frame, named after the roll or its day and numbered, never over an original; adopted with the roll's settings, its grid and no flat-field, a second before the roll; Prepare the Roll's measure lays the sheet from its measuring copies and writes over the roll's former sheet; the Details tab dims Sharpening and Chroma Denoise on a sheet and says why.
outcome: oni-app/tests/contact_sheet.rs drives both gestures, the Details tab and a second measure on the headless window (one photo, a roll never measured and a photograph's live details as twins); oni-measure sheet.rs twins ContactSheet.selfCheck (filling, the gutter, one step past the cap, the copy onto a photograph, the unsanitised name); sheets.rs reads the file back within 2e-5 and under sRGB's profile far off; ONI_BENCH=sheet makes six roll #8 NEFs' sheet in the real window, opened and drawn in 6.9 s.

title: Frames scanned as three RGB passes: grouped by threes in Prepare the Roll, the order read off their light, Shift by One File, each triplet registered as measured, the status bar's seal
detail: RGBPasses.grouped (three files a frame from the offset, the files left over, the stretched frames said), shares read at 360 px and PassOrder(fitting:) ported with the held triplets every lead's preview and measure consults first. Prepare the Roll groups its files on RGB Passes, reads the first frame's three files off the interface thread for the chips and the order, moves a band by DSReorder's drag, and shifts by one file, with the count and Check the grouping. RGBRegistration ported whole (edges of the log signal, cells at floor 0.3, weighted least squares trimmed at 2.5 medians, the fit's inverse in Core Image's frame): the measure reads each band's magnification at full resolution on the first three triplets and each frame's shift on its preview, then joins the passes to their lead and flags them in the index. The status bar wears the RGB seal of a lone lead, in the gallery and on the open frame.
outcome: oni-measure registration twins (Swift's synthetic frame read back, laid back, the identity and the wrong direction as twins), oni-library grouping, shares and held twins, oni-settings pass-order twins; oni-app/tests/rgb_passes.rs drives a seven-file roll of synthetic passes through grouping, the order read, a drag, three shifts, the measure, the gallery's seals and one undo.

title: Updates: the appcast read on its own, the bar's UPDATE key, Check for Updates…, archives verified by EdDSA and only downloaded
detail: The feed (SUFeedURL) read at launch and every 43 200 s from SULastCheckTime, off the interface thread through web.rs; its items compared with this build as SUStandardVersionComparator compares them, the newest signed one this system can run offered as UPDATE TO x.y.z in the export slot (orange, outranking export and import); the key and Help > Check for Updates… ask again and end on Sparkle's dialogs (found, up to date, error); Download fetches the archive, checks its length and its sparkle:edSignature against SUPublicEDKey (ring Ed25519), keeps it in Downloads under a free name and shows it in the Finder, never opening or installing it. A development build (no ONI_BUILD stamped) looks only when asked; benches never look. FEEDBACKS opens Report a Bug.
outcome: updates.rs unit twins (feed parsing with deltas and the older attribute spelling, version order, a key pair generated in the test with forged, truncated and foreign signatures refused, ONI_RELEASES_DIR verifying every published archive with a one-byte twin); oni-app/tests/updates.rs drives the schedule, the key, the dialogs, a forged then a genuine download and FEEDBACKS through an injected fetcher, never the network.

title: The year on film: the journal written on each gesture, and Show My Year on Film
detail: One journal per support folder for the process, so two tables never hand one index to two names. Every Swift call site notes its gesture: opened as a photo loads; edited once per settings row a gesture moved, read against the settings the last settle left when the sidecar write settles; medal per photo with its rank; preset per target with its name; pasted and rolled with the photos reached; the balance key; exported and measured as before. WrappedYear builds the year off the journal in this machine's calendar, the ONI Trash's photos left out, sittings split at 600 s; the deck says Swift's cards in Swift's words. The summary shows the title in Enriqueta over the year's gold seal, deals after DS.Motion.wrappedHold or a click, turns by click, →, Space and Return, ← back, closes past the last card or on Esc; the gold card shows the thumbnails already on disk. December offers it once a year (wrappedShownYear), never under a bench; ONI_WRAPPED_SAMPLE shows the sample year; the Help item is live while it is not shown.
outcome: oni-library/src/wrapped.rs twins WrappedYear.selfCheck (a year later counts for nothing) and the trash and sitting rules; oni-app/src/wrapped.rs checks every card's wording; oni-app/tests/wrapped.rs drives each gesture into the journal (six notches one record), the deck, its keys, Esc, the trashed photo left out and the December offer.

title: The editor's leftovers: the Details loupe, the settings pasteboard, New Roll's name, block help and folds, Esc in a crop drag, scroll and keycap timings, help bubbles that fit
detail: The Details loupe renders the band's region of the full-resolution frame off the interface thread at 150 % or 200 %; Copy Settings, the framing and the measuring window ride the macOS pasteboard under Swift's own types, the other two laid back after a clear; New Roll from Selection names its folder in the archive's column; Sharpening, Chroma Denoise and Texture carry Swift's help and every panel block remembers its fold under sectionFold.<title>; Esc in a crop or window drag puts the frame back; a slider takes a wheel's lines at 10 points and holds the hand until 0.16 s pass; a keycap stays down 0.14 s; tooltips are held Space.sm inside the window. The pipette's only Swift caller is the base pick, already ported.
outcome: oni-app/tests/editor_leftovers.rs on the headless window with twins (the copy crossing a relaunch on a named NSPasteboard), tests/keycap.rs on the catalogue, the loupe's region checked against the exported pixels with a crop-first twin. Real window on roll #8's test copy: ONI_BENCH=loupe, first loupe 1.26 s with the full decode, a Sharpening notch reaches it in 36 ms median; ONI_BENCH=crop, Esc in a drag put the frame back and the roll undid to its start. Left: the screen gamut's stripes on the loupe, a typed pasteboard on Windows, the help bubble's block width.

title: Select Roll Type: the stocks by brand with their artwork, for a roll and for an export row
detail: StockPickerSheet with FilmStockCatalog.byBrand, each stock's SVG artwork shipped with the app and decoded once, the picked one marked, a click picking and closing, Done and Escape changing nothing; the roll's info shows the stock's artwork as heroStock does; the export's film field opens the same sheet for its frame alone.
outcome: oni-app/tests/stocks.rs (Escape and Done twins), stocks.rs's artwork check with an unknown stock as twin; the export window test picks through the new sheet.

title: The gallery's bar keys overlapped FEEDBACKS
detail: Each key set in the bar's centre zone took the zone's whole width while shifted to centre, so the gallery's wider set spilled over FEEDBACKS; each set now keeps its own width, and the zone holds the wider of the editor's and the gallery's.
outcome: Headless shots of the gallery bar before and after; the oni-app suite green.

title: Split the window's controller into one file per part
detail: app.rs (4 052 lines) keeps the shared types; publishing, cropping, de-dusting, rendering, the archive, the gallery, the phone link, actions, keys, gestures, menus, wiring, the background workers, the shell and the state's reads each move to their own file under app/, unchanged.
outcome: The oni-app suite green before and after; no behaviour moved.

title: Split the editor's panel into one Slint file per tab
detail: panel.slint keeps the tab bar; its globals, its shared pieces and each of the five tabs live in their own file under ui/panel/, each importing only what it uses.
outcome: The oni-app suite green, the block-order and field-wiring checks reading the split files; the headless editor shot unchanged.

title: The roots catch-up sheet's title wraps, its steps align, and no bench opens it
detail: The sheet's title wrapped instead of cut off; each step's number in a keycap-wide column and its text aligned left, as RootsCatchUp lays them; a bench never meets the sheet, as Swift's --bench leaves before it, so its clicks reach the gallery.
outcome: ONI_BENCH=flows green in the real window again; the navigator test shoots the sheet with its title on two lines.

title: An iteration loop under a minute: the Slint interface in its own crate, an incremental dev profile
detail: The interface moves to crates/oni-ui, so a change to the Rust side no longer type-checks and generates Slint's code again; the dev profile is incremental, the workspace at opt-level 1 and every dependency at 3; --release stays the shipped build. The 33 window checks are one binary whose runner starts each in a process of its own, several at once; doc-tests, which no crate has, are off; a guard keeps every source file under 400 lines, the larger ones grandfathered at their size. scripts/check builds once then runs every test binary at once, each threading its own tests: nextest's process per test costs about 0.6 s each on macOS. The editors check, the longest, is seven checks.
outcome: A change to oni-core, rebuilt and checked across the whole workspace: about 30 s, from 15 to 20 minutes; a failing check fails the script (twin: a 401-line file).

title: The gestures check waits for the frame before its framing keys
detail: Mirror and rotate act on a decoded frame only; under load the check pressed ⇧⌘M before the decode landed.
outcome: Green with 6 and 12 checks at once.

title: Dye Separation, optimised end to end
detail: The separation has its own file (oni-pipeline/src/conversion/separation.rs); the POC crate's copy of its rows leaves with the crate, whose pieces oni-app carries; ONI_BENCH_FIELD drags any parameter in the real window, dye-separation included. A Dye Separation gesture ends by laying the dose on every other frame of the roll, read and written on the interface thread: each sidecar write flushed through sync_all, F_FULLFSYNC on macOS, 3.6 ms a file. The write now flushes with a plain fsync, still handing the bytes to the drive before the rename, where Swift's .atomic flushes nothing. Each notch's render waited on the render thread for the levels' and curves' input distributions, a GPU readback of 24 to 32 ms, before reaching the canvas; the render is now delivered first and the distributions after it.
outcome: Real window, 60 notches on roll #8 (38 frames), three runs: the gesture's last frame came 206 to 253 ms after the one before, now 41 to 59 ms (Exposure: 35 to 41 ms). 38 sidecar writes: 117 ms, now 13. Left: about 20 ms of reading and writing the roll on the interface thread at the release. Notch to screen, p50: 33 ms, now 4 to 9 ms on Dye Separation and Exposure, the cadence held at 33 ms. Then the roll's sidecars are read side by side and written side by side, a few threads at once, the transforms kept on the interface thread and in path order (a path twice is read once), as Swift's SidecarBatch moves its files off the main thread; adversarial review found no way to lose an edit. A release taking over 5 ms says so in the log. Dye Separation on DSC_6432, roll #8, release build, three runs each: the release 26-31 ms, now 14-15 ms.

title: The histograms measured and traced as Swift's: zoom-proof, at the plot's own size
detail: The panel's histogram counted the canvas, dithered 8-bit levels of whatever the zoom showed, in 256 bins, and drew them linearly at a fixed 680 by 300. It now counts the picture rendered, point-sampled to 640 on its long side, clipped to the screen's gamut and counted in linear Rec. 2020 in 1024 bins with its luminance (MetalImageView.encodeMeasure), and every plot (main, saturation, levels, curves) is traced as HistogramTraces: the luminance as a grey backdrop, the channels added, the 0.42 power off the ends, one column per point of the plot's width, drawn at its size in pixels. The editors' shell splits into ink, drawing, running and wiring; scripts/check stops a binary past 120 s.
outcome: GPU count against its CPU reference within 0.2 % (twin: a P3 screen's count differs past 1 %); the headless shot shows the trace.

title: A frame switched to shows its thumbnail at once; one load bar under the card in every mode; the base loupe at full resolution sooner
detail: Opening a photo lays its gallery thumbnail on the canvas until its render lands. DSStatusBar's busy row (title, count on the LCD glass, a rail lit to the fraction or a swept segment) is one CardStatus under the card in the gallery, the editor and Prepare the Roll, fed by loadBar's sources (thumbnails, reading the library, the contact sheet, full resolution). The base step's full scan decodes on its own thread once the hand rests instead of waiting behind every roll tile.
outcome: Every check green.

title: Slop hunt: twelve reviewers' findings checked, the confirmed dead code removed
