detail: Twelve read-only reviewers covered the workspace; each finding sampled was checked by grep before acting. Removed: max_params, THUMB_SIDE, zoom_over_fit, resting_position, circle, archive_paths, is_roll_field, the Gpu area_average/area_maximum wrappers, missing_paths, is_listing, maker_crop, tab_title, beyond_working, rotated_bounding_size, ANCHOR_CLAMP, HUNT_REACH, Discovery::announce, cert_pem/key_pem, Surveys::covering; the TIFF doc now says associated alpha.
outcome: Then the app shell's two copies of the file-stem helper read oni_library::paths::stem. A preference write that fails is written to the log by Preferences::set itself, so the seven callers that let it go no longer lose it silently.

title: The histogram follows each frame within a few milliseconds; full decodes one at a time, the latest winning
detail: The histogram was counted and read at the 100 ms pulse, so it trailed the picture by 100 to 200 ms. It is now counted right after each frame is encoded, at most once an image interval (30 Hz), and its readback is polled every 2 ms while one is under way, then traced at once. The open frame's preview, its full resolution and Prepare the Roll's full scan each go through a gate: one decode at a time, a decode superseded before its turn never runs (a quick walk piled one 0.4 to 0.7 GB decode per frame).
outcome: Real window, 60 notches: frame to histogram on the panel p50 5.9 to 7.3 ms, p99 20 to 36 ms (the input distributions' readback on the same GPU); every check green.

title: Compare's before laid from the left edge, the feedback form sends, icons centred, tabs that follow Rust after a click, labels read files as what they are
detail: Compare: the before's clip had no place, so Slint centred it, and its guide followed a hovering pointer; the kept before is keyed on the photo too. Report a Bug: typing replaced the message's one-way binding, so Send never lit. Every icon-only key held a gap for its empty word, two points left of centre. Tabs bound one way (the export space and format, the crop ratio, the roll's film, capture, film type, encoding and dye family) lost their binding at the first click; they are two-way now. A label written on a TIFF or JPEG read its sidecar as a RAW mosaic's.
outcome: Every check green; to be seen in the real window.

title: The library column's thumbnails, its layout key, and the column re-centred on every edit
detail: SidebarLayout and TreeEngineLayout: beside a photo the column lays its photos as names, two thumbnails a line (the default) or one, the layout stored under sidebarLayout.editor; a key cycles them, another reads the folders again, a third shows the selected photo. Every edit, frame switch and layout change brings the open photo back to the column's middle (TreeEngine.reveal). Rows are laid by Rust and drawn at their places in a wheel-only scroller.
outcome: Layout and centring checked by unit tests with twins; the headless editor shot shows two thumbnails a line under the three keys.

title: Prepare the Roll and the measuring copies read RAWs at half size
detail: LibRaw's half_size, set only for a copy no longer than half the sensor: each 2x2 block one pixel, no demosaic. The roll's tiles (360 px), its card and base scan (1400) and every measuring copy (2000, the auto keys' and the roll's measure) are read so; the base loupe and the editor keep the full demosaic, so no render moves.
outcome: DSC_6440.NEF (24 Mpx): 980 ms to 345 ms a decode, channel means within 0.01 %; checked against the full decode with a twin (a longer copy reads whole).

title: Memory: the editor's full frame and copies let go in the gallery, Compare's before with Compare off, the console read only while shown
detail: From the RAM reviewers' findings, each checked in the code: back in the gallery the full-resolution source, the fitted copy, the measuring copies and the pool's idle textures are dropped (up to 1.6 GB on a 24 MP frame); Compare off drops its before texture; the console window's timer no longer reads the whole log every half second once closed.
outcome: Every check green; measuring resident memory before and after is the next step.

title: Readouts in the slider's sense, Dye Separation in percent, a gain's double click at zero, tracks on the frame's own ranges
detail: From the Swift-parity reviewers: the Black point read the stored value's sign, not the slider's (DSSlider formats the shown value); Dye Separation read 0.60 where Swift reads 60 %; a Source Balance double click landed on the roll's stops instead of Gains.base, the block reset keeping the stops; a B&W frame's Contrast and points, and a plain file's density ceiling, slid on the colour RAW range instead of Knob::range.
outcome: Unit tests with twins on the readout sign, the double-click base and the monochrome track; every check green.

title: The working-space popover's tabs pick the tab under the pointer
detail: The Popover (a PopupWindow) had no size, so its content was hit at another width than drawn: a click on sRGB from Display P3 picked Adobe RGB, and Custom could not be reached.
outcome: A window check clicks the chip, then sRGB, Custom and DP3 by the pointer; without the size it picks Adobe RGB and fails.

title: Auto White Balance reads at once: the measuring copy kept and made when a frame opens
detail: Each press decoded the file again (355 ms of 420). The measurer keeps the last two measuring copies by path and reading, and the open frame's copy is made off the interface thread once its preview stands, through a latest-wins gate.
outcome: Roll #8 frame, M2 Max release: 420 ms a press before, 40 ms once prepared. A unit check with a twin counts the decodes.

title: Panel controls follow their owner: switches after an undo, Crop and Source Encoding resets, menus under their picker, size boxes after typing
detail: From the panel reviewers' findings, each confirmed in the code: Toggle assigned its own `on` on click, so every bound switch (flat-field, Vertical, export, Prepare, presets, report log) stopped following undo or another photo; it now only asks and the owner republishes. Source Encoding's RESET sent block 12, past Block::ALL, and did nothing; it now writes no encoding as Swift's `resetting: $settings.sourceEncoding, to: nil`. The Crop section gained Swift's RESET (Geometry.reset(keeping:)). The flat-field mask and export profile menus opened at their block's corner: MenuPicker and LinesPicker drop them under the field, and Menu and ContextMenu are sized as their panel. The chip's popover closes before Load a Profile… and Get Paper Profiles… open their window. TextField gained `value`, pushed in on change, so Full resolution or a preset reaches a size or EXIF box once typed in.
outcome: Two window checks by the pointer (panel_bindings): each fails with its fix reverted (switch after undo, Crop reset, encoding reset, menu line under the picker, W box after Full resolution, popover after Load a Profile…).

title: Sheets are modal: Escape from a sheet's field, no scrim dismissal of typed work, nothing behind a sheet or Prepare the Roll moves, the export's Replace prompt answers
detail: From the sheets review, each checked in the code: Esc never left a sheet's text field, the sheets being siblings of the key monitor (a FocusScope in Sheet and PanelSheet turns it into dismissed()); a stray click on the scrim dropped a typed report, the preset Save sheet or a mask rename (scrim-dismisses, true only on the welcome, notice and advice sheets); menu shortcuts and bare keys reached the library behind every sheet (one sheet-shown flag republishes the menus and stops keys.rs); during Prepare the Roll ⌘E, framing, zoom, undo, labels and the rest acted on the hidden editor; a report's late answer thanked the next one; the What's New menu said 1.1; app.slint's own ConfirmSheet shadowed the export's, so the batch clash showed a blank generic prompt whose Replace exported nothing (Confirm moved to confirm.slint, the export's renamed ExportConfirmSheet); a roll's current step was lost on closing the window (the draft written and waited for in close_requested, Swift's step-change cadence kept otherwise); Picker Size wrote the preferences at every notch and every publish read them back (held in memory, written on release).
outcome: Window checks sheets::a_sheet_is_modal_and_escape_closes_it_from_its_own_field and sheets::the_exports_replace_prompt_answers_the_export, each failing on the old code (Escape scope removed; the generic sheet restored); prepare's check asserts the menus dark in the roll, the draft written by a close and not before, and the preference written only on release; a unit test with a twin on the release; the touched window checks green.

title: The preset deck and its sheets answer as Swift's: the strip, the "+" card, the wheel, the preview, the form
detail: At rest the deck answered 6 pt above its strip and swallowed canvas clicks there; the "+" card's hit rose with its face and flickered in its bottom band; a wheel over the deck dropped it and its hover, and a vertical wheel did not scroll it; two automatic cards in a row left the second unmeasured; the preview stayed under Crop, the Lab and the sheets; Save as Preset… stayed lit over an open sheet and dropped the editor's pending edit; Save stayed lit on blanks; the proposed name was not selected; the balance menu opened at the block's corner, unticked; the picked swatch ringed in the window's ink; each keystroke rebuilt the editor's rows; the cards' notes never showed; the description was one line; Return in an editor field did nothing; the Carries blocks stood at their rows' gap.
outcome: A window check drives the deck by the pointer and the sheets by their fields, each step with a twin; the strip, "+" card, wheel, Crop, Save as Preset… and in-place steps fail on the earlier code. The fade at the roll's ends and the dashed "+" edge stay open: Slint has no mask nor dashed stroke.

title: The library column keeps the wheel's scroll and its rows, opens on a double click once; a switched photo shows nothing of the last
detail: From the review of the library column and the canvas. The column centres when the photo it follows changes, when it is shown again and on its key, never on a notch; a resize relays its rows in place and clamps the scroll; a thumbnail drawn again reaches its row; a double click's second click does nothing by itself, so a photo opens once and a group folds once, and opening the photo already open loads nothing (Swift's takeOff). Opening a photo restarts the correction numbers and clears the patch sources; with no thumbnail the canvas empties with its texture and Compare's before; a full-resolution build clears only its own mark, is dropped under a reading left since and is not retried after a failure; a failed heal is not retried on every render and heals are kept per frame; the patch stats and the De-dust lists are no longer renewed on every notch; the tab bar leaving De-dust darkens its key; a brush double press shows the reset at once. Not done: a render error carrying its path needs render/worker.rs. The trash highlighting finding is unreachable, the archive's rows showing only beside a photo.
outcome: Two window checks (library_column, canvas_switch) and a unit test, each fix reverted in turn makes them fail (12 mutations); the gallery, archive, headless, masks, gestures and editor checks stay green.

title: The levels and curves inputs read only when what enters them moves, on the small copy under the hand, cells read by selection
detail: After nearly every notch the render thread read both input histograms on the full 1400 px copy (40 ms, the hand's small copy never used since the slot was always quiet), purging the pool each time. Each stage now keeps its reading while the settings entering it (truncated) and the copy hold; the small copy reads under the hand and the full one once it has rested 150 ms; Blocks' cell medians and tails are found by selection instead of four sorts per cell; no purge.
outcome: Roll #8 frame, M2 Max release: a gains notch 40 ms to 16 ms on the full copy, 8 to 4 ms on the small one; a slider past the levels (vignette, curves for the levels input) reads nothing. Unit check with a twin: selection equals the sorted cell. Every check green.

title: The canvas render starts from the stage its slider moves: a frontier cache of the unchanged results a changed stage reads
detail: The graph's cache was index-addressed, kept every stage (about a gigabyte at the canvas's size) and was never passed by the app, so every notch re-ran the whole chain from the preview. The cache is now addressed by node key; its frontier mode keeps only the unchanged results a changed node reads, measured against the last render, so from the second notch of a hand on a slider only that stage and what follows run. The engine's canvas render holds one, cleared when the editor is left.
outcome: Roll #8 frame, 2000 px, M2 Max release, GPU waited: a Texture notch on a heavy frame 10.4 to 2.6 ms, Sharpen 10.5 to 2.2 ms, Exposure at rest 4.7 to 2.4 ms, the CPU side 1.2-2.5 to 0.3-0.7 ms. A graph check counts the dispatches notch by notch, its twin an early change rerunning all.

title: A render failure names its frame: one landing after the frame was left no longer blanks the next
detail: The worker delivered a bare error string, so a failure of frame A landing once B was open blanked B's canvas and said Not rendered. The error now carries its path and the landing drops it unless that frame is open.
outcome: Unit check on the worker: the failure carries the job's path; the landing compares it to the open frame.

title: One uniform ring for every dispatch; the histogram traced off the interface thread
detail: Each stage created two or three uniform buffers per render; they are now written in turn into one 4 MB ring at the device's offset alignment. The picture's and the saturation plot's traces (1.5 ms each at 640 x 280) run on a worker thread, a trace overtaken by a later one dropped, the latency recorded when it lands.
outcome: Notch probe, roll #8, M2 Max: the CPU side of a notch 0.3-0.7 to 0.2-0.5 ms; the interface thread no longer traces (3 ms a histogram before). Per-feature GPU cost measured on the 2000 px preview: bare chain 1.6 ms, Texture +2.6, sharpen +0.25, chroma +0.2, vignette and Chrome under 0.1. Graph checks and the window checks green.

title: An unreadable sidecar never rewritten as defaults; Cmd+Q writes the draft and the open frame; heals retried on reopen
detail: From the adversarial review of #102 and #104. set_label, set_exif and set_roll_draft read the sidecar with .ok(), so a broken one was replaced by default settings around the one field: they now return the read error. Cmd+Q ends AppKit's loop without closing the window, skipping every close-time write: a winit exiting hook now writes the roll's draft and the open frame's settings. A draft write first flushes the store, so it cannot read back older settings of the open frame. A heal that failed is tried again when its photo is reopened.
outcome: oni-settings check: a broken sidecar is left byte for byte and set_label errs; twin: a readable one takes the label with its settings kept. The exit hook and the flush order were read, not driven: Cmd+Q is to be tried in the real app.

title: The last stage writes into a reused output texture; publish timed in the bench
detail: Each canvas render allocated a 43 MB owned texture and copied its last stage into it. The last stage now writes straight into an owned output the pool keeps and takes again once no source holds it (four kept); a fresh texture written by a kernel is cleared by wgpu first, which made the direct write alone slower (2.2 to 3.3 ms). The bench report gains the interface thread's publish centiles.
outcome: Notch probe, roll #8, M2 Max: a light notch 2.2 to 1.7 ms, Sharpen on a heavy frame 1.9 to 1.6, Texture 2.5 to 2.1. Graph checks green.

title: Every kernel compiled at launch, off the interface thread
detail: Metal builds a compute pipeline at its first dispatch, so the first notch of a stage never used yet waited for its compile (595 ms for Texture's chain). At launch a thread renders a 64 px frame through each face, film and finishing branch (busy Pro, joint detail, monochrome, Scanner on ONI and on Frontier) and their input readings, then lets the pool go.
outcome: Real window, ONI_BENCH=1 on Texture, M2 Max: first notch end to end 595 ms before, worst 33 ms after; the warm-up takes 38-55 ms at launch.

title: LibRaw's buffers let go before the float copy; the camera-to-linear conversion on every core
detail: LibRaw's raw and working images (about 245 MB at 24 MP) stayed alive while the 390 MB float copy was built. The inset is now kept in the decoded struct and libraw_recycle frees them right after the processed image is made. The conversion to linear Rec. 2020 runs in bands of rows on every core, the same arithmetic per pixel.
outcome: DSC_6440.NEF, M2 Max release: full decode 1.00 s to 0.90 s, the same checksum over the frame; decode peak about 245 MB lower. oni-decode checks green, the concurrency check included.

title: The preset deck rises from the canvas's own bottom edge, full width, as Swift's overlay
detail: Owner's report: the cards came out of nowhere 30-40 px above the canvas's edge. The deck was laid a card padding above the canvas's bottom and narrowed by it on each side; Swift overlays PresetCarousel on NegativeView's bottom edge across its width. The presets bench aimed at the lift's band the photo now keeps, and is aimed at the strip.
outcome: Window checks presets and preset_deck green; the real-window presets bench raises the deck, previews 2.30 EV under the pointer and applies it on the click.

title: The tile memory held to about 270 MB, the least recently shown dropped first
detail: Swift's memoryLimit of 2,500 tiles is about 680 MB of RGBA at 320 x 213, too much beside an editor on an 8 GB Mac, and its eviction dropped the oldest inserted even when on screen. The cap is 1,000 tiles and each read notes its use, so the least recently shown half goes; a dropped tile is read again from its JPEG.
outcome: Unit check: past the ceiling half remains, the newest kept; a tile read again outlives newer ones (twin of the insertion order). Steady memory of a 2,000-photo library about 410 MB lower.

title: The installation and update ping to the recorder, a generic User-Agent; checks and benches kept out of the owner's journal
detail: Ported from Swift's Updates.reportInstall: GET /installed?v=<version>[&from=<previous>] once per version on a published (stamped) build, the version remembered only once the recorder answers 2xx so an offline launch retries, from=inconnue when the copy had checked before without a remembered version. Every request now carries OpenNegative/<version> Sparkle-compatible, so the recorder counts Rust copies and their version as it does Sparkle's, and learns nothing of the Mac. Options::default() (the checks') takes a scratch support folder and a reporter that sends nothing; ONI_BENCH runs note their gestures in a scratch journal; the app passes the online reporter itself.
outcome: Window check updates: the first launch asks the feed and /installed?v=… with no from, remembers the version; the next launch asks nothing. Unit check on the URL and the agent, twin on the Mac's name. Open: a user moving from the Swift app is counted as a first installation, since its UserDefaults are not read; the displayed version comes from ONI_VERSION, which no release script stamps yet.

title: A narrow bar folds RESET SCAN and FEEDBACKS into glyph keys; the report sheet wide; the folder star sized to its key
detail: Owner's requests. Short of room for every word (measured on hidden copies, so the window's width never loops through the choice), RESET SCAN becomes a square key with the reset glyph and FEEDBACKS one with Trinil's chat glyph, their names kept as tooltips. Report a Bug takes the wide dialog, so its row of keys stays inside the card. A folder row's star was an unsized image inside its 12.8 px key, so it drew at the file's 24 px: it now fills its key, as Swift's DSIcon(size: iconSize * 0.8).
outcome: Window shots at 1280, 1100 and 980 px: words at 1280, glyphs at 1100; the report sheet's keys inside its card. No binding loop left in the build. Every check green.

title: ONI Wrapped measures at Swift's level
detail: From the #115 audit: journal writes off the interface thread (Swift's utility queue, Journal.swift:34-35); offer_wrapped after the library and the index are read (EditorScene+Stages.swift:76-83); paste-to-roll counts the open frame once and a paste counts only the photos changed (EditorScene+Paste.swift:47, 65, 92-95); the export subject's path canonical (EditorScene+Export.swift:155).
outcome: The journal writes on its own thread (Journal.swift's utility queue): a gesture is handed over and the read waits for every write handed before it, and quitting waits for it too; the check holds the thread and sees the caller wrote nothing, then reads all 51. The launch's Wrapped offer waits for the opened folder's rows, at once when none is read. Paste to Roll counts the open frame once (rollReach + 1). A paste counts as Swift's before.count does: every target rewritten, the open frame whether or not the paste moved it (the audit's 'only the photos changed' misread SidecarBatch, whose paste transform never returns nil). The exported photo is noted under its canonical path.

title: The release stamps ONI_VERSION and ONI_BUILD; a Swift user's last version seeds the install ping
detail: The install ping (#115) fires only on a stamped build, and a copy moving from the Swift app would be counted as a first installation since Swift's UserDefaults are not read. Both settle with the release script, which needs the owner's word.

title: Fewer passes for the M1: Texture's ten to seven, per-pixel runs fused
detail: Measured on the M2 Max (#108): bare chain 1.6 ms, Texture +2.6 ms on the 2000 px preview; an 8 GB M1 has about a sixth of the bandwidth. Fold luma into the narrow blur's prologue, moments and coefficients into the blurs' epilogues, then fuse the per-pixel stages after the curves, each with its CPU reference and a GPU-vs-CPU check.
outcome: Texture in seven passes: luma, moments and coefficients are read through the next blur's taps (BlurOf, Before::{Luma, Moments, Coeff}), their math in texture_math.wgsl shared by the passes and the folds. fused.rs checks each fold against the step then the CPU blur, and the seven-pass chain against the ten at 780 px (narrow blur under its floor) and 4000 px, error 1.5e-7, twins at 6e-3. cost.rs (ONI_BENCH_COST=1), interleaved medians on 2000 px: ten passes 7.48 ms, seven 6.81 ms once #138 is in. The per-pixel stages after the curves are left to fuse. Then the per-pixel runs: kernels reading only their input are composed into one pass (stages::laid, Fused), each instance's names suffixed and its Params one member of a shared uniform, so a kernel may run twice with its own parameters; the finishing lays the spectrogram, the points' saturation, the saturation and the vignette as one pass, and the sauce, the monochrome luma and the output clip as one. fused.rs checks seven kernels in one pass against one pass each (error 4e-8, twin in another order 8e-3); the renaming has its own check with a twin on a field named as a function. cost.rs on 2000 px, machine under builds: six kernels 1.8-2.2 ms one pass each, 0.75-1.35 ms laid; Texture 4.1-4.3 ms in ten passes, 3.4-3.7 ms in seven. The prewarm also renders the usual sets of finishing kernels (vignette, spectrogram and sauce off in turn, all at rest), since each set is a shader of its own: 46-52 ms at launch once Metal has cached them.

title: One gate for every full decode, the thumbnail painter, the heal and the export included
detail: The decode peak of an open during a thumbnail pass reaches about 3.2 GB at 24 MP; weigh the open's latency against an 8 GB Mac before choosing the order.
outcome: Every decode (LibRaw, linear scan, plain file) takes a place among DECODES = 2; the threads of background work (thumbnails, roll tiles, measuring copies, dust patches) mark themselves and take at most one, and wait while the hand's decode waits, so an open, a zoom's full resolution, an export or a mask never queues behind them. A decode that waits over 5 ms says so in the log. Roll #8, ONI_BENCH=1 on DSC_6432 with an empty thumbnail cache, machine loaded by builds: the hand's decode never waited (0 of 5 runs), background ones waited up to 717 ms; peak memory footprint 3.16 and 3.31 GB before, 2.37 to 3.13 GB after (median 3.1): in this flow the peak is one whole 24 MP decode and its upload, not decodes stacked. decode_gate's check runs its own slots: one background decode leaves the hand a place, a second waits, a waiting hand goes first; a mutant without the reserved place fails it.

title: A folder the disk refuses is never listed as empty; FEEDBACKS keeps its width; sheets capped to the window; the keycap plate in the design system
detail: Owner's report: on the T7 (exFAT) the Scans folder showed as a dead end and the editor's column held no photo. A listing the disk refused (a drive still waking, access to removable volumes not granted yet) was kept as an empty folder for the whole session, and the opened folder stayed unread. Now a refusal leaves the folder unlisted with its chevron; a click reads it again, and the mounts' reader tries every refused folder each second, listing it and reading the opened folder again once the disk answers. Folders the Finder hides by their flag (Recovery, System Volume Information) are left out as Swift's .skipsHiddenFiles does. FEEDBACKS was stretched by its zone: it keeps its own width. Every sheet stops at the window's height less its margins and scrolls past it, WelcomeSheet's fit. KeyPlate, Swift's KeycapPlate, joins the design system with Button.fills.

title: Scroll knobs only where a surface overflows, as AppKit's overlay scrollers
detail: Owner's ask: scroll bars only where something scrolls. Every Swift ScrollView and List keeps the default automatic indicators, the macOS overlay knob. The design system's one Scroller now draws a ScrollKnob over the edge, only while the content overflows, lit while it scrolls, 0.8 s after and while the pointer is on the edge strip, fading out; it reserves no gutter and takes no click. ListView is the same Scroller, its rows still virtualised, so the fluent list's permanent thumb and its 14 px hit strip over the paper rows' Install buttons are gone, with the phantom sideways bar: a vertical surface pins its content width and never slides under a diagonal swipe. The preset deck keeps no knob (.scrollIndicators(.never)); the paper sidebar sets its content height; the Info sidebar scrolls as InfoSidebar's ScrollView; the gallery grid, scrolled by Rust, shows the same knob. ScrollStyle and Colour.knob hold the values.
outcome: Window check scroll::the_knob_shows_only_where_the_content_overflows_and_only_while_it_moves: the catalogue's knob lights on a wheel and goes out after its linger, lights on the edge strip only; its twins, a scroller whose content fits, stays dark under the same wheel and edge hover, and a diagonal swipe never moves the page sideways.

title: Sheets, notices and popovers laid out as Swift's: hung from the top, no scrim, leading titles, keys on the right
detail: Owner's words: the What's new sheet must be responsive like Swift's, as tall as the window allows and scrolled, and every sheet, modal, popover and menu laid out as in Swift. Every sheet hangs from the window's top a margin down, draws no scrim yet ignores a click beside it (Swift's sheets are modal: the welcome, RAW notice and notices no longer close on one), and stops a margin above the window's foot, scrolling inside. Titles are leading: the title face for full sheets, the section face for DSDialog questions. The welcome bleeds its 3:2 photo edge to edge, cropped to fill, under the splash caption at 0.8 (SplashCaption, shared with the splash), with Swift's 24/8/4 groups in one scrolled column. Confirms, choices, notices and the export's clash and notice put their keys right-aligned in one KeyPlate; Delete Project, Delete/Replace Preset and Reset to Default are red and take no Return; option keys are neutral. Return presses Got It, OK and Done. The quit alert keeps Swift's order, Quit Anyway then Cancel as the default, drawn over every other sheet. Report at 420 with the switch before its words and Cancel/Send on a plate; RAW notice at 420 with dotted bullets; Roots catch-up at 400 with numbered discs; the paper board and preset panels capped to the window, the board closed by Escape and modal; the popover on the panel's ground at 16 padding; a rule before Delete a Preset.
outcome: Window check sheet_layout: GET STARTED reached unscrolled in a tall window and only after the wheel in a short one (twin), a notice's OK at the card's right and nowhere in its left half (twin); launch, sheets, presets, rolls and quit checks follow the modal sheets and the destructive keys.

title: The sidebars' keys laid as Swift lays them: keycap plates, switches before their words, the panel's rule, the warning band
detail: Owner's report: the keys of the sidebars sat apart, reversed and right-aligned against Swift's. Every group Swift lays on a KeycapPlate now sits on a KeyPlate, words in capitals: Measured Roll's JOIN / ROLL OF, the flat-field's LOAD / RENAME / FOLDER, the Crop's COPY / PASTE / PASTE TO ROLL, the Measuring Window's reset, word (confirm green when armed, the note as its tooltip), copy and paste, the mirror pair (the second glyph turned 90°, never lit), Auto White Balance with the crop warning inside its plate, Auto Paper Correction. Beside a photo the column shows one row, Swift's SidebarKeys: target and layout on a mini plate at the left, then the folder's pill, without the reload key Swift never shows; the navigator's Parent and Favourites share a mini plate; the Projects surface gets its row: fold or open every project, then the ONI Projects pill. Each column part pads itself as Swift's does. Switches lead their words (Vertical, Flat-field), the Mask label stands above its picker, warnings are DSWarning's band with its triangle, one rule closes the panel's pinned header, a black and white photo hides the Color block and Chrome (ColorPane's isMonochrome), Kept reads on the LCD, tree photo rows carry the film glyph and projects the sticky note, and the Info sidebar's stock rows lead with their icon, its date clears by a reset glyph and its description is a fixed-height multi-line box.

title: One unified bar on macOS; the card flush; a hidden column back by its key or its edge; roll headers with their trail and pinned; medals and seals in Swift's corners
detail: The main window's title bar is transparent, untitled and under the content (winit's macOS attributes through the backend's hook, the main window only), the traffic lights centred in the bar with their room read from AppKit; the bar's empty room drags the window and a double press does the system's title-bar action. The gallery always lists the library; beside a photo the canvas carries Swift's column keys (menu-left at the top left, menu-right last in the zoom bubble, which was laid off the card and never showed) and a hidden column slides over the card from its edge while hovered. The card is flush with its columns and the status bar, inset on four sides only on export, where the status bar leaves. Roll headers read 'trail / title' with no count and stay pinned while their band scrolls. Tiles wear the medal bottom-left and the RGB seal bottom-right, Space.sm in. The status bar sets the seal after the name, the medal picker at the end, and shows the picker beside a photo too. The bar's centre keys sit on the window's centre when there is room. The canvas shows the read-only badge, the decode progress with no stand-in, '<file>: could not be decoded', and turns darker while cropping.
outcome: Window check canvas_layout (twins for each piece); the real app's content view measured at the window's full frame, the lights at 9-69 pt centred in the 48-point bar, the bar's room hit-testing to the content view.

title: The bar's worded keys keep their widths as the window widens
detail: Owner's report: EXPORT and ADD FOLDER stretched with the window. A worded key took a stretch of one, so a row's spare room went into it. A key now keeps its own width unless it fills; a row of keys none of which fills still shares its room out, as Slint grows every item when none stretches, so a filling KeyPlate is unchanged.
outcome: Window check toolbar.rs: at 1280 and 1700 px the last key, the gap and FEEDBACKS keep their widths while the room before them grows (twin); with the old default ADD FOLDER went 150 to 255 px and the check failed.

title: A RAW held in portrait opens upright, as CIRAWFilter hands it out
detail: Owner's decision. LibRaw ran with user_flip 0, so the file's orientation was ignored: a portrait RAW opened sideways and a Swift sidecar's crop fractions fell elsewhere. LibRaw still hands out the unturned image; the camera-to-linear conversion now reads it turned by the file's flip (flip_index's arithmetic), so no extra copy is made, the default crop turning with it. Renders of turned RAWs move; the owner's test-build edits do not matter.
outcome: oni-decode linear tests: every flip against LibRaw's flip_index on a numbered window, twin the two quarter turns differ. tests/orientation.rs on a roll #8 NEF copy whose Orientation tag reads 6 and 8: sides swapped, corners where a turn puts them, twin the two turns differ; with the flip forced to 0 the check fails. No RAW on the owner's disks carries a turn today.

title: The editor's preview and the thumbnails read RAWs at half size
detail: Owner's decision. A RAW at least twice the preview's 2000 px is read by LibRaw at half size, one pixel per 2x2 block without demosaic, then reduced to the preview: about 0.35 s instead of 1 s for a 24 MP NEF, and a quarter of the memory. Full resolution (zoom, export, roll previews) still decodes whole.
outcome: Preview and thumbnails share render::decode's `alone`, now `mosaic(path, PREVIEW_SIDE)`; decode_full stays whole. Every check green.

title: A slid value reaches the image at each render's landing, not on a 30 Hz clock
detail: Owner's decision. The hand handed a dragged value to the store at most every 1/30 s, so an image waited up to 33 ms for its tick. It now hands at most once a 120 Hz frame and the render slot (one in flight, the latest waiting) paces the image. The histogram still counts at 30 fps.
outcome: Real-window drag bench on DSC_6432, release, M2 Max: exposure 13 renders for 60 notches, cadence p50 33.4 ms, to 41 renders at p50 10.1 ms; contrast 18 at 32.9 ms to 52 at 9.9 ms; a notch's handed-to-shown p50 6.1 to 3.2 ms. track.rs test restated on the interval, its twins kept.

title: The RAW preview read whole again, half size a choice in the View menu
detail: Owner judged the half-size preview visibly softer. The editor's preview reads a RAW whole by default; View > Read RAW Previews at Half Size switches to the half-size read (kept in preferences as halfSizePreviews) and re-reads the open frame so the two can be compared. The measuring copies and Prepare the Roll stay at half size.

title: The canvas band's keys centred in their 40-point band
detail: The zoom bubble and the library key were laid at the top of the band over the image, against the bar. Each row now takes its own height and sits centred, as Swift's zoomBubble does; canvas_layout checks the panel key's margins by pixel, with a twin on the old top placement.

title: A decode is laid on the GPU beside the engine, so no render waits on its upload
detail: The owner's log showed view renders at 20 to 190 ms in pairs 1.5 to 2.5 s after a frame opened, when its full resolution landed: the 24 MP upload (about 390 MB, 100 ms) held the engine every render locks. oni-graph gains an Uploader that makes a source's textures from any thread; the shared engine uploads through the surface's gate alone, then locks only to reduce. Opening, thumbnails, full resolution and the dust patches' decode go this way. The zoom bench now pans in bursts while full resolution is built, walks the ladder and pinches, at a laptop's full screen, and reports the interface thread's longest tick.
outcome: P1073044.RW2 (owner's settings), release, M2 Max: upload 96 to 101 ms off the engine; pans during the build p99 5.5 to 8.1 ms end to end, ladder worst 12.6 ms, pinch worst 7.8 ms. The interface thread still pauses about 40 ms once during the upload (wgpu's queue), unchanged by 8 MB bands. upload_tests checks an upload lands beside a held engine and waits on a closed gate, its twin a lock that waits; a mutant uploading under the lock fails it.

title: Thumbnails read RAWs at half size, kept for the editor only when it reads them so
detail: With the editor's preview whole again (#130), each thumbnail decoded its RAW whole. A thumbnail of 320 px reads it at half size; the preview it makes seeds the editor's cache only when the editor reads RAWs at half size too, so an opened frame is never the softer copy.
outcome: Roll #8 (40 frames), release, M2 Max, empty thumbnail cache: every thumbnail made in 14 s instead of 37 s, about 370 ms each instead of 1 s; the frame opened in the editor still decoded whole (1011 ms), so the editor never took the halved copy.

title: The Windows run green: checks that need Unix links or modes run everywhere or only where they can
detail: The Windows CI built every crate but failed to compile oni-library's swift_checks, which made a symbolic link with std::os::unix. The link half of that check runs on Unix only (a link needs a privilege on Windows); the quit guard's failed write is now caused by a folder standing where the sidecar goes, which fails on both systems, instead of Unix permissions. The Windows run now cancels a run of the same branch a newer push supersedes, and caches the cargo build between runs (Swatinem/rust-cache), as a cold build took about 40 minutes. Windows mounts no disk in one folder: Computer::system names the drives (DRIVES), each drive's root a volume, Computer's rows the home then every drive present, a drive other than the home's one that comes and goes; the mounts watcher compares Computer's rows, so it reads drives as it reads /Volumes. The first full Windows run built everything and failed 23 checks, all but two on separators: the archive keeps paths as strings and Windows hands `\`. Paths are now kept with `/` alone on Windows (paths::normal, which every paths function and canonical apply; a no-op on the Mac, where `\` is a name's character); the places that turned a Path into a string without it go through it. A copy on a board in memory is shared by its holders (pasteboard::Shared), so the leftovers check reads its copy back off the Mac; the panel's ⌥⌘] check goes through its menu on Windows, where Slint reads a bare Ctrl+Alt from a headless rig as AltGr. The second run failed 3 checks: a roll's trail cut on the system separator (now `/`, the archive's), and two checks that wrote their expected paths with `\`. The third run failed 2: a former library's folders were laid back from their parts with a leading `/`, which no drive takes (now rooted at the drive Windows names first, checked on the Mac with drive paths), and a burst of renders spaced by 2 ms sleeps that last 15 ms on Windows (now submitted at once).
outcome: The Windows run green for the first time (run of 0b541d3): every crate built and every check passed on windows-latest, the GPU checks included.

title: The library column follows the photo opened: its folders unfold, its row comes into view, and a click reads as Swift's
detail: Ported from Swift's revealInTree, expandAncestors on the ring's move, centreSelected and TreeEngine.reveal/anchoredHere: each time the photo the column follows changes (grid double click, the column, an arrow walking the roll, a file opened at launch), the folders above it unfold once and its row is centred, held inside the column, with no animation; a fold made by hand afterwards stays until the photo changes, and the centre key unfolds again. Opening a folder unfolds every folder under it (openFolder). On the Projects tab the photo rings under the first project holding it, which unfolds, and the list centres it; the centre key is on that tab too. A click in a tree never scrolls it. The click itself follows TreeEngine.click: the chevron's zone folds and nothing else, a folder or project row beside a photo opens the first photo it holds (openFromTree), and a double click on a folder types over its own name.
outcome: A window check (sidebar_reveal) opens a photo in a hand-folded roll from the grid, walks with the arrow, clicks rows and chevrons, presses the centre key and opens a project's photo, asserting folds, rings and the row in view with a twin each; the library_column check now asserts a click leaves the scroll and the chevron folds; unit tests for unfold_to, find and first_path. Disabling the archive unfold, the project reveal or anchoredHere each makes the window check fail.

title: The scroll knobs grabbable: a drag, a page per track press, Option to the spot, as AppKit's scroller
detail: Every ScrollKnob takes the pointer on a 17 pt edge strip (NSScroller.scrollerWidth) where it widens to 10 pt over a faint track: a press on the knob drags the content by the knob's travel scaled to the content's; a press on the track jumps a page less NSScrollView's 10 pt verticalPageScroll toward the pointer and, held, repeats after 0.4 s every 75 ms (NSCell's periodic delay) until the knob stands under the pointer, the system's default 'Jump to the next page' (AppleScrollerPagingBehavior unset); Option inverts it and jumps the knob's middle to the spot. A Scroller writes its Flickable's offset; the gallery's knob calls Library.scrolled, the wheel's own way, so tiles, the pinned heading and thumbnails follow. The content itself still never drags.
outcome: scroll::the_knob_drags_the_content_and_its_track_pages_as_appkit_s (catalogue): a 120 pt knob drag moves the content 120 × its ratio within 1 pt (twin: not one for one), clamps at both ends, a click pages 440 pt, a held press stops after exactly two pages, Option lands at a quarter, the wheel still scrolls over the strip and a content drag does not. scroll::the_gallery_knob_scrolls_the_grid_the_wheel_s_way on 1200 photos: the grid follows within 1 pt, the visible tiles, pinned heading and thumbnails follow, the slowest knob move 1.2 ms (dev build), a track click pages, a drag on the tiles scrolls nothing. Mutants: the page jump without page-keep and the gallery knob without its handler each fail them.

title: The phone pairs with the desktop end to end: the QR's link through the phone's own FFI, reconnection after a restart, Forget Phones
detail: Audit of the path the Android app takes (zxing reads an oni-link:// payload, parse_pairing_code, RemoteSession.pair, then RemoteSession.connect with the stored key and addresses) against the desktop's Host. The protocol, the URI and the Kotlin bindings already lined up (bindings regenerated from this branch are byte-identical to the app's). Fixed: a press was marked taken when the link thread read it, before the interface thread applied it, so a screen published in between by another hand dropped it from the phone; HostEvents::receive now hands a Receipt that Link::handle marks between the store's apply and the publish. The port a code names is kept in <support>/Link/port.txt and a later launch listens there first, so a phone paired while 53318 was taken still finds the desktop. The link stops with its Shell. The sheet names the phones connected (or how many are paired) and carries FORGET PHONES, which revokes and cuts every paired phone, as the phone app's Forget Desktop tells the owner to do on the desktop.
outcome: tests/window/phone.rs drives oni-link-ffi, the phone app's own code, against the real window: the sheet's pixels are its URI's QR (twin: another URI's are not), a wrong secret pairs nothing (twin of the pairing), the phone pairs, Step D +3 moves the store and the phone reads it, its undo returns it, Walk opens B and stops at the end, the closed sheet's code refuses a late phone; after a restart the trusted phone reconnects without a code on the same port and steps the frame, a stranger is refused, and FORGET PHONES cuts it and refuses it again. oni-link remote.rs: a press read but not applied stays shown through another hand's screen, its twin marking on read loses it. phone.rs: the link listens on the port the last code named, its twin an unreadable file naming none. Not tried with a real phone.

title: The texture pool keeps an idle texture for eight renders, so a notch never makes its chain's textures again
detail: The pool freed every texture not reused by the very next render. A notch's own small reads (the input histograms, the loupe, a one-pixel read) sit between two of its renders, so each render allocated and cleared its whole chain again, about 1.5 ms per 43 MB texture on the M2 Max. An idle texture now waits IDLE_RENDERS (8) renders before it is freed; purge() still frees everything at once under memory pressure.
outcome: cost.rs on 2000 px: Texture's chain 11.0 to 7.5 ms (ten passes), 6.8 ms (seven); two chained per-pixel passes 2.40 to 1.44 ms; 41 textures made over 41 runs to 0. Real-window drag on DSC_6432 (Exposure, thumbnails read, machine loaded by builds): notch end to end p99 23.2 ms to 5.7-6.3 ms on two of three runs. The pool check (now tests/pool.rs) adds a small read between renders of a chain, its twin the old one-render policy failing with 12 textures made.

title: The day key counted once per frame by its count, not by a ratio of timings
detail: swift_checks' the_day_is_computed_once_per_frame compared two timings and failed under a loaded machine. film_group counts the keys its thread computes; the check asserts one per frame for the cut and two for the twin keyed twice.

title: The flows bench says a roll was never prepared instead of waiting
detail: On a roll never prepared, requireRoll opens every frame on Prepare the Roll, which holds the editor; ONI_BENCH=flows waited forever for the gallery. It now ends at once naming the cause. Real flow on roll #8 after the night's merges: 3 frames picked, double-clicked open and edited through resizes, no failure. Back in the gallery, the flow waits 300 ms before it looks: the grid lands on the open photo in a change handler Slint runs later, and a click computed on the scroll before the landing reached the last row in 1 run of 3; 6 of 6 since.

title: An unreadable support file is set aside, never written over; a photo never moves without its settings
detail: From the reviews' data list. Favourites, projects and the flat-field index read through read_json: a file that does not parse is read again after 100 ms (the Swift app writes its mask list in place) and, still the same and still unreadable, renamed <name>.unreadable-<nanoseconds> before anything writes it; roots.json, which neither app writes, is only read. The flat-field index is written through a sibling and a rename. roll_folder::move_items moves a photo's sidecar first and brings it back if the photo cannot follow, where the photo moved first and could land without its settings. set_label, set_exif and set_roll_draft already refused an unreadable sidecar.
outcome: Adversarial review twice: the first pass's refusal of a move onto an existing sidecar could split a roll on undo and was dropped; the torn-read race with the Swift app is covered by the second read. Checks: an unreadable favourites file set aside whole and its twin kept; a photo whose settings cannot follow stays with them, its twin the old order landing it bare; a stale sidecar at the destination replaced as before.

title: The parity counts and the ten largest gaps as they stand
detail: The zoom bubble's column key and the traffic lights' inset are done (#125, #131); sidecar batches are partial (#89). The ten largest gaps rewritten from the partial and missing rows: an unconverted frame's embedded preview, Windows' own surfaces, sound and touch, the watchdog, Prepare the Roll's leftovers, pickers, the archive tree's hand, the design system's interactions, sidecar batches, the instruments.

title: The interface thread's watchdog writes its blocks and the console counts them
detail: Diagnostics.startWatchdog's rule: the interface thread beats every 0.1 s with what the window shows, a thread of its own writes BLOCKED past 0.35 s of silence and recovered when it answers, each with the process's footprint (proc_pid_rusage on macOS, GetProcessMemoryInfo on Windows), one block however long it lasts; the console shows the count. The blocked thread's stack, read through Mach on the Mac, is not ported.
outcome: The check drives one silence of 0.9 s as one block and its end, its twin 0.2 s as none. Roll #8's real flow under the release build wrote no block.

title: The editor's routes as Swift's: the measuring window armed and disarmed, Return, ⌘K, De-dust, Space, ⌘A, the brush kept, a preset's balance unasked
detail: From the reviews' editor list, items 2 to 6. adopt (EditorScene+Actions.swift:73-82): a frame no balance touched opens with its window proposed and armed, a sheet dropping the margin an earlier opening proposed; onChange(of: tab) (OpenNegativeApp.swift:509-512) records the panel left on every route and disarms on leaving Crop; validate(with:) (EditorScene+Propagation.swift:181-188) applies the window then leaves Crop; ⌘K and the bar's key are openCrop (EditorScene+Menus.swift:110); toggleCorrecting leaves the Lab first; correctionBrushRadius is kept; columnKeys (EditorScene+Disk.swift:46-60) takes Space in the Lab to the gallery and ⌘A beside a photo; live(.emulator) is a photo beside the editor; applyPreset runs the balance Each without the question (EditorScene+Paste.swift:189). The window is drawn on Crop and Color only (EditorScene+Card.swift:96).
outcome: A window check drives every route on four graded scans with the GPU canvas, each with its twin; unit checks on the route, the opening window and the editor's ⌘A. The scanner and gestures checks now assert Swift's Space and ⌘K. The tree rings no folder, so columnKeys' ringed-folder step stays unreachable.

title: The gallery lands on the open photo, renames its headings in place and takes a Finder drop; Prepare the Roll applies and keeps the remembered flat-field sliders
detail: From the reviews' gallery and Prepare the Roll lists. GalleryEngine.land: each time the grid shows (from the editor, Export or Prepare the Roll) and on each surface switched to, the open photo's middle at the viewport's, clamped, else the top. RollHeaderContent: a heading in place or pinned takes the click and picks no cell; its double click types over it, opened on explicitName (a roll's name, empty on a plain folder, a project's name); Return, the focus leaving or a click on the grid commits a trimmed new name through renameFolder or renameProject, Escape cancels, the ONI Trash renames nothing. dropDestination: in the gallery only, add(_:) opens the first item's folder (the item itself when a folder) and then the first photo among the items in the editor; nothing is copied, moved or written. Prepare the Roll opens on the first frame's flat-field through withRemembered and keeps the three sliders as its own move. A flagged frame that cannot be decoded is written onto the roll, as Swift queues its job before the decode (EditorScene+RollReference.swift:375-376): the review's finding was Swift's rule, now pinned.
outcome: Window checks: back from the editor A48 lands centred and the first photo at the top, the hidden grid keeping its place (its twin); a heading's single click picks nothing, its double click renames the folder on the disk, Escape renames nothing, a click on a cell commits, a project renamed trimmed and an empty name refused; a drop refused beside a photo, then a file opening its folder and the first photo, a folder opening no photo, the dropped files byte for byte unchanged. Prepare the Roll: the colour kept applied with the Amount whole (its twin), a dialled frame keeping its own, the Picker Size keeping nothing and the Temperature all three; a flagged unreadable frame on the roll, an unflagged one left as it was. Each check fails with its fix taken out. Adversarial review of the heading rename and the drop found no loss; its findings fixed: the open frame's settings are written before its folder moves (a failed write keeps the folder's name), a folder read in flight under the old names is superseded, a heading half typed is dropped when another folder opens or the surface changes, a drop under a sheet is refused, and on Windows a name holding `\` is refused as `/` is. Left: a scroll that moves the heading being typed may commit it (unverified). Off Unix two paths name one item when they resolve to one spelling, so a rename changing only a letter's case is not refused as taken on Windows.

title: A phone on a spent code learns it is refused; the link's key and trusted phones are written whole and owner-only
detail: From the reviews' phone list. The Host takes the pairing window before Welcome, so a second phone that finished the handshake on the same code is hung up on instead of welcomed then dropped; Remote::pair reads any refusal as Error::Spent, which the FFI hands over as Failed and both apps show as a used or expired code (Refused stays the revoked phone's). host.key, trusted.txt and port.txt are written through a sibling, synced and renamed, 0600 on Unix; a host.key left readable by others is closed on start; on Windows the support folder's profile ACL is relied on. Previews and discovery wait on the phone: neither app draws the wire's Preview nor runs a multicast query.
outcome: Checks: two phones finishing the handshake on one code, the first welcomed and the second hung up on with one Paired, its twin the old order failing it; a closed window reads Spent and a stranger by key stays Refused; through the FFI a reused code is Failed with the spent reason, a stranger Refused; the key and the list 0600 with no sibling left, a blocked write leaving the list whole, an older 0644 key closed on start, its twin a plain write readable by others. scripts/check green. No real phone driven.

title: A canvas texture Slint refuses is tried again and said once, never a silent blank
detail: The canvas's texture was kept for its size even when Slint refused to import it, so every later render of that size drew into a texture nothing showed. It is kept only once imported; a refusal is logged and said once in the session.

title: Copy Settings on the Windows clipboard under the app's own formats
detail: On Windows the board was the process's memory, so a copy never crossed windows or relaunches. It is the system clipboard under formats registered by the types' names (app.opennegative.settings, .framing, .measure-window), opened for each operation with a few tries while another program holds it, through clipboard-win (already in the tree under arboard). A Windows check writes the settings and reads them back, its twin a text that leaves no settings; a runner whose clipboard will not open skips it.
outcome: The Windows run green with it (run of 6d289a5); the parity rows for Copy Settings and the settings pasteboard are done.

title: A help mark's note shows at once, a tooltip after the system's delay
detail: Both drew on the one tip layer after the tooltip delay; Swift's dsHelpBubble shows at once. Tips.note raises Tip.at-once, which a state without delay reads; Tips.hover lowers it. The sidebars check hovers a key (not at once, the twin) and notes a help mark (at once).

title: The library column's trees take ⌘ and ⇧ picks, Swift's context menus and a project's rename in place
detail: TreeEngine.click (TreeEngine.swift:401-425): each tree keeps its own pick and anchor; ⌘ toggles a row in, the row a plain click anchored on joining the first ⌘ pick; ⇧ adds the rows between the anchor and the row shown; the pick's photos, and on the archive every surveyed photo under a folder picked (pickInColumn, EditorScene+Disk.swift:34), become the selection and nothing opens; a plain click empties the pick. The right click acts on the pick when it lands inside it, else on its row (TreeEngine.swift:232): filmContextMenu (EditorScene+Gallery.swift:112) gives a folder alone Rename… (renameRequest, revealed and typed in place), Make a Roll or Back to a Folder, New Folder Inside (no navigator naming), a divider and Show in Finder, photos alone Edit when one then the cell menu on them, anything else Show in Finder; projectContextMenu (EditorScene+Rolls.swift:179) gives photos alone the same, one project alone Delete Project, several none. A project's double click types over its name (rename, then renameProject, trimmed, an empty or unchanged name keeping it); a click, a fold or another rename commits what a row's field holds (exitEditing). A click on no row of the archive tree drops the picks and the ring (clickEmpty). Name rows show a photo's whole file name and a folder's own name (FilmRow.title, ProjectRow.title), a thumbnail its stem (TreeLayers.caption). Every file operation goes through the existing paths: rename_folder, set_roll, new_folder's create_dir, the cell menu's gestures and save_projects.
outcome: A window check on two rolls and two projects: ⌘ and ⇧ picks lit and opening nothing, a folder picked bringing its photos and the anchor; the menus' lines on a pick, a lone photo (Edit first), a lone folder (four lines, the divider before Show in Finder) and a mixed pick (Show in Finder alone); Make a Roll writing then Back to a Folder removing the marker; New Folder Inside twice; Rename… cancelled, then committed by a click elsewhere, the folder renamed on the disk; a click on no row unlighting every row; a project renamed trimmed into projects.json, an empty name refused; the projects' photo pick and its menu, Delete Project, no menu on two projects; then through the window's pointer a plain click, a click with ⌘ held and a right click. Each assertion has its twin; the check fails with ⌘ ignored or the project's rename taken out. Unit checks on the pick's arithmetic and pickInColumn. Left: the archive tree rings no folder, so ⌘A's ringed-folder step stays unreachable; no drop on the project tree, no pinned parent row, no thumbnails on the projects, no click on the projects' empty ground.

title: Prepare the Roll takes a frame and loads a picture as its mask; the measure and the roll's previews lay the custom mask and dust patches
detail: Use This Frame as Flat-Field (EditorScene+RollReference.swift:278-297) decodes the picked frame through the mask library at the whole Amount and unticks it, Setting… meanwhile, No Mask Set on a failure, no offer to move it out; Load… (FlatFieldControls.swift:106-127) names the chosen picture as the roll's mask with its Amount kept, Loading… meanwhile, No Mask Loaded on a failure. Swift's Pipeline.framed lays a frame's custom mask and cached dust patches in front of every reading, roll preview and sheet tile (Pipeline.swift:254-266, RollPreviews.swift:124-135, EditorScene+RollReference.swift:359-373); oni-pipeline's Resident reads them from the support folder and the caches onto the measurer's and the previews' graphs, the mask kept by id, each patch read afresh per reading, one missing left out. Checks: oni-measure/tests/laying.rs (mask and patch reach a reading; twins: files gone, no files, another id) and the window check prepare_masks (Load… and the take with their failures and Amount rules, a preview through the mask and back without it, the measure on the panel apart from the bare roll, the same mask measuring the same as twin); each check fails with its half of the change taken out. Auto White Balance and New Contact Sheet share the measurer, so they lay them too, as Swift's do. Left: the editor's input histograms read without them.
outcome: A mask's TIFF is now written through a sibling and a rename, so a crash never leaves a truncated mask the next load would take whole.

title: Presets and printer profiles sort as localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare
detail: Both lists sorted by lowercased bytes, which put an accented name after Z. oni_settings::collation::case_insensitive orders by base letters (Latin accents folded, æ œ ß spelt out), the accents only where the letters tie, never the case; the preset shelf and the printer profiles use it. The check sorts Élan and émulsion among the E's, its twin the byte order putting Élan after Zeiss.

title: Each feature's share of a busy render, measured
detail: cost.rs (ONI_BENCH_COST=1) times the whole pipeline on a 2000 px preview with every finishing feature on, then each at rest in turn.
outcome: M2 Max, release: busy 6.96 ms, at rest 2.77 ms. Texture 3.65 ms of it, chroma denoise 1.49, sharpen 1.35; vignette, sauce, spectrogram and curves under 0.3 now that they share one pass. Texture's blurs are bound by their reads, 13 rgba32float taps a pixel a pass: the next steps would be tiles shared in workgroup memory, which the graph's per-pixel stage model does not offer, or the luma carried in fewer channels, which the rgba32float rule forbids; both are the owner's call.

title: The editor's levels and curves input histograms lay the custom mask and dust patches
detail: refreshLevelsInput and refreshManualCurvesInput (EditorScene+Measurements.swift:88-128) read through Pipeline.reading and Pipeline.histogram(of:), whose Pipeline.apply lays the frame's custom flat-field mask and cached dust patches (Pipeline.swift:254-266). oni-measure's Reader now takes a Laying: nothing, read from files (the measurer's Resident) or held, the inputs the canvas engine already keeps; Engine::inputs lays the engine's own mask and patches, its kept reading also keyed on how many patches and whether the mask were laid, and a forgotten patch drops the kept readings. Every other Swift reading through Pipeline.reading, Pipeline.measured or Pipeline.apply was already laid: the automatic keys (balance, filter balance, roll reference, the base pipette) and the sheet tiles through the measurer (#151), the loupe, the canvas and its output histogram, the export and the roll previews through the engine or Resident. Check: render/inputs_tests.rs (a mask and a patch move both readings; twins: a missing mask or patch reads the bare frame, and the file arriving later moves the kept reading); it fails with the engine's inputs left out.
outcome: M2 Max, release, ONI_BENCH=settled on a scratch copy of two Roll #8 frames, three runs a build: a held reading (the small copy) p50 4.37 ms before and 4.49 after on a plain frame, 4.37 before and 5.03 after on a frame naming a custom mask (p90 5.1 to 9.6), the mask's division now in it; the rest reading unchanged (43 ms masked, 72 to 76 plain); the notch's end to end p50 2.2 to 2.4 ms either way, its p99 within the machine's noise.

title: Rust twins for the Swift self-checks that had none
detail: Each from the Swift check's body, beside the code it checks, each with its twin. Rendering: CaptureExposure's render (a scan shot 0.67 stop over and brought back renders as the frame shot alike), FilmProbe.axisChecks (the density a reading names is the kernel's axis at both ends of the ceiling's range), GainPanel and TemperatureTintPanel (each slider's label and track measured through the kernel and read off the panel's Slint), the sheet rendering sharpening and chroma denoise off, the thumbnail criterion (opposite to its negative on a thin and a dense manufactured negative, a flat plate refused; on roll #8 under ONI_RAW_DIR), NegativeView's Compare reference (extracted as oni_core::compare::reference, behaviour unchanged). Data and interaction: GeometryPanel's reset, turns, mirror, proposed window and remembered framing; Viewport's every-width 100 % rung, the ladder walked, the corner clamp; CanvasEvents' hand-following pan and device doses; MemoryBudget; Thumbnails' scan rules; WhatsNew's headings; the menus' shortcuts claimed once and their bare keys gated on the window's focus; every icon present; AppFolders' stand-ins and single routes. A check's folders: Options::default's caches is a stand-in named after its run (the app hands system::caches() itself, so the app is unchanged), patches::caches is system::caches, and the window rig gives its dust patches a caches folder of its own, where the scanner and editor window checks, handing only a support folder, opened the machine's real library index. checks.md marks what the port lacks as blocked.
outcome: checks.md: 104 twin, 32 partial, 11 none, 15 blocked (from 91, 23, 48). Divergences reported, not changed: the console log names frame stems and its own path, which Swift's tokens never do; the thumbnail's inversion bar is frame-dependent on roll #8, three frames of nine at rest reading -0.78 to -0.86 against Swift's -0.90, Swift's figure on them unmeasured.

title: The library column's last tree gestures: the pinned parent row, the projects' thumbnails, a drop on the projects, their empty ground
detail: PinnedRow (TreeEngine.swift:139-152,332-380): on both trees the nearest open row whose children pass under the top is held there on the panel, pushed up by the row after its children; its chevron's zone folds it, elsewhere it clicks the row and centres it (sidebar::pinned, tree_column::pin_column, ds PinnedTreeRow). The projects' tree is laid as the archive's (TreeEngineLayout.frames), a photo a thumbnail by its stem when the layout asks, and the layout key stands on the projects too, cycling sidebarLayout.editor beside a photo and sidebarLayout.gallery in the gallery (EditorScene+Card.swift:386-441, OpenNegativeApp.swift:253-254); the projects' reveal is centred by Rust on the laid frames. A press moved 4 points on a project row carries the pick when its row is in it, else the row; TreeDropTarget.resolve picks a join or a landing, ringed or lined, and the release joins a project (addToProjectDrop) or reorders (reorderProjectTreeDrop) through project::add_to, reorder_drop and reorder_root, written to projects.json alone. A click on no project row drops the pick, the selection and the ring (clickEmptyProjects). Checks: sidebar.rs (TreeDropTarget.selfCheck's and rowViewSelfCheck's reading and pinning, each with its twin), project_drop.rs (join and land, twins refused), the window check tree_leftovers (thumbnails and both layout keys, the pin held, pushed and clicked through the pointer, drags joining, landing and reordering projects through the pointer, a short press clicking, the empty ground), and sidebar_reveal and tree_hand following the margin and the thumbnails.

title: The Custom space lists the printer profiles ColorSync knows, beside the folders walked
detail: OutputProfile.installed walks the profile folders, then adds what ColorSyncIterateInstalledProfiles lists (its iteration is unreliable alone: 10 in one context, 78 in another), the checks asking nothing more. oni-colour::colorsync reads each profile's URL through ColorSync and CoreFoundation; off the Mac it lists none. The check sees the system's own profiles among the files ColorSync lists, each a file that exists.

title: The window checks under a whole run: limits that wait for a loaded machine
detail: With 66 window checks in parallel processes the window binary takes about 125 s, past scripts/check's 120 s stop, and the contact sheet's 10 s waits timed out under that load while it passes alone in 5 s. The stop is 240 s by default (ONI_CHECK_LIMIT still overrides it) and the contact sheet's waits 60 s; a wait returns as soon as its condition holds.

title: A Settings sheet behind a gear in the header, and a phone key beside it
detail: The header gains two square keys left of the export key: the phone opens Pair Phone, the gear a Settings sheet holding the half-size RAW previews and the key clicks, each the same preference as its menu item. Escape and DONE close it. The bar turns compact a little earlier (the toolbar check now compares 1440 and 1700 px).

title: Key clicks, silent by default
detail: Swift's click-down/up.wav (copied with the owner's leave) play on a key's press and rise, a switch, a tab change, a medal and a reorder, the pitch drawn within ±120 cents per press and kept for the rise, at volume 0.5, each click stopping the last. Rendered in Rust and played by NSSound on macOS, PlaySound on Windows, no audio crate. soundMuted unset reads as muted: the owner's default where Swift clicks.

title: The log names no person: session tokens for photos, every path scrubbed from a sealed report
detail: Swift's Diagnostics.token: a photo or folder is written to the log as # and six hex digits of SHA-256 over a per-run salt, the same all run and unreadable back. Render, thumbnail, dust and full-resolution lines and the watchdog's witness use it; the phone's name and the log's own path are no longer written. The sealed log is this run's alone (the last run is kept beside it as oni.previous.log, never sent) and passes a scrub turning the home into ~ and every remaining path into <path>. A source scan fails when a log call takes a stem, a name or a displayed path.

title: The phone holds the desktop panel's Roll, Color and Details tabs and its Scanner or Pro face, in the desktop's design system
detail: oni-link protocol 2: Command::Face, StepParam and ResetParam, and ToPhone::Screen carrying a Panel (the face, and each slider the panel shows on that face with its tab, block, label, readout, track position and modified mark); State keeps the panel out of its own encoding, so the desktop answers a protocol 1 phone in protocol 1 with the scanner's screen it always read, and the pairing code keeps its own version 1. oni-link-ffi mirrors it additively (Face, PanelTab, Param, PanelRow, Panel, DisplayState.panel, Command::SetFace/StepParam/ResetParam); its scanner types moved to scanner.rs to stay under the file ceiling. oni-core: Command converts from a phone key by TryFrom, a slider's step being the host's to resolve; link::Sliders lets the host lay out rows and resolve steps; a face switch lands as Command::Face (refused without a photograph, as toggleLab) and comes out as Outward::Face. oni-app: app/phone_link/panel.rs lays the rows as the Slint panes do (Flat-Field when masked, Source Balance with the mode's end labels, Density Ceiling, Dye Separation and Balance Strength off the Scanner face, monochrome and RGB passes; Color, Lighting and Effects on Pro, Paper Correction on a paper; Sharpening and Chroma Denoise off a contact sheet, Texture), readouts by Field::readout, a step a hundredth of the track in the shown sense, a reset the double click's base, applied as Command::Set like the panel's own writes (one undo step, the sidecar written, the flat-field sliders remembered); the face from the phone is remembered as the bar's switch remembers it. Android (open-negative-initiative-mobile, branch rs-tabs): a Pro | Scanner face switch and Roll | Color | Details tabs as the desktop's segmented Tabs; Pro sliders as −10 −1 readout +1 +10 keys over a track mark; the Scanner face keeps its screen above every tab but Details and its machine and keypad on Color. ds/Tokens.kt generated by scripts/ds-tokens.py from crates/oni-ui/ui/ds/tokens.slint, ds/DS.kt rebound on it as theme.slint binds the tokens, screens free of literal sizes and colours.
outcome: Checks: oni-link tests/panel.rs (protocol 1 answered without the panel, twin a protocol 2 phone gets it; too old a phone turned away; the panel out of State's encoding), oni-link-ffi tests (panel and keys across the bindings, every Param mirrored), oni-core tests/link.rs (face and step through a host resolver, one undo step, twins), oni-app phone_link::panel unit tests and the window check phone_tabs (rows equal the panel's readouts, a step reaches the sidecar and undoes, the Scanner face from the phone moves the bar and the Lab, a slider hidden there does not move, the bar's switch reaches the phone). Android: PanelLayoutTest, TokensTest (the copy's source hash against tokens.slint, no literal in a screen, each with a twin), ds-tokens.py --check in the build script and the workflow; debug APK built. Not run on a phone: none attached.

title: The Android launcher icon is the desktop app's
detail: The APK carried ic_launcher_art.png, a blurred photographic orange-and-green backdrop behind the dashed ring and half disc, which is also the iPhone app's AppIcon.png, not the desktop's icon. The adaptive icon is now AppIcon.icon's: its visible layer, App Icon keycap test.png, on the 72 dp the launcher's mask shows (mipmap ic_launcher_foreground at every density), over its fill as a vector gradient from display-p3(1, 0.694, 0.384) in sRGB (#FFAD50) down to #FF4700. The hidden final layer stays unused.
outcome: The APK's resources hold the new foreground and background and no longer the old art. The iPhone app still carries the photographic icon.

title: Texture speed: the exact paths first, a Fast choice only if it earns its place
detail: docs/research/texture-speed.md: weights from the CPU, Texture folded into its last blur and one pass per blur with rows in workgroup memory are exact (about 3.65 to 2.0 ms at 2000 px) and need no setting; one- or two-channel luma is exact but needs the owner's word on the rgba32float rule; half-resolution wide blurs are the only inexact path, offered in Settings as screen-only Fast if they pass an error bound and save 30 % at 1:1. Also found: the prewarm's 64 px frame never reaches Texture.

title: Apple's decoder against LibRaw, and a recovery strategy for rolls prepared in the Swift app
detail: scripts/decoder-gap/run decodes RAWs with CIRAWFilter set as RawDecode.configured (apple-decode.swift) and with oni_decode (examples/blocks.rs) on one 8-pixel grid, fits gains and a 3x3 matrix (examples/decoder_fit.rs) and renders the frames through their Swift sidecars (oni-pipeline examples/decoder_gap.rs). Roll #8 leans +0.11 stop red, -0.10 blue against the Swift render; gains recover about three quarters, a per-camera matrix all but the demosaic noise. docs/research/decoder-apple-vs-libraw.md weighs a matrix at decode, a sidecar migration and a decoder marker; no app behaviour changes.

title: Frontier Look Lab plan
detail: docs/research/frontier/lab-plan.md: the 27³ table as a chain of named parameters with neutral and Frontier values plus a measured-character blend that reproduces today's cube; a probe on frontier.cube puts skin +10.6° and blues +12.0° against neutral, mostly from the matrix's green-borrows-red term and the steep paper curve; ten steps, the first four changing no render.

title: Frontier Look Lab, step 1: the paper model and its bake
detail: oni-pipeline look_lab: LabParams with the plan's published neutral and Frontier sets, the matrix and the Fritsch-Carlson paper curve around the neutral green pivot, and a bake onto the machine's density lattice. Measured on the 1 440 constrained nodes: paper model at Frontier values median ΔE 1.67 against the cube (pivot 0: 2.07; identity and common paper: 3.47); 27³ bake p99 ΔE 0.34 against the chain (9³: 2.72); the diagnosis probe gives skin +10.6° and blue +12.5° against the neutral reference, green borrows red at neutral −12.5° on skin. No render, setting or interface change.

title: Frontier Look Lab, step 2: the colour stage, the measured character and the Frontier refit
detail: look_lab gains the Oklab stage (hue, twist and chroma by sector, saturation by L, grey cast), the character (the cube's residual against the shipped Frontier set, trilinear between its nodes) and a Levenberg-Marquardt fit; examples/look_lab_fit.rs writes resources/scanner/lab.json, which LabParams loads. Fitted Frontier full model: median ΔE 1.18 on the constrained nodes (colour stage at rest 1.94); character 1 gives frontier.cube back exactly. The full model's 27³ bake reaches p99 0.575 against the chain, past the 0.5 target (33³: 0.41), left for step 6.

title: Frontier Look Lab, step 3: the neutral set refitted against ONI Pro at rest
detail: look_lab::pro reads a synthetic grid around scanner::check_roll's grey both as the Frontier's cube input and through Pro's CPU references at rest (stage47, the points' saturation, the output clip) to display code; look_lab_fit refits the neutral set on it and the Levenberg-Marquardt step now holds values on their stops. Neutral against Pro: median ΔE 0.19 (seeds 5.61, Frontier set 15.2); the neutral matrix and sector chroma share a gauge (chroma gains 1.1 to 1.5), noted for the N ticks. Frontier refit: 1.19.

title: Frontier Look Lab, step 4: strips of roll #8 for the eye, and the Rust Frontier against Swift's
detail: examples/look_lab_strip.rs renders frames through five cubes side by side (the table, Lab Frontier without character, Lab neutral, Lab Frontier with green-borrows-red and the 240-300° sectors at neutral, the same with the seed's green-borrows-red) and measures named regions in Oklab; scripts/frontier-swift-dump.sh makes the Swift app's own Frontier renders it compares against. On DSC_6432 and DSC_6442: the refitted sets flip green-borrows-red (its neutral turns skin 6° more yellow; the seed's turns it 7° redder); the blue sectors at neutral take 7-9° of violet off the sky; LibRaw's decode puts the Rust Frontier skies 4-6° more violet than Swift's (mean gap 0.02-0.03).

title: The Swift app's icon on the desktop window and in the Dock
detail: A bare binary has no bundle: the 256 px render of Swift's AppIcon.icns is the window's icon (Windows' title bar and taskbar) and NSApplication's icon image (the Dock).

title: The prewarm reaches Texture: its shaders no longer compile on the first notch
detail: Texture rests under a 750 px side, so the 64 px prewarm frame never compiled its blurs and kernels and the first busy notch waited on them. The prewarm also renders 768 x 8 and 6048 x 8 strips, both blur reaches; Graph::stats counts compiled pipelines and a check asserts a prewarmed engine's busy notch compiles none, its twin that the small frame alone misses Texture.

title: A photo whose original cannot be found opens read-only, never as a new photo
detail: With the roll's disk unplugged, the sidecar's absence read as a new photo: rest settings, writable, Prepare the Roll opened on it (its base step decoding nothing) and every settle tried to write a sidecar for it, which a reconnected disk would have taken over the Swift roll's own. The store now checks the original first: absent, the frame opens read-only on the rest settings with a message saying its disk may be disconnected, nothing is written and Prepare the Roll is not offered. Beyond Swift, whose read has the same gap. Test fixtures that opened imaginary originals now create them.

title: The phone's sliders drag as the desktop's, in the desktop's simplified design system, and a dropped link is seen and redialled
detail: oni-link protocol 3, additive: Command::SetParam { param, position } places a panel slider's knob on its own track (0 to 1, the desktop mapping it by track_on and stored_on as the panel's drag does) and Command::ReleaseParam ends the drag; a protocol 2 phone is still answered with the panel.
