Remote::slide keeps one place on the wire, the latest parked behind it, and Remote::let_go sends the last place then the release; the knob is predicted at once, its readout stays the desktop's. oni-core link::Link holds the store on a phone's first place and releases it on ReleaseParam, any other key or the phone's disconnection, so a drag is one undo step even past the history's coalescing window; link::Move replaces Option<i8> in Sliders::command. The link's liveness: Remote now ends a session the desktop has not answered for QUIET (6 s, three pings), where a Wi-Fi drop leaves TCP half open and the phone believed itself connected while its presses fell into the socket; a dropped session shows the desktop's last answered screen, never an unanswered guess, and takes no press; Display.unanswered flags a guess; a desktop that is slow or cut off during the handshake now reads Unreachable, only a hang-up Refused. oni-link-ffi: RemoteSession.slide and let_go, DisplayState.unanswered. Android (open-negative-initiative-mobile, branch rs-sliders): the keycap components are gone; ds/ holds one Kotlin file per desktop component (Label, Button and IconButton, KeyPlate, Slider, Tabs, Section and Divider, Surface, Keypad with Key, KeyRow and LabScreen, WarningBand, StatusLine, Progress, TextField, Dialog, Icon with the Trinil glyphs) on a DS theme mirroring theme.slint, with Inter and Enriqueta bundled; every screen rebuilt from them; every panel slider a Slider (label, readout, rail with its fill, relative drag, double tap to reset); the link's state on top, a status line while the desktop answers, a warning band while redialling or down, every control out of reach meanwhile; the session survives five seconds off the screen, so turning the phone or a notification no longer hangs up, and redials on its own with backoff while in front, never giving up.
outcome: Likely causes of the drops, found in the code (no phone attached to measure them): every configuration change (the phone turned, the screen resized) recreated the activity, whose onStop hung up and onStart dialled again 0.15 to 0.3 s later; a link cut by the network was never noticed by the phone, which pinged without checking for answers, so it stayed 'connected' while the desktop had dropped it, and its dial loop gave up for good on a handshake timeout read as a refusal. Checks: oni-link tests/liveness.rs (two idle minutes on a paused clock keep the link, twin a silent cut is seen by the phone within QUIET and by the desktop, the unanswered press unshown; a silent desktop is Unreachable, twin a hang-up Refused), tests/panel.rs (one place in flight, the latest after, the release last; twin presses all fly; protocol 2 still served), oni-link-ffi drag test (twin a hung-up session sends nothing), oni-core tests/link.rs (a drag past the coalescing window is one undo step, twin two steps are two; a drag cut by a key or a lost phone still records), phone_link::panel unit test (a place lands where the panel's drag puts it on the frame's own track, twin the fixed range's place differs), window check phone_tabs (a phone drag lands, one undo, the readout the panel's, twin). Android: DesignSystemTest (no styled primitive, Material or keycap in a screen, twin the old lines are refused), ShadeTest, SliderLooksTest, LinkStatusTest, TokensTest; APK built. Not run on a phone; the iPhone app's Swift bindings were not regenerated.

title: The transition: each camera matched once to Apple's decode by a 3x3 folded into LibRaw's conversion
detail: oni-transition fits, once per camera (LibRaw's make and model), the 3x3 from LibRaw's Rec. 2020 to Apple's CIRAWFilter set as RawDecode.configured (in process through objc2), on the pooled clear squares of three frames spread over the camera's RAWs, aligned to the pixel; <support>/Transition/cameras.json keeps matrix, frames and residual, written atomically; oni-decode/src/rendition.rs folds it after conversion() for every decode of that camera (DNG, linear scans and absent cameras untouched; decode_native skips it). At launch and on each folder opened (macOS only) the library's RAWs are named off the interface thread, a camera the table lacks is matched behind a blocking sheet while the thumbnails' pass waits, then its frames' previews and thumbnails are drawn again. No sidecar is read or written. Z f roll #8: 4.2 s, render gap to Swift 0.0182 -> 0.0016 (gains 0.0051), blacks back to Swift's; S1R ColorPlus roll: 7.0 s, 0.0462 -> 0.0095. Windows has no table.

title: What LibRaw lets us tune, against the Swift app's CIRAWFilter
detail: docs/research/libraw-knobs.md: Swift sets colour noise reduction to 1 and turns luminance NR, sharpening, moire and lens correction off; LibRaw's AHD leaves 4.9 to 6.7 times the fine colour detail; no LibRaw knob matches Apple's colour NR, a fixed chroma blur of about 1.25 px in log space would; adjust_maximum_thr is still automatic (0.75).

title: A phone's step reaches the canvas with the panel folded
detail: A window check pairs a phone over loopback and steps Exposure with the panel shown then folded, each step rendered; ONI_BENCH=folded does the same in the real window and counts each step drawn, on Pro and on the Scanner face's keypad. Both pass: the owner's missed presses came from a link that dropped and never came back (no established connection, log ends on 'phone disconnected'), handed to #174.

title: The canvas follows every render with the panel folded
detail: The canvas card's rounded clip makes the renderer draw its children into a cached layer, redrawn only when a property inside changes; a render rewrites the canvas texture in place, so the layer kept the old texels whenever nothing else on the card moved, as with the panel folded and the phone or a key driving. Canvas.frame-revision and before-revision, read by Picture.revision, are bumped on every write. ONI_BENCH=folded now compares the drawn screen per step: before, the folded steps moved 0.00 on the Scanner face; after, 4.1 and 4.0 on Scanner, 4.2 and 4.2 on Pro. Only these two textures are rewritten in place; every other picture is a new Image.

title: LibRaw's white level stays the camera's: adjust_maximum_thr pinned to 0
detail: Left at 0.75, LibRaw lowered a frame's white level to its own brightest pixel when that passed 0.75 of white, up to +0.41 stop on a brightly exposed scan and different per frame (docs/research/libraw-knobs.md); roll #8 peaks at 0.56 so it never moved there. Owner's call. A test reads pinned.c for every automatic knob, its twin a copy without this pin.

title: Swift against LibRaw per camera: the hue gap depends on the hardware
detail: docs/research/decoder-per-camera.md: on greys Rust leans red-orange on the Nikon Z f (Red-Cyan +0.083 EV, Blue-Yellow -0.086 EV, 1.5 dE) and yellow on the Lumix S1R (+0.040, -0.292, 2.6 dE); constant within a camera (0.001-0.002 EV across 38 frames). The owner's -8 red-cyan matches the measured 8.5; the leftover yellow is the skin's extra chroma. The deeper blacks come from the decode's colour matrix, which a gain cannot remove. Only three cameras on the Mac with the T7 unplugged.

title: Sensor colours: the decode without the camera matrix, prototyped and measured
detail: oni-decode gains Colours (Matrix, the app's only path; Sensor, the 5000 K multipliers as a diagonal; SensorUnbalanced) and decode_in, tested with twins; oni-measure/examples/sensor_colours re-measures a roll as Prepare the Roll does in each colours (base pick found again in the rebate band) and renders both faces; scripts/sensor-colours compares with the Swift app's --render. docs/research/sensor-colours.md: neutrals closer to Swift on the S1R (2.9 to 1.7 dE x100), about equal on the Z f; foliage yellower and duller (-35 deg, x0.70), sky chroma x0.51, skin redder; blacks unchanged; fewer pixels outside sRGB; the 5000 K diagonal chosen over no balance (same once prepared, same rest look). Proposed: a Settings default for new rolls and a per-roll choice in Prepare the Roll, the transition skipping sensor rolls. No app behaviour changed. Its decode checks moved to oni-decode/src/tests.rs, as lib.rs passed its line ceiling.

title: The Frontier as the hand's own LUT on ONI's inversion, edited in any LUT tool
detail: Owner's call: the parametric Lab's strips were rejected; the Frontier goes through ONI's inversion first, then a LUT the owner edits. Settings > Frontier look: EXPORT writes the look in use, else ONI's own scanner look re-laid on display sRGB code (33 nodes), as a standard .cube; USE A FILE reads one and stands it in for the measured table on the Scanner face's Frontier machine, the file read again within a second of each save, a broken save keeping the last; MEASURED returns to the measured table. The path is ONI's: Pro's render, encoded to sRGB code, the hand's cube, then the warmth look. Kept in preferences (frontierLook), no sidecar field. Gallery thumbnails of Frontier frames refresh on their next render.

title: A roll's row in the tree draws its stock
detail: TreeRowChrome.defaultStock: the stock a hand picked for the roll, else its first photo's mode's generic stock, drawn as its artwork in a slot the size of Swift's mini canister (22 px), so glyphs and canisters share a starting edge. Folders holding no roll keep their glyph.

title: A stranger phone reads as refused on Windows too
detail: Windows CI: the window check's unpaired phone was not refused, as Windows reports a desktop's hang-up during the handshake as an aborted connection, which the phone took for a slow desktop and dialled again. ConnectionAborted now reads as a refusal like a reset or an end of stream; a timeout still dials again (unit test with its twin).

title: The transition's review: a camera that cannot be matched is remembered, a failed naming thread misnames no file, a failed search frees the thumbnails
detail: cameras.json gains `unmatched` (serde default, same version): a camera whose frames all stayed reachable but would not match is not measured again at every launch behind the blocking sheet. survey::named keeps one answer per file when a worker panics, so no file takes its neighbour's camera. The app's search runs under catch_unwind, so a panic there releases the thumbnails' pass instead of holding it for the session.

title: The Frontier Look Lab in the app: the measured table edited live from the Scanner face, every value a distance from the machine
detail: Steps 5 to 8 of docs/research/frontier/lab-plan.md, with one change: the sidecar's `frontierLab` stores each value's distance from the shipped Frontier set, so every slider rests on the measured render (the bake at zero equals frontier.cube) and a later refit keeps each edit's meaning. Settings: oni-settings FrontierLab (tolerant reader, clamped), in the look family so paste, roll sync and presets carry it with the Scanner keypad. Render: Pipeline::frontier bakes the Lab at 27³ when the frame has edits and keeps the measured cube otherwise. Panel: a Look Lab section on the Scanner face under Machine when Frontier is picked: twelve sector tabs with hue, twist and chroma, the matrix, the paper's gains and offsets, the grey cast by lightness, saturation by lightness and the character; each slider rests at 0 = Frontier, a double click returns it there.

title: The Look Lab's sliders read each effect from no effect: zero takes the Frontier's effect away, each slider opens on the machine's
detail: The owner's call: a slider's zero is no Frontier effect (identity matrix, no hue turn, chroma and paper gains at one, no cast, no character), and each slider opens on the fitted Frontier's own value, so the panel shows what the machine does on each parameter while the image stays the measured render. The sidecar still stores the distance from the machine's value, now held in twice the plan's travel so every effect is reachable from any fitted value; a double click returns a slider to the machine's value. The paper curve keeps the machine's until its graph ships.

title: Builds under a minute and a target directory that stops growing: one feature set, no kept debug objects, no empty test builds
detail: Four read-only research agents measured the causes: target/ held 47 GB of debug objects that split-debuginfo=unpacked keeps forever (30 GB of them the Slint crate's), the Slint crate (44 MB of generated Rust) was rebuilt 38 times in two days because `cargo run -p oni-app`, scripts/check and one-crate tests resolve different feature sets, 88 test binaries plus 11 examples were linked per check, and LibRaw compiled on one core. Changes: oni-hack (cargo-hakari) unifies features across commands, the phone-link crates excluded so an Android build never takes the desktop's; dev split-debuginfo off and no debug info for dependencies; oni-ui without debug info or incremental cache in dev (kept at opt-level 1: at 0 the 72 window checks slowed past a 120 s wait under the check's load) and without debug info in release; i-slint-compiler optimised in release; a profile `app` for the app the owner runs (release numbers, incremental, 256 units); `scripts/check` builds --tests only and the targets without tests skip their test build; cc's parallel feature for LibRaw.

title: scripts/live: the interface reloaded on each .slint save, no build
detail: A .slint edit still costs 87 s in dev and 212 s in the app profile (rustc's front end alone reads 44 MB of generated Rust for 75 s). Slint 1.18's live preview, enabled from the script (`--features slint/live-preview`, SLINT_LIVE_PREVIEW=1) so the workspace hack never takes the Slint compiler, makes the app interpret the .slint files and reload them on each save; checked by planting a parse error in a running app, which reported it at once. Built in target/live so the checked build and its features are untouched.

title: The Frontier unmixes at the frame's own Dye Separation, not a fixed 0.6
detail: The owner asked for the Frontier-mode mapping faults the study of the synthetic checker found to be fixed. Measured in the study's harness: the machine's fixed 0.6 dose unmixes a crosstalk-free negative it should leave alone; reading the frame's own Dye Separation (0.6 at rest, so every frame at rest renders as before) brings the chart's p90 from 4.97 to 3.53 against the virtual Frontier with the grey anchored. The chart's large median gap (9.9) is its roll median sitting 0.11 D above its grey, a click under rule 1, not code. The scale and pedestal changes help only together and with the roll measured on the same pedestal-free axis, on scanner TIFFs only: not taken.

title: Proto, a third Scanner machine: ONI's inversion then the virtual Frontier's look fitted on the synthetic checker
detail: The owner's call after the checker study: the look is what the virtual Frontier does after a faithful inversion. The owner converted the synthetic negative in ONI; a 33³ table from that export (display sRGB code) to the virtual Frontier's Base render was fitted on 2 235 pairs (the 507 patches and both gamut bands), greys weighted onto the Frontier's grey curve and monotone, smoothing chosen by 5-fold cross-validation: median ΔE 0.24 / p90 1.29 on held-out patches, 0.12 over the whole chart against 13.5 for the export alone. The worst patches are saturated reds and magentas that ONI's export already clips to the sRGB edge. The ONI machine's path reads it in plain display code (resources/scanner/proto.cube). Stored as `scannerProto` beside `scannerMachine: oni`, so the Swift app reads a Proto frame as ONI; picking ONI or Frontier leaves Proto; the phone's protocol keeps its two machines.

title: Proto reads the frame at its own print exposure, as Pro's render the table was fitted on
detail: The owner found Proto very dark: ONI prints about +1.5 EV in Pro (the negative's resting print exposure) and the ONI machine resets the print to no exposure before its own look, while Proto's table was fitted on Pro's export of the chart, exposure included. A first fix, a constant 0.2 D anchor fitted on scanner::check_roll, was still dark on the owner's roll and is gone: on_oni_machine now keeps the frame's print exposure for a Proto frame, so its input is Pro's conversion. check_roll's grey enters at 0.69 and prints at 0.51/0.55/0.48; a twin without the exposure lands in the toe.

title: Proto removed
detail: The owner's call after trying it on roll #8: Proto (#191, #192) is taken out whole, its machine tab, its scannerProto field and its table. A sidecar written while it existed keeps a `scannerProto` key, which the reader ignores, so the frame renders on the ONI machine.

title: The Look Lab's paper curve: a graph with five handles on the Frontier's curve
detail: The owner asked to see and edit how the Frontier prints: its toe (blacks) and its shoulder (whites and intense colours clipped). The Lab Paper block now draws the paper curve over negative density (blacks left, whites right): the machine's measured curve, a print without the look in grey, and the frame's. Five handles sit on the curve at densities 0, 0.4, 0.75 (the machine's neutral), 1.15 and 1.6; each stores its distance from the machine's curve (`frontierLab.paper`, five values), spread over the curve's fifteen nodes by a smooth Hermite curve held past the end handles, so the blacks' handle moves the whole toe and the whites' the whole shoulder; the curve is held climbing. A handle follows the hand between its neighbours, one undo step a press; a double click returns it to the machine's. At rest the curve is the machine's exactly.

title: The Frontier prints Pro's black black: the roll's grey on the machine's neutral, Pro's black on the table's
detail: The owner saw lifted blacks the paper curve could not reach. Measured on DSC_6442 and DSC_6432: the Frontier stretched density by 1.3 over the roll's green window about its median (Swift's densityGain), which laid the frames between 0.26 and 1.1 D of the table, whose grey prints black under about 0.14 D and white over about 1.54 D: blacks came out at code 0.06-0.07, whites at 0.80-0.85. Laying the whole window on the table's ends (the owner's first ask) blacked the blacks but darkened the mid-tones (median 0.25), as the table is steeper than Pro's print. Chosen with the owner on renders: the roll's median stays on the machine's neutral and the density where Pro prints its grey black (its window, print exposure and curve included) lands on the table's black: blacks 0.002, median 0.43 as before, whites 0.90, clipping as the Frontier does. scanner::fitted_density keeps the old stretch for the Look Lab's fits.

title: The Frontier prints on ONI's paper curve
detail: The owner's call: the Frontier's paper curve is ONI's (the neutral set's, fitted to Pro at rest), not the measured machine's S; the five handles move it, a double click returns a handle to ONI's. Every Frontier frame now renders through the Lab's bake (once per set of edits, about a millisecond), so a frame with no edit prints on ONI's paper too; the measured curve stays drawn faint for reference.

title: The Frontier prints without Pro's +1.5 EV: ONI's paper slid to Pro's grey without its exposure
detail: The owner found the Frontier much lighter than the ONI machine on the same paper curve: ONI's curve in the Lab is the neutral set's, fitted to Pro at rest, which prints at +1.5 EV, so the roll's grey on the machine's neutral came out near 0.76. The owner asked for the +1.5 EV out: the curve is slid along density, its shape kept, so the machine's neutral prints the reference roll's grey as Pro renders it with the print exposure at 0 (computed through Pro's own chain); the graph draws the slid curve.

title: The Frontier prints on a straight paper; the Lab's curve bends it
detail: The owner's call: the paper curve is taken out of the Frontier mode, which now prints on a straight line from the table's black to its white (ONI's slid paper of #196-#197 is gone), and the five-handle graph becomes the Look Lab's own Curve block, straight at rest, a double click returning a handle to the line, its round key resting the whole curve. The measured machine's paper stays drawn faint. A research agent looks for the paper the Frontier emulates and its ICC profile, to build a paper curve from it later.

title: The Lab's curve acts on the image it is given, black and white in the corners
detail: The owner did not understand the flats at both ends of the graph: its x axis ran over the table's whole density domain while the straight paper spans only the table's window (black 0.14 D, white 1.54 D), so the black and white handles sat on the clipped flats. The curve is now drawn and applied over the image the straight paper gives (0 to 1): the diagonal at rest, handles at 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 1, the corners black and white; the measured machine's paper is drawn over the same axis, faint.

title: The Frontier takes ONI's conversion whole, its print bypassed for its look; the Lab's curve gives way to the Curves block
detail: The owner found the Frontier burning raw0021 (its export: median luminance 223 against ONI's 147, 36.7 % of pixels with a channel at 255, against 0.3 %) and asked for every stage identical to the ONI machine but its clicks, print curve, look and output. The Frontier now runs on_oni_machine like the ONI machine: Pro's conversion with the same density, per-channel window, stretch and separation, the same gains and clicks; Pro's print is bypassed, and the Frontier's look (the Lab chain, baked on 33 nodes over each channel's share of the window, read as the table's density from its black to its white, on a straight paper) takes its place, then the warmth and the output. The B anchor of #195 no longer drives it (it remains for Frontier 2's density path). The Lab's five-handle curve is removed: the Scanner face's Curves block, the app's own editor, shapes the tone.

title: The Frontier is the ONI machine's render with the Lab's look in place of ONI's
detail: The owner's words: duplicate the Scanner face's ONI render and replace only its look table by the Lab's. Pro's print is no longer bypassed: the Frontier runs the ONI machine's conversion whole (print curve at rest included) and its look table reads that render in display code where ONI's reads its square root.

title: Back to 8fed395 at the owner's word
detail: The owner asked to stop and return to the version running before raw0016's burnt whites were reported, the only one that still suited them: the tree is set back to 8fed395 (#199), which undoes #200 to #202 (the Frontier on the ONI machine's path, the Lab's curve removed, Frontier 2's plumbing); the uncommitted work (Frontier 2's paper from Fujifilm's datasheets, the Lab's CurveSet) is kept aside as a patch, outside the repository.

title: Back to the ONI-toned Frontier and Frontier 2, their curves shown as the Curves block draws them
detail: The owner asked to return to the last build (#201 with the work set aside in #203: the Frontier on the ONI look's tone, Frontier 2 printing each window share through the Crystal Archive's curves, the frontierCurves field) and to show the curves. The Lab gains a Lab Curves block, a copy of the Curves block on frontierCurves (its tabs, a press adding or taking a point, a double click removing it, one undo step a press, the block's key resting it), applied on the Frontier's look in display code; Frontier 2 shows its paper in a Frontier 2 Paper block drawn by the same code, one layer a tab, read only. The editor's geometry and its drawing conversion are reused as they are.

title: The Frontier rests on D+1 M+3 Y-3
detail: The owner's neutral for the Frontier's look: every frame took about +3 M, -3 Y and +1 D to sit with the ONI look's neutrality. The Frontier machine's keypad now rests there (scanner::FRONTIER_REST, added to the frame's clicks before they become gains); the screen and the sidecar still read the hand's own clicks, zero at rest. The ONI machine and Frontier 2 rest on zero.

title: Frontier 2 is the ONI machine's render with the ONI look's tone then the paper in place of the look
detail: The owner found Frontier 2 far underexposed and asked for ONI's pipe with the look replaced by the paper curves plus the ONI look's exposure. Frontier 2 no longer bypasses Pro's print: it runs the ONI machine's conversion whole, then, where the ONI look stands, the ONI look's tone (its grey axis, the brightness it lends) and the Crystal Archive layer curves, composed into one 33-point curve a channel, which the Frontier 2 Paper block draws as it is applied.

title: The Frontier rests on D+0.5 M+2 Y-2
detail: The owner's revised neutral for the Frontier's look: two M, two Y toward blue and half a D, where #205 had D+1 M+3 Y-3. The half D, which no keypad count holds, is half of one D click's measured offset added to the rest's (scanner::FRONTIER_REST_D).

title: Frontier 2's paper lends its colour and not its contrast
detail: The owner's call: each channel's curve is the ONI look's tone plus that channel's Crystal Archive layer minus the three layers' mean, read at that tone, so the channels' mean is ONI's tone and only the layers' differences (the paper's colour) remain; the Frontier 2 Paper block draws these curves.

title: The Frontier's look locked: baked once as ONI's is; the Lab and Frontier 2 removed
detail: The owner locked the Frontier look and asked to remove Frontier 2 and to bake the Lab's parameters and the per-channel rest into a table as ONI's is. The Frontier machine now reads frontier_look::CUBE, the Lab's chain at the machine's own values on the ONI look's tone, baked once (33 nodes) over the ONI machine's render in display code. Baking the rest into the table was measured and refused: a density offset before Pro's print does not map to one code curve after it, as the print sits where each frame's window puts it (against the exact rest, median 0.03-0.04 and 99th centile up to 0.16 of code on raw0021 and DSC_6442); the rest D+0.5 M+2 Y-2 stays in the gains, exactly, the screen at zero. Removed: Frontier 2 (scannerPrint, its paper and its block), the Look Lab panel, its curve, and the frontierLab and frontierCurves fields (a sidecar carrying them still reads, the keys ignored). The research module look_lab stays in the pipeline, the bake's source.

title: Dead code of the locked look removed
detail: FrontierLab and its edit machinery (oni-settings frontier_lab.rs, look_lab/edits.rs) are gone; the bake and the ONI look's tone live in frontier_look.rs. The old Frontier density mapping (scanner::density, pro_black, roll_median) is gone; scanner::fitted_density, self-contained, keeps the Swift machine's coordinates the Look Lab's fits and the CPU replica read. An unused binding in the sidebars window check is dropped. decode_gate's one-at-a-time test gave its count back after leaving the turn, so another thread could find it raised: it now gives it back inside the turn.

title: contact_sheet's window check times out waiting for the roll measure under a check that rebuilds
detail: Seen about six times on 2026-10-20 and 21, only when scripts/check rebuilt before running (12 binaries at once): Prepare the Roll's measure never lands within 120 s, where it lands in under 3 s alone. The measure's job always ends in land_measure (a superseded MEASURE ticket only skips a frame), so the wait is elsewhere, likely a decode slot (decode_gate::Slots) starved while the thumbnail pass and the open frame hold places under load. To do: log each slot's taker and waiter in that check, reproduce with ONI_BINARIES=12 after a touch, then fix the starvation rather than the timeout. Found (2026-10-22, the stalled run's threads all idle, the advance landing on the Film step): opening the roll's first frame enters Prepare the Roll by itself, and the check's own Prepare key, its roll read off the thread, landed after the hand had reached the Window step and entered the roll again, back on Film; MEASURE then stepped instead of measuring. The roll shown, asked again, now keeps its step. 0 stalls in 30 runs, against about one in thirteen.

title: Spec: editing several frames together, and the contact sheet as a marked-up proof
detail: docs/research/multi-edit-and-contact-sheet.md: Option A (Edit Together: the selection six to a row on the canvas, every notch setting the same absolute value on each frame, 300 px half-size sources cached, per-tile renders benched before any atlas, one undo step a gesture) and Option B (a Mark tab on the contact sheet: pen, circle and cross, a circle labelling its frame favourite, marks as vectors in the sheet's sidecar, burnt in at export), compared, A first recommended, four questions for the owner.

title: Edit Together: frames selected in the gallery open six to a row, a step sets the same value on all
detail: Opening a frame among a gallery selection of two or more opens them together: the canvas lays each frame's own render six to a row at 300 px (half-size decode reduced on the CPU, three decoders), every step on the open frame is laid by the store on the others at the same absolute value as part of that one undo step, each frame's own fields (film, order, framing, dust, roll, balance method) never move. The grid renders every tile on the GPU before one readback (Graph::read_back) and is encoded by the canvas's display kernel. Leaving: a single open or back to the gallery. Checks: store test with twin, window check (three frames, a drag, one undo, a frame left out), grid layout and reduction tests, tiles-together against alone, batched readback against renders. ONI_BENCH=grid on roll #8, 36 frames: sources 6.4 s, notch to canvas p50 14-17 ms, p99 38-117 ms (spikes while the GPU allocates the 36 outputs).

title: Edit Together's grid laid on one GPU sheet, no readback
detail: The grid's tiles are evaluated in one submission and copied onto one clear sheet (Graph::laid_out), which the canvas's display kernel encodes as any render: no readback, no CPU encode, no upload. The software canvas reads the sheet back once. ONI_BENCH=grid counts only the drag's grids. Roll #8, 36 frames, drag only: notch to canvas p50 16-23 ms, p99 47-84 ms; each grid costs about 10 ms of dispatch recording (36 tiles, one dispatch a stage each), the rest waits for the interface loop.

title: De-dust: the brush follows the pointer, a stroke reuses the frame's full resolution
detail: The brush disc follows the pointer in Slint (TouchArea's moved fires only while pressed), over the picture alone, hiding the system cursor only there; scroll zooms under the brush; Space pressed mid-stroke finishes it and is let go with the focus; ⌘-drag pans; a press gives the keys back their focus. A move appends one segment to the stroke's path (0.3 µs a move, was a full republish of every correction). The full resolution is built as De-dust opens and each patch search reuses it (fullIfReady) instead of decoding the RAW again; the search window covers only the farthest candidate; the cost map's taps skip the clamp inside the region; the engine is taken per correction and purged once. A stroke stays painted until its patch lands; a patch made for a correction removed meanwhile is dropped; removal never locks the engine on the interface thread. ONI_BENCH=dedust on roll #8: patch 185 ms after its search starts, was 2.2 s.

title: The open frame's full resolution built ahead once it has stayed a second
detail: Owner's call: the open frame's full resolution is built in the background once it has been shown one second (never under a hand, at once in De-dust), so a stroke's patch and a zoom read it at once; one frame's at a time, dropped on another open or the gallery. Arrows walking a roll pass sooner and decode nothing. Swift builds it only on demand (corrections, Details, zoom). Roll #8 NEF: 907 ms decode, 46 ms upload, about 390 MB held; ONI_BENCH=dedust peak footprint 2.9 GB, resident 1.7 GB.

title: De-dust reminders: each correction's dust shown unpatched in the tab
detail: Owner's ask: each correction's row in the De-dust tab shows a 56 pt square of the frame about its stroke as it looks with no patch, so a dust healed away is remembered. Rendered on the preview with every correction removed, cropped to the stroke's box, brush and margin, reduced to 112 px on the GPU, off the interface thread, kept until the frame's look moves. ONI_BENCH=dedust waits for it: 112 x 112 beside the patch.

title: Edit Together follows the selection, zooms as a contact sheet, averages Auto White Balance
detail: Owner's asks: beside the photo, a ⌘ or ⇧ pick of two frames or more in the column shows them together at once (the frame on screen joins the first pick and leads), one frame shows alone again; the gallery's selection shows together as the editor comes back; the selection stays the frames shown. Tiles 400 px on their longest side; the sheet zooms, pans and double-clicks to 100 % as a frame does; sources a former group decoded are kept for the next. Auto White Balance over frames together runs Average without asking: each frame measured, the mean laid on all, one undo. The block reading's 30 ms budget is read as the best of three runs, so a machine busy with the other checks no longer fails it.

title: The interface draws in 1.9 ms: femtovg keeps its wgpu pipelines
detail: Measured during a drag: each interface frame took 8.7 ms to draw (p99 11.9 ms), most of it in femtovg's wgpu renderer creating render pipelines, MSL compilation included. femtovg 0.27.0 drops every pipeline a flush did not use, and Slint draws a frame in several flushes (layers, shadows, clips), so each one dropped the others'. femtovg is vendored in vendor/femtovg (MIT OR Apache-2.0, licences kept) with every pipeline kept, through [patch.crates-io]. Frames now draw in 1.5-1.9 ms (p99 2.6 ms), across the whole interface.

title: One compute pass a render and one uniform copy a submission, in the shared graph
detail: The graph ran each stage in a compute pass of its own (a Metal encoder each, about ten microseconds a stage on the CPU and the GPU) and wrote each stage's uniforms through the queue's lock. A render now lays its sources first, then records every stage in one pass, and stages its uniforms for one copy before each submission; a pipeline is found by its static shader's address, not by hashing the shader's text. Every render gains: the editor, thumbnails, the grid, export. Edit Together's sheet is drawn at the share of its size the view shows, in eighths, never past 400 px a tile. ONI_BENCH=grid on roll #8, 36 frames, 480 notches: notch to canvas p50 2.0 ms, p99 4-6 ms (was 24 / 68 ms), images every 8.3 ms, the hand's pace.

title: Edit Together: frames on the other face follow, held previews make tiles at once, checks open behind
detail: The frame that did not follow was on the other face: roll #8 holds 25 frames on Pro and 13 on Scanner, and a value moved on Pro is written but unseen on a Scanner frame. Each step now carries the face it was taken on with the fields it moved. A frame whose preview the editor holds (the open one first) gets its tile reduced from it on the GPU, before any decode. A bench, or ONI_BACKGROUND=1, opens behind the other apps' windows without taking the focus (winit's activation and the window's active flag off), so the owner keeps working while checks run. A window check opens five frames together three ways (gallery, editor key, column) and finds every sidecar on every step.

title: A resize follows at once with no render; input distributions read once a settings
detail: Owner's ask: a clean, simple resize with no lag. While the canvas changes size, the picture shown is laid again by arithmetic alone (the same texture, at the same share of the whole image the view now places), nothing renders, and one render at the new size is asked once the hand rests (viewport::SETTLE). The input distributions hang on the frame and its settings only: the render thread reads them again only when those changed, never for a view, a resize or a zoom (the resize study measured 4.3 ms an event on the interface thread and up to 19 ms on the render thread). ONI_BENCH=resize resizes with no hand on a slider and counts the renders asked meanwhile (0). A window opened behind other windows draws no frame, so the interface's frames are measured only when it shows. The app is always launched in the background (CLAUDE.md).

title: Each photo opens fitted; Keep zoom in Settings
detail: Owner's ask: every change of photo resets the view to fitted; Settings › Rendering gains 'Keep the zoom from one photo to the next' (preferences keepZoom, off by default), which keeps the former behaviour, the zoom kept and the view recentred, to compare grain across a roll.

title: A zoomed picture covers the canvas while the window resizes
detail: Owner's ask: zoomed in, the picture behaves as a CSS background in cover mode while the window resizes, its zoom scaled from the gesture's start by the larger of the two size ratios, so no edge of the texture ever shows; fitted stays fitted. ONI_BENCH=resize zooms to 100 % first and counts the resizes leaving an edge inside (0; 29 of 60 with the zoom kept).

title: The thumbnail waiting for a render lies where the photo will
detail: Owner: the thumbnail shown while a photo loads was not the size of the photo. It was laid fitted once, so a canvas resized after (the editor opening from the gallery, a window resized) left it at the old size, and a kept zoom drew it fitted. It is now laid by the viewport on a size guessed from the last photo's long side, and laid again on every resize.

title: Edit Together tiles at 1024 px
detail: Owner's call: tiles 1024 px on their long side (from 400), the gap 30 px so the sheet keeps its look. ONI_BENCH=grid on 36 frames: notch to canvas p50 2.1 ms, p99 7.4 ms; peak footprint 2.76 GB (2.2 GB at 400); 1600 px jumped to a 12.9 ms p50.

title: De-dust's strokes and the curves drawn where their points are
detail: Owner: the red stroke painted in De-dust did not sit on the drawing the patch follows. Slint fits a Path's viewbox inside its size less the stroke's width and shifts it by half of it, so a stroke slid towards the canvas's centre by up to half the brush; LiveStroke, SourceTrace and the plots' lines now lay their commands unfitted (fit: preserve).

title: A run of dust patches frees its textures one by one
detail: Owner: dozens of large strokes at once took the app 2 GB up. Each search lays textures of its own size, kept until the run ended; the engine now purges after each patch. ONI_DUST_STROKES=24 on the largest brush: peak footprint 5.2 GB to 3.1 GB, 24 patches in 6.5 s against 6.3 s.

title: A reduced dust patch lands where the full one does
detail: Owner: patches moved a little between the full frame and the preview, in no fixed direction. A reduced patch was laid as Core Image lays it, its origin rounded (x) and its bottom anchored in Core Image's y: up to a reduced pixel off, three full-resolution pixels on a 2000 px preview. AnchoredLanczos takes a sub-pixel shift (kernel and its CPU reference), and corrections::placed covers the whole pixels the exact edges touch with the shifts that set the content in place. A departure from Swift, which has the same offset: its check now holds our tile within a pixel of Swift's and the mask on Swift's.

title: The editor reads the full resolution; a preview copy in Settings
detail: Owner's ask: the full resolution shown from the start, so a zoom never renders twice, the preview mode kept as a choice. The full resolution is built as a photo opens and every render reads it once built (fitted down at fit, a region when zoomed); Settings › Rendering 'Edit on a preview copy' (previewEditing, off) keeps the former way. Roll #8, against the preview copy: a 10 s Exposure drag p50 0.3 ms both, p99 7.2 ms against 6.2 ms; a pinch from fit p99 7.6 ms against 12.1 ms; peak footprint 2.37 GB against 2.41 GB, the preview copy building the full resolution after its 1 s dwell anyway. A departure from Swift, which edits on its preview.

title: A zoom reduces from the full resolution's halvings
detail: On the full resolution (#230) a pinch from fit reduced the whole 24 Mpx frame on every event: notch p50 25 ms. The fitted copy is now reduced from the smallest halving of its base still past it (kept per base, down to 512 px). ONI_BENCH=zoom, pinch from fit: p50 2.0 ms, p99 4.5 ms, gap p99 11 ms, as on the preview copy (0.6, 7.9, 10.6). Peak footprint of that bench 4.3 to 4.7 GB against 3.7 GB on the preview copy.

title: Renders follow the canvas, not the frame, at any zoom
detail: Owner: on the full resolution, the further out from 100 % the slower a pan or a pinch; Edit Together zoomed in edited at a low rate. Four changes on the one render path. (1) The region a view renders keeps one size, the visible part plus a pixel, where it alternated between two as a pan moved fractionally. (2) The display texture grows by 256 px steps and is shown clipped (Picture.clip-width/height), so a pan or a pinch rewrites texels instead of importing a texture into Slint: ONI_BENCH=midzoom 36 imports to 2, ONI_BENCH=zoom 59 to 10. (3) The canvas reads the smallest halving of its base past the scale shown, halvings kept for the preview and the full frame down to 64 px, reduced lazily so the chain pulls only the region's share; a reduction the canvas nearly holds whole (two canvases) is kept for the notches at fit. Pinch at 60 % p50 1.9 to 0.4 ms; peak footprint of the zoom bench 4.3-4.7 GB to 3.1 GB; a 10 s drag at fit p99 12.5 to 5 ms. (4) Edit Together draws only the tiles its view meets, on a sheet the size of their box laid at its place: ONI_GRID_ZOOM=1 notch p50 2.2 to 0.4 ms, p99 12.9 to 3.3 ms; at fit unchanged. ONI_BENCH=midzoom added: at 60 %, a pan and a pinch on the full resolution.

title: A RAW opened whole is its own full resolution
detail: Opening a RAW decoded it whole, reduced it to the preview and let the whole go, then the full resolution decoded the file a second time (about 0.9 s). The upload the preview is reduced from is now kept as the frame's full resolution when the decode read the frame whole: ONI_BENCH=zoom, full resolution 643 ms after the double click to 8 ms; opening and peak footprint unchanged.

title: The histogram counts the whole picture at one size, whatever the zoom
detail: Owner: on one photo the histogram stopped following the edits once zoomed in; in Edit Together it changed while zooming with no edit. It counted the render shown, and only when that render was the whole picture; the grid's was drawn at the zoom's scale. The histogram now counts a picture of its own, made again only when the settings move: the photo's preview through the chain at 1024 px, the grid's sheet whole at an eighth (128 px a tile). ONI_BENCH=midzoom at 60 %: 0 histograms through the pan and the pinch, 3 to 4 through a 30-notch Exposure drag, where none followed it before.

title: Whole decodes kept on disk
detail: A frame opened again skipped nothing: LibRaw demosaiced it anew, about 0.9 s a 24 Mpx frame. oni-decode keeps each whole decode in Caches/Decodes: the camera's 16-bit window (145 MB a 24 Mpx frame), its flip and the matrix that converts it, keyed by the file's path, size and date, the reading asked and a hash of the decoder's own code; written off the decode's thread under a name of its own then renamed, the oldest let go past 4 GB. The original files are only read. Roll #8, reopening a frame: 1061 ms to 135 ms to its first render; the kept decode is LibRaw's bit for bit (oni-decode/tests/kept.rs).

title: Idle textures held within a byte budget
detail: Owner: the app reached 7.16 GB, its memory following the zoom, not the edits. The pool reuses a texture of the exact size only and kept every idle one for 8 renders; a zoom asks new sizes at every step, about 1 GB of intermediates each, so 5 to 8 GB stayed idle and remained once the hand stopped. Idle textures are now held within 1 GB, the newest kept (Graph::idle_budget); the pool test bounds a run of new shapes by the budget, with a twin.

title: Quick wins: less held, less republished, the histogram after the canvas
detail: From the ten agents' review (owner's go). A render landing where the last one lay republishes nothing (lay); De-dust builds its strokes and marks only while painting, its rows always; Compare off lets the render thread's kept before and the canvas's before image go; leaving the editor lets the last group's tile sources go (SPARE, up to 400 MB); the decode cache writes from LibRaw's rows and reads a row at a time, with no 145 MB copy either way (first open 1080 ms, reopen 171 ms, warm peak 2.66 GB); the histogram's picture is made after the canvas is handed over and at the image's cadence (Delivery::Counted), not before each notch. ONI_BENCH=midzoom: 0 histograms through the pan and pinch, 8 through the drag.

title: The interface thread neither traces the input histograms nor polls the GPU
detail: The levels' and curves' plots were traced on the interface thread, about 3 ms a reading at 30 Hz; they are now traced off it with a ticket, as the picture's histogram is (Ctl::traced and app::premultiplied deleted). The histogram's readback was polled every 2 ms by a repeating timer, about 500 wakes a second through a slide; the count's map callback now publishes it, and a single-shot timer waits only for the image's cadence (HISTOGRAM_POLL gone). ONI_BENCH=long: 229 histograms in 10 s, frame to panel p50 6.9 ms (9.1 before); ONI_BENCH=midzoom: 0 through the pan and pinch, 9 through the drag.

title: A pan or a zoom moves the picture at once
detail: Nothing moved on the canvas until a render came back from the render thread, a thread hop and up to a refresh late. navigate now lays the picture shown where the new view puts it, by the same arithmetic a resize uses (resizing::followed), on the interface thread, and the render asked refines it. Benches unchanged: ONI_BENCH=midzoom pan p50 0.3 ms, pinch 0.4 ms.

title: One frame in flight, presented as soon as drawn
detail: Slint's femtovg renderer configured the surface with AutoVsync and wgpu's default frame latency 2: up to three drawables on the layer, a drawn frame waiting for a refresh and possibly behind another. It is vendored (vendor/i-slint-renderer-femtovg, 1.18.1, [patch.crates-io]) with desired_maximum_frame_latency 1 and AutoNoVsync (Immediate on Metal); the CADisplayLink still paces the draws and the window compositor still syncs to the screen. The owner judges the feel; benches run in hidden windows that draw no frames.

title: A pan shows no bare edge: the view is rendered with a margin
detail: Owner: the edges flickered while panning a zoomed picture. Since #239 the picture moves at once with the hand, but its texture covered the visible part plus a pixel, so the strip a pan uncovers showed the ground until the next render landed. The region rendered now reaches an eighth of the view past each side (PAN_MARGIN), the size still one per view. ONI_BENCH=midzoom: pan p50 0.3 ms, pinch about 2 ms (from 0.4), peak footprint 6.5 GB as before. A graph render also polls the device once ended, so what the GPU has finished with is let go without waiting for another poll.

title: The header fits a narrow window, and fifty alignment slips found by eight reviewers are fixed
detail: Owner: at a small width the header's keys did not fit. Its fixed widths summed to about 1219 px against a 1100 px floor: compact now also turns PASTE TO ROLL into a glyph and halves the gaps, the key zone keeps only the shown mode's compact width, and the compact threshold counts the row's five gaps (it counted seven) and no Export while a roll is prepared. A fixed key elides a word longer than its room; a lamp gets its own room. Alignment, measured from the Slint layout solver (a fixed-height child sits at the top of its row): the column pill beside the key plate is as tall as the plate; Prepare's flat-field toggle, De-dust's remove key and help mark, Crop's rotate key, the trash row's RESTORE key and the preset badge are centred on their rows; the base note row, the paper rows and a Field's label row keep their height whether a key or '?' shows; folder and trash rows put their icon in the tree's slot; a rename starts where the title stood; roll rings follow the picture's corners; stock icons grow on hover without moving the names; Scanner screen cells and level readouts are equal columns; Levels' tabs, plot and readouts share one inset; the Settings sheet is wide enough for its rows; the Paper Profiles sheet has its top inset; the read-only banner clears Compare's labels; the tile medal is level with the RGB seal; tree captions sit 2 px under their pictures as the layout budgets.

title: De-dust's red stroke has round joins and ends
detail: Owner: the red stroke's ends looked flat and its trace had artefacts. Slint's paths default to mitre joins (limit 4), so every jitter of the hand grew a spike up to twice the stroke's width; Swift draws round caps and joins. Every stroke path now joins round. A kept stroke's path drops a point within a canvas point of the last (a zero-length segment folds a round cap flat), and a lone point draws as a dot. The vendored femtovg merged repeated points by looking one past the contour's last point, so it never merged; it now reads the last.

title: Sources in half floats; pooled textures shared across a chain's stages
detail: Unification, first step (owner's go, 2026-10-22). A decode, its preview and the halvings the canvas reads are held in rgba16float (Graph::upload_half, materialise_half: a render packed by one pass), half the memory; stages still write rgba32float, and a bare half source is read through a pass before any readback or copy. The pool rounded nothing: each stage's region, a few pixels apart in reach, took a texture of its own, so a render's working set needed a 1 GB idle budget. Pooled sides are now rounded up to 128 px and each dispatch clamps its reads to the rectangle held, so a chain's stages share textures; the idle budget falls to 512 MB. midzoom (2 x 24 MP): pinch p50 19.4 -> 7 ms, pan frame gap 10 -> 8.8 ms, graph textures peak 2.2 GB -> 1.4 GB; zoom from fit pinch p50 21.4 -> 1.4 ms. Benches log the graph's texture peak. Edit Together's group lives in the app's state, and the sources of a group left (SPARE) are no longer kept: held in thread-locals, they were freed after the GPU's own at the thread's end.

title: No preview copy: the editor always reads the full resolution
detail: Unification (owner's decisions of 2026-10-21). Settings' 'Edit on a preview copy' and 'Read RAW previews at half size' (and its menu item) are gone, with the settled flag, the debounce re-render after a navigation and Swift's MemoryBudget (needs_full_resolution, the budget formula and their checks): the full resolution is built as a photo opens and every render reads it once built, the preview serving only until then. A RAW's opening decode is always whole, so it is the full resolution too. Parity rows: MemoryBudget marked departed.

title: No software canvas: every render stays on the GPU
detail: Unification (owner's decision of 2026-10-21). The render thread no longer renders pixels on the CPU and encodes them for a window without wgpu: the worker asks the engine's resident render only (Picture, Renderer::render, the on_gpu flag and the generic Worker<I> are gone; Renderer stays the seam a check fills). The canvas's GPU is always there, on the engine's device; on Slint's software renderer, the windows the checks drive, the display kernel's output is read back and shown, so the checks see the very kernel the app runs. Edit Together and Compare follow; Engine::read_sheet goes.

title: One GPU device for the whole app
detail: Unification. The automatic keys' reader and the roll previews opened a wgpu device each; they now record on the window engine's device, each in a graph of its own (64 MB idle budget), every submission and upload through the door the window's surface reconfigure closes (oni_graph::Door, render::graph). The engine's gate becomes that door. The worker's slot check runs on the engine, its first render's kernel compile awaited.

title: Edit Together's sheet reuses the last one, cleared
detail: Every grid laid a fresh owned texture, a sheet's allocation and zero fill each notch. The device now asks for CLEAR_TEXTURE where the adapter has it, and laid_out takes an output no source holds any more (the one before the sheet shown) and clears it in place; without the feature a fresh texture as before. grid bench (36 frames): notch to canvas p99 49 -> 19 ms, 283 -> 334 grids over 480 notches.

title: The Details loupe goes through the canvas's display kernel
detail: Unification. The loupe's region was read back under the engine's lock and encoded for the screen on the CPU; it now stays on the GPU (Engine::loupe returns the materialised region) and the display kernel encodes it into a texture the band shows, read back only on Slint's software renderer, as the canvas. The engine is held for the render alone. loupe bench: a Sharpening notch reaches the loupe in 6 ms median, as before.

title: The log is written on a thread of its own
detail: Every render's line was written to stderr and the log file on the thread that said it, the interface thread for each landing, where a busy disk could hold a frame. Lines now go to a log thread in order; timing::flush waits for them before the log is read (report, console) and as the app ends (⌘Q or the loop's end).

title: The alignment slips left from the audit
detail: From the eight UI audits (#242), the ones Swift does not decide: the gallery heading's folder caption elides rather than pushing the title out; the load bar's title is the idle line's 11 px secondary, so the status text no longer grows when loading starts; the status row ends `s` from the card at both ends (the medal's own inset counted); a profile menu dropped under its field is as wide as it (MenuPicker passes its field's width); Settings' sections sit flush with the sheet's title and keys, closer under it; the Paper Profiles sheet's title has the sheets' padding; the Scanner keypad's narrow keys start from one width, so −3 is no wider than −; the Working Space chip is limited to the room the zoom keys leave and elides its hint, the dot spaced evenly. Left as Swift draws them: the crop's edge bars on the frame line, Compare's labels at ±34 from the split.

title: The export's decode held in half floats, as the canvas's
detail: An export laid its full-resolution decode in rgba32float, 390 MB on a 24 MP frame; it is now held in rgba16float as the canvas holds the same frame (#244), so the file starts from the pixels the canvas showed, at half the GPU memory. The display kernel's upload helper, which only the checks used once the software canvas went, moves into its checks.

title: The interface's frames submitted in slices of 16 passes
detail: Metal keeps about 2.6 MB of driver memory per render pass until its command buffer completes, and wgpu gives each pass a command buffer of its own. The first interface frame draws 222 passes (colourised icons, box shadows and layers rendered offscreen, cached after), so it held 590 to 618 MB of IOAccelerator memory in one buffer. The vendored femtovg now submits a frame every 16 passes and keeps one slice in flight: 60 to 130 MB on the midzoom bench, every later frame (4 passes) unchanged. A check draws 40 layers and finds each in its place and colour, and the first row as one buffer draws it.

title: Colourised glyphs drawn as masks, with no copy rendered aside
detail: Slint's femtovg renderer colourised an image by rendering a copy into a texture of its own, two passes each and again at every change of ink (a hover), 42 icons on the first frame. A solid ink now draws the image's alpha in that colour in the current pass (femtovg Paint::image_mask, tex_type 3 in both shaders): the first frame falls from 222 to 144 passes, and the window reads within 1/255 of the copy on 207 icon pixels. A check draws a glyph both ways and finds them within 1/255, and its twin tells a multiplied tint from them.

title: The allocator's large-block cache off, so freed decodes go back to the system
detail: After a frame opened, 710 MB of MALLOC_LARGE stayed dirty although only 4 MB was live: macOS's allocator keeps freed large blocks (the f32 decode, the cache read, LibRaw's buffers, the upload bands) for reuse, and malloc_zone_pressure_relief returns none of it. libmalloc reads MallocLargeCache only at launch, so the app execs itself once with it at 0 (10 to 15 ms). On the midzoom bench with a prepared support folder: MALLOC_LARGE 710 MB to 4 MB, steady footprint 2.25 GB to 1.5 GB, peak 2.8-3.0 GB to 2.0-2.2 GB, notch renders unchanged.

title: Edit Together's sheet recorded in one compute pass
detail: The sheet evaluated each frame in a compute pass of its own and copied its result into place, and wgpu gives every pass and every copy run a Metal command buffer: about seventy a notch on a 36-frame grid, each with its driver allocation. Every frame's sources are now laid first, then all their stages run in one pass, each last stage writing at its corner of the sheet (Frame.out_at): one command buffer a notch. Grid bench, five interleaved runs on a loaded machine: notch to canvas p50 10.3 to 5.0 ms, p99 unchanged. The sheet check now also counts no copy for staged frames, and its twin counts one for a bare source.

title: Large Rust blocks mapped directly instead of the allocator's cache switched off
detail: Switching macOS's large-block cache off at launch (#255) also took it from the Metal driver, which allocates a large block per command buffer: Edit Together's notch rose from 5.8 to 7.3-10.2 ms. The app's allocator now maps and unmaps blocks of 16 MB and more itself (the f32 decode, the cache read, the upload bands) and leaves the rest to the system's, cache included; the relaunch goes. Midzoom with a prepared support folder: MALLOC_LARGE 710 to 166-181 MB (LibRaw's own blocks stay cached), peak 1.9-2.0 GB, renders unchanged. A check grows a block past 16 MB and shrinks it back with its bytes kept, its twin sees one byte spoiled.

title: The pool lends a slightly larger free texture, and the whole-frame reduction goes
detail: A pinch asks the graph a new size every step; the pool reused only exact sizes, so each step made about 600 MB of new textures while the GPU, 15 to 80 ms behind, still held those just let go. Acquire now takes the smallest free texture within 1.3 times the requested area (stages already read through in_size). The reduction kept whole when it held at most two canvases (KEPT_WHOLE, reduced(), Fitting.kept) goes: the render cache keeps the reduction for the next notch. Measured on midzoom over four runs: graph peak 1362 to 1180-1190 MB, pinch p50 1.4-8.3 to 0.6-3.9 ms, p99 25-30 to 14-18 ms; zoom bench peak 1845-1931 to 1587 MB, pinch p50 7.5-9.7 to 1.0-1.4 ms. A pool check renders a step-smaller shape with no texture made, its twin a five-times smaller one that makes one.

title: Edit Together shows each frame's thumbnail until it decodes, and counts the frames in the load bar
detail: A tile stayed empty until its frame decoded. Each lacking frame's gallery thumbnail is now read from disk, carried from sRGB to linear Rec. 2020 and laid on the GPU off the interface thread; the sheet scales it into the tile through the same render (render_laid takes Laid::Frame or Laid::Shown) until the frame's own source replaces it, and the histogram counts only frames. The load bar reads 'Opening the frames together' with the decoded count. A check lays a 40 x 20 picture at a side of 100 and finds it covering 100 x 50 at its place, its twin the sheet clear past it.

title: Prepare the Roll's tutorials play again, from GIFs every system decodes
detail: Swift's TutorialVideo played a square muted loop above the Base, Flags and Window steps' controls. The three HEVC clips are converted once to GIFs at 20 fps and 580 px, each frame written as the box of pixels that moved (18 MB for the three, 31.6 MB as whole frames), and decoded frame by frame with the pure-Rust gif crate, so Windows and macOS play the same file with no system media library (owner's call). Each frame is written into one texture the panel's Picture shows by revision, as the canvas is; a window that cannot import a texture takes the pixels. The clip stops while the roll is measured, on another step and when the panel closes. RollStepKeys moves to the toolbar that shows it, so prepare.slint's ceiling falls to 479. A check plays each clip square at 50 ms a frame back to its first picture, its twin a loop that would come back at once; another finds no clip on the steps without one.

title: The interface's offscreen layers and needless redraws removed
detail: A rounded clip, or an opacity under one on an element with children, makes Slint's femtovg renderer draw the subtree into a texture of its own and redraw it on any change inside. The cards keep their round but clip nothing: CardCorners covers the four corners in the ground's colour over the canvas, gallery, export and roll cards. The slider rail no longer clips its fill, which is rounded itself; the hidden RESET key is invisible rather than transparent; the tooltip waits its delay on a timer instead of an animated opacity that redrew the window for a second; the progress glow no longer re-blurs through an animated width. The shared box-shadow cache is emptied after each frame, items on screen keeping theirs in their item cache. The toolbar's outer spacing no longer depends on its width, which closed the binding loop Slint warns may panic. Midzoom against 4b1bf38: passes 4 to 2 a steady frame and 144 to 98 on the first, interface frame drawn p50 1.8-2.0 to 1.6 ms, about 35 textures fewer; footprint unchanged within the bench's noise.

title: Deleted oni-render's storage-buffer GPU path, which the app never ran (b0c62e3)
detail: gpu.rs, each kernel's impl Gpu dispatch and WGSL buffer entry point, and the kernels no stage uses (correction cost and bias field, screen gamut zebra, area average, maximum and histogram, colour clamp, linear and radial gradients, RGB passes, source-over) go: 3,193 lines out, 355 in. oni-render keeps only bytemuck and the scalar references the stage tests compare against. Its buffer tests went; the branches oni-pipeline's stage tests missed moved to oni-pipeline/tests/branches.rs on the render graph, each with a twin. Parity citations were repointed.

title: The token generator and the design-system guard leave the app library (b661cb2)
detail: tokens.rs moves into the oni-tokens binary, whose tests now run with it, and strict.rs beside the window design-system check; neither is part of the shipped oni-app library.

title: The pipeline tests' duplicated helpers merged, and a blind NaN check fixed (d189f40)
detail: noise, judge, error, dump and gap now live once in oni-pipeline/tests/common. The kept error scores a NaN pixel as infinite; fused.rs's copy folded it to 0 with f32::max, so its checks could not see a NaN. A new check asserts the judges fail a NaN pixel, with the blind fold as its twin.

title: The file-size guard tightened (a64a019)
detail: Entries for files gone or back under 400 lines are dropped and every remaining ceiling is set to the file's line count, so a grandfathered file can only shrink.

title: The gallery keeps its cells, and the base step stops resending its whole frame
detail: publish_tiles set a new tile model at every scroll row, pick, medal and landed thumbnail, so Slint rebuilt every visible cell and uploaded every thumbnail again (about 10 MB a publish, some 200 MB while a 38-frame gallery opened). The model is now kept: each photo holds the slot its index gives while it stays in view, a cell is rewritten only when its place, marks or caption change or it gets its first picture, and a landed thumbnail is relayed to the cells showing its photo. The base step set its scan (5 MB) and its loupe's source, the whole frame (97 MB as RGBA8), at every pointer move, which Slint compared pixel by pixel; each is now set when its path or size changes, and the loupe stays instantiated while the pointer is away so its frame is not uploaded again. A check finds a cell kept when only its held picture differs and rewritten on a pick, a move or a first picture.

title: Auto White Balance over many frames decodes three at once
detail: Measured on 12 frames of roll #8: a frame's balance took about 0.4 s, 0.35 s of it the measuring copy's decode at Swift's preview side and only 0.05 s the reads, so reading one sheet for every frame would have saved little. The run now balances BALANCERS = 3 frames at once, each decode off the GPU's lock and behind the hand's in the decode slots, the progress counting frames as they land: 4.55 s to 2.25 s for the 12. Each frame is still measured on its own copy at Swift's side, so its outcome is unchanged.

title: The sidebar's thumbnails no longer compared pixel by pixel
detail: At every gallery publish the sidebar compared each thumbnail row's picture with the cache's, and relaying the column compared every row whole, pictures included; Slint compares images pixel by pixel, about 10 MB read a publish for 38 rows. A row now records whether it holds its thumbnail: a pending one is filled when it lands, a held one only when its photo's thumbnail is drawn again (relay_thumbnail), and the relay compares rows with their pictures set aside.

title: A hovered preset previews on every frame of Edit Together
detail: The single frame's render laid the hovered preset over its settings (preset_preview, Swift's previewedSettings) but Edit Together's grid did not, so a hover showed nothing on the group a click would change. The grid now lays the preview over the lead's and every other frame's live settings, and the hovered preset joins the grid's key so a hover asks a grid. Swift has no grid to copy; the preview follows what the click applies, the whole selection.

title: Edit Together and the canvas wait for the GPU before the next render
detail: The GPU audit found renders landing 15 to 80 ms behind their request while the CPU queued more; waiting at most 100 ms for the last render before taking the next halves the latency to photon and frees 250 MB, but the benches, which time the CPU side, read worse (pinch p50 1.4 to 19 ms). Diff kept at docs/research/gpu-settle.diff (against 6564fed); needs the owner's eye on a real pan before it lands.

title: State split per feature, reset by assignment
detail: State's per-photo fields are grouped: rendering::Requests (rendered, requested, inputs, inputs_drawn, requested_view, requested_live, hand), dedusting::Dust (numbers, sources, fallback, healing, patched, unhealable) and rendering::Compare (split, before_placed, befores). Opening a photo resets them with Dust::next_photo and one Requests assignment instead of fourteen field writes; leaving Together keeps its two. app.rs ceiling 540 to 517. The use super::* imports stay as they are.

title: One display encode, one latest-value slot, one live-settings builder
detail: Gpu::encode (canvas_gpu.rs) writes the display kernel into a kept texture or a new one and imports or reads it back; the landing, Compare's before, the gamut restripe and the loupe go through it. crate::latest::Latest<T> is the one latest-value slot: the render worker, Edit Together's drawing thread and a new loupe thread (busy/again replaced by the key last asked) take from it. State::live_settings and State::previewed replace the three hovered-preset constructions. Loupe bench: a Sharpening notch reaches the loupe in 8 ms median; grid bench unchanged.

title: Full resolution built in one place
detail: Ctl::ensure_full is the one place a full-resolution build starts (decode_gate::FULL, one at a time, never before the opening decode, never again after a failure): the render (Settings' whole decode, or corrections to heal), the Details loupe and ready_full go through it. The heal no longer decodes a full frame of its own outside the gate: it waits for the build, whose landing asks the render again, and reads that. ready_full and its one-second dwell stay: with RAWs opened at half size (#287) it is what brings a zoom its full resolution. De-dust bench: one decode, one patch in 518 ms.

title: Every gesture a Slint enum, Act
detail: The bar keys, menu items, Settings rows, Crop's keys and shortcuts ask an Act (ui/act.slint, 74 gestures) instead of a string, and Ctl::act matches it exhaustively: a gesture no arm answers no longer compiles, where a string fell to "not in this build yet" (Compare, De-dust, Crop, New Roll and Reset to Default did so when their moment refused them). Crop's keys go through act; export_act and lab_act take no string; the medals are medal-none to medal-gold; PanelState.pick and confirm-yes/no, asked by nothing, are gone. The sheets, the mode, one Ask dialog and one RowTree move to #290.

title: The scanner vocabulary leaves the phone link crate
detail: Letter, Effect, Machine and Channel move from oni-link's scanner module into a crate of their own, oni-keys (serde only, outside hakari like the phone crates), which oni-link re-exports so the wire and the phone's code are unchanged. oni-core depends on oni-keys instead of oni-link and loses tokio; the phone's glue on the store (oni-core's link.rs, the command and face conversions, now free functions command_of, link_of, face_of and face_for) moves to oni-app's link module with its tests. Removing the phone link now touches the app alone.

title: The sidebar tree laid like the gallery
detail: The library and projects trees kept every thumbnail row's picture, and Slint the texture of every row once drawn, about 270 MB at 1,000 photos scrolled through. A row now holds its picture only within a screen of the column's view: laying the column gives the rest none, and a scroll (tree-scrolled, project-scrolled) lets the pictures of rows gone far away go and fills those come near. Every row stays in the model, so row indices, selection and keyboard walks are unchanged.

title: Prepare the Roll keeps its cells, and a redrawn scan is laid again
detail: publish_prepare, which runs at every pointer move on the base step and every slider notch, set a new cell model each time, so Slint compared every cell's picture pixel by pixel. The model is kept: a cell is written when its photo, its picture's source (none, thumbnail, tile) or its marks change, or its tile was drawn again (fresh_tiles, filled where a tile lands). The scan and the loupe's source, set only on a new path or size since #266, are now also laid again when the preview worker draws them again for the same photo.

title: Histogram plots kept as textures written in place, traced on one thread (96e0a6f)
detail: Each histogram plot (output, saturation, levels, curves) is one Rgba8Unorm texture kept while its size holds and rewritten with queue.write_texture; a revision per plot (Plots.*-revision to Plot.histogram-revision to Picture.revision) redraws it, and the software window keeps pixel images. One long-lived plots thread holds a Tracer whose buffers are reused, replacing a thread and about 23 MB of allocation per publish at 30 a second; the bytes are made non-premultiplied for the texture. Checks: kept and fresh tracers give the same bytes (twin: no clearing differs), alpha conversion (twin: truncation). A refused import (a texture lacking RENDER_ATTACHMENT) is logged.

title: The Details loupe keeps its texture (9c74d63)
detail: The Details loupe keeps its texture while the region keeps its size and bumps DetailLoupe.revision, which LoupeBand reads, as Compare's before does; the texture is dropped with the band's picture. Real run: 10 Sharpening notches through one texture, notch to loupe 10 ms median.

title: Export previews rendered at the size their slot shows (4540cc9)
detail: Export previews render at the long side their slot shows: Exporting.preview-room from ExportColumn, crop included, capped at Swift's 1600 px (preview_side, tested with a twin), and rendered again when the room grows; the size lands before the render, which waits up to 1 s for the room. publish_lines sets only changed rows. The Exporting global moves to export_state.slint, and export.slint's ceiling drops from 518 to 401. Measured 1600x1268 to 704x558 (8.1 to 1.6 MB) a preview in a 1100x680 pt window.

title: The window keeps three drawables
detail: With one frame queued (desired_maximum_frame_latency 1, two drawables) the interface thread waited in CAMetalLayer nextDrawable whenever a render shared the GPU ahead of it: 1,181 samples against 5 with three drawables in the same pan. The vendored femtovg-wgpu renderer now asks a latency of 2; a frame still presents as soon as it is drawn, at most one more frame queued when the GPU runs late.

title: The whole reduction near fit kept again
detail: #258 removed the reduction kept whole when it held at most two canvases (KEPT_WHOLE, reduced, Fitting.kept), so every pan render near fit read the full frame through two Lanczos passes and textures of hundreds of MB the pool could not keep; on a 5K canvas the picture fell to 25-30 updates a second. The view.rs hunk is put back; the pool's FIT stays.

title: A pan renders only once the picture rendered no longer covers the view
detail: Each pan event asked a render although navigate had already moved the picture and the margin rendered around the view still covered it. request_render now skips a move of the offset alone while Placement::covered_by the picture laid holds: on the S1R bench 2 renders for 60 pan steps instead of 59. A check pans within the margin with no render needed, its twin past it.

title: Gestures render lighter, the sharp render follows the stop
detail: A drag, a wheel or a pinch (by_hand) marks the hand; while it moves the view renders at most GESTURE_PIXELS (4 MP, about a 1440p window's view) and shows the texture stretched, and 150 ms after the last move (SETTLE) the view renders sharp. The view key carries the gesture so the sharp render is asked. Owner's call after testing on a 5K 120 Hz screen.

title: ONI_HZ shows the picture's real rate
detail: hz.rs counts each second the frames the window draws and those in which the canvas changed (a render landed or the picture moved), 0 at rest; ONI_HZ=1 shows it by the zoom and the log keeps every second something changed. It told a near-fit pan at 73-93 Hz from a fully zoomed one at 111-118 on the same input. A check counts frames after changes, its twin a meter counting every frame.

title: The columns and the bar cached as layers
detail: femtovg redraws the whole window at every frame, so a pan redrew every row of the library tree, the panel and the toolbar: the sample's interface thread spent most of its drawing in the tree's rows and tiles. The Tree, the Panel and the Toolbar carry cache-rendering-hint: each is drawn once into a texture and copied while nothing inside it changes. With it the near-fit pan on a 5K canvas runs at the display's rate (owner's eye).

title: RAWs open at LibRaw's half size, whole on the Settings' choice
detail: An opening decoded the whole RAW: 0.90 s for a 24 MP Nikon, 1.4-1.55 s for a 47 MP S1R, seconds past 200 MP, the first time a photo opened. The editor now reads LibRaw's half size (a sensor pixel a 2x2 block, no demosaic; 0.33-0.38 s cold) and builds no full resolution beside it; Settings > Rendering > Decode RAW files at full resolution brings the whole decode back (preference fullDecode, render::FULL_DECODE). Details, De-dust's search and every export still read the whole RAW. Half decodes are kept on disk as whole ones are (oni_decode::HALF, its side in the key): 14-31 ms read back. Owner's call: no difference seen on screen.

title: The frames either side of the one opened are decoded into the cache
detail: Each opening decodes its gallery neighbours, the next and the previous, into the disk cache behind the hand's own decode (background slots), so a step to one reads it back in tens of ms; a later opening drops the rest. Only the decode passes through memory, one at a time.

title: Dust patches searched on the GPU and shown as each lands
detail: A run of patches showed nothing until its last was written (79 strokes at the largest brush: 65 s with no patch on screen), and each search scored every candidate on the CPU: the fine pass's 100,000 candidates times up to 4,096 ring cells. The search's costs now run on the GPU as Swift's correctionCost does (heal/cost.wgsl, the region laid once for both passes through the app's door), with the CPU's cost_map kept beside it as reference and as fallback, and each patch lands on the canvas as soon as it is written (patch_landed). 20 strokes at the bench's largest brush: 6.5 s to 2.9 s, a patch every 110-150 ms. heal.rs's cost map moves to heal/cost.rs. A check scores a grid on both and finds every finite cost within 1e-3, its twin a ring of another size that differs.

title: Sheets and the mode as Slint enums, one Ask dialog, one RowTree
detail: Eighteen sheet flags are ORed in app.slint and mounted one by one, and the mode is three booleans read at 25 sites; six copies of Swift's DSDialogRequest and two near-identical trees (archive, projects) remain. An enum for the sheet and the mode, one Ask dialog, one RowTree.

title: A Settings window with sections
detail: The Settings sheet lists its sections on a rail, as the systems' settings windows do, and shows one page at a time: General (key clicks), Editor (keep the zoom, show what the screen cannot show, decode RAWs whole), Frontier look (export, use a file, measured), Phone (pair, forget, the phones paired or connected) and About (version, check for updates, what's new, welcome, report a problem, console). A key that opens a sheet of its own closes Settings first, so two never stack; the section shown stays while the app runs. Section gains foldable, false on these pages. SheetStyle gains settings-width, settings-rail and settings-height. The session check shoots each page.

title: The app in English, French and Spanish
detail: Every text the app shows is translated. Slint writes @tr (about 540 texts, arguments as {}), bundled from crates/oni-i18n/lang/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/oni-ui.po with no default context; the Rust side reads the same catalogues through oni-i18n (tr, tr! with named places, trn for plurals with French counting 0 as one, marked for constants; about 390 texts in oni-app, oni-core, oni-library and oni-export). Settings > General picks Automatic (the system's language, English when the app does not speak it), English, Français or Español, kept as the language preference; the interface changes at once and every text the Rust side lays is published again. scripts/i18n lays new texts into the catalogues. Checks: every text in both catalogues with its places kept, no .slint word outside @tr, the extraction's own twins, French plural rule and locale reading; the session check switches to French and back. ONI_LANGUAGE stands in for the system's language, the window checks reading English. Logs, keys, file names, preset defaults and what the Swift app reads stay English; the Scanner face's machine screen keeps the Frontier's own English.

title: The Scanner face's keypad rows become sliders with step keys
detail: Owner's call. On the Scanner face's Color tab, D, C, M, Y, TEMP, Contrast, Vignette and Chrome are each a StepSlider (ds/keypad.slint): the title and its readout above, a rail running from the minus band colour to the plus one in whole steps between the letter's or the effect's range, a mark at rest, and a small keycap either side for one step, three with Shift; a double click on the rail or the title rests it.
