A slide holds the store (Lab.hold), so it is one step to undo; each step still goes through Link::Step and StepEffect, as the phone's keys do. Rust lays every slider's steps, range and readout (app/lab/sliders.rs, with its test and twin); lab.rs's tests move to lab/tests.rs under the 400-line ceiling.

title: Every help mark's note is a card with a place for its clip
detail: Owner's call. A "?" (HelpMark, Tips.note) shows a card instead of a line: a 4:3 place above, empty on the skeleton ground until its GIF is made (Tip.clip), then the note in medium weight, white. Tooltips stay lines. TipStyle gains card-width, card-padding and card-radius, Type gains medium (500). The catalogue check shoots the card and checks a tooltip stays a line (twin).

title: A design-system state board shows every component in every state, one family a page
detail: Owner's call, for the design review that brings back the raised and inset 3D effects. Board (ds/board/, exported from app.slint, `oni --board`, arrow keys walk the pages) lays thirteen families: buttons, icon buttons and plates, tabs and toggles, fields, sliders, the Scanner keypad, containers, lists and trees, tiles and pictures, menus, feedback, plots and tokens; each component a group, a row per variant, a column per state, every look forced without a pointer. Forced states added with live defaults, no look changed: `look` on Picker (MenuPicker, LinesPicker), HelpMark, ScrollKnob (widened), TrashRow, FolderRow, GlyphKey, ColumnPill, Chip, PresetRow and PinnedTreeRow; `hover-tab` on Tabs; `focused-look` on TextArea. The window check `board` shoots each family to ONI_SHOTS as board-<nn>-<name>.png at scale 2, sized to the page; twin: an unknown family lays nothing and its blank window is seen as blank. The i18n check skips ds/board/ as it skips the catalogue.

title: Design system: one component, its variants as props (text, keys, groups)
detail: Owner's call: the app uses instances of a few components whose props give them their look. Text: Note, Warning, CautionNote and GroupHeading are Label roles and tones (TextRole.note wraps in the tertiary ink; Tone.warning, Tone.caution). Keys: IconButton, the Scanner's Key, GlyphKey and Swatch are Button variants (ButtonSize.mini and .key, fill for a band or a tint, square, wide, glyph-ink, the keycap's hold and Shift read), Button moving to ds/button.slint. Groups: KeyPlate and SheetKeys are ButtonGroup with plate, mini, fills and trailing; KeyRow and Keypad, asked by nothing since the Scanner sliders, are gone. Every window check shot before and after: the app's screens match pixel for pixel but for run-to-run noise (temporary folder names, render dither); the catalogue and the board lose the keypad.

title: Design system consolidation: fields, rows, sheets and menus, tiles and badges, the board in the app
detail: Next phases of #296, after #298 and #299 merged the fields, rows, menus, pickers, badges, toggles and preset faces, and #300 rebuilt the board on the base components in the app. Remains: Sheet, PanelSheet and BoardSheet stay three for now (Slint lays a component's children in one place and their layouts differ), with #290's one Ask dialog; StatusLine and SealedStatusLine, Progress and LoadBar, Surface, Card, BoardCard and Well, the tile family (TileView, RollCellView, StockCellView, PresetFace, TileGhost) and Slider and StepSlider are not merged; one Notice.

title: Design system: one TextField, one FormRow, one Row, one Heading
detail: Part of #296. TextField takes a suffix (SuffixField), a width for numbers (NumberField) and multiline with its own height (TextArea); FormRow takes spread for LabelledRow. ds/row.slint's Row is every line of a list or a tree: ListRow, TreeItem, PinnedTreeRow, FolderRow, TrashRow, PresetRow and RenameRow become instances (kind, depth, expandable, folds, open, stock or glyph, trail, caption, detail, badge, selected, picked, quiet, rounded, pinned, present, star, a hovered action, renaming); RowKind gains none, opened and trash, FolderKind goes. TileHeading and PinnedHeading are one Heading. Every window check's shot matches the one before but for a board line.

title: Design system: one Menu, one Picker, one Badge, one Toggle, one PresetFace
detail: Part of #296. ds/menu.slint holds MenuEntry, MenuPanel, Menu and Picker: Menu takes words (entries, current), a context menu's lines, or the folder pill's choices, and closes on a choice or a click outside; ContextMenu and FolderMenu are gone. Picker takes entries or lines and drops its own menu under its field, MenuPicker and LinesPicker gone, the preset form's BalancePicker an instance. Badge (base.slint) with BadgeTone warning, dark, seal, alert, news and step replaces WarningBadge, the frame's Badge, Seal, NewsSeal and StepNumber. Toggle takes labelled for ToggleRow, keeping its own width alone so a row's label pushes it to the end. PresetFace takes new and lit for PresetNewFace. Sheet, PanelSheet and BoardSheet stay three: Slint lays a component's children in one place and their layouts differ. Every window check's shot matches the one before.

title: The design system's board: one base component a page, live beside its forced states, opened from Help in dev builds
detail: Owner's call, for the review before the raised and inset 3D effects. Help > Design System… shows when updates::stamped() is false (App.dev, Act.design-system) and opens the Board window, one kept in State.board; `oni --board` still opens it alone. The board is rebuilt on #296's base components: fourteen pages (Text, Badge, Button, ButtonGroup, Toggle and Tabs, Slider, TextField and forms, Picker and Menu, Row, Tiles, Containers, Scanner and overlays, Plots, Tokens), each a title, the variant props, a row per variant and a column per state, the first live under the hand (the live column holds its own state: a toggle flips, a slider drags, a step slider steps, a picker drops its menu, a row selects, folds and stars, a crop frame drags, the Scanner screen reads its sliders), the others forced through look, focused-look, hover-tab, on and enabled. The window, titled ONI Design System, lists the pages on its left, scrolls the page and draws the tooltips and help cards. No component's look changed. The window check `board` shoots each page as board-<nn>-<name>.png and counts inks right of the list alone (page-x), so a blank page is still seen; twin: an unknown page lays nothing and its blank page is seen as blank.

title: Label takes an ink of its own and a spaced tracking; the last raw Text in the design system's badges, preset faces and passes become Labels
detail: Label gets `ink` (a colour over its tone's, as Icon's) and `spaced` (the seal's 1.2 px tracking). PresetFace's monogram, name and "+", PassReorder's R, G and B letters (each its channel's ink) and WrappedCard's eyebrow are Labels, each keeping its face, size, weight and alignment. No pixel moves.

title: Two inks become tones: on-warning for the warning band, lcd for the scanner's glass
detail: Tone.on-warning (Colour.ink-on-warning) and Tone.lcd (ScannerStyle.lcd-ink). WarningBand's sentence and glyph, the keypad's Lcd (mono, as LabScreen) and LcdReadout (Inter at the value's size, as DSLCD) read them instead of a colour written in place. No pixel moves.

title: WrappedHint is a Label, caption role, secondary, centred
detail: The hint under the Wrapped deck inherited Text with its own face, size and ink; it is now a caption Label. The card's eyebrow keeps Swift's seal tracking (1.2 px) through `spaced`. No pixel moves.

title: One seal, as Swift's DSGoldSealView: every seal a capsule 20 high, padded 9, 9.5 strong with 1.2 tracking, its foil gold, holographic or red
detail: Badge's seal, alert and news tones were three geometries (14 high on a 2 px radius, 20 high, the Wrapped year's hand copy); they become one `seal` tone with `metal` (DSFoil.Metal: gold, holographic, red) at DSFoil.size's width (the last letter's tracking off, rounded up), printed in one dark ink as DSFoil prints them. Flat foils: the medal's gold, the holographic foil's body (#c7ccdb), the destructive red. The gallery tile's RGB seal (hand-drawn) and RollCellView's, SealedStatusLine's (standing out of the 18 high bar as Swift's overlay does), the FLAGGED seal (its dead `true ?` ternary gone), the news seals and the Wrapped year are all Badge seals. The tile's medal stays level with the seal's centre, so it moves 3 px up. Visible: every seal is taller, its letters heavier and dark.

title: The dark badge takes Swift's DSBadge padding, and CorrectionMark's number is that badge
detail: Swift draws the correction's number, the loupe's ratio, the crop's size, the preset hint and the tree's drag count with one DSBadge, padded DS.Control.badgePadding (6) on every side. The Rust dark badge was padded 5 by 2 and CorrectionMark drew its own (3 by 1); both are now Badge dark at 6. Visible: those badges grow 2 px across and 8 px in height (the correction's 6 and 10). Swift's rounded badge also differs in radius (8 against 4), face (value, label for the correction), fill (overlay, 60 % black) and ink (on-fill): left for the owner.

title: The preset editor's tint badge is a Badge tint, its monogram centred as Swift's frame centres it
detail: Row's badge was a 30×22 rectangle around a raw Text; Badge tone `tint` takes the preset's fill and ink, at DS.Control.presetBadgeWidth × presetBadgeHeight on Radius.badge, the monogram centred by the badge itself. Slint already placed the Text at the middle, so no pixel moves.

title: Badge holds no literal size
detail: BadgeStyle (base.slint) holds DSBadge's padding, its radius (Radius.badge / 2), and the seal's height, padding, size and tracking; the badge's 11 px is Type.chip. The Badge's own text is a Label with an ink. Badge, BadgeTone, Metal and BadgeStyle live in ds/badge.slint, so base.slint stays under its 400 line ceiling.

title: The board shows the new tones, a Label's ink and spacing, and every Badge tone with the seals' three metals and the tint
detail: Text page: on-warning on its band and lcd on the glass in every role and glyph row, and a row of Labels with an ink or spaced. Badge page: warning, dark, seal gold with its note, holographic and red, step, tint. The Tiles and Scanner pages show the seals through TileView, RollCellView and SealedStatusLine.

title: Action keys keep DSActionButton's on-fill ink
detail: A kind's tint (accent, destructive, update, confirm) keeps the on-fill ink as Swift's DSActionButton (keycapTextColor textOnFill), caution's yellow its dark ink; only a key's own fill (keypad bands, swatches) takes its ink by its lightness.

title: Text fields behave as AppKit's: entered by a click, Tab or their owner they select their whole value; once in, a click places the caret, a double click selects a word, a triple click the line
detail: Owner's request. The DS TextField (every single-line, suffixed, number, multiline, rename and date field) selects its whole value when it gains the focus: a TouchArea over the unfocused field takes the press and selects all, Tab and a programmatic focus select all from the input's focus change (Slint selects on Tab only off Apple). Once the field holds the focus the TouchArea steps aside and Slint's TextInput takes the clicks: a click places the caret (it was eaten before, single-line fields never placed a caret by a click), a double click selects the word, a triple click the line. A field the window gives back after another window or a popup keeps its selection: a global serial of the last field entered tells a return from a new entry. The window check text_fields drives a probe window (ds/board/probe.slint, FieldProbe): a click then a key replaces the value, a double click replaces the word, a triple click the line, Tab into the next field replaces its value, a click into the multiline field selects all; twin: a click into the focused field types beside the value, and the old TextField fails the first assertion ("Xalpha beta gamma").

title: Button: one tint path for every kind and fill, a ghost kind, DSPanelButton's capitals, no mini, 46 px or wide keycap
detail: Owner-approved merges K1, K2, K3, K5, K6, K7, T3. One tint: a kind (accent, caution, destructive, update, confirm) is a shortcut that sets the tint, `fill` a tint of the key's own; every tint hovers 0.1 brighter (ButtonStyle.lift), presses 0.2 darker (ButtonStyle.press) and takes its ink by its Rec. 709 lightness (KeyInk.light): UPDATE (#ff9f0a, 0.66) now reads dark ink, where Swift's DSActionButton keeps textOnFill; `on` on a tinted key keeps the tint and rings it, as Swift's tint overrides `pale`; the per-kind hover and pressed colours left the theme. ButtonSize.mini (26 px) is gone: the column headers' glyph keys are small (24 px), ButtonGroup `mini` became `small`, the column pill 26 px tall (NavigatorStyle.key = ButtonStyle.small-height). ButtonSize.key is now the step slider's 24 px square keycap (ScannerStyle.step-key), holding 140 ms in the legend's face; the 46 px height and `wide` are gone. ButtonKind.ghost: a glyph alone on no ground, tertiary then secondary under the hand, silent; HelpMark is a ghost Button (its note through the new `note`, shown as a card), and so is the row's star (`glyph-size`, `glyph-ink`). Button puts its word in capitals as DSPanelButton does (`capitals: false` for the console's AppKit keys and the DSActionButton keys whose busy title keeps its case). The Section's fold key is `square`. The button role of Label carries ButtonStyle.tracking, so a Label in that role draws as a Button's word. Not done: LoupeBand's ratio badge stays a Badge in a TouchArea (a ghost Button draws no badge face).

title: ButtonGroup `align`, key rows on Swift's plates, one Pager
detail: G1: ButtonGroup's `fills` and `trailing` became `align: start | end | center | fill` (GroupAlign); the canvas's zoom keys use `align: center`, the redundant `fills: true` on keys of a filling plate and the `fills: false` defaults went. G2, each against its Swift screen: the export panel's presets (KeycapPlate(fills:)), Load a Profile / Get Paper Profiles (KeycapPlate(fills:)) and Cancel / Export (one plate, Cancel at its width, EXPORT taking the rest) and Prepare's footer (one plate, Cancel and Back at their width, the step's key taking the rest) sit on plates; the report's Send is Swift's confirm tint; the preset save sheet's Save is plain and plateless, as Swift's; the welcome, console and preset editor rows have no plate in Swift and keep none. G3: `Pager` (ds/roll.slint), Previous, a name, Next, for the frame scrubber and the base pick.

title: Picker's faces: the column pill and the Working Space chip are Picker variants
detail: K4: ColumnPill (folders.slint) and Chip (forms.slint) are gone; Picker gains `face: field | pill | chip`, `prefix` (the chip's secondary words), `choices` (a column's folders), `pressable`, `enabled` (dimmed) and `help`, one hover ground (Colour.hover) for every face, the field's included where it was the raised grey. The navigator's folder list drops from its pill as wide as it (the old Menu took `width:` and stayed 260 px); a pill out of reach dims.

title: Toggle's words at either side, wrapping, flipping it
detail: O1: Toggle's `labelled` became `label-side: none | after | before`, `after` the default as DSToggle, and `wrap`. Every FormRow-spread-around-a-Toggle (export ZIP, HDR, colour-only; the preset's carried rows), Prepare's hand-made flat-field row and the report's Label + TouchArea are a Toggle with its words after the switch, as Swift; a disabled toggle's words dim (export HDR) and a click on them flips it with its click sound.

title: Tabs only ask: a click emits picked, the owner writes the choice
detail: O2: Tabs' `selected` is an input; a click no longer writes it, so a one-way binding (Settings' language) keeps following its owner. The sixteen two-way sites write their global in their picked handler before Rust's, as the binding did; Settings' language is written by Rust's publish_settings. Window check tab_bar: a click asks, the bar stays on the owner's value and follows it after; twin: the owner writing the asked tab moves the bar there.

title: One RenameField for the heading, the row and the editable title
detail: F1: RenameField (controls.slint): text, placeholder, edited, committed, cancelled; entered at once with its value selected, Return or the focus leaving commits, Escape cancels. TileHeading (was HeadingField), the Row's renaming FocusScope and EditableTitle use it; EditableTitle gains Escape.

title: TextField: centred, a title's face, its placeholder in every form, faded whenever disabled, a number's width
detail: F2: TextField gains `centred` and `role` (label or title); DateFields' boxes are TextFields (DateBox gone). F3: the placeholder is drawn in multiline too, so the preset's description overlay went. Fixes: a disabled TextField fades as a suffixed one did (export Camera, Lens, ISO, Date, Artist, Copyright, W and H); FormStyle.size-field adds the hollow's padding to Swift's 64 px digits, so 3000 shows whole; `focused-look` hides the placeholder as a focus does (the board's Focus column).

title: One Field in three layouts
detail: F4: Field and FormRow are one `Field { layout: stacked | column | spread; help }` (FieldLayout): stacked is DSField, column the EXIF line's fixed label width, spread the label taking the room before its control (Crop's Kept). F5: the preset's white balance is a Field with its help, as Swift's DSHelp over its DSPicker (its label now the secondary ink).

title: The board's pages show the merged components
detail: Button: kinds, small glyph keys, ghost, the 24 px key, capitals on and off (no mini, 46 px or wide rows); ButtonGroup: small and each align; Toggle: label-side none, after, before and wrap, the live tab bar written by its owner; TextField and forms: multiline placeholder, centred title face, Field's column and spread layouts, RenameField; Picker and Menu: every form with a disabled column, the pill (folders, a name alone) and the chip. The catalogue's keycaps are the 24 px step keys. FieldProbe (board/probe.slint) holds the fields and the tab bar the window checks click.

title: Design system: one Knob, one Rail, one value header for every slider
detail: Phase of #297. ds/slider.slint holds the slider's parts: Knob (DSBarHandle: centre, fill, grip, grip-ink, grown, slide) draws Slider's, StepSlider's and the levels track's handles (TrackKnob is gone); Rail (DSRail: fill level, ramp, bipolar, metal or none, at, from, tint, low, high, overhang, rest, glow) draws Slider's, StepSlider's (bipolar plus its rest tick) and LevelsTrack's tracks, and Progress is a Rail lit in Colour.selected with its glow, LoadBar following; ValueHeader (DSReadout) is the name and value above Slider and StepSlider, the latter's double click and tooltip on the name included. Slider moved from controls.slint to slider.slint, SliderFill with it (new: none); the Knob enum is gone, Slider.knob is a colour as Swift's DSSlider.knob. One look changed, copied from Swift: DSBarHandle's grip lines are DS.Palette.textOnFill on every cap, so SliderStyle.grip-ink is white instead of the secondary ink (a flat white cap keeps the dark ink, its lines otherwise vanishing); every other pixel is unchanged.

title: Design system: Slider absorbs StepSlider as its stepped mode
detail: Phase of #297, after #320. Slider gains stepped: whole steps from lowest to highest (value), the rail a bipolar gradient from low to high with its rest ticked, a key either side in those colours (one step, three with Shift, the StepKey Button in one place), the name's double click and the rail's resetting (reset), the name's tooltip (help, minus-help, plus-help), held(bool) around a slide, every move through step(field, by); no Option fine mode and no wheel in that mode. LabSlider (panel/parts.slint) is a stepped Slider; the Scanner Color tab's calls into Lab (press, step-effect, clear, clear-effect, hold) are unchanged. StepSlider is gone from keypad.slint. The board's Slider page shows Knob, Rail, Slider and the stepped Slider, its columns Live, Hover, Pressed, Disabled; the Scanner page's letters are stepped Sliders. No pixel changed.

title: Design system: one Plot for the main histogram, AxisCaptions down a plot's side
detail: Phase of #297. The panel's HistogramFrame (a stretched Picture on the panel's ground) and PrintOverlay nested in it are one Plot (plot 5: screen, grid and hit test off, PlotStyle.main tall, Plots.output as its histogram, Lighting's curves on the Color tab alone), square-cornered on the panel's ground as Swift's DSHistogram; HistogramFrame, PlotSize and PrintOverlay are gone. The plot's own resized sets Plots.output-width/height, the size Rust traces the output histogram at, and reports plot 5 to the editors: read from the editors' sizes instead, the trace missed the histogram in the navigator's and the trees' shots, plot 5's size not yet known when the first count landed. AxisCaptions takes axis: Orientation.vertical, its captions down the plot's side inset by Space.s, which the saturation editor's Saturated and Desaturated now use. The board's Plots page shows the main histogram's Plot, an editor's screen and the vertical captions, the levels track live; the knobs moved to the Slider page. No pixel changed.

title: Design system: PlotInkStyle folded into PlotStyle, Colour and SliderStyle
detail: Phase of #297. PlotInkStyle repeated other groups: its track, knob-width and knob-height are SliderStyle's, its grab is SliderStyle.grab (DS.Control.grabSize, which SplitStyle.grab now reads), its histogram is PlotStyle.block, its guide, guide-faint, handle-active, handle-idle and channel-red are Colour's, and its marker is the new Colour.marker. PlotStyle now holds the plots' own: main, block, radius, and the inks Swift's views write as literals (the levels greys and the spectrogram's bands). No value changed, so no pixel.

title: Sliders as Swift's DSSlider: the knob's hover, settle and the wheel everywhere
detail: Seen on the board after #320 and #321. A disabled slider never grows its knob (the board's Disabled column did). The stepped slider grows its knob and shows the grab cursor over the knob alone, as DSSlider and the continuous one; its name's double click and tooltip are off while disabled, and its ± keys dim with it. The knob follows the hand unsprung and settles on a value arriving from elsewhere (a reset, an undo, another photo) along Motion.settle (DS.Motion.settle's 0.38 s response, eased out), never while held or within Motion.settle of a scroll event; the stepped slider used to lag its slide by 0.14 s. The levels track shows the grab cursor within a handle's grab, its hover measured from the track's origin (it was a half-knob off), and its handles settle the same way while no hand is on it. Every slider takes the wheel as DSScrollAdjust does: the Brush Size (now a BrushSlider wrapper), the export's Quality and Prepare the Roll's sliders, which ignored it, move along their track and run their release's work (the brush and Picker Size kept, the export weighed) once the scroll rests, through Ctl::slider_scrolled; a scroll across a track is still left to the pane. Ink.primary has its own branch in Inks.of. Window checks: the brush, the quality and the Picker Size scroll along and refuse a scroll across (twins), the Picker Size written only once the scroll rests.

title: Design system: one raised surface, Raised, and one popup, PopupPanel
detail: Phase of #297. The sheet's card, PopoverPanel and FloatingColumn drew the same surface: the panel's ground rounded as a card. Raised holds it once, its content in a column (pad and gap as Gap), with lift none (a hairline: a popover, a menu), float (the scanner's shade, no edge, clipped: a hidden column slid over the card) or sheet (a hairline, the scrim's lift, clipped); menu takes the raised grey and the menus' round (MenuStyle.radius), as Swift keeps a menu apart from a popover. A press on it stays on it, but on a slid column. Menu and Popover, both a PopupWindow closed by a click outside and sized on their panel, are one PopupPanel, kind menu (raised grey, radius 8, padding xs) or popover (ground, radius 12, padding and gap m, at the export panel's width); Menu is PopupPanel of kind menu with its lines. MenuPanel, PopoverPanel, Popover and FloatingColumn are gone, and MenuStyle.padding with them (the menu's pad is Gap.xs). No value changed, so no pixel.

title: Design system: one Inset for the summary box, the board's card and the corrections' well
detail: Phase of #297. SummaryBox (forms), BoardCard (forms) and Well (frame) were the same box sunk in the panel: the canvas's dark, rounded, a column of lines. Inset holds it, with pad and gap as Gap (m and xxs by default, the summary's) and radius (Radius.card; Radius.control 16 for the De-dust corrections' list, as CorrectionsPanel). The paper profiles' card is Inset pad l gap m. No value changed, so no pixel.

title: Design system: one TipCard for the tooltip and the help card
detail: Phase of #297. TipLayer drew the tooltip and the help mark's card, and the board's Containers page copied both by hand (HelpCard, TipLine). TipCard draws either, card or not, with its natural size out; TipLayer is a TipCard placed by Tips.place and shown after the delay, and the board shows TipCard itself. No pixel in the app.

title: Design system: one Sheet for the dialog's card, the presets' panel sheet and the paper board
detail: Phase of #297. Sheet (over Dialog), PanelSheet and BoardSheet copied one frame: the blocking TouchArea, a FocusScope for Escape, the card at SheetStyle.margin on a raised surface. Sheet now carries every variant: card-height (0 fits the content and scrolls past the window's room; else the card is that tall at most, its content laid in the height it shows), header leading (the title over the content, the section face for a question) or bar (the title beside its exit key, Done by default, above a rule, the content edge to edge), bleed, and gap (a notice's groups a step l apart). Dialog, PanelSheet and BoardSheet are gone; BoardSheet's row of sidebar and card moved into PaperSheet. One way to title a sheet: NoticeSheet, TransitionSheet and RootsCatchUpSheet wrote their own title label only to get the wider step, they now set title and gap l; PresetSaveSheet takes the leading title. StockPickerSheet redrew the bar by hand at padding m all round: it takes the bar header, whose title and Done sit at SheetStyle.padding (24) from the sides instead of 16, the only pixels moved.

title: Design system: one AskSheet for the six questions, as DSDialogRequest
detail: Phase of #297 and the Slint side of #290's one Ask dialog; the five globals behind it stay. ChoiceSheet, AdviceSheet, ExportConfirmSheet, ExportNoticeSheet, ConfirmSheet and MaskDialogSheet built the same panel. AskSheet copies Swift's DSDialogPanel: a question's title, the message in the secondary ink, a field when it asks for a word (focused, Return pressing default-key), then Cancel and its keys on one plate at the end; each key an AskKey { text, role } with DSDialogRequest.Role's confirm (accent, the default), destructive (red, deaf to Return) or option (neutral, deaf to Return). answered(index, text) gives -1 for Cancel and Escape. The six sheets are AskSheet instances bound to their globals; Choice.keys is now [AskKey] (every key an option). Return and Escape stay Rust's, per global, as before. No pixel.

title: Design system: one StatusBar, as Swift's DSStatusBar
detail: Phase of #297. StatusLine (base), SealedStatusLine (roll) and LoadBar (forms) drew the one bar under the viewer. StatusBar copies DSStatusBar's two states in one shape: idle, the line and its seal (holographic) after it; busy, what loads, its count on the glass and its progress, sweeping below zero. CardStatus switches it on loading instead of swapping two components. No pixel. Swift's idle seal stands Space.s after the text and its busy title is in the label face and primary ink; this port keeps 2 × s and the value face in the secondary ink, as before.

title: The dark badge as Swift's DSBadge: radius 8, the value face, black at 60 %, white ink
detail: Follows #305. The dark Badge had DSBadge's padding (6) but a radius of 4, the chip's face, the contrast edge's fill and the handle's ink. It now takes DSBadge's rounded outline (DS.Radius.badge, 8), DS.Typo.value (11), DS.Palette.overlay (black at 60 %, new Colour.overlay) and textOnFill; role: label gives a correction's number the label's face, as NegativeView sets it. Seen on the loupe's ratio, the crop's size, the preset deck's hint, the tree's drag counter, the correction marks and the console's count.

title: The export preview slot: a state enum, its ground, and Swift's sweep while it renders
detail: PreviewSlot.state was an int 0/1/2: it is PreviewState { rendering, shown, failed }, which ExportLine carries. Swift's slot shows DSProgress(fraction: nil) at the inline progress's width while it renders, not a dash; the slot does so. The slot lays the canvas's dark it sits on as its ground, so its size reads on the board in every state; the export card is that dark, so no pixel moves there.

title: Board: the Containers page shows Sheet's variants, AskSheet, Raised, PopupPanel, Inset, StatusBar and TipCard
detail: The page shows AskSheet (Cancel and a destructive key, option keys wide, a notice's one key), Sheet (leading fitted and wide, gap l, card-height, the bar header over a list and an Inset), Raised in each lift and as a menu, PopupPanel opened by its keys, Inset in its two gauges, the StatusBar idle, sealed, counted and sweeping, and TipCard in both forms; the badge page adds the dark badge in the label's face. The bar sheet's list column keeps its lines at the top (alignment start), the card-height sheet hangs whole with its bottom margin, and each Surface swatch is outlined so the ground reads on the ground. The menus page shows the menu's Raised, the overlays page the corrections' Inset.

title: The gallery's tiles round their corners under the ring
detail: TileLayers clips a tile to Radius.card; the gallery and tree tiles stay unclipped (a rounded clip draws each tile to a layer) and paint their corners in the ground behind them (CardCorners, which takes a radius and a ground), so the photo no longer pokes past the rounded selection ring.

title: One RowTree lays the archive's and the projects' trees
detail: library_tree.slint and project_tree.slint laid two near-identical trees: the Scroller, the TouchArea under no row, each Rust-laid row as a Row, a TileView with its thumbnail's TouchArea or a renamed Row, then the pinned Row over them. Both are one app-side RowTree (ui/row_tree.slint): rows, pin, content-height, viewport-y both ways, indexed callbacks, projects (its kinds) and draggable (a press moved carries the pick); the projects' DropRing, DropLine and drag chip are its children. project_tree.slint is gone, with its broken indentation. The archive's pinned row now carries the roll's stock artwork, which it dropped (a pinned roll showed the film-roll glyph). No pixel moves otherwise.

title: Row's form: list, navigator, sidebar; the sheets' side lists rounded
detail: Row takes form: list | navigator | sidebar in place of the rounded, quiet, folds, open and absent props repeated by the navigator's folders and trash, the board and the catalogue; NavigatorStyle.absent (0.4) was State.disabled and is gone. The sheets' side lists take the sidebar form, rounded as the presets' already were: Settings' sections, the board's pages and the Paper Profiles makers. As PaperProfilesSheet.group, the chosen maker shows on the hover's band (picked) and each group's heading is a Row of the new heading kind: tertiary, out of reach, no band, an xs above its first line. Visible: Settings' and the papers' rounded bands, the papers' choice on the hover band, its rows an xs lower.

title: Divider draws every rule, across or vertical, line or hairline
detail: Divider gets vertical and hairline and is bounded across alone, so a layout stretches it along its length. It absorbs VerticalRule (0.5 pt, Settings, the presets' editor, the board) and the rule Row drew by hand under a pinned row. No pixel moves.

title: The folder pill's choices are Rows in the menu form
detail: MenuEntry's folder mode drew a pill's ancestors as a second kind of line; they are Rows in a new menu form (kind folder, no chevron zone, its glyph in its own width, a check at the end, MenuStyle.row tall) and MenuEntry keeps the menus' words alone. Slight: the band's corner 6 to 8 pt (Radius.badge), the check 4 pt further in.

title: One SelectionRing, and TileView draws Prepare the Roll's frames
detail: TileView's square ring, RollCellView's double and outset rings and DropRing were three rings; Swift builds all three alike (TileLayers, RollFrameCell, TreeRowChrome.dropRing): a contrastEdgeIdle stroke inset by Stroke.line, the 2 pt selected ring over it. One SelectionRing { placement: inset | outset; tone: selected | destructive; radius } in ds/marks.slint draws them, copied from Swift: the gallery's ring gains the inner edge and Radius.card corners, the roll cell's rings go Radius.badge to Radius.card with the inner edge under the ring (Stroke.line in, not Stroke.emphasis). RollFrameCell is built on GalleryView.tile, so TileView absorbs RollCellView: marks medal | apart (the apart dot top-right, every seal an xs in), flagged, ring inset | outset, rounded (Radius.card), clicked; an unticked frame fades with its marks, as Swift's .opacity on the whole cell. tree.slint and RollCellView are gone. The gallery's pictures stay square: Swift rounds them at Radius.card, which a rounded clip would draw tile by tile into a layer of its own. Visible: the gallery's and the roll's rings. Prepare the Roll's state (Preparing, RollCell) moved to prepare_state.slint, as export_state.slint, so prepare.slint falls under the 400-line limit and leaves the grandfathered list.

title: Picture's fit; the Wrapped cells, the welcome photo and the splash are Pictures
detail: Picture takes fit: contain | cover | fill in place of stretched, and a radius (Radius.badge by default). The Wrapped deck's photo cells, WelcomePhoto and SplashWindow (which now holds a WelcomePhoto at its own radius and a caption at scale 1) draw through it. TileGhost is a Picture at TileStyle.ghost (0.85, GalleryEngine's dragged tile); the card stack's 0.8 and 0.55 are TileStyle.stack-middle and stack-back. Row draws a roll's stock through StockIcon. No pixel moves.

title: One Ring with guide and sharpen tones, one Trace with live and source tones, the source's line dashed
detail: Ring (the base pick's), BrushDisc and CorrectionMark's ring were three circles; Swift strokes all three with Circle().stroke, centred on the edge: DSGuide.width(true) over its shadow for the base ring and the brush, the sharpen tint at DSGuide.width(false) with no shadow for a correction. One Ring { tone: guide | sharpen } in ds/marks.slint draws them: the brush's ring is centred (a point further out), a correction's ring is 1 pt, not 0.5, and a circle at the box's shorter side as Circle() in a frame, not a stadium. LiveStroke and SourceTrace, the same Path but for the ink, are one Trace { tone: live | source; dashed }; the line from a patch to its source is dashed four on four as NegativeView's StrokeStyle(dash: [4, 4]), its ends flat: Slint strokes no dash, so live::dashed lays the dashes in Rust (unit test with its twin). Visible: the brush ring, the correction rings, the dashed source lines.

title: One Dot for every disc, one Medal for the tile and the picker
detail: The hand-made discs (the tile's medal, MedalPicker's three, the roll cell's apart dot, Tabs' swatch and mark, Button's lamp, Toggle's thumb, BulletLine's bullet) are one Dot { size; ink } in ds/marks.slint; the tile and MedalPicker share Medal { rank }. No pixel moves.

title: The measuring window's corners in unalignedBalance; the loupe's ratio a pressable Badge; Row's RESTORE clear of its count
detail: The measuring window drew its corners white at rest: Bracket now takes the frame's rest ink, unalignedBalance on the window as CropOverlay's cornerHandle strokes DSGuide.stroke(rest: style.rest). LoupeBand's ratio is a Badge with pressable and clicked, no TouchArea of its own (no pixel). A hovered trash line's RESTORE stands an xs further from its count. The board's Picked column says the band is held with the pointer away, which is why it shows no star or RESTORE: Swift's rows show them under the pointer alone. ListView stays: Slint virtualises a for only under an element whose type is named ListView with the content and visible lengths, which the export's lines use.

title: The board shows the merged components
detail: Row page: the four forms, the heading kind, the menu form's check, the Picked column's meaning. Tiles page: TileView as the gallery's tile and as Prepare the Roll's frame (marks apart, rounded, every state of the old RollCellView), SelectionRing in each placement, tone and radius, Picture's fit, Dot and Medal, the ghost as a Picture. Scanner page: the canvas marks in cells of one size over a photo (the Well with rows, Ring in both tones, Trace live and source with its dashed line, DustOriginal on a scene), and the measuring window's teal corners. Picker page: the pill's folders as menu-form Rows.

title: Every duplicate design token folded into the one it equals
detail: Tabs', fields' and menu rows' heights and the tabs' and fields' radii read ButtonStyle's, the menu panel's Radius.badge; NavigatorStyle.key and ScannerStyle.step-key are ButtonStyle.small-height; SheetStyle.panel-width is FormStyle's, RollStyle's and the board's panel width ShellStyle's; RollStyle.canvas-padding and FormStyle.chip-height are CardStyle.padding; ScannerStyle.label-weight is Type.medium; both sockets are Colour.well; Colour.paper is white and focus the accent; channel blue is the accent's token, not a literal; TipStyle has one padding; CropStyle.hairline is Stroke.hairline; the split guide's shadow is Stroke.emphasis as the ring's, the preset deck's peek Space.m. Dead tokens removed (SplashStyle.minimum, RollStyle.plate, PresetStyle's badge sizes, ButtonStyle.label and weight, SheetStyle.radius, ScannerStyle.key-gap and socket-radius, NavigatorStyle.rest), and the unused imports of every file touched, keypad.slint's among them. No pixel moves.

title: A disabled slider keeps its rail opaque, and the levels' handles slide once
detail: As DSSlider: off limits, the readout fades and the track stays opaque. LevelsTrack no longer animates its knobs on top of Rust, which already springs every handle but the one held or scrolled with DS.Motion.settle, as DSTrackHandle; the Slint slide doubled that spring. The board's slider and plots pages say so.

title: One showcase: the catalogue gives way to the board
detail: ds/catalogue.slint, its window check and the --catalogue flag (ONI_CATALOGUE) are gone; the board already showed every piece it held but a scroller whose content fits, now a line of the Containers page. The checks that clicked into the catalogue read probe windows beside FieldProbe: ScrollProbe (a page taller than the window over a scroller that fits) for the scroll checks, KeyProbe (a step keycap) for the keycap's hold, and the help card's shot and its twin moved to the board's check. README, ui-spec, the parity rows and the Lab plan name the board.

title: A key hovers and presses as Swift's keycap, never by a fill
detail: KeycapPress: no face changes colour, plain, tinted or on. A depth of 0 at rest, KeycapStyle.hoverPressFraction (0.25) under the hand and 1 pressed shrinks the face toward scalePressed (0.95) over the black socket and sinks its word and lamp by the small variant's travel (0.525 pt). The pressed plain key, #272727 on the #282828 ground, was invisible; the hover equalled the separator; brighter() turned the accent's and the update's hue. Colour.raised-hover, raised-pressed and on-hover and ButtonStyle.press and lift are gone; the slider's knob keeps its own lifted grey.

title: A heading is Swift's DS.Typo.heading: Inter 24
detail: Type.heading read the box title's Enriqueta 26, which Swift never uses; Swift's Export, Prepare the Roll's steps, a paper profile's name and What's new are all set in DS.Typo.heading, the sans at 24. Type.brand-family, no longer read, is gone.

title: Tips round on the radius scale
detail: A help mark's card rounds at Radius.control, as DSHelpBubble; a control's tooltip, the system's in Swift, takes the scale's smallest round (Radius.track, 6) instead of half a badge's 4.

title: Edit Together's every-way check counts only the frames together and presses past the double-click interval
detail: together_all failed on Windows from its first run (0cd7755, #221) and on the Mac when it ran beside together: a press within the system's double-click interval of the last resets the slider to its base, so whether a drag was a drag hung on the machine's speed, and the column scenario counted B and C, never together, as lagging. Each drag now rests past system::double_click(), swings the other way so every step moves the value (asserted), counts only the frames together, and its twin asserts the frames left out keep their own (a wrong set, A and D without E, fails).

title: Edit Together's zoom check waits for the sheet's render to land
detail: Frames together move on the canvas only when their render lands; together read the frame width after one pump, which the Mac's GPU answers in time and Windows' software adapter (WARP, seconds a render) does not: 'twin: back to fitted' failed there from df870fd (#217). Both double clicks now wait up to 60 s for the width to change, then to come back to fitted.

title: Windows binaries take an 8 MB main-thread stack, as the Mac's
detail: The design-system board (#295) overflowed Windows' 1 MB main-thread stack ('thread main has overflowed its stack' in four runs until #300 split it into pages); Slint builds a window's tree on that thread. .cargo/config.toml links every MSVC binary with /STACK:8388608, the size macOS gives its main thread.

title: One GPU device a process: every graph, kernel and check records on oni_graph::gpu()
detail: Nearly every Windows run since 2026-10-20 lost one or two test binaries (oni-app's lib, graph, fused, stages, senses, branches, swift_checks) to STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION, whatever the commit. Measured on the runner (Microsoft's software adapter, WARP): the graph checks crashed in 4 runs of 15 with every backend, 2 of 15 on DX12 alone, and in none with one test thread; the stages checks 1 of 15 and none. Each check opened a device of its own beside the others. oni_graph::gpu() now opens the high-performance adapter's device once a process, at the adapter's limits with CLEAR_TEXTURE where offered; Graph::new, Graph::with_max_side and oni-app's render::Device::open take it, as do the display kernels' and the interface drawing's checks; the shared-device check now asks the graph to follow that device's limit both above and under it. The app already shared one device (render::door), so its behaviour does not move.

title: Two window checks judge Windows as they judge macOS
detail: missing_original builds its roll under the temp folder's canonical spelling and compares the folder Show the Folder opens as the archive writes it ('/', long names), so Windows' RUNNER~1 and backslashes no longer fail it; editor_leftovers asserts a wheel gesture still held only when its pump came back inside the 0.16 s idle window, a slow runner otherwise failing a correct app.

title: An injected volumes' folder holds its paths in any spelling the system takes
detail: Computer::is_on_volume, is_volume_root and parent, and absence::volume_root, compared the volumes' folder byte for byte, so on Windows a folder handed with '\' (missing_original's) or a path under a short RUNNER~1 temp folder (adding's) lay on no volume and a disk unplugged read as a file deleted. They now go through paths::holds, same and below ('/' or '\', case on a case-blind volume); the drives of a real Windows machine stay drives. The adding check builds its folders under the temp folder's canonical spelling, as missing_original does (an_injected_volumes_folder_is_read_in_any_spelling_on_windows; twin: a sibling named like it and the folder itself lie on no volume).

title: The single-instance check never reads the lock file it holds
detail: a_second_instance_does_not_write snapshotted every support file's bytes, instance.lock included, while its own handle held the lock: Windows refuses a read of a locked range (os error 33). The snapshot keeps the lock file's length and modification date instead of its bytes, so a write to it still fails the check; the app's lock is unchanged and never reads the file.

title: Windows notes a favourite's file index and volume serial number in bookmarks.json
detail: bookmarks::place gave Windows no identity (file_id and volume None), so a_swift_launch_keeps_the_volume_identities failed there. GetFileInformationByHandle on a handle opened with backup semantics (folders included) now gives the 64-bit file index and the volume serial number (kept as uuid, XXXX-XXXX, which a new drive letter keeps), GetVolumePathNameW the mount; the check asserts the volume's identity on Windows as on macOS (windows-sys 0.61, already in the tree).

title: The Windows label scan passes a system identifier
detail: windows_labels_say_explorer_and_ctrl flagged the xattr name com.apple.FinderInfo (oni-library roots/finder.rs) as a Mac word shown to the user; literals starting with com.apple. are identifiers read from the disk, never labels, and a twin keeps one passing while a planted label is still caught.

title: A move supersedes the folder read in flight, so New Roll and its undo keep the photos selected
detail: followed() maps the selection to the moved paths, but a read started before the move (the folder watcher's, after the previous undo) landed after it with the old paths, and lay_grid dropped every pick: after a partial undo the bar said "5 photos" with its keys greyed instead of "3 selected". Lot 17's 50 ms second look at freshly written files (roots::settled) widened that window; under the window suite's load the check failed 4 times in 6, never before lot 17. followed() now bumps the read generation itself (locate.rs did it alone), as Swift's followed keeps the moved selection; told::an_undo_that_cannot_put_every_photo_back_says_how_many asserts A and B picked in the roll and C in Scans after the partial undo, its twin that the set as if every photo came back is told apart.

title: An export never lands on an original
detail: Before anything renders and again at the rename, a destination holding any file ONI did not export (P1.JPG beside P1.NEF, found as P1.jpg where the volume ignores case), a frame's own source or a name the batch gives twice is refused. A ledger in the support folder (Exports.json) vouches for ONI's earlier exports by path, length and modification date, so only they are offered Replace; a clash with anything else offers Rename alone, the Finder's way (P1 2.jpg), and Return renames. The dialog says the originals are not touched only once that has been checked. Closes safety-export-overwrites-other-original.

title: Export and contact-sheet names are portable
detail: One sanitiser, oni_library::file_names::portable, for every typed export name and every sheet name: separators, Windows' refused characters and control characters become '-', trailing dots and spaces go, a device name (CON, NUL, COM1, LPT1…) gains a '-'. The joined path is checked to sit directly in the chosen folder. Closes windows-export-names.

title: Exports and contact sheets are written atomically and say why they failed
detail: Every export and sheet is written to a hidden temporary file beside it, flushed, then renamed: a new file holds its name first (create_new) so one arriving meanwhile is never replaced, an earlier export is swapped whole. A failure keeps the previous file and names its cause: disk full, read-only, not allowed, folder gone. A sheet's free name is taken at the write, not before minutes of decoding. Closes safety-export-not-atomic.

title: A photo whose original cannot be read says why on the canvas, before any decode
detail: Opening a photo checks its original first (oni-library absence: its volume not mounted, moved or deleted with the disk there, EACCES/EPERM, 0 bytes, any other refusal; oni-decode unsupported_format: HEIC, PSD, AVIF; a lead's pass missing beside it). The canvas keeps the cached thumbnail and lays a note in the hand's words with Show the Folder (the nearest folder still there) and Back to the Gallery; no decode is asked, nothing writes '· decoding' over it, the store refuses every hand on a frame out of sight and its sliders take no press. 'could not be decoded' stays for a real decode failure. A lead's missing pass is named by the decode too.

title: A sidecar refused on switching photo keeps the edits and asks
detail: Leaving a frame whose write fails (disk gone, read-only share) keeps its settings in the store's unsaved list instead of dropping them; a sheet asks Retry or Discard, Escape keeps them, a volume coming back retries on its own, reopening the frame shows them, and quitting asks as a failed write does. A retry never writes beside an original out of sight.

title: A move on disk takes the selection with it, as Swift's followed does
detail: followed() moved the index rows, the order and the open frame but left the selection, its anchor and cursor on the old paths, so a photo moved into a New Roll then opened from the gallery opened where it no longer was. EditorScene+Disk.swift:125-137 maps selection and ring too; so does the port now.

title: No sidecar is written beside a missing original
detail: sidecar::original_present guards write and every setter (label, EXIF, roll draft, ONI Trash), so a medal, a trash, a paste, a reset, an undo write-back or a deferred flush never leaves X.NEF.json beside nothing for a later namesake to adopt; the refusal is a typed sidecar::Error::Unreachable, not an io error string. A batch gesture checks the original before reading its sidecar, acts on the present photos and says once "N photos were left out: their originals cannot be found" (oni_library::refusal). A medal journals only the photos it reached.

title: A restore on a disk away changes nothing and says so
detail: set_trashed checks the original before its absent sidecar can read as a fresh, untrashed photo: a Restore or an undone trash on an unplugged disk reports "N photos were not restored: their originals cannot be found", records no step, and library::refreshed keeps a row whose sidecar cannot be seen (original away, sidecar unreadable) instead of clearing its mark, medal and roll.

title: A write never overwrites a newer or unreadable sidecar
detail: write() decodes the sidecar standing at write time: a newer format (written by another app after the photo opened) is refused with sidecar::Error::Newer, an unparseable or unreadable one with its error, and both are said, never rewritten around empty envelope fields. set_label, set_exif and set_roll_draft now return Newer instead of a silent success.

title: A sidecar keeps the keys a newer app added
detail: The format moves its version only for a field whose meaning changes, so a newer Swift adds keys at version 19. A rewrite carries every key of a same-version document this version does not write (oni-settings kept.rs), at the top, in the settings and deeper, unless carrying them changes what this version reads (a retired key would fold twice), in which case none is. Keys inside arrays are not carried.

title: The ONI Trash names every cause of a mark that did not land
detail: trash::Outcome counts refused (newer), unreachable (original missing) and failed sidecars, each failure with its file and cause; report says each cause with its count, names three failed sidecars and counts the rest, instead of hiding io errors behind the refusal and keeping only the last.

title: One spelling per path: composed on macOS, compared by name
detail: exFAT lists `Été` decomposed while its real path is composed, so the navigator's row, the opened folder, the survey's rolls and the favourite star named one folder two ways. paths::normal and canonical compose (NFC) on macOS, where every volume resolves either form to the same file; Windows and Linux keep the disk's bytes, as their disks tell the forms apart. holds, same, below and moved compare and cut by names, never by bytes, so a rename's follow (navigator, favourites, projects, gestures, the opened folder) never slices mid-letter. Favourites and the navigator's remembered rows are respelt on read. Closes names-exfat-nfd-nfc-split and tests-08.

title: A case-only rename outside ONI keeps the favourite
detail: On a volume blind to case (APFS and exFAT by default, NTFS), `roll 8` holds and names what the disk now spells `Roll 8`: holds and same fold case there, each Mac volume asked once through pathconf(_PC_CASE_SENSITIVE), and only when two paths differ by case alone. A star off takes its own spelling first, so two favourites differing by case on a case-sensitive disk never merge. Closes windows-case-only-rename. ASCII paths fold without allocating, as a survey compares thousands.

title: A Windows share or mapped drive has one spelling
detail: canonical reads `\\?\UNC\nas\film` as `//nas/film`, and keeps a mapped or subst drive's letter rather than the share or folder behind it, so a favourite starred as `Z:/Film/Roll 12` holds the photos the survey canonicalises. Presence of a share off the volume list stays with the presence work. Partly closes windows-unc-mapped-canonical.

title: The Finder's order puts Été among the E's
detail: paths::standard_order (paths/order.rs) reads names decomposed: base letters first (æ, œ, ß expanded), then accents, then case, a small letter before its capital, digit runs as numbers, the composed and decomposed spellings of one name equal; ASCII names take an allocation-free pass that orders alike. Closes names-finder-order-accents.

title: The index respells its keys at open and never loses a row
detail: LibraryIndex keys every write in the archive's spelling and names both spellings in each update and delete. At open, one transaction respells rows an earlier build keyed decomposed (or with `\` on Windows); where both spellings hold a row, the respelt one keeps its values and takes what it lacks from its twin. A busy database is respelt at the next open. index.rs's tests moved to index/tests.rs, its ceiling back to 400.

title: One presence model, computed off the interface thread
detail: oni-library presence.rs: Present, Offline (Disconnected, Denied) or Missing, told by absence.rs's reasons (absence::refusal shared, so the canvas and the gallery say the same). roots::surveyed records each refusal's state in Survey.away and reads the roll markers on the survey's thread (Survey.rolls). The interface keeps each photo's state (organising/presence.rs) from the read's survey and from looks on a thread of their own (probe_presence after every read, and for paths a lay meets unknown); lay_grid, lay_archive, navigator_read and the ONI Trash rows read no file any more. presence::on_look lets a check refuse any look on the interface thread. Closes missing-main-thread-stat and its duplicates (model-10, scale-ui-stat-every-photo, parity-disk-stats-on-ui-thread, tests-11, bench-exists-on-ui-thread).

title: A read stopped or a disk leaving mid-read drops no row
detail: read_rows returned the rows of a survey cut short by a newer folder opened as gone: every row not yet walked left the index. A stopped survey now returns before pruning; a root that no longer reads after its walk is counted unreadable; an entry listed then refused leaves its folder unread. Rows under any refused folder, offline or missing, are always kept.

title: The launch keeps the remembered folder whatever its state
detail: open_remembered opens openedFolder as Swift does (EditorScene+Stages.swift:71), never filtered by is_dir nor replaced by roots.json, and reads no disk on the interface thread; the reference roll opens only under ONI_RAW_DIR or a bench. The first volumes listing runs on the volumes thread, the home alone shown until it lands. Closes model-07 and its duplicates, windows-first-launch-fixture.

title: A disk leaving or coming back, answered in one place
detail: volumes_moved (navigator/memory.rs) takes the volumes' thread's listing and the refused folders that answer: a volume gone turns every path under it offline from the paths alone; a volume back clears what was known under it, reads the opened folder again once when it lies there (or was refused and answers), clears tried for its favourites, and writes the kept edits (lot 2's retry). Closes the marking part of scale-unplug-no-refresh.

title: A path named on the command line, dropped or picked is looked at first
detail: add looks at the item on a thread of its own: not there or on a disk away, nothing opens and the status says Not found: …; denied says so; a file at the top of the home or of a volume never opens the whole of it. OPENED_FOLDER is written only by a folder that opens.

title: The thumbnails pass leaves unreachable originals out
detail: fill and redraw skip photos whose original is not present; the pass counts those with no thumbnail kept and says it once. Closes missing-thumbnail-pass-spam.

title: A folder away is laid as it was last seen
detail: kept.rs keeps each opened folder's last whole shape (subfolders, creation dates, roll markers) under the caches' Surveys folder; a survey whose folder the disk refuses wears it, so roll headings and empty folders stay. The ONI Trash reads only its rows (index.in_trash), a roll marker written by the app is laid without being read back, the Survey is shared by Arc across landings. Closes missing-unreadable-roll-loses-rolls and the disk part of scale-ui-lay-archive-disk.

title: A gesture's failure is told wherever the hand is
detail: One notice for every gesture that fails or lands in part, over the gallery, the organiser and the editor alike: the design system's Toast (containers.slint), laid low over the window, gone after SheetStyle.linger (held while hovered), by its OK key or by Escape, an optional action key beside it; told.slint's Told global, app/gestures/told.rs. gesture_as titles it with the gesture as Swift's reportFailure (Move to ONI Trash, Restore, Undo, Redo, Reset to Default, New Roll); the medal's refusals, the projects', favourites' and roll marker's saves, the index that cannot open and a folder handed over that cannot open use it too, never the editor's status line the gallery hides. A success says nothing. Closes ux-gallery-errors-invisible and parity-gallery-failures-invisible.

title: An undo or redo of a roll that cannot move every item says how many
detail: The store's take_back keeps roll_folder's moves (Walked: the moves made, the folder holding what stayed) and says Swift's sentence, plural-aware: "2 of the items could not be put back: their folder moved or a file took their name."; a redo says its own. The notice carries Show in Finder on the roll folder left behind, and the gallery follows the moves the disk made rather than guessing them from what exists. Closes missing-undo-partial-silent, safety-undo-partial-silent, parity-undo-disk-shortfall-unreported and tests-04.

title: New Folder, Back to a Folder, Make a Roll, Rename and Show in Finder say why they failed
detail: refusal::cause words the disk's common refusals (not there, cannot be written to, name taken, read-only, full, name refused). New Folder Inside and Back to a Folder, silent before, tell their refusal; Make a Roll and Rename name the cause, never a raw os error. Show in Finder looks off the interface thread: a folder gone shows the nearest folder still there and says so, a disk away or a refused folder says why. Closes ux-silent-folder-ops, missing-small-silent-failures (its messages), safety-silent-folder-failures and bench-reveal-missing-silent.

title: A folder name holding a separator or starting with a dot is refused with its reason
detail: file_names::refused, read by every folder rename (navigator, archive tree, band heading): "/" (and "\\" on Windows) would move the folder, a leading dot would hide it; on Windows its refused characters, a trailing dot or space and the device names too. The reason is told instead of the old name coming back without a word. Closes names-slash-in-rename-silent.

title: The navigator's reveal reads no disk on the interface thread
detail: navigator_reveal takes the folder as adding.rs's looked already made it canonical off the interface thread, instead of resolving it again on it. Lot 4's leftover.

title: Windows reads a RAW by a handle Rust opened: any folder name, any path length, the file left free to rename
detail: LibRaw's char* open goes through the ANSI code page and MAX_PATH and denies FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so an accented or long path failed and a rename during the thumbnails pass was refused. On Windows the decode, the preview and identify now hand LibRaw a stream (csrc/stream.cpp, LibRaw's own FILE* stream over a handle std opened, shared for delete); macOS and Linux keep libraw_open_file, unchanged. Every pinned knob is set before either open. Checks a_dng_in_an_ete_folder_decodes (a mosaic DNG built in the check, in 'Été 🎞' and past 260 characters; twin: the name route fails there on Windows), the_handle_route_decodes_bit_for_bit_as_the_name_route (full and half size, preview, identify; twin: 1.007 gain differs), a_file_being_read_renames (Windows; twin: a handle without share-delete refuses). The fixture's decode hashes identically before and after the change on macOS.

title: Thumbnail names are portable: a dated photo keeps its tile on Windows, and Swift's tiles still read on macOS
detail: file_name escapes every byte outside letters, digits, '-', '.' and the space as '_' and its hex, so an EXIF date's ':' (refused by NTFS and exFAT) never reaches a name. Where the system allows it, Swift's colon name is still read (the newer of the two wins), a persist removes it and forget removes both, so no tile is lost and none shows stale. Check a_dated_fingerprint_persists_on_every_platform; twin: Swift's name contains ':'.

title: Explorer gets backslashes, a share keeps its two slashes, and thumbnails leave the roaming profile
detail: reveal and show_folder hand explorer.exe the path with backslashes and no \\?\ prefix (reveal_hands_explorer_backslashes; twin: the archive spelling holds '/'). suggested() keeps //server/share as one root (a_former_library_on_a_share_is_offered_on_that_share; twin: a one-slash path never becomes a share). On Windows the Thumbnails folder sits under LOCALAPPDATA when the support folder is the roaming default (windows_keeps_rebuildable_files_off_the_roaming_profile; twin: a check's own folder and other systems keep it).

title: A favourite or a folder out of reach fades with its state in words, and a click shows it in the gallery
detail: The navigator's rows read row_presence: offline or missing, the title and glyph fade, a mark (a disc struck through, a caution, a question) and a caption say it ("T7 not connected", "Not found", "Access denied"), a tooltip says where, and no chevron promises a folder inside. A click opens the folder in the gallery instead of waiting on a listing that never answers. Its menu keeps Open and the favourite, greys Rename, the roll and New Folder Inside, and offers Show the Parent Folder; the archive tree's folder menu greys the same inside an opened folder out of reach. The base out of reach or holding no folder says so in the column; the welcome shows a former folder on a disk away without offering it (a_favourite_moved_away_on_the_home_fades_and_its_menu_greys; twin: a favourite there stays whole, its menu whole). With no volumes' folder known (Computer::none, every check's default), no path is on a volume, so the home's folders never read offline (twin in navigator/tests.rs).

title: The ONI Trash stands in every view of the navigator
detail: Owner's decision D5: the trash's rows sit under the folders in Favourites, a base and Computer alike, published from the launch; No Favourites lies in the column above it rather than over it.

title: An opened folder out of reach is said by a banner over its kept tiles, never as an empty folder
detail: A design-system Banner (Raised, its state's glyph, a title, words, keys) stands over the grid while the opened folder is offline or missing: "T7 Not Connected" with the last thumbnails kept, "No Access", or "Folder Not Found" with Remove from Favourites; the empty state says nothing then, and "No Photos" stays for a folder there and empty. The status bar adds "N originals missing". Shown on the board's Notices (an_opened_folder_gone_is_not_an_empty_folder; twin: a real empty folder says No Photos and shows no banner).

title: A missing original's tile greys its picture alone, as Swift's faded layer
detail: TileLayers' faded layer: the thumbnail greyed to its luma in Rust (kept per buffer, made again once redrawn) and faded on the picture alone, the well, medal, seal, ring and rounded corners whole, in the gallery and the tree's thumbnails; a corner disc marks its state and the tooltip says where it was. A frame left out of the roll keeps the whole tile's fade (left-out) (a_missing_tile_is_grey_on_its_own_layer, twin of galleryCellSelfCheck's faded layer; twins: the photo there keeps its colour, and its picture is drawn otherwise while the medal and the corner are drawn alike).

title: The cell menu on missing originals counts them first and leaves them out of every write
detail: A greyed "N photos missing" line opens the menu; Paste, Reset, Reset to Default, the medals, New Roll, Ungroup and the ONI Trash act on the photos there, are greyed when none is, and say once how many they left out; projects still name every photo, Export and Show in Finder kept to the present ones. The cell menu moved to organise/cells.rs, so organise.rs leaves its grandfathered ceiling.

title: A triplet with a pass gone wears the seal that names it
detail: The presence looks behind the interface read each lead's passes from its sidecar: one gone turns the lead's seal to the destructive foil reading "R MISSING" (G, B), its tooltip naming the file; back beside it, the RGB seal returns (a_triplet_with_a_pass_gone_is_marked; twin: the whole triplet keeps its plain seal).

title: The ONI Trash is the whole library's: a photo trashed in one folder is listed and restored from any other, one on a disk away says so
detail: read_trashed reads every trashed row of the index (LibraryIndex::trashed_frames, Swift's trashed(index.all()) without reading the whole index: a pass whose lead the index holds is left to its lead), whichever folder is open or none; the launch counts it before any folder opens. A photo on a disk away tiles as offline in the trash; Restore and Restore All restore what they reach and the notice says how many stayed and why, nothing written where the disk was. Check a_trash_made_in_a_lists_after_b_opens_and_restore_all_restores_it; twin: the same trash cut to the opened folder reads empty, and the disk back, the same key restores in silence. OniTrash twin the_trash_lists_a_triplet_once_whichever_folder_holds_it; twin: cut on the trashed rows alone, a restored triplet leaves its passes in the trash.

title: A project lists its members from the whole library, whatever folder is open; a member gone shows as missing, a trashed one stays hidden
detail: project_standing::standing reads, per member, the index row at its recorded path or of its fingerprint beyond the opened folder's rows (Swift's checkProjectPhotos), and lays a member no row holds at its recorded path; State::reach is what every project listing and gesture resolves against (bands, tree, info, New/Add/Remove, drops, save). A trashed member is hidden and kept a member; a member whose original is gone tiles as missing. Checks a_project_from_a_still_lists_after_b_opens and a_project_resolves_beyond_the_opened_folder_and_never_shows_its_trashed_member; twin: resolved against the opened folder's rows alone, the project lists nothing.

title: A rename or a move carries every recorded path: the projects' paths, the selection, the rings and the folds
detail: followed (now gestures/disk.rs with New Roll, gestures.rs split under its ceiling) moves the index rows, the rows held, the projects' members beyond the folder and the trash's rows, the selection, the anchor and the cursor, both trees' picks, the projects' ring and every folder a hand folded (Archive::folded, which every relay of the archive now keeps at any depth, not only the top rows), then runs project::moved and saves projects.json when a project records paths, as Swift's followed. Check a_rename_moves_the_projects_recorded_path; twin: a rename of another folder leaves the recorded path where it was, and an open folder stays open.

title: Favourites are read again and merged before each save, and each favourite's volume is kept in a Rust-only file
detail: Favourites::save_merged lays this app's changes since the last read (stars added, stars taken off, renames followed) over favourites.json as it stands, so a favourite the Swift app added or removed meanwhile stays so; the file keeps Swift's {version, paths} shape (a_favourite_added_by_another_app_survives_our_save; twin: the whole save from memory loses it). bookmarks.json, which Swift never reads, keeps each favourite's volume (UUID and mount on macOS) and file id by path, noted off the interface thread; a disk away or another volume under the same path never erases the identity known (a_swift_launch_keeps_the_volume_identities; twin: the same identity inside favourites.json is gone after Swift's launch).

title: Projects are merged with projects.json as it stands before each save
detail: merge::save_projects reads projects.json again and merges by id: a project another app added survives, one this app deleted stays deleted, one the other deleted stays deleted unless edited here; name, description, order and members merge field by field, so a member added in Swift survives a rename in ONI; the member paths a save writes down are no edit (a_project_added_by_another_app_survives_our_save; twin: the plain save drops it; a_project_the_other_app_deleted_survives_an_edit_here).

title: A damaged preferences.json is set aside whole and the known keys go on, written atomically
detail: Preferences::set no longer rewrites an unparsable file with the one key: the file is renamed preferences.json.unreadable-<stamp> and the keys this holder knows are written with the new one; a file the disk refuses to read is never replaced; the write goes through oni_library::write_atomically (unique temporary, fsync, cleanup) instead of a fixed .part (a_damaged_preferences_file_is_kept_aside_not_lost; twins: a readable file is never set aside, a refused one is left as it was).

title: Moving a photo out across volumes syncs the copy, compares it byte for byte, then trashes the original
detail: flat_fields::move_out across volumes copies into a new file, syncs it and its folder, reads both back and compares them whole, and only then sends the original to the system Trash; a short or altered copy is removed and the original, its sidecar and its row stay. The sidecar goes to the Trash instead of being deleted, through the app's discard, so a check's Trash is its own. The moves are injectable (Moving). The dead library::move_out and its test are gone (a_move_across_volumes_syncs_checks_then_trashes_the_source; twin: a short copy, or one with a byte changed, keeps the original).

title: One app at a time on a support folder: a second launch says so and writes nothing
detail: main takes an exclusive lock on <support>/instance.lock (std File::try_lock, released by the system when the process ends, a crash included) before any write, the log included. A second launch prints why on stderr, shows the system's alert when launched by hand, and exits with code 2 (a_second_instance_does_not_write, which launches the real binary on its own folders; twin: once the lock is let go the same launch goes on and writes its log).

title: The index waits for the Swift app's writes and never drops its table on a version it cannot read
detail: LibraryIndex::open sets a 5 s busy timeout explicitly (the Swift app shares index.sqlite and sets none); prepare_schema treats an unreadable user_version as an error instead of -1, which dropped the table (a_write_waits_for_the_other_apps_write, with an integrity check; twin: a connection with no busy handler, as Swift opens it, is refused at once).

title: New Roll asks first, names the folder it makes and counts the files it moves; photos of two folders are refused with the reason
detail: The plan is laid off the interface's thread (roll_folder::plan: the dated folder's name, each frame, every file it carries), then the confirm says “ONI makes the folder “2026-10-24” in “Scans” and moves 4 files into it…”, its key MOVE 2 PHOTOS; Cancel moves nothing. roll_folder::one_folder refuses a selection spread over several folders before anything is asked, so a roll is always made inside its photos' own folder and never crosses a disk (a_new_roll_asks_names_the_folder_and_counts_files, window; twins: two folders refused with no folder made, Cancel leaves every file in place; new_roll_takes_the_photos_of_one_folder_only).

title: A frame moves whole or not at all: its passes, its RAW+JPEG pair, its sidecars and other apps' never split, never replace a file
detail: roll_folder::carry moves each unit (an RGB triplet, a RAW with its same-stem JPEG, each photo with its .json and the .xmp/.pp3/.dop/.on1 kept by other apps, a RAW's <stem>.xmp) once every place is free, through an injectable rename; a refusal halfway moves back what already moved and names the frame and the cause. rename_new never replaces (renamex_np RENAME_EXCL on macOS, a look first where the volume refuses the flag or elsewhere). A stray sidecar at the destination is a taken name: planned past it, refused when the place is fixed, never overwritten. A cross-volume rename is said as “it lies on another disk” (a_triplet_moves_whole_or_not_at_all with a locked green pass; a_stray_sidecar_at_the_destination_is_a_taken_name, twin: the plain rename replaces it; a_raw_takes_its_jpeg_and_the_sidecars_of_other_apps; rename_new_never_replaces_a_file).

title: Undo of New Roll removes its folder on exFAT; a redo into a folder made meanwhile is refused and its step kept
detail: remove_if_left counts macOS's ._ twins, .DS_Store and Thumbs.db as leftovers, removes them with this roll's own marker, then the folder with remove_dir only; a marker of another roll keeps the folder. lay refuses a folder of the roll's name it did not make (no marker of this roll): nothing moves, no marker is written, the notice says why and GalleryHistory::give_back offers the redo again; the roll's own folder left by an undo is taken again (undo_on_exfat_removes_the_folder_and_its_appledouble on an hdiutil exFAT image, twin: the literal marker-only check finds the folder not empty; redo_into_a_folder_made_meanwhile_is_refused, twin: the roll's own folder takes the photo again).

title: Move to ONI Trash, Restore and the undo or redo of a roll's moves run off the interface's thread
detail: Ctl::on_disk runs one gesture's writes or moves at a time on a thread, its name on the status bar, and lands the outcome back (rows, notice, followed moves). EditorStore splits the mark (mark_begun closes a trashed open frame before, mark_run off the thread, mark_landed records the step) and hands a disk step to the host as a Walk. While one runs, every other gesture, a medal and opening the editor are refused and said; a quit waits for it (wait_for_disk), so no frame is cut halfway. The window checks wait on disk_busy (Rig::landed, Rig::roll_confirmed).

title: A roll's reference reaches its own folder: a copy of the roll beside it is never reset nor written
detail: roll_membership::beside bounds reset_reach to the folders of the photos picked, and measured_with to the open frame's folder, so Reset to Default, Paste to Roll, Roll Settings and Roll of the N leave a Finder copy or a backup naming the same RollReference untouched (a_copy_of_a_roll_beside_it_is_out_of_reach; twin: a pick in both folders reaches both).

title: Locate… follows a folder gone to the folder picked, once its photos are recognised there
detail: A Missing favourite or folder carries Locate… in its menu and on the banner. The folder picker (Options.picker) chooses; each indexed row is stamped at its place under the new folder off the interface thread (relink::recognised). With one recognised the folder follows at once and a notice says "N photos of M recognised"; with none a sheet asks first. Following runs one path for a rename in ONI and a Locate (follow_folder): Navigation::follow, Favourites::follow (now kept once when it lands on a favourite already there), the opened folder and its preference, then followed() for the index rows, picks, folds and projects' recorded paths. A row whose new place holds another file is dropped so that file is stamped afresh; a folder back meanwhile is never followed away. Writes only the app's own files (locate_follows_favourite_rows_and_projects; twin: a folder sharing no photo asks and Cancel changes nothing).

title: A disk remounted under another name, or a favourite renamed in the Finder, is offered on the banner and never followed by itself
detail: bookmarks::Identify names a path's volume (statfs and getattrlist in the app, a check's own through Options.identify) and records places with it. Bookmarks::lead finds, off the interface thread, the volume known by its UUID mounted under another name ("T7" as "T7 1") or the favourite's file id on the same volume (beside it, else /.vol by id on macOS), never in a Trash. The banner says "“T7” seems to have become “T7 1”." or "It seems to have become “…”." with FOLLOW, which runs Locate's fingerprint check on the whole volume or the favourite; only the favourites still held lead (a_t7_remounted_as_t7_1_is_offered_to_follow; twin: another disk under the new name is offered nothing; bookmarks unit checks with a twin each).

title: Remove from Library… forgets a folder gone, never one offline, and touches no file
detail: Only a Missing folder carries it, in its menu and on the banner when rows remain. A sheet says "ONI forgets the N photos indexed under …. No file is touched"; the folder is looked at again off the interface thread and only one still gone is forgotten. LibraryIndex::forget takes its rows in one transaction; thumbnails go only when no other row claims their fingerprint; the favourites and folds under it and its kept shape go; sidecars, originals and projects stay. Nothing is forgotten on its own and a disk away keeps its rows forever (forget_touches_no_file: listing byte for byte identical; twins: a touched sidecar is seen, a folder offline is offered no Remove from Library).

title: A photo or a folder another app adds, removes or renames under the opened folder shows by itself
