detail: oni-library watching: the notify crate (FSEvents on macOS, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows) watches the opened folder whole and the navigator's base and unfolded rows a level down, on a thread of its own; a burst is told once the disk is quiet for 500 ms (3 s at most), so a copy of 300 files is one read; sidecars, hidden files and tags count for nothing; never a volume, the home or a folder holding either. The opened folder is read again (once more if the read was running), a listed folder listed again (a_file_dropped_in_the_opened_folder_appears, twin: a folder not opened is not read once the disk has spoken of it; three_hundred_photos_copied_are_told_in_one_or_two_calls; a_burst_waits_for_the_disk_to_quiet, twin: no quiet is 300 calls; neither_a_disk_nor_the_home_is_ever_watched). The watches are made again when a disk comes back and on Refresh, as a watch on a folder away is dropped (a_watch_comes_back_with_its_disk, twin: unwatched, the same drop shows nothing). The checks that take an original away to show a missing tile (missing_original, visible, presence, canvas_switch) turn the watch off, since a watched folder now drops the row.

title: The window's return looks at the opened folder again
detail: Going to the back keeps the opened folder's listing (names only, off the interface thread); coming back lists it again and reads it again only when a photo or a folder moved, else only looks at its photos (probe_presence). It covers disks whose changes no event tells, as a network share (focus_rereads_the_opened_folder, twin: nothing moved reads nothing).

title: Recheck Originals and Read the Folders Again become one Refresh, ⌘R, that says what moved
detail: Refresh reads the opened folder, every favourite (as Swift's rescanAll) and every navigator listing again, then says through the notice: Nothing changed, or N photos added, N no longer in the folder, N cannot be found. Dark while a read runs; the tree's reload asks it too (refresh_says_what_changed, twin: nothing moved says so). Parity rows updated.

title: The volumes' probe never waits on a drive or a mount that sleeps
detail: Computer::computer looks at each Windows drive letter and each /Volumes mount's realpath on a thread of its own, 400 ms at most: one that does not answer gives its last answer and is not asked again until its look lands, so an offline mapped drive or a dead network mount never holds the volumes' thread (a_mount_that_hangs_is_left_out_and_asked_once_until_it_answers, twin: the same mount answering is listed).

title: A disk back within the session, and a rename changing only a letter's case
detail: a_disk_back_reopens_the_opened_folder: unplugged and plugged back in one session, the opened folder lists the photo added meanwhile, read once (twin: another disk arriving reads nothing). a_rename_changing_only_case_renames_and_a_true_collision_is_refused (twin: another folder's name is refused).

title: A favourite is a bookmark: no tree read to draw its icons
detail: Owner's decision D3 (model-02). A star reads nothing more: the navigator no longer surveys each favourite's whole tree (Surveys, Area, favourites::read and the pass over them are gone). A row's roll icon comes from its own listing, one look at its .oni-roll.json, which covers every listed folder and not only those under a favourite; favourites.json keeps Swift's {version, paths}.

title: A row stuck in its disk never holds the other rows' listings
detail: parity-stuck-favourite-read. favourites::read_apart reads each listed folder on a thread of its own, at most four counted at once; a read held past 250 ms stops counting, so a starred folder on a NAS asleep lets every other row land. The navigator lists its rows through it (a_stuck_favourite_does_not_block_the_others, twin: a pool that waits for every read it started holds the others).

title: The index forgets the rows of files gone, and the thumbnails no row claims are swept
detail: scale-index-never-forgets (pruning) and scale-thumbnail-no-sweep. Once a launch, after the first read and off the interface thread (library::tidy): a row whose file is gone from a folder the boot disk still lists, or whose folder is gone under one that lists, is taken out in one transaction, each path looked at again inside it; a row on a volume, a share or a drive other than the home's is left to its folder's own read, so a disk away, another disk under its name or a reused drive letter keeps every row; the opened folder and the favourites keep theirs for Locate and Forget. Then, on an index a day old, Thumbnails/ files no row claims are removed, none newer than 10 minutes, 5,000 at most (a_dead_row_on_a_present_disk_is_pruned_and_one_away_is_kept, twin: a volume not known as one loses its rows; a_thumbnail_no_row_claims_is_swept, twins: a fresh or claimed tile stays; a_launch_prunes_the_dead_rows_and_sweeps_only_on_a_settled_index).

title: Thumbnails are written atomically and two copies of one file keep a tile each
detail: safety-helpers-bypass-atomic-write (thumbnails) and names-duplicate-copies-shared (thumbnail key). persist goes through write_atomically (its own temporary name, fsync, cleanup); the sweep removes the halves a cut write left. A fingerprint two index rows hold names its tile with the path too (thumbnails::key), so an edit on one copy never shows on the other's tile; a print held once keeps Swift's name (two_copies_of_one_file_keep_a_tile_each).

title: A photo rewritten at the same size, or a sidecar edited by another app, is read again
detail: missing-stale-under-outside-changes and tests-12. A stamps table beside photos, which the Swift app never reads, keeps each row's size, modification date and sidecar date. A read compares them with the survey's own look: a new date on the original stamps it again and reads it whole when its print moved, a sidecar changed or gone has its envelope read again; both after the first landing. A row older than its stamp takes the disk's word once (a_photo_replaced_by_another_size_or_mtime_is_read_again, twin: a rewrite with its date put back is not seen; a_sidecar_edited_by_another_app_is_read_again, same twin).

title: An unreadable file gets no fingerprint, and a cloud placeholder is never downloaded to index it
detail: missing-unreadable-fingerprint-collision and windows-cloud-placeholders. relink::stamp gives None when the file or a block refuses a read, so unreadable files of one size never share a print and a tile, and when the bytes live in the cloud (SF_DATALESS on macOS, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS, RECALL_ON_OPEN or OFFLINE on Windows): such a photo stays a waiting tile, told 'In the cloud: opening it downloads it' (an_unreadable_file_gets_no_fingerprint, twin: readable again, each gets its own).

title: The camera search no longer holds the thumbnails, and seen.json forgets files gone
detail: scale-transition-scan-blocks-thumbnails. The thumbnails' pass is held only while a camera is matched, not during the search; a frame drawn before its camera's match is drawn again once matched, as before. seen.json drops a file gone from a root read whole and keeps one under a folder refused or a root away (a_file_gone_leaves_the_list_and_one_on_a_disk_away_stays).

title: Re-reading rows is linear and in one transaction; the walks lose a realpath per entry
detail: scale-reread-quadratic and scale-walk-costs. library::refresh finds each row by its key and writes them all in one transaction (upsert_all) instead of a linear search and an fsync each. The survey resolves its root once and joins each child's name, a link never being followed; the navigator's listing leaves files out by the listing's own type and looks only at folders; the read queue is a VecDeque.

title: The gallery's undo history is bounded in bytes too
detail: scale-history-unbounded-bytes. Beside its hundred steps, GalleryHistory holds at most 256 MB of settings, as their JSON weighs them; the oldest steps go first and the newest stays whatever its size (the_stack_keeps_its_steps_under_a_ceiling_of_bytes, twin: counted by steps alone every gesture is kept).

title: An unreadable favourites or projects file is never replaced
detail: Data loss found by lot 15. favourites.json or projects.json that the disk refuses (access denied, a disk error) read as never written, so the launch re-seeded the favourites from roots.json and the first project gesture saved an empty list over the user's file. Favourites::save and project::save now go through replace_readable: a file that exists and cannot be read is kept as it is and the save refused and said; a file that does not parse is still set aside by read_json; a missing one is made (an_unreadable_favourites_file_is_never_replaced, an_unreadable_projects_file_is_never_replaced, chmod 000 and skipped under root; twin: a missing file is created). The thumbnails pass and the camera search also leave a cloud placeholder unread.

title: A click opens a folder, the chevron alone folds, a late listing opens nothing (D4)
detail: ux-click-semantics, model-06, bench-delayed-open-race: Navigation::click opens any folder on the first click, whatever it holds, and the second of a double click opens nothing more; the navigator's rows take the chevron's zone as the tree's do (Row.folds), wired to row-folded. The `deciding` set, Clicked::Read and Landed::Open are gone, so no listing lands as an open. The grid's empty state says click. Checks a_click_opens_and_the_chevron_folds and a_late_listing_never_opens_over_a_newer_open, each with its twin; the navigator's window check walks the new gestures.

title: Renaming is by the menu or Return, never by a double click; the arrows walk the navigator
detail: ux-click-semantics, ux-no-keyboard-in-columns: the archive tree's double click on a folder no longer types over its name. A click on a navigator row gives the rows the keys until a click on the grid: ↑ ↓ walk the pick, → ← unfold and fold (← on a folded row climbs to its parent's), Space folds, Return renames as in the Finder's sidebar, ⌘↓ opens, ⌘↑ is Parent. Return keeps D4's meaning (rename), so opening is ⌘↓. Check return_renames_and_double_click_does_not (twin: once the grid is clicked, Return opens the photo); library_column's and the navigator's checks keep their intent through the menu.

title: Add means star and open everywhere; Open Folder… opens alone; ADD ADD fixed (D7)
detail: ux-add-means-open, model-08: the welcome's ADD {name} and ADD FOLDER…, the catch-up's ADD and its ADD FOLDER…, and the toolbar's ADD FOLDER… (Act.add-folder) star the folder, then open it; Open Folder… (⌘O), a drop and the command line open without starring. The welcome key no longer prefixes ADD to a title that holds it (ADD ADD SCANS).

title: One folder menu for the navigator and the tree; New Folder named where it was asked
detail: ux-folder-menus-differ: State::folder_lines builds Open, Add to/Remove from Favourites, Locate… when gone, Rename…, Make a Roll / Back to a Folder, New Folder Inside, Show in Finder (or the parent's) and Remove from Library…, with the same presence rules, for both columns; folder_acted runs them, renaming in the column asked from. New Folder Inside from the tree now types over the new row in the tree (rename_request). tree_hand's check expects the shared menu.

title: The gallery's bar and menus act on the selection alone, never on the photo opened last
detail: ux-invisible-target: Ctl::targets, State::target_count (bar and menus alike) and export_now fall back on the open photo beside it only; in the gallery an empty selection reaches nothing, so Trash, Reset, Paste, Prepare and Export go dark. The Trash key's help counts (Move 3 Photos to ONI Trash). Check the_gallery_bar_acts_on_the_selection_only (twin: a photo picked is the one trashed).

title: Add to Project asks before taking photos from another project, and an emptied project stays
detail: ux-add-to-project-moves: project::leave and remove_from no longer drop a project left empty (name and description kept, Delete Project still asks); project::leaving names each project a photo would leave, and the menu's Add to Project asks 'Move to “Print”?' before such a move. Check adding_to_a_project_never_drops_another_silently, its twin the old rule losing the project.

title: The home or a whole disk asks before it is read whole; a drop says what it refused or left out
detail: ux-wide-open, critic 2: a click or Open on the home, a volume's top or `/` unfolds the row and asks 'Show Every Photo on “T7”?'; a drop or the picker's choice of one asks alike (Added::Open.wide). A drop under a sheet, the export or a roll being prepared says 'Go back to the gallery to open these files.'; from the editor the gallery comes back for it. Items outside the opened folder are counted and said ('2 items from other folders were left out…'), and a dropped photo opens in the editor only from inside that folder. Pending::Run carries a confirmed gesture. Checks a_drop_from_two_folders_says_what_it_left (window) and its unit twin in adding.rs; gallery_leftovers' drop check updated.

title: Names: the system's words for standard folders, a trail for two favourites alike, middle elision
detail: names-localized-standard-folders, ux-favourite-names-ambiguous (+ names-favourites-same-name, bench-favourites-same-name), names-long-names-elided-at-end: Computer::name words the home's Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Movies (Videos on Windows), Music and Pictures in the reader's language (Images in French), from the path alone, rows and pill alike; navigator::trails gives two favourites named alike the folders above them as the row's trail; split_end cuts a long title so its head elides and its last eight characters stay (Row.head/tail, FolderLine and TreeRow).

title: Wording: the Forget sheet without 'indexed', Open the ONI Trash, Undo on a favourite removed, Explorer and Ctrl on Windows
detail: ux-wording-polish: the Forget sheet says 'the photos it knows in'; the No Favourites state says 'ready to open'; Open on a trash folder's row reads Open the ONI Trash; taking a favourite away says so with UNDO, which stars it again; Show in Finder reads Show in Explorer on Windows in the folder menus, the tree, the trash rows and the notices (reveal_word); the toolbar's shortcuts read Bar.command, Ctrl+ and Ctrl+Shift+ on Windows. The cell menu's Show in Finder and the Help's Reveal Log stay for lot 18.

title: scripts/check says which checks skipped and why
detail: Every binary runs with --show-output, and the window runner forwards a passing check's skip lines under libtest's header, so the script reads each SKIPPED or 'not exercised' line with its check's name. It lists them under === SKIPPED and prints one summary line, SKIPPED N checks: n no ONI_RAW_DIR, n no GPU..., on its own line before the unchanged 'N binaries, M failed' line. The roll8 checks name themselves in their skip line (roll #8 rebuild, trash, membership...). Closes the silent-skip half of tests-10.

title: The roll #8 archive proofs that hold on any roll run on one the checks make
detail: oni-library trash/round_trip.rs: the mark rides in the sidecar alone (date, settings and EXIF round-trip, the original untouched by a byte, a later write keeps it, the key itself goes on restore; twins: a write without the read-back loses it, a file moved away is seen), a newer sidecar is left byte for byte and said (twin: one of this version is marked), a triplet goes and comes back whole (twin: unexpanded, the lead alone), every listing leaves it out and a project keeps it a member. made_roll.rs: the index rebuilt from the sidecars, the marker's roll and heading, a disk away inventing no row, and the roll membership by reference, each with roll8's twins. The newer-sidecar proof leaves roll8.rs. oni-core roll8's copies get a placeholder per NEF, as no sidecar is written beside a missing original since #390. Parity row #60 now rests on proofs that always run. Closes tests-10.

title: A folder the disk refuses is neither empty nor gone
detail: oni-library tests/refused_folders.rs (unix, skipped under root): a folder at mode 000 lists None in the navigator, is unreadable and Offline(Denied) in the survey, its photo Denied, the folder itself present. Twins: a readable empty folder says empty, a folder gone is Missing, the same folder opened again lists its subfolder and photo. Shown to fail with children() reading a refusal as empty. Closes tests-07's navigator and survey part; the favourites read is reported, not changed (favourites.rs is lot 13's).

title: The two blind trash twins can fail
detail: system::trash's guard takes the platform call injected (guarded): a missing file never reaches it, an existing one reaches it once and its answer comes back, on every platform. oni-core roll8's trash check compares every sidecar but the marked one, every original, and the settings read before against those after (twins: an original moved is seen). Shown to fail: a guard refusing everything, a mark that renames its original, a mark that rewrites the settings (on a stand-in roll under ONI_RAW_DIR). Closes tests-14.

title: Rust twins of OniTrash.selfCheck, OniTrash.wiringCheck, GalleryHistory.selfCheck and galleryCellSelfCheck
detail: oni-core tests/oni_trash.rs: a triplet's lead moved to the ONI Trash through the store marks its three files, one undo restores them, redo marks again, a restore from a pass brings all three back, the settings and originals untouched. oni-core tests/gallery_steps.rs: every batch gesture of the store reaches a gallery record through any chain of its own methods (twin: with the record calls taken out every gesture is named). oni-library tests/trash_wiring.rs: Move to ONI Trash asks no dialog and lays its step, the opened ONI Trash selects into its own set and a tile opens nothing, a trash row restores under the hover and has no star (each with its adverse twin). oni-app window gallery_cell.rs: a tile's pick, medal and picture, and a slot re-filled for another folder's photo of the same name keeping nothing of it (shown to fail with the cell comparison ignoring its marks). Closes parity-checks-twins-incomplete.

title: The file system's parity rows say what the code does
detail: archive.md: Favourites partial (the empty view promises indexing; a refused favourites.json is reseeded and replaced); rows added for a disk leaving or coming back (done), an unreadable member waiting for Refresh (partial), and port-only rows for Locate…, Remove from Library…, other apps' changes, the instance lock and the files merged with Swift's; the checks of the rename, trash, project and missing-tile rows point at today's tests; window checks cited at their tests/window path. checks.md: #20 and #61 partial with their gaps named, #60, #84 and #120 cite their new twins. README counts recounted: editor 147 of 153 with a check, archive 98 / 7 / 0 and 104 of 105, all 441 / 26 / 7 and 450 of 474; checks 104 twin, 36 partial, 9 none, 12 blocked. Closes parity-doc-archive-wrong-done.

title: app.rs back under its ceiling after the explorer and index merges
detail: Lots 13 and 14 each added a line to crates/oni-app/src/app.rs, taking it to 520 against its 519 ceiling; two oni_settings imports share one line, so the file is back at 519 without raising the ceiling.

title: Packages are told by the system, and a dropped one opens nothing
detail: roots/finder.rs: is_package asks CoreFoundation (kCFURLIsPackageKey) on macOS, which knows the bundle bit (the Photo Booth library, no extension) and each installed app's declared extensions (a .lrlibrary no app declares lists as the folder it is); the extension list stays the answer on Windows or when the query fails. package_holding refuses a package, or a photo inside one, handed by a drop, the picker or the command line (Added::Package, said in words). Checks: roots/tests.rs photo_booth_library_is_a_package (twin: the folder without its bundle bit is listed), archive_view/adding.rs a_dropped_package_opens_nothing (twin: a folder beside it opens). Closes names-packages-by-extension.

title: A format no reader of ONI takes is listed with its seal
detail: Decision: listed as the Finder lists it rather than hidden, so a folder of iPhone HEICs never reads as empty and moves keep it with its roll. oni-decode PLAIN_EXTENSIONS and named_decodable are the one table of what the image reader takes; the presence probe looks at the files their name leaves in doubt (unsupported_format) off the interface thread; tile_marks seals the tile with its format (HEIC) in the destructive foil and says "Format not supported (HEIC)" under the pointer; the thumbnail pass never tries it and says nothing. Lot 2 already says it on the canvas. Checks: oni-decode tests.rs every_plain_extension_has_its_reader_compiled_in (twin: avif, HEIC and psd are not), window gallery_cell a_raw_jpeg_pair_is_one_tile_and_a_heic_is_sealed. Closes the listing part of names-unsupported-formats-listed.

title: CR3, RAF, HEIF and PNG carry their capture date
detail: exif.rs moves to oni-settings (oni_library::exif re-exports it) with exif/containers.rs: a RAF's embedded JPEG (offset at 84), a CR3's CMT2 box under Canon's uuid (its first directory the EXIF IFD), a HEIF or AVIF's Exif item (iinf then iloc), a PNG's eXIf chunk. DateTimeOriginal only, as ImageIO's fingerprint text reads it, so both apps' prints match; LibRaw is not opened for it. A photo with no import date in its sidecar now sorts by its file's modification date, never by the read's now(). Checks: exif/tests.rs raf_and_cr3_carry_their_date (twins: a RAF offset off its JPEG, a CR3 under another uuid carry none), a_heic_and_a_png_carry_their_date (twins: an item typed mime, a tEXt chunk). Closes names-capture-date-formats.

title: A file still being copied waits, and a RAW cut short says so
detail: roots.rs: a file the Finder marks busy (birth in 1946) or written within SETTLE (2 s) is looked at again 50 ms after the walk; one that grew or changed is settling, neither printed nor decoded (read_rows keeps it waiting and its row as it was), and the folder is read again 4 s after a read that left one (archive_view read_once_settled). A date ahead of the clock never settles. pinned.c registers LibRaw's data-error handler: an offset of -1, the file's end, makes oni_unpack return CUT_SHORT (-5); the decode says "the file ends before its picture does: an interrupted copy?" and the canvas "{name}: cut short". Checks: roots/tests.rs a_file_still_being_written_is_settling_until_it_rests (twin: once the copy ends nothing settles), oni-decode source/tests.rs a_truncated_raw_says_so (twins: the whole file decodes, a garbled head is refused otherwise). Closes names-growing-truncated-files.

title: A stray sidecar is never adopted by a new namesake
detail: sidecar/identity.rs: each write stores the original's print (size-date-digest, the library's fingerprint, now computed in one place that relink uses) under originalPrint, a key Swift skips and a Swift rewrite drops. A sidecar is foreign when both prints carry a date and both the date and the digest differ: a date set right in place keeps its bytes, a file saved over keeps its date, a file with no date is never told foreign. A foreign sidecar reads as none (sidecar::read, the index's envelope, refreshed) and is set aside whole at the first write as "X.NEF (orphan).json", numbered when taken, which no survey reads as a sidecar; a cloud-held original is never read for it. Check: oni-settings tests/foreign_sidecar.rs a_foreign_sidecar_is_not_adopted (twins: saved over, redated in place, a Swift sidecar with no key, a second stray). Closes the identity part of names-orphan-sidecar-adopted.

title: A RAW+JPEG pair is one tile, the RAW leading
detail: folders::paired: a JPEG beside a RAW of its stem (case and composition aside) with no ONI sidecar of its own stands behind the RAW, in the tree and the gallery; the RAW is read off the survey's files, so one in the ONI Trash still keeps its JPEG hidden. The RAW's tile carries a +JPG badge (TileView companion, Tile.companion). Lot 10 moves both. Swift shows two tiles. Its JPEG is never drawn by the thumbnails' pass. Checks: folders.rs a_raw_jpeg_pair_is_one_tile (twins: a JPEG with settings of its own stays, unpaired every file is a tile), library/tests.rs a_raw_jpeg_pair_is_one_tile_in_the_archive (twin: a JPEG with its sidecar is a third tile), window gallery_cell a_raw_jpeg_pair_is_one_tile_and_a_heic_is_sealed (twin: a TIFF beside them has no mark). Closes names-raw-jpeg-pairs.

title: Links, junctions and Finder aliases to folders are shown and followed
detail: navigator::children lists a symbolic link, a Windows junction (std reads it as a link) or a Finder alias (its kIsAlias flag, then CFURLCreateByResolvingBookmarkData with no UI and no mount) by the folder it leads to, never one holding the listed folder (a sidecar, an XMP or a document is never looked at for an alias); Navigation::walk never unfolds a row already above it. The survey walks a link under its own name, once, never one holding the root, inside it or inside a folder a link reached already. Checks: roots/tests.rs a_symlinked_folder_is_listed_and_a_loop_is_not_followed (twins: the loop rows, a dangling link), a_finder_alias_to_a_folder_is_listed_by_its_folder. Closes names-symlinks-aliases-invisible and windows-junctions-hidden.

title: A long name saves its settings, and one too long says so
detail: atomic::temporary names every temporary .oni-<hash>-<pid>-<stamp>.tmp, about 45 bytes, for sidecars, the support files and exports; a photo whose name with .json passes 255 characters is refused as sidecar::Error::TooLong, said in words. Checks: atomic.rs a_long_name_writes_through_a_short_temporary (twin: the former temporary's name is refused by the disk), tests/foreign_sidecar.rs a_name_too_long_for_its_sidecar_says_so (twin: four characters shorter it writes). Closes names-long-name-sidecar-temp.

title: Home from USERPROFILE on Windows; move_out and flush cost looked at
detail: navigator::home_folder reads USERPROFILE before HOME on Windows (HOME first elsewhere), for Computer, support, caches and the trash headings. safety-dead-move-out and parity-move-out-duplicate: lot 16 already removed library::move_out; flat_fields::move_out is the one left. windows-flush-cost: not measured, no Windows machine here; each sidecar write still flushes (FlushFileBuffers on Windows), the batch left until a measure says it costs.

title: Parity rows for packages, links, copies, stray sidecars, pairs and formats
detail: archive.md: Packages left out (done, counted), and port-only rows for links and aliases, a file still being copied, a stray sidecar, a RAW+JPEG pair and a format ONI cannot read; the relink row names the capture dates read. editor.md: a RAW cut short says so. README counts: archive 99 / 7 / 0 and 105 of 106, all 442 / 26 / 7 and 451 of 475.

title: One name check for every folder and roll name, refused in words before the disk is asked
detail: oni-library names.rs: refused(name, Platform) holds the separators, the leading dot and, on Windows, the reserved characters, control characters, a trailing dot or space and the device names (CON, NUL, COM1, with or without an extension); file_names.rs keeps the export's portable() on the same tables. Rename (navigator, tree, band heading) and the New Roll folder (roll_folder::make) go through it. Check a_trailing_dot_or_con_is_refused_in_words, twin: the same names pass on a Mac, CONTACT and Roll 8.5 pass on Windows. Closes windows-rename-names.

title: A move or rename another app holds is tried again for half a second, then names the file
detail: roll_folder::retried: a busy file, Windows' sharing or lock violation (32, 33) and its access denied on a folder (5) are tried again after 30, 60, 120 and 240 ms; any other refusal returns at once. rename_new (New Roll, its undo and redo) and the folder rename use it; refusal::cause says 'another app is using it' and the folder rename says a file in it is open in another app. Check a_locked_file_is_retried_then_named with an injected rename, twins: a NotFound and a Windows code on a Mac are tried once, a denial on Windows is tried five times. Closes the retries of windows-file-locking.

title: A roll draft's base is found again by its file name once its folder moved
detail: prepare/draft_base.rs: on resume the stored absolute path matches a frame's own path first, else the one frame of that file name; none or two give no base, so the note never says 'On DSC_0001.NEF' for a base the measure lacks. The next draft writes the path back in this machine's spelling; Swift's field is unchanged. Check a_draft_base_moved_with_its_folder_is_found_by_name, twin: an unknown name and a name twice find nothing. Closes windows-draft-base-absolute.

title: The draft writes queued are waited for before a rename or a New Roll moves their frames, and a refused one is said
detail: prepare/measure.rs drain_drafts (at most DRAFT_FLUSH, never behind a measure) runs before rename_folder and New Roll; a draft write the disk refuses is now told with its cause instead of dropped. The read-modify-write race of set_roll_draft against a main-thread label lives in oni-settings sidecar.rs and needs a per-file lock there. Partly closes safety-draft-thread-races.

title: Windows says Explorer and Ctrl+ everywhere; one place words the two systems
detail: oni-app platform.rs: reveal, reveal_photos, reveal_log and keys(Platform) are the only sources of Finder, ⌘, ⌥ and ⇧; the cell menu, the ONI Trash cell menu, the console's Reveal Log, the filter's empty state, the update key and Slint's KeyWords global (toolbar, canvas tooltips, the colour tab's Shift hint) read them. trash::heading shows a Windows drive as 'D: › Scans/One'. Check windows_labels_say_explorer_and_ctrl scans every label source, twin: a planted Mac word is caught in Rust and Slint, a comment and a check's literal are not. Closes ux-platform-wording and windows-finder-wording.

title: The archive tree's dead Roll and Day nodes are gone
detail: archive_tree.rs keeps Folder and Photo only; the match arms in library.rs, tree_pick.rs, tree_menu.rs and gestures/disk.rs follow. No serialised field depended on them; FilmKey::Day stays for Prepare's grouping. Closes model-11.

title: Words: the catch-up under D3, New Roll says it moves, a folder row's Restore can be undone, a partial restore says what came back
detail: The catch-up says 'N photos of your former library lie outside your favourites' (plural) and 'Every photo of your former library lies in a favourite.'. The menus and the cell menu say 'Move into a New Roll…'. A folder row's RESTORE says what came back with UNDO, which walks the gallery step back only while it is still the last one. trash::report drops 'Nothing was changed.' when other photos went ahead and says how many did.

title: Windows notes a favourite's volume by its serial number, so a drive under another letter is offered to follow
detail: bookmarks.rs: on Windows the volume is GetVolumePathNameW's mount and the serial number GetFileInformationByHandle reads (the same as GetVolumeInformationW), the approach of win-ci2 #367; Bookmarks::lead then finds the drive under its new letter as it finds a renamed Mac volume. Closes windows-drive-letter-drift's identity.

title: A link to a whole disk, / or the home is never walked
detail: The survey follows symlinks, junctions and aliases to folders (#536); a link whose target is a volume's mount point, a drive root, / or a folder holding the home is now left out, so a link inside a scans folder never walks a whole disk; check a_link_to_a_whole_disk_or_the_home_is_never_walked with a plain folder's link as twin.

title: The French refusal after a partial restore reads in one sentence
detail: '{head} : {why}' joined two colons ('… n’a pas été restaurée : son original est introuvable : son disque …'); the why now reads 'son original est introuvable (disque débranché ou fichier déplacé)'.

title: A 2.5D lab shown live by slint-viewer, no build
detail: crates/oni-ui/lab/ holds Slint copies of the Swift app's raised and sunken elements on three shared effects (depth.slint: Keycap, Swift's lit frustum for keys; Outward, a plain raised surface; Inward, a sunken well), every look a live tunable; scripts/ds-lab opens it in slint-viewer 1.18.1 (installed once in ~/.oni-toolchain/slint) and redraws on each save, --check compiles it and --shot renders a component to a PNG. The final styles then move into ui/ds/.

title: oni-keycap: the Swift keycap rasterised on the CPU, matched against the Swift bench's own render
detail: crates/oni-keycap ports KeycapStyle (fields, defaults, depth interpolation, Variant large/small/mini, the app's instances), Frustum and KeycapSurface/KeycapChrome/SocketShadow: walls grown by the bleed and blurred at seamBlur, the 7-stop dish, the socket's centred blurred stroke, travel and scale, the continuous corner as UIKit's three cubics, everything clipped to the silhouette. SwiftUI's `.shadow` after a clip shadows each layer, so the face darkens the wall below it: ported as such. Blur and shadow radii are Gaussians of 0.9 radius, fitted by reference::sweep. Against keycap-lab/exports/variantes.png rebuilt at its own style (2 pt contour, white backing, ambient loss): mean 0.91 levels, 99th percentile 6; twins: azimuth +30° 2.23, blurs ×2.5 14.49. About 4 ms for a 120 × 40 key at 2×.

title: oni-lab: the 2.5D lab in Slint's interpreter, reloaded into the same window, its keycaps drawn by oni-keycap
detail: crates/oni-lab (bin oni-lab) loads crates/oni-ui/lab/lab.slint with slint-interpreter 1.18.1, polls the lab's and ui/ds's .slint files every 250 ms and rebuilds into the same window, carrying every global value the hand moved unless the file changed that default. It answers the `Raster.keycap` pure callback at the window's scale, cached by its numbers with the depth in 1/256 steps. `--check` compiles; `--shot FILE [COMPONENT] [WxH]` renders the lab or one page headless at 2× (ONI_LAB_SCALE). ONI_BACKGROUND=1 opens it behind.

title: The lab's Keycap draws Raster's image: Swift's look, children on the face
detail: depth.slint: KeycapLook, the Raster global and KeycapVariant; Keycap keeps albedo, radius, face-radius, depth and @children, gains variant/factor, level, shadow, rim and an edge (DSBarHandle's strokeBorder), lays its children on the face rect moved by the travel and scaled by scale(at:) about the key's centre, and stands a flat cap in for slint-viewer. Depth gains seam blur, rim rest/pressed/softness, scale pressed, the 0.1 s / 0.02 s curves and the 0.14 s hold; the left panel tunes them.

title: scripts/ds-lab runs oni-lab
detail: Builds oni-lab once when missing, then runs it; --check and --shot FILE [COMPONENT] [WxH] go through it, so a shot shows the real keycap. slint-viewer --check still compiles the lab: the pure callback answers an empty image there.

title: The lab's Keys page: the app's keycap keys, live beside their forced states
detail: keys.slint: LiveKey presses as KeycapPress (reference curves, 0.14 s minimum hold, hover at 0.25, a release while hovered rises on the release curve). Rows: DSPanelButton word plain, pale, tinted, icon, the four heights; DSActionButton and its busy plate; the app bar's 40 pt icon and word keys; the scanner keypad's five letters on one plate; step keys; KeycapPlate small and mini. The Depths page's key is a LiveKey.

title: The slider knob and step keys draw through Keycap
detail: sliders.slint's ScaledCap is now Keycap at a free factor (0.525 by default), no cast shadow unless asked, no rim when level, the 1 px edge when edged: DSBarHandle's knobStyle.

title: The 2.5D lab's pages: tabs, fields, sliders and the rest, on a full Outward and Inward
detail: tabs.slint (DSTabBar, DSToggle, DSPicker with a mini keycap, DSMedalPicker), fields.slint (DSTextField variants, DSField layouts), sliders.slint (DSSlider rail, BarHandle on the raster keycap, stepped slider, step keys, Levels, plot screen, histogram) and misc.slint (DSLCD, DSLamp, DSFoil seals, cards, wells, popover, dialog, status bar, progress) copy the Swift elements with live instances, forced states and per-page tunables; depth.slint's Outward copies dsFloating and Inward the whole dsRecessed (12 nested strokes for the folded blur, the trackLine edge, the rim lip, hollow and lit). The lab is a sandbox outside the file ceilings.

title: The lab's keycaps cast no shadow, their bottom wall lifted toward the face
detail: Owner's call: no cast shadow under a keycap (Depth.shadow-opacity 0, Swift's 0.2 kept as the tunable's history in the comment), and a softer foot: oni-keycap's bottom_lift (0 = Swift) moves the bottom wall's Lambert shade toward the flat face's, 0.4 in the lab, a tunable of the left panel; a test with its twin checks the bottom wall lightens and the top wall keeps its shade.

title: The three depths and the keycap raster move into the design system, one mapping for the lab and the app
detail: ui/ds/depth.slint now holds Depth, KeycapLook (with the window's scale, so a change of screen draws the keys again), Raster, KeycapVariant, Keycap, Outward and Inward; lab/depth.slint re-exports them, so the lab tunes the app's own Depth (every lab page shot identical to the pixel). oni-keycap's look module maps a look's numbers to KeycapStyle and Frame and keeps the renders in a Cache keyed by those numbers, the depth on a 1/256 grid, bounded in bytes; oni-lab and oni-app (keycaps.rs, served by the Shell on the main window, the board and the console) both use it. Depth.look() builds the look in one call per key and a cap without cast shadow draws no margin (a test shows nothing lies past the key).

title: Every key of the app is a keycap: Button, ButtonGroup's plate, the step keys
detail: Button draws the lab's keycap: regular the 40 pt small key (DSPanelButton standard), small the same at 24, a new mini size at 26 (sections, header plates, the card's keys, the zoom plate, as Swift's .mini), key the scanner's 46 pt key, a stepped slider's keys at 40 with an 18 pt sign. A kind or fill is the albedo, on a pale cap (a ring on a tinted one), the legend bold capitals inked by the cap's luminance, disabled fading the legend alone, the ghost bare. KeycapPress for every key: hover sinks it Depth.hover-press, a press whole in 0.1 s, held 0.14 s at least, risen in 0.02 s, the release click with the cap. ButtonGroup's plate sets its keys flush on the black socket at the cap's outer radius. The bar grows to the 40 pt keys (56). Board pages, ds/README and ui-spec updated.

title: The keycaps' cost, measured by a window check
detail: keycap_cost: the editor's first frame at 2x (1440 x 900) asks its keys and renders each distinct look once, a hundred still frames render none; a press renders at most one key a frame and nothing once risen, a new scale draws it again, its twin that the press and the hover do render. Measured on the test profile: the editor's 29 distinct keys (187 asks) in 47 ms, 1.6 ms each, 2.5 MB kept; a press 9 to 10 renders over its curve, 0.7 ms each, one a frame at most; still keys 0.

title: The design-system board leaves the app; the lab is its showcase
detail: Owner's call: the board (ds/board/, 27 MB of the 85 MB the interface generated) is removed with Help > Design System…, --board and its window check; the checks' probes move to ds/probes.slint; the 2.5D lab is the showcase, and oni-lab/tests/lab.rs checks it compiles (twin: an unknown component is refused).

title: Dev and test builds read the interface at run time
detail: oni-ui/build.rs sets SLINT_LIVE_PREVIEW for the debug profile, slint gains live-preview: the generated layer falls from 103 MB to 1.1 MB, oni-ui compiles in 12 s, a .slint edit reaches a window check in 15 s, the full check in 128 s instead of about 650. The app profile and release keep the compiled interface. Slint's @tr texts stay English in this mode (no bundled translations in the interpreter), so the French look is judged on the app profile.

title: The splash closes when the interface is interpreted
detail: The splash's timer held it weakly; with Slint's live preview a shown window's handle goes with the function's own, so the timer found nothing to hide and the app stayed on its splash. The timer holds the splash strongly, in both modes.

title: A Windows tester's build: ONI.exe in a zip, by hand
detail: The owner wants a tester on Windows. .github/workflows/windows-package.yml (workflow_dispatch only, never a release) builds the release on windows-latest and keeps ONI-windows-<sha>.zip (ONI.exe and a README in English and French: unzip, double-click, SmartScreen's Run anyway, where settings live) as the run's artifact for 14 days. The Windows release links the C runtime in (+crt-static) so a bare PC runs it, and opens no console (windows_subsystem).

title: Too many open files: the folder watch uses FSEvents again, and the app raises its descriptor limit
detail: Owner's report: 'Too many open files (os error 24)' after an Edit Together of 36 frames. Slint's live preview (#564) enables notify's macos_kqueue for the whole workspace, which made RecommendedWatcher kqueue: one descriptor per file under every watched tree (245 806 held, ~/Documents and its node_modules), past the Mac's 256. notify 8.2.0 is vendored (vendor/notify, CC0) with FSEvents kept on the Mac whatever the features, oni-library's watch names FsEventWatcher, and main raises RLIMIT_NOFILE toward 10 240. A check with its twin: a deep watch of 400 files holds under 50 descriptors with FSEvents, kqueue over 400.

title: The selection controls stand on the depths: Tabs, Toggle, Picker's field, the medals
detail: The 2.5D lab's Tabs page moves into the design system, its values unchanged. Tabs is DSTabBar: a 40 pt Inward hollow at track-shade 0.4, tabs a line apart, one Outward pill (the canvas lifted 15 % toward white) sliding on the grab spring (spring 0.38 over 220 ms), hover lighting the label alone, the idle opacity on the whole tab; a new `dimmed` fades a tab that changes something else, used by Export's ProPhoto in JPEG as Swift. The Pro/Scanner bar is that bar at modeBarWidth. Toggle is DSToggle: a 52 x 20 hollow holding a cross and a check, the white Outward thumb on the state that holds. Picker's field face is DSPicker: the value in a hollow at the card radius, the chevron on a mini Keycap that sinks Depth.hover-press under the hand and whole on a press; the pill and chip faces keep the hover ground. Medal is DSFoil's spun metal in gradients; MedalPicker's cells are the medal's size, a press shrinking it to 0.86 on the spring, `pressed-rank` forcing it. The gauges live in ds/theme_tabs.slint (TabsStyle, ToggleStyle, PickerStyle, MedalStyle), their in-out values tuned live by the lab, whose Tabs page now shows the DS components. Window checks clicking under the taller bars move by their 8 pt (tree lists, panel bindings).

title: The text fields stand in the lab's hollow
detail: ds/fields.slint holds TextField, RenameField, SizeFields and DateFields on depth.slint's Inward { hollow: true }: a card's corner floored in the canvas, DS.Space.md across, DS.Space.sm down a multiline one, the rim lit while focused (focused-look forces it), the placeholder shown while empty as SwiftUI does, a disabled field fading its words alone. FieldStyle moves to theme_fields.slint. The export's W x H and the shot date share one hollow a keycap tall; a multiline field's lines-height is the text's, inside its padding (Swift's frame before dsTextField); a title typed over takes DS.Typo.title, led out by the hollow's padding; a renamed row's text stays where its title stood. Behaviour unchanged: select-all on entry, double and triple click (text_fields reads the new inset). Cost: no raster, the hollow is twelve strokes as every Inward.

title: The lab's Fields page shows the design system's fields
detail: crates/oni-ui/lab/fields.slint lays the real TextField, Field, SizeFields and DateFields, their states forced through focused-look and enabled; the chrome's tunables leave the page for FieldStyle, the hollow's Depth tunables stay.

title: The lab's sliders and plots move into the design system
detail: ds/theme_sliders.slint holds SliderStyle and PlotStyle (out of theme.slint, re-exported by it), the lab's values in-out so the lab tunes them live. Rail is DSRail in dsRecessed: the ground or the bipolar gradient, the fill on its own round, Inward's shade, the black edge, the lit rim over an opaque `under`, the rest tick; `vertical` added. Knob is DSBarHandle: a Keycap at the small factor, level walls, no shadow or rim, a 1 pt black edge, two white grip lines centred on the face; it grows on the rise spring (120 ms) by a scale, so its raster is drawn once, and its cap is the keycap grey. Slider moves rail and knob together on the settle spring (380 ms, cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.25, 0.5, 1)) for a value from elsewhere, never under the hand; the stepped knob gains its grip; the step keys read SliderStyle.step-key and step-legend. Plot's screen sinks with Inward { hollow } over the canvas, quarters engraved at white 0.12, its rim lit; CurvePoint is DSHandle.

title: The lab's Sliders page shows the design system's own sliders and plots
detail: crates/oni-ui/lab/sliders.slint drops its copies: DS Slider (live and stepped, driven in Slint as Rust drives them: drag, ⌥ a fifth, a second press resting it, the sideways swipe), Rail and Knob (the vertical slider and the specimens), Keycap at ×4, Plot, LevelsTrack with its five grips held in Slint, CurvePoint; the tunables bind SliderStyle and PlotStyle. keycap_cost's window check drags a slider and springs it home: no knob is drawn again (twin: the knob moved).

title: The surfaces take the lab's relief: Raised, Inset, the cards, the popover, the glass, the lamps and the seals
detail: The 2.5D lab's misc family moves into the design system, its values as approved. Raised stands on Outward (dsFloating: the lit rim, the gradient, the inner hairline, the cast shade, lengthened for a sheet), so every sheet, notice, banner, slid column and popup takes it; Popover (surfaces.slint) hangs it under DSPopoverShape's tail, which PopupPanel draws for a popover (tail-x, centred by default). Inset, Progress (its glow) and LcdReadout (its glowing ink) sink as Inward, as does the passes' reorder hollow (DSReorder). PresetFace (lifted), WrappedCard and TipCard (DSHelpBubble on the canvas) are Outwards. Divider is DSSeparator's engraved groove, two lines; hairline or engraved: false stays flat (a menu's rule). Badge seals print DSGoldSealView's foil (gold, holographic, red), the glint swept on glinting or a hovered note; Lamp is DSLamp, laid on a key at its legend's top right. SurfaceStyle, SealStyle and Foil live in theme_surfaces.slint.

title: The lab's Misc page shows the design system's own surfaces
detail: crates/oni-ui/lab/misc.slint lays the real Raised (each lift, menu), Inset, LcdReadout, Lamp and Button's lamp, Badge seals (glint-at for a still glint), PresetFace, WrappedCard, Divider, Popover and a live PopupPanel, TipCard, AskSheet, StatusBar and Progress; its tuning strip moves SurfaceStyle live. The flat DSWarning, the plot screen and the depths' own specimens keep their lab copies.

title: A click beside a focused field ends its editing and gives the keys back to the window
detail: The key monitor (a FocusScope) took the keyboard only from a press no item accepted, so a click on a key, a row or the canvas left the field focused and the shortcuts dead. The window's pointer hook (oni_app::outside::pressed, from the winit filter) now counts each press in the Outside global before Slint reads it; an Entry holding the keyboard whose words and hollow padding are not under that press bumps Outside.released, and KeyMonitor (the window's monitor) takes the focus back. The field's focus-out commits as before: a RenameField commits, as the Finder does on a click elsewhere, Escape still cancels; size, date and text fields hand their value over. The click itself still reaches what it lands on.

title: A click on another picker while a menu is down opens that picker's menu
detail: Every menu, picker list, popover and context menu is a PopupPanel (close-on-click-outside): Slint closes it on a press beside it and dispatches that press to nothing, so no hand-made overlay was left open. The one gap was the opener: the swallowed press never reached another picker. Its release still arrives with no press before it, so a Picker whose field takes a release without its press opens, unless that press closed its own menu (the Working Space chip counts its chooser as its menu, own-popup).

title: Window checks: a press beside a menu or a field
detail: OutsideProbe (ds/probes.slint) lays a key monitor round a field, a rename, a key and two pickers. outside::a_menu_closes… : a click beside a menu closes it and the key under it counts nothing (twins: the key counts a click with no menu down, a click inside picks its line); a click on the other picker opens it (twin: a click on the open picker closes it and opens none). outside::a_field_ends… : a click beside the field ends its editing and the next key reaches the monitor, a rename commits (twins: a click inside keeps the focus and the key goes in at the caret; a click inside the rename keeps it, Escape cancels). Each mutation of the rule makes its check fail.

title: The panel's binding checks aimed again after the taller keys and tab bars
detail: panel_bindings pressed at fixed points that the plate keys (52), the 40 tab bars and the export column's new rows had moved: the Vertical switch, the Flat-Field chevron, the size box and its Full resolution key and CANCEL fell beside their controls. No behaviour broke: each control answers at its new place. The panel's presses are now measured from MainWindow.panel-x and tabs-foot, so a taller header moves them with it; the export sheet publishes no anchor and keeps its points. The undo twins (the switch back off, then on again) and the popover twin (its sRGB tab gone from under the pointer) stand.

title: A section ending on a well or a raised face draws its lip and shadow whole
detail: Section clipped its content at its bounds even unfolded, so a tab bar, a text field or a plot screen ending a block (Film Type, Machine, Source Encoding, Camera Body, Description, a curves plot) lost Inward's lit lip, the two lines under the well, and an Outward lost its shadow. The content clips only while folded, the one state that needs it; Depth.lip-reach names how far the lip reaches (2 px), and the scrolled columns that can end on a well (the export panel's summary, the preset save sheet's form, Prepare the Roll's step) leave it under their content. The wells keep Swift's sizes: reserving the lip inside each component would have shrunk every well by 2 px (a 14 px rail to 12). Checked by window check depth_lip on DepthProbe: a field ending a section draws the same lip rows as a field alone; its twin, a box clipped at the field's bounds, reads the ground there (and the old clip fails the check); folded, the section still shows nothing of its field.

title: The Scanner keypad steps by half a unit: 0.5 a key, 1.5 with ⇧
detail: The owner's call, apart from Swift: ScannerClicks counts steps of half the unit the screen reads (density ±48 steps for ±24 units, TEMP ±20 for ±10). A density step is a quarter of the measured click, read on the line between its neighbours, so a whole unit renders as before; TEMP's share is per unit. The Frontier's rest D+0.5 M+2 Y-2 is now one plain count (FRONTIER_REST_D gone). The sidecar keeps Swift's whole counts under d, c, m, y, w (toward zero) and the half step left over under `halves`, which Swift ignores and which is absent on whole units, so an old sidecar reads unchanged. The screen, the slider readouts and the link demo spell steps as units with halves (oni_keys::spelled); the rails have 97 and 41 places. The phone link's Clicks are in steps: a phone app must read them halved. The effects (Contrast, Vignette, Chrome) keep their 5 %, 0.1 EV and 5 % steps.

title: ButtonGroup is Swift's KeycapPlate: the socket at the cap's corner, keys wall to wall, a spaced row Space.s apart
detail: Owner: "il faut réimplémenter les buttongroups, base toi sur swift". KeycapPlate draws HStack(spacing: 0) on a RoundedRectangle of the socket colour (black) at cornerRadius + contourWidth, 16 × the variant's factor with contour 0. ButtonGroup's socket now reads Depth.corner × the variant's factor, so a corner tuned in the lab moves the cap and its plate together; `small` became `mini` (KeycapPlate(variant: .mini)); `radius` and `gap` are out properties. Without `plate` a group is a spaced row at Space.s, Swift's DS.Space.sm between keys off a plate (PresetEditor, WelcomeSheet, PaperProfilesSheet, GeometryPanel, FolderNavigator, the zoom bubble), in place of 2 px.

title: The 52 pt plate key: ButtonSize.plate on every key Swift sizes .plate
detail: DSPanelButton(height: .plate) is DS.Control.keycapPlateHeight, 52 pt, against the standard 40: ButtonSize.plate (ButtonStyle.plate-height). On it: Measured Roll's PREPARE THE ROLL… and JOIN / ROLL OF, the flat-field's USE THIS PHOTO, LOAD / RENAME / FOLDER and APPLY TO SELECTION, Crop's COPY / PASTE / PASTE TO ROLL, the Measuring Window's four keys, AUTO WHITE BALANCE and AUTO PAPER CORRECTION, the export panel's presets, Load a Profile / Get Paper Profiles and Cancel / EXPORT, Prepare the Roll's Cancel / Back / step key. The report sheet, the dialogs and the bar keep Swift's 40.

title: The app bar's keys on Swift's plates
detail: EditorScene+Bar's centreKeys plates every family: editing, framing / compare / contact sheet, undo / redo, copy / paste / PASTE TO ROLL, De-dust alone and never plated, RESET SCAN on its own plate; in the gallery the contact sheet alone on its plate, undo / redo, the filter and PREPARE ROLL loose, RESET SCAN / trash on one plate. rollStepKeys is one plate of the five steps. The bar's groups were spaced rows without a socket.

title: The canvas's column keys each on a mini plate
detail: columnKey(_:) is KeycapPlate(variant: .mini) around the one key: the Library's at the canvas's top left and the Panel's last in the zoom bubble now stand on their socket as the zoom pair does.

title: Window check: a plate's keys touch, a spaced row keeps Swift's gap
detail: button_group: GroupProbe lays two .plate keys on a plate, two mini keys on a mini plate and two keys on a spaced row. The plates' keys share their walls (gap 0), the row's stand 8 apart, the socket is as tall as its 52 pt keys, rounded 16 × 0.525 and 16 × 0.38, the row draws none. Twins: the gap measure reads the row's room and a plate is no row, each variant's radius tells the other's apart; a plate spaced 1 px fails it.

title: The measure's screen draws each frame's histogram and morphs it into the next one's
detail: While Prepare the Roll measures, the card shows the frame just read, the count, and its histogram in the plot well (ds TraceWell, TraceStyle): luminance under red, green and blue, each area tinted under its line, the line glowing in two widths, the three frames before as fading luminances, a hairline at the luminance's median. The measure's thread counts each frame's tile as the editor counts its picture (128 bins) and sends it once per frame; this thread eases the curves from one histogram to the next over 320 ms at the frame tick, then stops ticking. A measure starting or landing clears it, so the well is empty until its first frame lands. Window check prepare_measure, with the stale-well twin.

title: Prepare the Roll's base loupe shows the full resolution first, decoded ahead
detail: The loupe showed the 1400-pixel scan, then switched to the sensor's pixels 300 ms after the scan landed plus a full decode, its span going from 32 to 64 pixels: the owner read the sharpening as a bug. Measured on roll #8 (DSC_6433.NEF, 6048x4032, app profile, a loaded machine): scan 2.2 s, full decode 2.5 s, 8-bit encode 0.23 s, so the full landed about 5.3 s after the step opened, the scan shown blurred from 2.2 s. The base frame's full resolution is now decoded from the roll's entry, its two neighbours on the base step (as background decodes), one at a time, let go past the base step; the loupe never shows the scan: a well at the full resolution's scale with its rings until it lands, the scan only when the full cannot be decoded. Window check prepare_loupe: the first picture on the scan is the full one, the surface stays on the reduced scan (twin), a frame two away is never decoded ahead (twin), a cold walk shows a well, never the scan.

title: A help mark's card in the editor panel opens left of the panel, under its tab bar
detail: TipLayer takes the panel's anchor from app.slint (its left edge, root.width less the panel's width, and the tab bar's foot, the bar's height plus PanelState.header the panel lays from its rule) and opens every card from a mark inside the panel with its right edge TipStyle.card-gap left of the panel and its top at the foot, held in the window by Tips.place so a short window lifts it. Marks off the panel (gallery Info, export and prepare columns, sheets) and every tooltip keep their place under the mark; a sheet over the window drops the anchor. Window check help_card with its twins (a card beside its mark, a note over the canvas, the gallery's column).

title: The sidebar trees follow every scroll, so the rows it reaches get their pictures
detail: The trees' scroll was bound both ways to Library.tree-viewport-y and project-viewport-y, but a wheel or trackpad scroll removes the Flickable's bindings (Slint's remove_binding before its smooth-scroll animation): from the first wheel on, Rust read a frozen scroll, the near-view rule gave pictures to the rows around the old place only, and the rows scrolled into view stayed empty until another event laid the column. The scroll now goes one way each: Rust asks a place (viewport-y plus a count of asks the RowTree applies), and the scroller reports every move, wheel, knob, key or reveal, with its value (tree-scrolled(y), project-scrolled(y)); Slint runs that change handler once a frame. A size change fills the rows a taller column brings near. Window check library_column::a_scroll_brings_the_pictures_of_the_rows_it_reaches: in a 1,100-photo column scrolled by the wheel without a resize, the scroll reaches Rust and the rows in view get their pictures, the top row left far away lets its picture go; after an ask far down, no row three screens away holds one (twin). The tree checks that scrolled by writing the property now ask as Rust does (common::scroll_tree, scroll_projects).

title: A tree asks only the thumbnails of the rows near its view, and asks again those memory let go
detail: Laying a tree asked every photo row's thumbnail file: past MEMORY_LIMIT (1,000) memory dropped its least recent half, often the rows on screen, and a scroll never asked them again (fill_tree_thumbnails only read memory). Laying now asks the rows near the view only, nothing while the column has no size, and a fill asks the near rows whose picture is not in memory, read off the interface thread as before. Same window check: with memory emptied (forget_tiles) and the column laid again, fewer than a quarter of the 1,100 thumbnails are asked (599 when every row asks, the twin), and the rows an ask brings into view read theirs back (a timeout when a fill asks nothing, the twin).

title: A long sidebar tree makes only the rows near its view and tells Slint only the rows that changed
detail: RowTree laid every row of a tree with a plain for: 2,000 photos made some 20,000 elements that every frame evaluated and drew, and publish_tree replaced the whole model on every photo opened (M34). The rows now live in one Rust model per tree (app/tree_rows.rs, TreeRows): Library.rows and project-rows still hold every row, each carrying its index, for Rust and the checks; Library.near-rows and project-near-rows are a window over them, the rows within the near-view rule's reach (a screen above the view to two below), the only ones the column makes. A scroll, a resize or a landing moves the window: rows leaving it are removed and rows entering it added, the rest kept; a row changed reaches the window in place; a tree laid again with the same count tells only the rows that differ, a new count resets. Rows keep their own x and y, as the archive's pairs lay two thumbnails a line, so the window is cut in Rust rather than by Slint's ListView, which stacks one element a line. mark_tree reads each row's mark without copying it. The revealed column carries cache-rendering-hint as the docked one does. Window check library_column::a_long_tree_makes_only_the_rows_near_its_view: in a 2,000-photo column, 17 rows made at the top and 26 mid-column, exactly the rows in reach and under a tenth of the tree (2,001 made when the window holds every row, the twin), every row in view made with its picture. Sixty Exposure notches handled and drawn by the software renderer beside it in the dev profile (interpreted interface): p50 59 to 258 ms before, 11 to 12 ms after, as beside a 30-photo tree (11.9 ms). Unit checks in tree_rows.rs, each with its twin. ONI_BENCH drags now also report the interface's frames.

title: A thumbnail landing reaches its tiles and rows in place, without laying the gallery again
detail: Each thumbnail landed, read from the folder or drawn, called publish_tiles, which relit the whole tree, rebuilt every tile in view, asked the cells again and laid the headings (M38): a 2,000-photo folder did so 2,000 times while loading, about 0.5 ms each on the interface thread. A landing now goes through thumbnail_reached: relay_thumbnail puts the picture on the tiles and rows already showing its photo, and the roll's cells are published when Prepare the Roll is shown, as before. The gallery, visible and prepare window checks pass unchanged.

title: The gallery keeps one slot count while it scrolls, so a scroll remakes no tile
detail: lay_tiles maps each cell in view to the slot index % slots, but the slot count was the range's length, which changes as rows and band ends enter and leave the view: the model was replaced and every tile remade at each such step (M35). The count is now the most cells the view can hold wherever it scrolls (gallery::Layout::slots: the viewport and a row of slack either side, one cut row at each end, one more for a band ending inside), the range's own length when it is ever larger. Unit check the_slots_hold_the_cells_in_view_wherever_the_grid_scrolls (2,000 scroll positions over three bands within the count, which stays near the view; twin: the range's length varies). Window check scroll::the_gallery_knob_scrolls_the_grid_the_wheel_s_way: a 300-point knob drag over 1,200 photos keeps the same tiles model.

title: The roll's histogram summed as the roll combines its frames
detail: Each measured frame keeps the levels histogram its tails and median were read off (Measured.counts), and roll::summed lays every frame's counts at the roll's gains, moved as the tails are, into the bins of 0…1, so the measure can show the roll so far with the black and white combined reads. Test the_roll_s_histogram_sums_every_frame_moved_to_the_roll_s_gains, its twin the last frame alone.

title: One CRT glass for the Scanner face's screen and the measure: ds crt.slint
detail: CrtScreen (LabScreen's glass, its scanlines in one cached layer), CrtLine (the phosphor ink with LabScreen's glow, a near and a far halo on the glyphs' outer stroke, since Slint has no text shadow), CrtTrace (a phosphor histogram, its echoes, the roll's ends and what lies past them dimmed) and CrtPicture (a cross-fading picture); CrtStyle holds their values. LabScreen now draws on it and gains the glow Swift's has.

title: The measure step as a bank of CRT screens: the place, the negative, three channels
detail: The 2.5D plot well in its card (TraceWell, TraceStyle) is gone. The measure shows FRAME 03/08 and the frame's name on a screen line, the frame's negative reduced on the measure's thread with its lights blooming and cross-fading as the next lands, and red, green and blue each on its own screen, morphing into the next frame's with the frames before as fading echoes. Curves are published as whole models: a screen reading its curve by index is not woken by a row written in place. Nothing ticks once the morph rests.

title: The roll's screen: its histogram building up frame by frame, its black and white placed
detail: After each frame that votes, the worker combines the roll so far and sends its summed histogram and each channel's black and white once per frame; the roll's screen draws them as three bands with their ends as phosphor lines that move as the estimate settles. The base is read before the frames, so the black shown is the one the roll takes; the reading itself is unchanged.

title: The measure's window check follows the CRT bank and the roll
detail: prepare_measure: every screen dark at the start, after a stop and after landing (no channel, echo, negative or roll); three channels per landing, the place on two digits, the negative shown; the roll's count never shrinks and reaches several frames, its histogram moves, each black left of its white. Twins: the histogram moved between landings, and a roll showing the last frame alone would stay at one.

title: A gallery undo or redo that lays the open frame back is an editor step too
detail: write_back put the open frame back with replace() alone, so the editor's history still stood on the state the gallery had just undone: an edit then recorded on top of a pasted state the user had undone, an editor ⌘Z brought the paste back, and under Edit Together the frames together showed and took the open frame's pre-paste fields. take_back now records the restored state with History::record_apart, a step neither the gesture before nor after merges with, as Swift's deferred record runs for every change but a replay. Test a_paste_undone_in_the_gallery_never_comes_back_with_an_editor_undo, its twin the paste left standing where the editor undo lands.

title: Edits made while files move, or kept after a refused write, follow the photo to its new path
detail: followed() moved the rows, picks and projects but never the store: the open frame's next write and the edits kept unsaved stayed under the old path, so the moved photo opened without them and Retry Unsaved answered 'cannot be found' forever. EditorStore::follow now carries the open frame, every Unsaved (its stamp read again), the frames together and the editor companions, and followed() calls it first. The deferred write waits while a disk gesture runs, so it never lays a fresh sidecar beside a photo about to leave; ⌘G back onto the open frame is refused while one runs, as open_in_editor already was; New Roll and a gallery undo or redo of one refuse to move the open frame when its settings could not be written, as rename_folder does. Test edits_kept_unsaved_and_the_open_frame_follow_a_move, its twin the unfollowed photo opening without them.

title: Sending the open frame to the ONI Trash after a refused write keeps its edits
detail: mark_begun and took() flushed, ignored the failure, then closed the frame, so the edits a sidecar refused were dropped silently and nothing asked on quitting. Both now close through close(), whose leave() keeps a refused write's edits in unsaved; sidecar::write keeps the trash mark, so a retry never restores the photo. Test a_frame_trashed_after_a_refused_write_keeps_its_edits_unsaved (the sidecar's place taken by a folder), its twin a write taken keeping nothing back.

title: The info sidebar's typing is written before ⌘G, Export, Prepare the Roll or a quit hides it
detail: The camera body, the shot date, the project's description and the roll's or project's name committed only on Return or on the focus leaving; ⌘G, ⌘E and ⌘Q destroy the sidebar with no focus-out, so the text was dropped. EditableTitle now hands its draft to Library.title-edited, and commit_info_drafts writes whatever the fields hold that differs from the roll or project, as one step, from toggle_mode, act (Export, Prepare the Roll) and last_writes; it leaves the drafts in their fields while a disk gesture runs. Window check gallery: the camera body and title typed write nothing until ⌘G, then are on the roll's marker.

title: Ungroup and a roll set from the sidebar put the open frame in the gallery step and record its editor step
detail: set_film changed the open frame with replace() alone: a gallery ⌘Z regrouped every frame but the open one, an editor ⌘Z dropped the last real edit with the film, and the film rode on the next unrelated step. The open frame is now in before and after and settles its own step, as Swift's applyFilm; Swift's updateRoll leaves it out of the gallery step, a departure kept since it is the same bug. apply_film counts the photos in its label as applyFilm does ('Ungroup · 2 photos'); set_film keeps updateRoll's plain label. Test ungroup_takes_the_open_frame_in_its_gallery_step_and_its_editor_step, its twin an editor undo taking a film change back alone.

title: A gesture on frames edited together writes each one once and its gallery step reads their true before
detail: lay_on, land_roll and reset_to_default settled the open frame first, whose propagate_together wrote its fields on the frames together, then read those frames back already written: the gallery step's before was a mix, and a paste dropped them from the step. settle_beside now leaves the frames the gesture writes itself to it; a frame together that no target names still takes the step. Test a_paste_on_frames_together_is_undone_from_the_gallery_to_their_own_settings, its twin the frame left out of the targets taking the paste.

title: Edit Together keeps a roll's measured fields on the frames of that roll and decode
detail: A levels handle, the gains, the density ceiling, the flat-field or the mode moved on the open frame were laid whole on every frame together, so a frame of another roll or another decode lost the windows measured on its own film base. propagate_together and together_live now skip the Roll Settings family for a frame whose roll reference or decode differs. Test a_roll_field_moved_together_stays_on_the_frames_of_that_roll, its twin a frame of the same roll taking the window.

title: Gallery undo follows a folder renamed or found elsewhere
detail: Renaming the folder New Roll makes, as the app proposes at once, left every gallery step under the old name: ⌘Z then found no file to put back and spent its step. GalleryHistory::follow rewrites every step's settings keys, trash paths, roll folder and moves; followed_outside calls it for rename_folder and locate, never for a step's own moves. Swift has the same gap; the owner accepts departures that fix real bugs. Test a_folder_renamed_after_a_new_roll_is_where_its_undo_walks_from, its twin a photo outside the folder keeping its path; window check new_roll renames the roll then undoes it.

title: ⌘Z within the settle delay, gestures on an inert open frame, Paste to Roll and Auto Balance during a move
detail: An undo or redo now records the step still waiting first, so a ⌘Z within 150 ms of a nudge takes that nudge back and not the step before (test an_undo_within_the_settle_delay_takes_back_the_step_still_waiting, its twin the redo bringing it back). lay_on, paste_to_roll, set_film, land_roll and reset_to_default leave an open frame whose original is out of sight or whose sidecar this version cannot write alone (takes_hands), as land_roll did (test a_gesture_on_several_leaves_an_open_frame_out_of_sight_alone, its twin the frame in sight taking the paste). Paste to Roll and Auto Balance refuse while a disk gesture runs, the balance at its landing too, so its step never cuts the one whose walk still runs.

title: A quit right after a disk gesture starts waits for it
detail: wait_for_disk took the gesture lock, which the spawned thread may not have taken yet: a quit landing first ended the process while the move began. Gestures are now counted in flight before their thread starts and uncounted once run (or once the spawn fails); wait_for_disk waits for none.

title: A view in a straightened frame's clear corner renders clear instead of blanking the canvas
detail: Plan::new refused any stage whose input region missed its input's extent (EmptyInput), so a crop-tool zoom into the clear corner of a straightened frame, where Resample maps the whole view past the upright frame, failed the render and showed 'could not be decoded'. An input region is now projected onto its input's extent (Rect::nearest_in): the intersection when they meet, else the edge rows or columns a clamped load reads, so every kernel reads what its `load` and `inside` give. Checks: oni-graph a_region_whose_input_lies_past_the_extent_reads_the_nearest_edge (twin: one edge pixel declared repeats down the rows) and oni-pipeline a_view_in_a_straightened_frame_s_clear_corner_renders_clear (twin: edges repeated read the frame, not clear); both failed with EmptyInput before.

title: A window resize during an export, a heal or a long render waits one submission, not the whole render
detail: The engine's guard counted as inside the surface's door for its whole life, so Door::hold on a Resized or ScaleFactorChanged event froze the interface thread until an export frame's full-resolution render and readback ended. The engine's graph now passes the door per submission (graph.through(door)) and its uploads per 64 MB band, as the reader graphs did; Shared::lock takes the mutex alone. Measured in the dev profile (render::door_tests, 12 MP export render under the busy settings, holds every 8 ms): 16 holds over a 191 ms render, median 0.0 ms, longest 3.5 ms; twin, the door held across the render: one hold of 162 ms.

title: The thread holding the surface's door passes it, so an interface-thread render before the queued release cannot deadlock
detail: Door::hold runs on the interface thread and its release is queued with invoke_from_event_loop; any engine submission on that thread in between waited for a release only it could run. The door records its holder's thread, which passes enter. Check the_holding_thread_passes_its_own_door_and_no_other, twin: another thread's render waits until the release.

title: The launch prewarm takes the engine one variant at a time and gives way to waiters
detail: The prewarm thread held the engine for the whole compilation, so Shell::new's engine locks, and the window, waited for it. Shared::prewarm locks per size and variant, and between two waits while another thread waits for the engine (Shared::give_way: std's mutex is not fair, and an immediate relock kept the waiter out). Check a_lock_during_the_prewarm_waits_one_variant_not_the_whole_prewarm: a lock asked 20 ms in is granted while the prewarm still runs (the prewarm goes on more than 10 ms past it); twin, the whole prewarm under one lock: the lock is granted only as it ends.

title: A full-resolution build landing after the return to the gallery is dropped
detail: leave_editor_memory let go of the full frame, but a build in flight landed later, kept s.full (up to 1.6 GB on a 24 MP frame) and rendered the hidden canvas. The landing keeps the build and asks a render only while the editor shows. Window check full_release::a_full_resolution_landing_in_the_gallery_is_let_go (failed before: kept resident, a hidden render); twin: back in the editor the build lands and is kept.

title: A sheet staging more than the 4 MiB uniform ring goes on in a fresh ring instead of overwriting its own first uniforms
detail: laid_out records every tile in one encoder; past 4 MiB of uniforms (about 8 000 dispatches at Metal's 256-byte alignment) the ring wrapped onto offsets the same unsubmitted encoder's first dispatches still read, drawing tiles with another's frame and parameters. The ring tracks where the submission began; a wrap that would reach it moves to a fresh buffer, the old one kept alive by its bind groups. Check a_sheet_staging_past_the_uniform_ring_draws_each_tile_with_its_own_uniforms (failed at error 0.61 before); twin: a tile judged on its neighbour's gains.

title: A readback the GPU fails to deliver is an error, never a panic in whichever thread polls
detail: render_piece, Graph::read_back and display::read_back called expect in the map callback, on poll and on get_mapped_range: a device loss or an invalid buffer panicked the thread that polled the shared device (the interface thread, or the render thread holding and poisoning the engine). The map result now comes back through a channel and turns into Error::Lost (an empty Option for the display's readback). Not reproducible without losing the device: no check.

title: An Edit Together sheet past the GPU's texture side is refused instead of laid on an invalid texture
detail: laid_out created the sheet without checking max_side, so a group of 745 frames or more at fit (a counted sheet past 16 384 px) left the grid and its histogram blank behind a logged validation error. It returns Error::TooLarge. Check a_sheet_past_the_texture_side_is_refused; twin: a sheet at the side itself is laid.

title: The Edit Together histogram leaves the sheet's clear gaps out instead of counting them black
detail: The histogram kernel ignored alpha, so the counted sheet's gaps and letterbox bands piled into bin 0. On a sheet (Counted.sheet, set where Together hands its counted sheet) a sample of alpha 0 is skipped, in the kernel and in its CPU reference histogram::measure_sheet; a single frame still counts its clear corners black, as Swift's CIAreaHistogram does. Check a_sheet_s_clear_gaps_are_not_counted_as_black against the reference; twin: off a sheet the 40 clear columns count black.

title: The engine keeps the masks and patches it reads under a 128 MB budget and lets them go with the editor
detail: Engine.custom and Engine.patches kept every custom flat-field mask (about 42 MB each) and dust patch read in the session. Both are now kept under INPUTS_KEPT (128 MB), the longest unused let go first and never one the current read names; trim (the return to the gallery) drops them, so a forgotten mask is read again from its file. Misses are no longer stored, as they were asked again anyway. Check the_patches_kept_stay_under_their_budget_and_go_with_the_editor; twin: a render naming more than the budget keeps every patch it names. The budget and its reads live in render/engine/kept.rs.

title: A LinearRaw DNG or an sRAW is read whole at factor 1 when a small copy is asked
detail: oni_open asked LibRaw for half size from the frame's size alone, but LibRaw halves only a mosaic (raw2image_start: filters set, no colour3/4 or float image), so a compressed linear DNG or a Canon sRAW came back whole while ONI counted a factor of 2: the maker's crop halved into a top-left window, full_width doubled, the wrong window kept under the HALF key. oni_process now clears half_size and the half flag on the same condition LibRaw shrinks on, and a decode is kept under its key whatever its factor. Mosaics take the same path as before. Check a_linear_dng_is_read_whole_at_factor_one (a LinearRaw DNG at HALF reads factor 1 and bit for bit the whole decode; twin: a mosaic of the same size reads factor 2 at half the crop).

title: The maker's crop is placed from the margins LibRaw cuts, as an ActiveArea DNG, a CR2 or a RAF holds it
