detail: LibRaw keeps raw_inset_crops in the raw's coordinates (a DNG's DefaultCropOrigin plus its ActiveArea margins), while the image it hands out starts at left_margin and top_margin: the window was shifted by the margins or, past the image, dropped. oni_process subtracts the margins and writes zero sizes for an unknown crop or one inside the margins. NEF and RW2 (margins 0) decode bit for bit as before at sides 0, HALF and 2000 in every colour mode; the Fujifilm RAF now takes its 6240 x 4155 crop instead of the uncropped 6246 x 4170. Check a_default_crop_lands_inside_the_active_area (a DNG with ActiveArea decodes bit for bit as the same frame without margins; twin: a window shifted by the margins differs).

title: An embedded RGB preview shorter than its sides is no preview, never a panic of the thumbnail thread
detail: LibRaw can hand out a bitmap preview whose data_size is the strip's declared length, shorter than width x height x 3, and turned() indexed past it, ending the only thumbnail thread. embedded_by takes a bitmap only when both sides are positive and the bytes cover them, cut to that length. Check a_bitmap_shorter_than_its_sides_is_no_preview (one byte short and a zero or negative side read None; twin: the whole rows read and a longer buffer is cut to the sides).

title: The TIFF probe reads its file a 64 KB window at a time, not a seek and a read a field
detail: Reader on a file did a seek and a read_exact per u8, u16 or u32, so a directory's arrays (strip offsets, a 4096-entry linearization table) cost thousands of syscalls per probe, on the UI thread for a selection. A Window keeps 64 KB around the last field (a quarter of it behind) and refills only when a field falls outside. Check a_probe_reads_a_window_not_a_field_at_a_time (a 256 x 256 LinearRaw TIFF with a 4096-entry table probes as its bytes in 3 reads at most; twin: a window as small as a field takes more than 4096).

title: LibRaw's name route keeps a path's own bytes, so a name that is not UTF-8 still opens
detail: Source::open built the C string from to_string_lossy, which replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD and names another file on a volume from another system. On Unix the CString is the OsStr's bytes. Check a_name_that_is_not_utf8_keeps_its_bytes (the name reaches the shim byte for byte; twin: the lossy text differs).

title: Two writers of one decode never share a part file, and a stopped writer's part is trimmed
detail: store wrote every writer of a key into one '<key>.part', and File::create truncated the file another writer was still filling, which could leave a zero band in a kept decode; a part left by a kill was never counted nor removed. Each writer now has its own part (pid and a counter), and trim removes parts older than ten minutes. Check two_writers_of_one_frame_never_share_a_part_and_a_stale_part_goes (two parts differ, a stale one goes; twin: a fresh one stays).

title: A decode read back is dated as used on Windows too
detail: read_in noted the use with set_modified on a read-only handle, which Windows refuses (FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES), so its cache let go the first written, not the least used. The date is now set through a handle opened for writing. Check a_decode_read_back_is_dated_as_used (twin: a decode not read keeps its date).

title: A tiled LinearRaw TIFF reads each tile's rows at the tile's width
detail: In one column of tiles wider than the image, a row's offset inside a tile was counted at the image's width, so every row after the first started early and the picture came out sheared with padding mixed in. The stride inside a tile is now the tile's width. Check a_tile_wider_than_the_image_reads_its_rows_at_its_own_width (5-wide image in 16-wide tiles decodes as the same strips; twin: the padding reads 1.0, which the picture never does; the image-width stride fails it).

title: LibRaw's handle stream reads through a 1 MB buffer, and on Windows without a lock per byte
detail: The handle route (Windows) wraps a FILE* whose get_char is fgetc, which takes the CRT lock on every byte, about 25 million for a 24 MP NEF, over the default 4 KB buffer. handle_stream sets a 1 MB buffer and, on Windows, reads with _fgetc_nolock: a stream is never shared between threads. The handle route still decodes the synthetic DNG and two frames of roll #8 bit for bit as the name route (the_handle_route_decodes_bit_for_bit_as_the_name_route with its twin). The Windows timing is not measured here.

title: The archive's tree is cut again only when its shape moves
detail: Archive keeps what it was cut from (folder, rows, survey, filter) and its rows laid flat. A lay on the same rows and survey keeps it (a read again on focus, opening a photo, a thumbnail landing); medals alone are set on its photos, groups and row captions in one walk; a filter alone cuts the groups again; anything else cuts it whole. The survey is compared on what a tree reads (images, rolls, folders, made, the JPEGs holding a sidecar), so an edit's sidecar moves no tree. The read's thread cuts each landing's archive, the copies and the tile keys, and the lay takes that archive when the rows held are its own. The rows are walked by reference, a folder's row no longer copying its subtree. library::cuts() counts the trees laid and the row lists laid flat; window check tree_cost (opening a photo, its thumbnail landing and a read that finds nothing new cut nothing; twins: a fold lays the rows again, a new folder cuts the tree) and unit checks of the delta with their twins.

title: A folder's rows are read from the index by the folder's head, never the whole index
detail: LibraryIndex::under, paths_under and stamps_under query `path LIKE` the folder's ASCII head (escaped), which LIKE folds as a case-blind volume does, then trim with paths::holds; shown_under reads the folder's rows alone, a pass's lead lying beside it. unresolved reads the paths alone and drop_invented asks SQLite for the invented prints. A read and each medal no longer read 20000 rows of other folders into memory (M36). Check: the rows by head equal the whole index trimmed, accents, % and _ included, with its twin.

title: Names weighed once for every sort of the tree and the survey
detail: paths::NameKey weighs a name once for standard_order (its steps, accents and composition kept lazily); a group's photos, a folder's subfolders, the survey's children and the navigator's listing sort on keys. A path under a folder named with an accent was weighed at every comparison: 7000 such paths sorted in 560 ms, now 16 ms. The tree and the gallery's groups are cut in one walk (folders::tree_and_groups, groups_of), the entries moved rather than copied twice, and paired cuts no stem when no lone JPEG is there. Checks: the key orders every pair as standard_order, a group lies in shot's order, the groups cut with the tree are the gallery's, each with its twin.

title: A thumbnail landing reads the tile flags rather than cutting them for every photo
detail: tile_flags is cut when lay_grid lays the bands and read after, rather than rebuilt for every photo at each publish_tiles; State::selected looks its picks up in a set (M37); landed_presence keeps each path's key. On 7000 photos the thumbnail pass's interface time fell from 24.6 s to 14.1 s (dev profile, before the virtualised tree), its longest landing from 181 ms to 77 ms.

title: The roll's frames found outlive a lay that keeps them all
detail: EditorStore::set_archive_paths no longer forgets every roll's frames found at each lay_archive, which reread every sidecar (M32): a roll whose frames are all still there stays found, as Swift keeps measuredGroups; one that lost a frame is scanned again on the next ask. Check with its twin.

title: The tree's cost measured on a library of 7000 photos
detail: library::bench::tree_bench (cargo test -p oni-app --lib tree_bench -- --ignored --nocapture) times the survey, the index reads, the pairs, the tree, the groups, the row list and each event's share on 5000 photos in 200 folders, 2000 flat and 20000 rows elsewhere; window check tree_cost::the_tree_s_cost_on_a_big_folder (ONI_TREE_BENCH=1) times the interface thread's share of the read, the thumbnail pass, a read again, opening a photo, a fold and a medal in the app.

title: A Windows installer dressed as the splash
detail: packaging/windows/oni.iss (Inno Setup 6.7, dark wizard): the version's splash photograph with the logo, the version and the credit behind the welcome and finish pages, dimmed behind the others (art.py draws them from the splash folder, Inter and the logo at every DPI size). Per-user install without an administrator, all users on offer; Start menu entry, optional desktop icon, launch at the end, uninstaller; English, French, Spanish. The manual Windows package workflow builds it beside the zip, as artifacts only, and with `shots` walks its pages into pictures.

title: ONI.exe carries the app icon
detail: crates/oni-app/build.rs compiles packaging/windows/oni.ico (app-icon.png at 16 to 256 px) into the Windows executable's resources through winresource, a Windows-only build dependency; the Explorer, the taskbar and the installer show it.

title: The roll #8 checks read the roll's own reference and frames
detail: roll8 membership reads the reference the first frame names instead of a constant a re-prepared roll no longer carries; the export windows mirror only the roll's frames and marker, so a contact sheet made in the roll never takes the first tile, and say which photo opened when ⌘G misses.

title: On the Scanner face, Compare's before is the Pro face's plain conversion
detail: compare::reference renders the reset frame on the Pro face whatever the live face, so the Scanner's table and keypad show as part of the after; the same before on either face. Owner's call, beyond Swift. Check on_the_scanner_face_the_before_is_the_pro_faces_plain_conversion, its twin the bar's reset keeping the Scanner face.

title: The info sidebar's roll and project resolution in its own module
detail: organising.rs passed its 400-line ceiling once project navigation and the submenus met; roll_stock, roll and project_group move unchanged into organising/resolving.rs.

title: Auto White Balance counts in the status bar and keeps its key in place
detail: The balance key no longer gives way to a shorter progress bar, which made the panel jump: it stays, idle while the run goes, and a run lasting past 300 ms counts in the card's status bar as 'Auto white balance n/N'; a quicker one never flashes it. Check a_balance_run_counts_in_the_status_bar_once_it_outlasts_its_delay, its twins a quick run and no run.

title: A slide opens without the measuring window armed
detail: Swift's adopt arms the measuring window on any frame never balanced, inviting its measure; slides are never measured since #920, so every slide opened on the window. opening_window now leaves a positive as it stands, proposing and arming nothing; its Auto keys still read the frame's default inset window. Check in balance's opening test, its twin a fresh negative still armed.

title: The merged slides and kept balance stay under their file ceilings
detail: Merging #920 and #910-911 took rolls.rs to 429 lines and oni-decode's lib.rs to 403: the Auto levels key moves unchanged into app/rolls/levelling.rs, the 3x3 arithmetic into oni-decode/src/m3.rs. The kept balance's checks read a slide's absent roll through its option.

title: The GPU histogram checks wait for their count to land
detail: Under a loaded machine the map's callback could trail a single poll, so two display checks read no histogram and failed now and then; they poll until the count lands, bounded at 10 s. Their assertions and twins are unchanged.

title: A roll's black and white: the chroma of the frames' median, the depth of a percentile
detail: Owner's call, beyond Swift. Each end's per-channel shape is the frames' trimmed median (10 % left out each side, one at least from three frames up), moved as one block so green sits at its 20th percentile for the black and 80th for the white. One or two tinted frames no longer tint the roll, and the roll keeps its contrast; a few frames' deepest shadows clip, the Blacks slider there to take them back. A picked film base still sets the black. Checks: the roll tests, and two warm-black frames leaving the roll's black neutral, the twin the former second-extreme rule taking their tint.

title: A tooltip hides on any press and with the help it showed, so none stays stuck on screen
detail: Tips.hover hid the tip only when the text left matched the one shown, so a key whose help changed under the hand (EDITOR/GALLERY, Show/Hide Library, De-dust) or vanished under it left its old tooltip floating. The window now hides a tooltip (not a help mark's card) on every press, as AppKit does, and Button hides the tip it told when it is left or when its help changes while hovered. Checked by a_tooltip_hides_on_a_press_and_with_the_help_it_showed, with its twins (hovered again, the key shows its new help).

title: The export's W and H boxes load the owner's values again after each commit
detail: A width refused (past the full edge, or no digits) left Resize::Full, so Rust republished the same text, `changed width-value` never fired and the box kept the refused value; the height typed next was then ignored, typed_size seeing W still edited. SizeFields now reloads both boxes after `typed`, as Swift's commit calls load(shown). Checked in the_size_boxes_follow_their_owner_and_the_chip_closes_before_a_window: 8000 refused shows 96, the H typed next resizes; twin, a width the photo holds still decides.

title: A hidden column revealed by the pointer stays while its menu holds the pointer
detail: A popup takes every pointer event from the window's tree, so the revealed Library or Panel lost its hover as soon as the pointer reached its menu and slid away, the menu with it. The card is now a TouchArea, enabled while a column is revealed, whose hover says the pointer is on the card: a column left after a press in it, with the card not hovered, is held until the pointer comes back to it or meets the card. Both columns are one FloatingColumn (floating.slint). Checked by a_revealed_column_stays_while_its_menu_holds_the_pointer, with its twins (no press: hides at once; menu closed over the column: kept until left).

title: Moving from one date box to the next keeps the editing and commits nothing half typed
detail: Each DateFields box ended its editing on a press outside itself, so a click from MM to DD committed the month half typed (and could clamp the day). The sibling boxes and the hollow now count as the box's rim, one focus for the three as Swift's. Checked by a_click_from_one_date_box_to_the_next_keeps_the_date_in_editing on OutsideProbe, its twin a click beside the date committing once, whole.

title: A tab bar whose selection lies beyond its tabs, as De-dust's, shows no pill
detail: The pill's x followed `selected` alone, so De-dust's tab 4 slid it out of the four-tab bar and back. The pill hides while the selection is outside the tabs and waits where it stood, as Swift's DSTabBar draws none. Checked in a_tab_bar_bound_one_way_follows_its_owner_after_a_click, its twin the pill back under the first tab.

title: A move to a screen of another density renders the canvas and traces the plots again
detail: The logical size stays across a 1x to 2x move, so no `changed width` fired: the canvas kept its old pixel count and the plots their old rasters until the next gesture. Card publishes its density (1px / 1phx), CanvasCard calls Canvas.resized on its change, and Ctl::resized traces every plot again when the window's scale factor moved. Checked by a_screen_of_another_density_renders_the_canvas_and_the_plots_again (render, output histogram and levels at twice the pixels), its twin the same density announced again rendering nothing.

title: The phone link names each connection, so a phone's old link ending after its reconnection leaves it connected and its drag held
detail: A phone back on a new link within the desktop's SILENCE saw its old link time out afterwards: Disconnected carried only the key, so the sheet dropped the live phone, the toast said it disconnected, and Link released the new link's slider hold, splitting the drag into two undo steps. HostEvent::Connected, Command and Disconnected now carry the connection number serve already kept; Phone keeps one entry per connection (a phone is gone, and toasted, only when its last link ends; it is toasted connected only when new), and Link records the connection that holds a slider and lets go only when that one ends. Checks: a_reconnection_and_its_old_link_carry_their_own_connection (oni-link), an_old_link_ending_after_the_reconnection_leaves_the_phone_connected (phone.rs) and the_old_link_of_a_phone_back_on_a_new_one_leaves_its_drag_held (tests/link.rs), each with its twin.

title: Phone link protocol 4: clicks in half steps, and a phone of protocol 3 or older adapted by the desktop
detail: #620 made the letters count half-unit steps without raising PROTOCOL, so a phone built before it read D +2 where the desktop read +1 and its keys moved half as far. PROTOCOL is 4 (wire::HALF_STEPS); for a phone speaking less, the host halves State.clicks toward zero before sending (wire::told, as the sidecar keeps whole counts) and doubles an incoming Step.by (wire::heard), so the old phone keeps whole units both ways. A phone of protocol 4 spells the steps itself: the mobile repository's branch protocol-4 (worktree ~/Documents/oni-mobile-protocol-4, not pushed) makes ScannerText.spelled write +0.5, +1, +1.5 as oni_keys::spelled does; its keypad sends the same ±1/±3 steps as the desktop's keypad. Check: a_protocol_3_phone_reads_and_steps_whole_units, its twin a phone of protocol 4 reading and pressing steps as they are.

title: The phone link's listener survives a failed accept()
detail: Host::listen looped on `while let Ok(..) = accept()`: the first error (EMFILE, ECONNABORTED) ended the task until a restart, the sheet still showing a QR code nothing could answer. The accept loop (host::accepting) logs the error, pauses 100 ms and goes on; it stops only once the Host is dropped. Check: a_failed_accept_leaves_the_listener_serving_the_next_phone, its twin a stream accepted after the Host is gone is never answered.

title: A vanished phone is let go within SILENCE, however much the desktop publishes
detail: The 10 s silence timeout was rebuilt on each select! turn, so every published screen restarted it, and a write to a phone that stopped reading blocked the loop until TCP gave up, minutes later. The loop keeps a `heard` clock, set only by the phone's own messages, with a sleep_until(heard + SILENCE) arm, and every write to the phone is bounded by SILENCE. Check: a_vanished_phone_is_let_go_while_the_desktop_keeps_publishing (5 kB screens every 200 ms on a cut wire, paused clock), its twin the same desktop with a reading phone stays connected two minutes.

title: Forget Phones forgets a phone trusted for this session only, and a late pairing stays forgotten
detail: forget_all revoked only the keys in trusted.txt: a phone whose trust failed to write, or whose Paired event was still queued, stayed trusted in the Host's memory, connected and passing accepts_import_pin, and the late Paired then wrote it back. Host::revoke_all clears the in-memory set and bumps `revoked`; forget_all calls it; the Paired handler writes a key only while Host::trusts it. Check: revoke_all_forgets_a_phone_trusted_in_memory_only, its twin revoking another phone leaves this one trusted.

title: The phone link closes a connection unheard past 16 handshakes at once
detail: Every accepted connection held a task and a descriptor for up to 5 + 5 s before its handshake timed out, without bound. A semaphore of 16 permits (HANDSHAKES), taken before the task is spawned and dropped once the Welcome is sent, closes any connection past it at once, on TCP and on Host::serve alike. Check: a_flood_of_silent_connections_closes_the_next_until_one_ends, its twin one silent connection gone and a phone pairs.

title: The open frame's place is counted in usize: a group of 65 536 frames or more no longer panics on a phone Walk
detail: place() cast the position and the count to u16: at exactly 65 536 entries the count read 0 and walk() clamped to (0, -1), a panic on the UI thread; larger groups wrapped. place() returns usize, walk() steps with saturating usize arithmetic and stops at the ends (phone_link::walked), and only the wire's State saturates at u16::MAX (wire_place). lab::screen takes usize. Check: a_walk_in_a_group_past_the_wire_s_u16_stays_inside_it with its twin.

title: The pairing code names every interface's address, the default route's first
detail: The QR named only the default route's source address: under a full-tunnel VPN that was the tunnel's, and on a Mac with Ethernet and Wi-Fi on two networks the Ethernet one, so the phone found no address. lan_addresses lists the default route's address, then each up IPv4 interface's (getifaddrs on macOS, GetAdaptersAddresses on Windows, with windows-sys's IpHelper, Ndis and WinSock features), without loopback or link-local, four at most, as the phone dials them in turn. Checks: the_code_names_every_interface_after_the_default_route with its twin, this_computer_lists_its_default_route_first.

title: LocalSend: head and handshake timeouts, a connection cap, a bounded peer table, a policy that must decide, an upload that cannot stall
detail: The receiver built hyper without a timer, so its header_read_timeout was dropped and a silent connection was kept for ever, without bound. It now runs TokioTimer with a 10 s head timeout and closes a connection past 32 at once (receiver::Limits). A policy that has not decided in 120 s rejects, so a stranger's prompt no longer holds the session slot for ever. Discovery keeps 64 peers at most, the one heard from longest ago leaving, and answers 4 announcements at once at most. The sender's upload ends as SendError::Stalled when its body stops draining, or its answer stops coming, for 30 s. Checks: past_the_cap_a_connection_is_closed_unheard, a_connection_that_sends_no_request_is_closed, a_flood_of_announcements_keeps_the_table_bounded_and_the_peers_heard_lately, an_upload_to_a_peer_that_stops_reading_ends_as_stalled, each with its twin. The policy's timeout has no check of its own, and the demo's stdin prompt is unchanged.

title: The phone inbox refuses a received sidecar, roll marker or dot name
detail: A peer could send DSC_0001.NEF.json or .oni-roll.json into a folder holding DSC_0001.NEF, and the file became the original's settings or the folder's roll marker, read as the truth on the next open. inbox::refused_name refuses a sanitised name that starts with a dot or ends in .json (ROLL_MARKER is both), and prepare-upload leaves such files out before the policy sees them, answering 204 when none is left. Checks: a_sidecar_a_roll_marker_or_a_dot_name_is_refused and a_sidecar_or_a_roll_marker_sent_beside_an_original_is_left_out, each with its twin.

title: A disk that stops answering never freezes the interface through the refused folders' lock
detail: The volumes thread filtered nav.refused under its guard, so read_dir on a hung SMB mount held the mutex the interface takes in publish_navigator, at every MOUNTS tick. The list is copied out and probed with the lock free. Check a_refused_folder_is_probed_with_the_lock_free (twin: the list filtered under its guard finds the lock taken).

title: Two reads of the opened folder at once land only the latest
detail: read_again reused the current generation, so a Refresh, the settle timer, a volume back or Locate during a read ran two reads that both landed: an older survey could land last, read_done flipped back and fill, tidy and open ran twice. Each folder read takes a ticket; a later read stops the earlier at its next alive() and its landings are dropped, the generation, and with it the thumbnails' pass, left alone. Window check two_refreshes_at_once_land_only_the_latest_read (twin: two Refreshes one after the other land whole twice).

title: Edit Together decodes of a group left give their place to the next group's
detail: A decoder thread checked GROUPS only before taking a path, then waited in decode_gate::slot() and decoded for a group gone, ahead of the current tiles and of a photo opened next. decode_gate::only_while sets a thread's predicate; slot() gives the place back when it no longer holds, and tile_source checks the group again before laying the tile. Check a_decode_superseded_while_it_waits_takes_no_place (twin: one still wanted takes its place).

title: A roll mask still decoding when its roll is left lands on no other roll
detail: roll_mask_taken and roll_mask_loaded wrote r.flat with no check of the roll, so a mask asked in one roll landed on the next one entered. Both landings compare the roll shown, by its frames, with the one asked; a measure that leaves the roll open keeps its mask. Window check in prepare_masks: a load held by a pipe until R2 shows leaves R2 bare (twin: the same load with R2 shown names the panel).

title: A folder read superseded after its survey removes no index row
detail: read_rows removed every row its survey did not list without checking alive(), so a read in flight erased the rows a New Roll move had just rewritten under their new names. The removal pass checks alive() before each row. Check a_read_superseded_after_its_survey_removes_no_row (twin: a read still alive drops the row).

title: The previous photo's histograms never show on the next
detail: A trace asked before clear() (no inputs for the new photo, or a failed render) still landed after it. Each slot counts its clears; a trace lands only when no clear came since its ask, its texture let go with the clear. Check a_trace_asked_before_a_clear_lands_nowhere (twins: the slot not cleared, and a trace asked after the clear, land).

title: One writer at a time per sidecar across the app
detail: set_exif after an export and the Prepare draft queue read a sidecar then wrote it back, so the store's debounced flush landing between them was overwritten with older settings. sidecar::write and every read-modify-write helper (update, set_label, set_exif, set_roll_draft, set_trashed) hold the sidecar's own lock from the read to the rename. Check a_field_set_waits_for_the_write_holding_its_sidecar (twin: another photo's sidecar is free).

title: An original re-dated by a tool keeps its sidecar; a new sheet never inherits a sidecar left behind
detail: A scan whose date exiftool set right by rewriting it differed in date and digest, so its sidecar was set aside as an orphan. Each write now stores originalTail, the digest of the last block, Rust's own key as originalPrint is; a last block alike is the same photo, and a block of under 64 byte values (a scan's black or clipped bottom rows) stores none, so namesakes ending alike stay foreign. A new contact sheet also counts a name as taken when its sidecar exists, so it never takes a trashed sheet's medal or mark. Checks an_original_whose_date_a_tool_set_right_by_rewriting_it_keeps_its_sidecar (twins: another photo of that name, and another scan ending in black, stay foreign) and a_sheet_never_takes_the_name_of_a_sidecar_left_behind (twin: a free name is taken).

title: The thumbnail sweep waits a day after the index's rows were thrown away
detail: tidy::settled read only the index file's birth, so after a schema drop in an old file the first read's few rows decided the sweep and up to SWEPT tiles of other folders were deleted. The index dates each creation of its photos table in a rebuilt table the Swift app never reads; settled uses it, the file's birth standing in for an index never dated. Checks a_schema_drop_dates_the_rebuild_and_a_plain_open_keeps_its_date and the_sweep_waits_on_the_rebuild_date_not_the_file_birth (twin: dated now, it has not settled).

title: A folder rename waits for a disk gesture and never replaces a folder; a trash row acts on the folder it showed
detail: rename_folder ran without busy_said, so a folder could be renamed under a running move or mark; it is refused and said now. Its rename looked for the target then renamed plainly, which replaces an empty folder made meanwhile: rename_new (RENAME_EXCL) renames, a change of case alone plainly. The ONI Trash's folder rows resolved their index against the trash cut anew (a tidy prune reads it without republishing); each row's folder is kept as published. Checks a_rename_waits_for_a_move_under_way (window; twin: once landed the rename goes through), a_rename_never_replaces_a_folder_made_meanwhile (twin: a plain rename replaces it) and a_trash_row_names_the_folder_it_showed (twin: the index read anew names another folder).

title: Entering export reads each scan's head alone, and its lines land from a thread of their own
detail: Entering export built every line on the interface thread, and each line without a typed box read the whole RAW for its Exif: 36 NEF were about 1.8 GB before the surface showed. The scan's Exif is now read from the file's head (1 MB, grown fourfold only while a directory or a value runs past it; a container through a buffered reader), and the lines are read on an 'export rows' thread of their own generation, landing one by one; the roll of each target comes from one map of the archive instead of a search per target. A write started before every line landed reads the rest at once. Checks: a_scan_s_facts_come_from_its_head_alone (roll #8 and the S1R RW2s: 1 MB of 30 to 70 MB read, the same facts as the whole file; twin: a 4 KB head grows, and parsed as it is lacks the lens) and the window check entering_the_export_reads_no_scan_on_the_interface_thread (2 frames: no line is read when enter_export returns, then both land; twin: read on the interface thread, the same lines are there at once).

title: CR3, RAF and ORF exports state their camera, lens, ISO and date, read by LibRaw
detail: The Exif reader opens TIFF, JPEG, PNG, HEIF and WebP only, so a CR3, RAF or ORF line opened empty and its file was written with no date. A RAW the reader cannot open now asks LibRaw through a new oni_describe shim beside oni_identify (maker, model, EXIF lens, artist, ISO; nothing decoded), and its date is the DateTimeOriginal the file stores, read by oni-settings' header reader. LibRaw names the maker its own way (Fujifilm, not FUJIFILM). Check: a_cr3_raf_or_orf_states_its_camera_lens_iso_and_date under ONI_RAW_DIR, skipped when none is there (run on a Fujifilm X-E4 RAF; twin: the Exif reader alone opens none of them).

title: An export holds one float frame at its peak
detail: resized took the frame by reference and cloned it at full size, and the shadowed binding kept the render alive to the end of the write: two float frames (768 MB at 24 Mpx) plus the quantised copy grown by doubling. resized now takes the frame by value and hands it back untouched at full size, the float frame is dropped once converted, and both quantised buffers are sized once. Checks: full_scale_hands_back_the_same_pixels_without_a_copy (twin: a reduction is a frame of its own) and an_export_holds_one_float_frame_at_its_peak, counted by the test binary's allocator on a 96 MB frame: 156 MB, under 1.75 frames (twin: a second frame held through the export breaks the bound; the code before this change fails it).

title: A profile export premultiplies alpha, so a clear pixel writes black
detail: OutputProfile::converted forced alpha to 1 without scaling the colour, so a contact sheet's clear gutters exported through a Custom profile came out in whatever colour the chain left there, where the matrix spaces write black as Core Image does. The band is now premultiplied before the profile's legs. Check: a_clear_pixel_converts_to_black_through_a_profile (twin: the same colour opaque converts far from black).

title: A JPEG past its format's limits says so
detail: A JPEG wider or taller than 65,535 pixels, or with a profile past the 254 APP2 segments the encoder takes (16.6 MB), failed with 'The file could not be written.' The write now checks jpeg::fits after the resize and returns Failure::TooLargeForJpeg, whose message names the limits, in French and Spanish too. Checks: a_frame_fits_up_to_the_format_s_own_limits (twin: one past any limit is refused, as the encoder refuses it) and a_frame_past_a_jpeg_s_side_says_so (65,536 px refused with its own message; twin: 65,535 px writes a JPEG).

title: A typed name starting with a dot no longer writes a hidden file
detail: name() trimmed only trailing dots, so '.Frame 3' or '..\x' wrote a file macOS hides. Leading dots and blanks are now dropped after the name is made portable, the original's name taking over when nothing is left; a dot inside the name stays. The Swift app writes the same hidden file. Check: a_typed_name_stays_in_the_chosen_folder (twin: 'Frame.3' keeps its dot, and portable alone still yields a hidden name).

title: A profile replaced at its path is read again
detail: The parsed profiles and the proof cubes were cached by path alone, so an .icc overwritten in the Finder kept exporting and proofing with the old one until relaunch. Both caches now hold the file's length and modification time and rebuild when either changes. Check: a_profile_replaced_at_its_path_is_read_again (twin: untouched, the same parse and cube are handed back).

title: The console reads only the log's new lines, off the interface thread, and shows its last 4000
detail: Every 500 ms the console waited on the log's flush (up to 2 s) and read the whole oni.log on the interface thread, then laid out all of it, so a long session stuttered while it was open. A Tail now reads the bytes written since its last read on a thread of its own, keeps Swift's Diagnostics.ceiling of 4000 lines (a first read starts 1 MiB from the end on a whole line), and sets the text only when lines came. Checks the_console_reads_only_what_came_and_keeps_the_last_lines (twin: a log started again is read from its start) and a_first_read_of_a_long_log_starts_near_its_end_on_a_whole_line (twin: the read began inside a line).

title: A start that fails writes its cause to the log and says it in a window of the system's
detail: main returned its error to Rust's runtime, which prints it on stderr: a windowed Windows build or an app opened from the Finder showed nothing and the log stopped after its first line. main now runs the start in run(); an error is written as 'fatal: ...', flushed, then said by rfd's alert with the log's path (not under a bench or ONI_BACKGROUND), and the process ends with 1. WGPU_BACKEND is now honoured, so a backend the system lacks stands for a refused device. Check a_start_that_fails_writes_its_cause_to_the_log_and_ends (tests/instance.rs; twin: the system's own backend passes the device and goes on) and a_failed_start_writes_its_cause_before_the_process_ends (twin: a child ending otherwise has no fatal line).

title: A panic is written to the log with its thread, place and backtrace
detail: No panic hook existed, so a panic left its words on a stderr no one reads (windowed Windows build, Finder launch) and never in oni.log or the sealed bug report. timing::keep_panics, installed once the log file is open, writes the thread, the message with its place and a forced backtrace, flushes (except on the log thread itself), then runs the default hook. Check a_panic_is_written_to_the_log_and_still_said_on_stderr, run in a child process of the test binary (twin: the same panic under the default hook alone leaves the log without it).

title: Windows: renaming a folder lets every watch go while it runs
detail: ReadDirectoryChangesW holds a handle on each watched folder, and Windows refuses to rename a folder with a handle on it or below it: renaming a parent of the opened folder in the navigator failed with 'another app is using it'. Watch::released lets every watch go, answered by the watching thread, until its guard drops, then watches what was asked meanwhile; rename_folder runs its rename inside Ctl::unwatched. Explorer renames and Safely Remove are not covered: DBT_DEVICEQUERYREMOVE is a window message sent to a window procedure winit owns (its message hook sees posted messages only), so it needs a window of ONI's own, a subclass of winit's, or CM_Register_Notification per volume, none of which builds or runs on the Mac. Checks a_release_lets_every_watch_go_and_its_end_watches_what_was_asked_meanwhile (twin: a resume with no release changes nothing) and a_photo_dropped_while_the_watches_are_released_is_not_told (twin: told again once the release ends).

title: Windows: a watch whose buffer overflows tells a rescan and reads on
detail: In the vendored notify, a ReadDirectoryChangesW completion with ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR (1022) ended the watch for the session, and one of zero bytes (the buffer discarded) parsed a zeroed entry and told nothing, so a bulk copy into the opened folder was missed. The decision is now notify::rdcw_completion::completion, compiled on every system: 1022 or zero bytes tell an Event flagged Rescan on the folder and start the next read; its codes are asserted equal to windows-sys's at compile time. Check an_overflow_on_windows_is_a_rescan_of_the_folder_and_the_read_goes_on (oni-library; twin: a read with bytes is parsed, an unknown error still ends the watch, and the same path as a plain change touches nothing).

title: Windows: sidecar, preference, index-side and export writes wait out a file held for a moment
detail: write_atomically in oni-settings and oni-library and the export's create and replace renamed once, so an antivirus or a cloud client holding the target or the temporary (errors 5, 32, 33) failed the save, the last flush at quit included. oni_settings::atomic::retried, with the half-second PAUSES, now carries the rule roll_folder::retried used for folder moves (which delegates to it), and every one of these renames goes through atomic::renamed. Check a_file_held_for_a_moment_on_windows_is_written_once_it_is_let_go, the hold simulated by an injected rename (twins: held past every pause, a missing folder, and the same violation off Windows fail at once and leave no temporary).

title: Windows: the GPU is opened on DirectX 12
detail: wgpu::Instance::default() enables every backend, and wgpu tries Vulkan and GL before DirectX 12, so a PC with a Vulkan driver ran an untested path while the checks ran WARP on DX12. The instance now asks DX12 on Windows and the default elsewhere, WGPU_BACKEND naming another for a try. Check windows_runs_on_directx_12_unless_a_backend_is_named (twin: wgpu's default holds Vulkan and GL). The unwrap on the surface configuration in the vendored femtovg stays: it needs an adapter that cannot present, and the panic is now logged (#752).

title: Windows: a two-finger touchpad scroll on the image pans
detail: winit reports a precision touchpad on Windows as LineDelta in fractions of a line, which the window hook took for a wheel, and a wheel zooms. viewport::lines takes a fractional line on Windows for a touch surface, in Slint's 60 points a line; a whole notch stays a wheel's. Check a_fraction_of_a_line_on_windows_is_a_touch_surface_that_pans (twin: a whole notch zooms, and a Mac's fractional lines stay a wheel's).

title: Windows: the drive probe raises no 'No Disk' window, and the executable carries a manifest
detail: Computer's rows probe A: to Z:, and an empty card reader or optical drive could raise the system's critical-error window; each probe thread now sets SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS and SEM_NOOPENFILEERRORBOX for itself. build.rs embeds a manifest beside the icon: longPathAware for the Win32 calls std does not prefix, Common Controls 6 for rfd's dialogs, asInvoker; per-monitor DPI awareness v2 is left to winit, which sets it when its event loop starts. Neither builds on the Mac: the probe's code was checked for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc in a scratch crate, the manifest parsed as XML.

title: Diagnostics: bounded timing samples, no zombie helpers, a paper download kept in its folder, a log that outlives stderr
detail: The notch, view, histogram and publish samples grew for the whole run; each now keeps its last 10 000 (the oldest half dropped), counts and session indices still whole (check a_long_session_keeps_a_bounded_tail_and_its_whole_count). open and explorer were spawned and dropped, leaving a zombie per Reveal or link; system::launched waits for each on a thread (check a_helper_program_leaves_no_zombie_once_it_ends; twin: a dropped child stays listed). A paper download took the link's decoded last segment as its name, so %5C or C: led outside its scratch folder on Windows; it is now file_names::portable inside the folder (check a_download_lands_inside_its_folder_whatever_the_link_spells; twin: a plain name is kept). The log thread's eprintln! panicked on a closed stderr and ended the log; it, the instance refusal and the lock warning now write and ignore the error.

title: A pasted preset code inflates to 1 MB at most
detail: from_share_code inflated the whole deflate stream before the checksum or the JSON could refuse it, so a short pasted code of zero runs claimed hundreds of MB to GB on the interface thread (deflate reaches about 1000:1). The inflate now stops at MAX_SHARE_JSON + 1 byte (1 MiB) and a JSON past the cap is refused. Check a_code_inflating_past_the_cap_is_refused_and_one_under_it_reads (a code under 10 KB inflating past 1 MiB, valid JSON and checksum, is refused; twin: the same code 1000 bytes under the cap reads). The Swift app inflates without a cap too.

title: The journal's name table numbers a new name by the file's lines
detail: index numbered a new name by the count of distinct names, so once names.txt held a duplicate line (a name with a newline is written with a space, then noted again in that spelling) every later name took another name's line. A new name is now the file's next line, the table is keyed by the written spelling, and a name whose line cannot be written records NOTHING. Check a_new_name_takes_the_file_s_next_line_past_a_duplicate (a table with a duplicate line, a name with a newline then its spelt form; twin: the distinct-name count lands on the duplicate). The Swift journal numbers the same way as before.

title: A .cube on a domain other than 0 to 1 is refused
detail: The Frontier table reader skipped every DOMAIN_ line, so a cube on another domain was sampled as if on display code 0 to 1, every colour at the wrong node. DOMAIN_MIN must now read 0 0 0 and DOMAIN_MAX 1 1 1, else the file is refused with its line. Check a_cube_on_another_domain_is_refused_and_one_on_zero_to_one_reads (1.2 max, a negative min, two values refused; twin: the domain ONI writes, spelt as 0 or 0.0, reads).

title: A contact-sheet grid without columns or rows lays no cell
detail: sheet_cells divided by grid.columns, so a sidecar grid of 0 columns panicked on the measuring thread when Auto was pressed; a huge frame count iterated without end. A grid without rows or columns lays nothing, and frames stop at columns x rows, past which every cell fell below the extent anyway. Check a_sheet_grid_without_columns_or_rows_lays_no_cell (0 columns, 0 rows, -1 columns; twin: a 3 x 2 grid lays its six, and 1000 or i64::MAX frames lay the same six).

title: An ISO date whose zone holds a non-ASCII character is refused, not a panic
detail: parse_iso8601 sliced the six-byte zone at byte 3, which panicked inside a two-byte character (2023-11-14T22:13:20+0é00), on any sidecar or preferences read. The colon is compared as a byte. Check a_zone_with_a_non_ascii_character_is_refused (parse and serde both refuse; twin: +00:00 reads).

title: The window checks on roll #8 close the RAW recalibration notice before they reach behind it
detail: A first launch on a library holding a RAW raises the neutral decode notice, a sheet: every menu goes dark under it, so ⌘G after a tile click opened nothing (export_window, export_paper_window), the bar's undo read false after a drag (headless) and the pointer never reached the base loupe (prepare_loupe with ONI_RAW_DIR). The app is right, the sheet is modal as Swift's; the checks close it. export_window asserts the notice is up and its twin that ⌘G under it opens nothing; prepare_loupe that RAWs raise it and TIFFs do not.

title: The roll #8 window mirrors lay the state their checks read
detail: auto_balance's mirror takes the first frame's balance off, so its twin (no press before the key) holds whatever the roll was left with; headless's mirror sets every medal to none and DSC_6435 on the Scanner face, so the medal keys and the Scanner-face twin never read the roll's own labels and faces.

title: The roll #8 sidecar copies stand beside stand-ins, as a write leaves them
detail: oni-core roll8, oni-measure roll_prepare and the phone link copy the sidecars beside empty stand-ins (roll_prepare and the link wrote none, and a write is refused beside a missing original) and write each once, so the print a write stamps (originalPrint) is in the bytes before a gesture: the byte-for-byte undo checks compare the gesture's own writes. roll_prepare lays the base-step draft on the frame its measure leaves out instead of reading one off the roll.

title: The real sidecar checks read the roll in Swift's form and lay the envelope they need
detail: real_files drops this app's own originalPrint line before comparing a roll #8 sidecar with the codec's Swift document (a roll touched by this app carried it), and its copies are written once beside their stand-in with no medal, the camera's lines and a base-step draft, so the read-write, label, trash and draft checks no longer need a roll still holding Swift's drafts.

title: Two sidecars agree on numbers one f32 ulp apart, whatever their decimal spelling
detail: semantic_difference compared the decimals as f64, where two neighbouring f32s spelt shortest lie up to 1.7 ulps apart (-1.0909756 against -1.0909758), so the one-ulp twin of real_files failed on DSC_6442's red gain. Each number is read as the f32 it stores. Check neighbouring_f32s_spelt_shortest_are_rounding (one ulp forgiven; twin: two ulps seen), with or without the roll.

title: oni-demos films the help cards' demos: coded scenes of the real controls over the real render, written as small looping GIFs
detail: A new crate, crates/oni-demos, and scripts/demos. Each demo is a Demo (film.rs): a scene in scenes/<topic>.slint built from the design system's own components (Slider, Button, FrameOverlay, Picture), compiled by oni-lab's interpreter machinery (oni-lab now has a library: compile, pick, serve, Raster, Headless with a clock), shown on a headless software window at 2 px a point on a clock that moves only when a frame is shot, and driven by the pointer's real events; the photograph is a frame of roll #8 through the app's own engine (Engine.render on the preview, Engine.unproofed on the full decode for a 1:1 detail), at settings held in the crate (scenes/DSC_*.json, never the roll's sidecars); Auto White Balance's values come from measuring::balance_outcomes. The hand is drawn over each shot (cursor.rs). encode.rs writes the GIF: one palette (interface colours exact, photograph and interface gradients learnt apart by NeuQuant), each frame only where it changed, a photograph's pixel redrawn only past a tolerance, the smaller of transparent or opaque per frame. 20 fps, 488 px square, no text. Checks: the same frames give the same bytes (twin: a pixel moved gives other bytes), the interface plays back exact (twin: a frame a step late is seen), a film of the roll shot twice is the same GIF (twin: other packing, other bytes).

title: Three help cards play a demo above their note: Sharpening, Auto White Balance and Crop
detail: Section.demo names a help topic, which the help mark hands to Tip.demo on hover; TipLayer calls Tip.play with the topic while the card is open and with none when it closes. oni_app::demos maps a topic to its GIF (resources/demos/<topic>.gif, include_bytes!); app/help/clip.rs decodes it frame by frame on a thread of its own with the tutorials' Frames and lays each frame on Tip.clip at its own delay, stopped with the card. The card's 4:3 skeleton box became a square demo box, laid only when the topic has a demo (Tip.has-clip). Checks: each demo weighs at most 300 KB (twin: a file a byte past is caught), is square, runs on 20 fps steps and loops; window check help_demo: the Sharpening mark's card plays and its frame advances; twin: the Chroma Denoise mark shows no clip box and leaving a mark stops the clip. help_card's short-window part now opens a card with a demo, the only tall one. TipCard and TipLayer moved from ds/base.slint to ds/tip.slint, base.slint staying under the 400-line ceiling.

title: oni-demos films scenes of sliders and editors: shared scene parts, the editors' drawings laid by the app's own code, a print proofed on a paper
detail: scenes/parts.slint holds the parts the Color demos share: Row (a Slider the hand drags, saying where its knob stands), Slides (the frame over two rows) and Edited (the frame over a Plot, square or wide, with or without its grid). A scene file re-exports its part under the part's own name, as the interpreter finds no alias. demos/slides.rs drags two rows in turn; demos/editing.rs replays strokes on a plot through an Editor (the app's curve::press and drag, spectrogram::grab and dragged, saturation::Presses), plot.rs turns the app's Drawing into the scene's PlotLine and PlotDot models, and Photo::proof lays a paper's proof as the canvas does. Each picture is rendered in two steps along a move, as each costs a GIF a redrawn photograph.

title: The Color tab's help cards play their demos: Paper Correction, Lighting, Effects, Curves, Spectrogram Finishing, Saturation Curve
detail: Six GIFs in crates/oni-app/resources/demos, 5.5 to 5.6 s, 153 to 282 KB: the automatic paper key springs the three gains to oni_colour::paper::automatic on an installed paper profile (ILFORD CANpro-300, the strongest correction among those installed); Exposure then Shadows dragged right; Contrast then Vignette; a curve point raised in the middle then one lowered in the shadows; the blue band turned toward aqua then the green pulled out; the saturation curve's middle raised and its highlights lowered. oni_app::demos maps the topics, TOPICS becomes a slice, and the Color tab's blocks name them with demo:. The Scanner face's Effects keeps no demo: its keys are not the sliders filmed. Every frame of roll #8 is a stand-in, each demo naming the kind of picture it needs.

title: Checks for the Color tab's demos: their marks play them, every mark's topic ships, every film is played
detail: Window check help_demo_color: the Lighting mark opens a card playing the lighting clip whose frame advances; twin: the Effects mark, scrolled up by the wheel, names its own topic and shows another picture. oni_app::demos: every demo: a .slint mark names has a clip and every clip has its mark (twin: a mark naming a topic never filmed is caught); the size, square and 20 fps checks run over every topic. oni-demos: every demo filmed is one the app plays (twin: a topic none films is absent). Two films of the six give the same bytes.

title: Help-card demos for Chroma Denoise and Texture: one slider's demo, shared
detail: oni-demos gains OneSlider (demos/slider.rs): a Spec names the topic, the frame and its settings, the field, the detail's centre and zoom, where the knob starts and the stops the hand drags it through; the picture is rendered at a few levels along the track, magnified past one to one when the effect is finer (photo::magnified, bilinear). Chroma Denoise goes from 0 to its most and back on a dark flat tone at twice one to one; Texture from its rest to its most, to its least and back on skin and fabric at one to one. Both scenes are the pilot's Sharpening scene re-exported (scenes/chroma-denoise.slint, texture.slint). Check: magnified keeps each pixel at its centre and mixes between (twin: a nearest-pixel scale jumps).

title: Help-card demo for Dust & Scratches: the hand paints over a speck, the app's own heal patches it
detail: demos/dust.rs and scenes/dust.slint: a detail of the frame three times one to one under the brush's Ring, the Brush Size slider beneath; the hand scrubs over a speck, the live Trace follows it, then the patch made by Engine::search_region and heal::generate (photo/heal.rs, written to a temporary caches folder this engine alone reads, removed at once) lands, with the CorrectionMark, the copied stroke and the dashed line to it, as the canvas draws them. Info sidebar: Film Stock, Shot Date, Camera Body and Film Stocks get no demo, their notes saying what a field never does (guessed, read off EXIF, a capture date, counted by roll), which no wordless clip shows; Roll, Project, Straighten, Rotate & Mirror and Measuring Window have no help mark.

title: The demos' checks cover the new topics; a window check plays the Dust & Scratches demo and finds no clip on the Film Stock card
detail: oni_app::demos: TOPICS is a slice holding chroma-denoise, texture and dust, each within 300 KB, square, at 20 fps and looping. Window check help_demo_details: the gallery's Info sidebar Film Stock mark opens a card naming no topic with no clip box; the editor's Dust & Scratches mark names dust and its frame advances, its card a square box taller than the Film Stock's. The pilot's help_demo, whose twin hovered Chroma Denoise, now asserts that mark plays its own demo (renamed a_help_mark_with_a_demo_plays_it_and_leaving_stops_it).

title: oni-demos films seven Roll tab demos: Measured Roll, Film Type, Flat-Field, Source Encoding, Density Ceiling, Dye Separation, Balance Strength
detail: Shared scenes in scenes/roll-parts.slint: SlideBody (a photograph, what a scene lays under it, the slider the hand drags) with PhotoSlider, PhotoTabs (three unnamed tabs) and PhotoToggle (the switch alone); Slint's interpreter shows no inherited property, so a scene with more forwards SlideBody's properties and the plain ones re-export the shared window under its own name. Shared gestures in demos/gesture.rs: Drag (the knob taken to a mark and back, the picture rendered at each step crossed) and Clicks (the hand clicking each aim at its second). Density Ceiling and Dye Separation are one Slide each, from the track's start to its end. Balance Strength reads Auto White Balance on a frame given a cool cast through Source Balance and doses its correction as Strength rises, Temperature and Tint following. Measured Roll moves Source Balance's Blue ↔ Yellow on this photo and three others of the roll. Film Type reads the frame as each mode carries it (parameters::carried). Source Encoding stands the decode for a linear unprofiled scan and reads it through oni_colour's Source as sRGB, Linear and Display P3. Flat-Field lights the decode with the shipped Valoi panel's fall-off and turns the flat-field on at the same Amount. Photo::restage re-lays a preview changed before the engine sees it. Each demo names the kind of photograph it needs beside its frame. Per-Channel Levels has no help mark, in Swift as here, so it has no demo. Sizes: 208 to 294 KB, 5 to 6 s.

title: The Roll tab's help cards play their demos
detail: roll_tab.slint names a demo on each of its seven helped blocks; oni_app::demos maps the seven topics to their GIFs. Checks: every topic a mark names has its GIF and every GIF a mark (twin: the reader finds film-type and not per-channel-levels, which has no mark); each demo stays under 300 KB, square, at 20 fps and loops; window check help_demo_roll: the Film Type mark's card plays and its frame advances, leaving the mark stops it; twin: the Measured Roll mark plays another clip, so a card shows its own topic's.

title: The info sidebar guides photos outside any roll into one, and an unmeasured roll offers Prepare the Roll
detail: Owner's design, beyond Swift. On the archive, a selection whose anchor resolves no roll shows a guide in place of Select a roll: the selection and its folders counted, a name prefilled with New Roll's date, the stock picker on a new target (StockTarget::Guide), and one key. The whole folder selected: Make this folder a roll writes the marker with the name and stock and the stock's dyes on its frames, one gallery step (a roll marker is now part of a gallery step, Marker in gallery_history, written and walked back by the store), no file moved. Part of it: Move into a new roll runs New Roll under that name (roll_folder::plan_named, numbered past a taken name) and stock, its confirm first, no rename asked in the tree; the dyes follow as a step of their own after the move. Photos of several folders disable the key with New Roll's reason. A roll no frame of which carries a rollReference, read off the interface thread and read again after every gesture, tops its card with Not measured yet and PREPARE THE ROLL…, the toolbar's Prepare Roll on the roll's frames. Window check photos_outside_a_roll_are_guided_into_one_and_its_stock_writes_their_dyes, with its twins (the roll card inside a roll, Move into a new roll on part of a folder, the banner gone once a frame is measured).

title: A roll's stock writes the dye family it names on every frame of the roll
detail: Owner's design, beyond Swift. film::STOCK_DYES maps every stock of FILM_STOCKS (as long as the catalogue, so a new stock cannot go unmapped) and dye_family reads it: Kodak C-41, Fuji C-41, ECN-2, E-6, generic C-41, none for black and white. Picking a roll's stock writes the marker (or the members' sidecar roll) and the family on every frame in one gallery step (EditorStore::lay_roll), a family picked by hand overwritten and the dose kept; a black-and-white stock writes no family. The open frame takes it at once, its Dyes tabs with it; the roll card notes Dyes: <family> under the stock. Checks every_stock_names_its_dyes (twin: an unknown key names none), a_roll_made_with_its_stock_writes_the_marker_and_the_families_and_undoes_as_one_step (twin: a frame outside the roll keeps its family; the marker alone is a step too) and the window check of #830.

title: Every help-card demo is filmed from the owner's photograph; no roll #8 frame or setting remains
detail: oni-demos reads one photograph, ONI_DEMO_PHOTO or the owner's Lumix RW2 scan on the T7 disk, read-only (photo::source); its sidecar's settings are copied into scenes/P1071951.json (photo::base) and nothing is ever written beside it. Each demo frames or changes it in memory: photo::framed keeps its left three quarters, the details are crops of it, Measured Roll's other photos are three framings of it, Balance Strength and White Balance lay their cast, Dust paints a real hair on the red sail. The eleven roll #8 settings files and the Demo::frame of each demo are gone. Without the photograph, oni-demos and scripts/demos say so and stop; the film check skips. Photo::cover renders again a little larger when the engine's rounding leaves the picture a pixel short of its box, which had letterboxed the flat-field demo.

title: The demos are drawn by the app's own FemtoVG renderer: round rail ends, clean tabs and toggles
detail: Slint 1.18's software renderer fills a linear gradient over its whole rectangle, ignoring the corner radius, and draws no drop shadow: every bipolar rail bled its colours past its round ends, and the tabs' and the toggle's raised pill showed a light square around it. The app draws with FemtoVG, which has neither fault, so the DS needed no change. stage.rs now gives the scene a window of its own (Offscreen) drawn by slint's FemtoVGWGPURenderer into a texture on the app's GPU device and read back by take_snapshot, the clock still the film's.

title: Demo scenes on one grid: the controls just under the photograph, rows aligned as the panel's
detail: scenes/parts.slint: Scene lays the photograph over the scene's controls Space.s apart, the photograph taking all the room they leave, so no gap is left between them; Row is a DS Slider without its readout (Slider.header, a new DS property defaulting to true, as a demo shows no words); Keyed lays a key's room, its key when asked, then a Row centred on the key's middle, so a key and a slider share a baseline and every slider starts at one left edge with one width (White Balance, Paper Correction); Balance Strength, Lighting and Effects stack full-width rows Space.xs apart. The per-scene windows forward the photograph's box, as an interpreted window's base hides its properties. roll-parts.slint is folded into parts.slint.

title: Each demo shows an obvious change: the picture follows the knob step by step, a double click brings it back
detail: A slider's demo now drags the knob from its rest, lets go, then double-clicks it as the panel's sliders take a double click: the value back to rest at once and, the second press answered as a double click (Row.double), the knob springing home (gesture::Drag, demos::slider); the picture follows in 4 to 16 renders along the drag, more where the change is cheap to draw. Views chosen where the effect lives: Sharpening, Texture and Chroma Denoise on details zoomed two and three times (the grating, the sand), Chroma's radius at its widest; Density Ceiling lowered to its least; Strength lowered to none so a yellow cast returns; Vignette darkening the bright corner; Crop tilted a few degrees; White Balance cast warm and green so both knobs travel; the spectrogram's yellow turned toward green and its red pulled out on a larger wheel; the saturation curve's shadows lowered so the red sail greys; a curve point's press redrawing the photograph at once; Source Encoding starting read right on its two named tabs; Flat-Field lit by the panel's fall-off with the photograph's own correction off; Paper Correction framed on the cream sail and the cap. The edits a loop undoes are undone just before it starts again, the springs settled by the seam. The hand's press disc is smaller. Dye Separation and Paper Correction change this photograph little by nature: their demos show the most they can.

title: Demo GIFs pack obvious changes under 400 KB: interface colours counted off the photograph, gradients dithered
detail: encode.rs: the exact interface colours are counted where the photograph is not, so a large even tone of the photograph stays loose within the tolerance instead of forcing a redraw on every step (density ceiling 609 KB to 294 KB at the same steps); the interface's greys, keys and knobs, map onto a ramp of 40 greys of their own, so no learnt colour tints them; its colourful shades are learnt apart, each weighed by the root of its count, and dithered by place on a 4 x 4 ordered pattern, so a rail's gradient runs smooth. The ceiling rises from 300 to 400 KB (oni_app::demos::CEILING), the owner's allowance for following steps; each demo's tolerance, palette and step count are set against it (largest 377 KB).

title: Demos showing words are filmed in English, French and Spanish and play in the app's language
detail: Film Type's and Source Encoding's tabs carry their names, from the app's own catalogues (oni_i18n::tr). Demo::worded marks them; oni-demos films them once per language into <topic>.gif, <topic>.fr.gif and <topic>.es.gif (oni_app::demos::file). oni_app::demos::clip plays the clip of the language the app speaks, clip_in falling back to English for a demo without words; WORDED lists them. Checks: every clip of every language weighs at most 400 KB, is square, at 20 fps, and loops; a worded topic has its own film per language (twin: Lighting plays the English film in French); the demos filmed per language are those the app plays per language (twin: Lighting is filmed once); window check help_demo_language: in French Film Type's card plays the French film and not the English one; twin: back in English, the English film (the check fails with the language ignored).

title: A context menu's submenu opens beside it as the pointer rests on its line, as AppKit's
detail: Add to Project and Remove from Project replaced the menu's lines on a click. The DS Menu now lays the submenu in a second panel beside the menu, in the same popup: it opens after MenuStyle.sub-delay (200 ms) with the pointer at rest on its line, at once on a click or →; another line at rest closes or swaps it, ← closes it, the arrows and Return walk and pick; a pointer heading for it (inside the cone from its last point to the submenu's near corners) keeps it open across the lines it crosses; it sits level with its opener, turns to the menu's left at the window's edge (Bounds, the window's size kept by AppWindow) and stays inside its bottom. The popup places itself from its owner's anchor-x, a turned submenu moving its origin left, and reports its state through state-changed. To stay under the 400-line ceiling, Picker moves to ds/picker.slint, AppWindow to ds/window.slint, the tree's row structs to library_rows.slint and the gallery check's hand to gallery/hand.rs. Rust lays the submenu on Library.menu-opened and acts on Library.menu-sub-chosen. Checks on SubmenuProbe: a_submenu_opens_on_the_pointer_at_rest_and_closes_on_another_line (twins: a plain line opens nothing, nothing before the rest), a_pointer_heading_for_the_submenu_keeps_it_open_across_other_lines (twins: the same sweep mirrored away closes it, the diagonal stopped on a plain line closes it), a_click_or_the_arrow_opens_a_submenu_at_once_and_it_turns_at_the_window_s_edge (twins: a plain line's click or → opens nothing, the middle of the window keeps it right); the gallery check rests the pointer on Add to Project in the real cell menu (twin: New Project from opens none).

title: In a project, the editor's walk follows the project, not the folder
detail: On the Projects tab the editor's arrows, the phone's Walk and the Scanner screen's FRAME count read the archive's group of the open photo: from a project they walked the folder open (A03 to A04 instead of the project's B04), stopped dead on a member from another folder, and the gallery came back on a photo the project does not show, so nothing was selected. Swift's labFrames: the open frame's project on the Projects tab (editingProject, the first project holding the photo opened), else its roll or day. State::lab_frames reads the project's band as laid, open_photo sets the editing project, and walk, place and Move Out read it. Window check project_walk::a_project_walks_its_own_order_in_the_gallery_and_the_editor_and_the_archive_its_folder: a project of photos from two folders, the gallery's arrows and ⇧ in its order, ⌘G on the ringed photo, → and ↑ in the editor along the project and stopping at its end, the gallery back on the photo walked to; twin: the same gestures on the archive walk the folder.

title: A batch export runs as a pipeline: two frames decoding, one on the GPU, one written
detail: Measured on roll #8's test copy (24 Mpx NEF, M2 Max under load, interleaved runs): one frame at a time, a JPEG cost 0.95 s of LibRaw decode, 0.16 s of render and readback, 0.93 s of conversion and 0.13 s of encode, and each stage waited on the others. export::batch::write_batch runs them as a pipeline: DECODERS (the decode gate's 2) threads decode frames in order, one thread uploads beside the engine (render_full_beside, through Shared::upload) and renders, this thread encodes and writes; each stage hands on through a slot of one, so IN_FLIGHT (4) frames at most are held. The renders move to export/renders.rs; oni_export::write is split into lands (the refusals before any work), file_bytes and land, the batch running the same three steps. A stop or a failure starts no frame and writes none after it; writing.rs only calls write_batch, its progress unchanged. Checks: export::batch tests a_batch_writes_in_order_and_holds_no_more_than_its_frames_in_flight (twin: an unbounded hand-on holds more than IN_FLIGHT), a_stop_or_a_failure_writes_nothing_after_it (twin: every frame without them), a_batch_writes_the_bytes_one_frame_at_a_time_writes (JPEG and TIFF, ICC creation date aside; the render beside the engine bit for bit the render inside it; twins: one byte, one ulp moved are caught).
outcome: 20 frames: JPEG 45.7 s to 11.0 s (2.29 to 0.55 s a frame), TIFF 16-bit 67.8 s to 30.3 s; 2 frames: JPEG 4.3 to 1.7 s, TIFF 6.5 to 3.9 s. Peak memory 1.26 to 2.05 GB (JPEG), 2.10 to 2.92 GB (TIFF), 4 frames held at most. Files byte for byte as before on 2 frames in both formats (export_speed bench, ONI_BENCH_SAME).

title: The conversion to the export's space runs on every core, the TIFF's strips made where they are compressed
detail: converted ran the space's curve on one core, 0.93 s a 24 Mpx frame. oni_colour::legs::banded runs pieces of PIECE (16) rows on every core, each writing its own slice of the output, so the bytes are the same whichever thread ran a piece; a profile's table is read pixel by pixel and takes the same pieces, a CMM's matrix keeps its 256-row bands on one core. The TIFF writer makes each strip's big-endian bytes inside the thread that compresses it, so the frame is never copied whole a second time. Checks: oni-export conversion::the_conversion_on_every_core_is_the_conversion_on_one (JPEG sRGB, TIFF P3 and ProPhoto, odd sides, values past both ends, varying alpha; twin: one sample a level off is caught); peak::an_export_holds_one_float_frame_at_its_peak still holds under 1.75 frames (its twin: a second frame held breaks it).
outcome: Conversion 0.93 s to 0.12-0.15 s a frame; TIFF encode about the same (Deflate, already on every core).

title: A change on the export screen costs nothing on the interface thread and weighs the estimate once
detail: Each change wrote the preferences on the interface thread (read, write, flush: 3 to 20 ms, every notch of the quality slider) and spawned a thread that rendered the first target's 500 px sample again, decoding it when no preview was at hand. The settings are now kept by a latest::Worker of their own (the latest asked written once; preference writes serialised across threads so no holder loses another's key), and the estimate by a second Worker that renders the sample once per frame and settings and then only weighs each export's settings on it. Checks: latest::tests::a_burst_of_asks_runs_the_work_twice_at_most_and_last_on_the_latest (twin: a thread an ask runs 20 times); window check export_speed::a_burst_of_changes_weighs_the_estimate_twice_at_most (ten quality steps weighed once or twice, the last quality kept in the preferences; twin: four steps each waited for weigh four times).
outcome: 20 targets: a change 3-6 ms on the interface thread (ten quality steps 56 ms) to under 0.3 ms; the estimate up to date after 6-59 ms instead of 53-120 ms; ten steps weigh twice instead of ten times.

title: The export's previews render on two threads
detail: The previews were decoded and rendered one after the other, 0.36 s a cold half-size NEF decode, 55 ms a frame from the decode cache. PREVIEW_WORKERS (the decode gate's 2) threads take the next frame in order, so the lines still fill from the top and a newer pass stops them.
outcome: 20 targets: entering 8.0 s to 3.9 s (cold decodes); a space change 1.0 s to 0.68 s until every preview is up to date.

title: The export bench: stages, batch, parameter changes, memory
detail: Window checks export_speed::an_export_is_timed_stage_by_stage and a_parameter_change_on_a_batch_is_timed, run with ONI_BENCH_EXPORT=<n> on roll #8 mirrored by hard links into a temporary folder: each stage of a frame timed alone, the batch's wall time, the most frames held and the process's peak memory; then the surface entered on n frames and each kind of change timed in the call, in the pumps and until every line and the estimate are current. ONI_BENCH_FORMAT=tiff, ONI_BENCH_KEEP and ONI_BENCH_SAME compare a run's files byte for byte with an earlier one's (the profile's creation date aside; twin: one byte moved is caught). Timing numbers come from --profile app.

title: An export unfolds beside the editor: the surface closes, the folder opens, a card counts the frames
detail: Owner's design, beyond Swift. On Export, once the destination is known and the export starts, the surface closes back to where it was opened (the editor, or the gallery), the destination folder opens in the Finder or the Explorer (system::show_folder, the folder itself), and ExportProgress, built on a new DS JobCard (Raised, Progress, one key), floats at the canvas's top-left (CardStyle.padding + Space.m): the title, n of N, the file under way, the bar and Stop, the existing cooperative stop between frames. Done lingers SheetStyle.brief (2 s), held while hovered, then leaves; Stopped says how many were written; a failure keeps the existing message (frame: error) in the card until OK, no sheet over the window. One export at a time: a second is refused, the surface reopened meanwhile saying 'An export is under way, n of N: this one can start once it ends.' with its key waiting; the surface's Cancel only leaves it; quitting mid-export asks through QuitGuard's alert (Quit Anyway). Window check export_flow::an_export_closes_its_surface_and_counts_its_frames_in_a_card_at_the_canvas_s_corner: three frames from the editor, the surface closed onto the editor, the reveal recorded with the destination folder, the count advancing to 3 of 3, the card gone after its stay, the reopened surface refusing a second export, the quit asking; twins: an unwritable folder fails and the card keeps the failure past the stay, its OK key found at the canvas's top-left, no question on quitting once idle.

title: Exports render on an engine apart, so the editor never waits a whole frame
detail: The export locked the shared engine for each frame's full render (190 ms on 12 MP, about twice on a 24 MP frame), so every editor render asked meanwhile waited it. Shared::apart builds an engine on the same device and door, reading the same masks and patches; the export card makes it once and hands it to write_one, whose API is unchanged. Unit check render::door_tests::an_export_on_an_engine_apart_leaves_the_editors_engine_free: the editor's locks wait under 50 ms (measured 0.0 ms) during an export render apart; twin: on the shared engine a lock waits the whole render (152 of 162 ms).

title: Every modal sheet is centred in the window's height
detail: The DS Sheet hung its card a margin under the window's top, centred across only. Its card now sits at (height - card) / 2, a SheetStyle.margin kept above and below, so every confirm, notice, dialog and sheet built on Sheet or AskSheet is centred at once; anchored popups (menus, pickers, the help card, tooltips) keep their anchors. Window check sheet_layout::every_modal_sheet_is_centred_in_the_window_s_height: a confirm, the New Roll confirm, the welcome, the report, the settings and the stock picker each move their key down by half of 200 px of growth (±1 px); twin: a picker's menu picks the same line at both heights, and the old top-hung card moves 0. Checks clicking at fixed places (preset deck, launch notice, export replace prompt, notice key) follow the centred cards.

title: The window's @tr texts stay English in dev builds: Slint 1.18's interpreter reads no bundle
detail: Read in slint-interpreter, i-slint-core and the live-preview generator 1.18.1: bundled translations are generated code only, the live preview passes no bundle to the interpreter, and its @tr asks an external translator (i-slint-core internals behind a feature no public slint feature enables) or gettext (unix, .mo catalogues and a libintl macOS lacks; one shared feature set would make the shipped app link Homebrew's). Not wired; written in docs/research/i18n-dev-builds.md. French and Spanish looks are judged on --profile app or --release.

title: The phone link is hidden behind one switch until the feature is ready
detail: phone::READY (false) is the one switch: Options.phone takes it, or ONI_PHONE=1, and publishes Pairing.available. Off, the toolbar's phone key, File > Pair Phone… and the Settings Phone page are hidden (About keeps section 4), Pair Phone opens nothing and no Host starts, a phone paired before included, so no port is opened. The folded bench and the phone checks turn it on through Options.phone. Options moves to app/options.rs, which keeps app.rs under its ceiling.
outcome: Window check phone::the_switch_off_hides_the_link_and_listens_nowhere (twin: on, the paired phone finds the desktop listening); toolbar check: off, the gear's gap meets FEEDBACKS with no phone key (twin: on, four keys as before).

title: A roll's row in the sidebar draws its film stock
detail: The navigator's roll rows draw their stock's artwork in place of the film-roll glyph, as the archive tree's rows do: the stock picked, else the first photo's mode's default (TreeRowChrome.defaultStock), the negative one when the photos are not read; a roll outside the opened folder reads the stock in its marker while listed, off the interface thread. Every roll row's artwork is drawn once a stock and a pixel side (stocks::row_icon, DS stock icon size at the window's scale) and shared, where an SVG source was drawn again, filters included, by each row the virtualised tree made.
outcome: Unit test stocks::a_row_icon_is_drawn_once_at_the_rows_side (twins: another side, another stock, an unknown one); window check rolls::the_navigators_rolls_draw_their_stock: Portra draws Portra (twin: not the default), no stock draws the negative default, a plain folder keeps its glyph, a listed roll its marker's stock.

title: Auto White Balance is read ahead and kept in the sidecar, so the press lands at once
detail: A frame's balance outcome (its roll reference and filters) is kept under a fingerprint of exactly what the reading reads: the reading's code (oni-measure build.rs hashes the measure, pipeline, render, graph, settings and decode crates, the app's decode, mask and patch readers, and Cargo.lock), the files it reads (original and passes by size and date, the installed rendition matrices, the custom mask, each dust patch) and the settings with every field no reading reaches laid at rest (key::balance_inputs: Lighting, curves, saturation, spectrogram, vignette, sauce, texture, denoise, sharpening, the Scanner face, the balance laid, paper correction, order, the roll's name). Kept in memory and in the sidecar under the Rust-only key autoBalance, written through the held atomic writer with the revision kept, never seeding, migrating or losing a key of a sidecar, carried by later rewrites; a fingerprint that differs is never served. Read ahead, off the interface thread and behind the hand's decodes: as the open frame's preview stands, as each frame of Edit Together decodes, at the hand's rest after an edit, and once the Roll, Crop or De-dust tab is left (never stroke by stroke there), or a dust patch lands after it. The measurer recovers from a reading that panicked, its copies dropped, rather than reading nothing for the rest of the session. The press lands at once when every target is kept (no worker, no count on the key); only the frames missing are read, counted as #705 counts. A roll of one keeps a fresh id at each press, as Swift measures it afresh. Measured on roll #8 (app profile): the press with the balance kept 1.4 ms on the open frame and 17-34 ms on six frames together, against 0.2-0.5 s and 1.7-2.4 s read again.
