outcome: oni-measure balance_kept: every input moves the fingerprint, no look does (twin), and on a scene every pixel-moving input moves the outcome while no look moves a bit of it, on a roll and alone; on roll #8 the kept half decode reads the filters LibRaw's own reads (twin: a shifted window reads others). oni-settings auto_balance: the key round-trips, a rewrite carries it, a Swift key survives the balance's write, a sidecar without it reads as before, none is seeded (twins). oni-measure kept: a reading that panics leaves the next to read (twin: its copy decoded again). oni-core: a kept outcome serves its own fingerprint alone (twin). Window balance_kept: a kept balance lands within the call with no reading, alone and six together (twins: an input moved reads each again, counting); De-dust's strokes are read once on leaving the tab (twin: in and out unchanged reads nothing). Window transition: the camera matched writes no setting, the frame opened keeping only its balance under Rust's key.

title: A measuring copy reads the half decode kept on disk, and Edit Together keeps its decodes there
detail: A RAW asked at a side LibRaw reads at half size is the editor's half decode pixel for pixel (pinned.c chooses half size on the sensor's side alone), so a kept half decode whose long side reaches the side asked serves it, in about 15 ms instead of LibRaw's 0.35-0.5 s; such a copy writes nothing to disk, so thumbnails and roll previews add no decode there. Edit Together decodes its frames at the editor's half size, kept on disk as the editor's are, so its balance read ahead and the frames reopened read them back. Every kept decode is keyed by the installed rendition table too, so a camera matched later never serves a decode folded without its matrix.
outcome: oni-decode half_kept on roll #8: the copy served from the kept half decode equals LibRaw's own bit for bit, and a preview-side copy keeps no decode (twin: a copy longer than half the sensor is LibRaw's whole decode, never the half one). oni-measure balance_kept roll8: the balance read through the kept decode equals LibRaw's on two frames.

title: A slide is edited as a plain RAW: no roll measure, no dyes or ceiling, decoded at 5500 K, Auto Levels on a click
detail: Owner's call beyond Swift, for ConversionMode::Positive only. Prepare the Roll on a slide roll walks Film and Flat-Field alone (Base, Flags and Window skipped), its key reads PREPARE N FRAMES and writes each frame on the roll's film and flat-field with no roll reference and its look at rest (roll::slide). An unmeasured slide raises no roll-guide banner nor Roll tab warning and opens in the editor without being sent to Prepare; Auto White Balance reads a slide as it stands and writes no roll (Outcome.reference is now optional). Dye Separation and Density Ceiling are hidden for slides; the render takes dose 0 and the axis' base ceiling, so an old sidecar's family, dose or ceiling no longer applies. A slide's RAW is balanced at 5500 K, tint 0 (oni_decode::SLIDE_KELVIN, Robertson's 175 and 200 mired nodes interpolated, Bradford to D65 as before); the reading, the disk decode cache and the kept previews key on it, the per-camera rendition still folds after it. AUTO LEVELS in the Levels block lays one black and one white read on the RGB composite (the darkest channel's low tail, the lightest's high one) on all three windows, gains at rest, one undo step over the targets; on any other film the same key is Classic's two steps. Levels has no master tab: equal per-channel windows are that RGB level at the density stage and keep the sidecar Swift's. Negative and B&W unchanged (5 frames of roll #8 measured byte-identical before and after). On the T7 slides (Sony ARW, own sidecars, dose 0.6 E-6, ceiling at base) the mean output B/G moves 1.13 to 1.07 on 326 and 2.42 to 2.64 on 329: dose 0 alone pushes blue up (1.15, 2.86), 5500 K pulls it back. Checks: window slides (twins: a negative roll walks to its measure, a negative's Auto levels aligns each channel), oni-measure positive_levels, oni-decode slide neutral and cache key, oni-pipeline dose and ceiling, prepare slides steps, roll guide predicate. The Swift check density_axis_sense_is_measured_in_every_mode now holds a slide's ceiling flat (its twin: a negative and a black and white frame still move).

title: The Scanner face renders a slide at a sensible exposure
detail: A positive on the Scanner face sat 1.1 to 1.4 stops over its Pro render (three ARW slides, mean luminance 2.2 to 2.7 times Pro's, on both machines): the ONI and Frontier looks add about a stop (OniLook exposure 0.9976 and its S), fitted on a negative entering them with Lighting's 1.5 rest left out, while a slide rests at 0 and loses nothing. The machine now enters the look at resting_exposure(mode) - 1.5: -1.5 for a slide, 0 for a negative or B&W, which render bit for bit as before. Slides land 0.25 to 0.4 stop over Pro, as negatives do (0.2 to 0.5), no clipping added. Pipeline::chain takes the machine's settings, so a check renders the former chain.
outcome: oni-pipeline/tests/scanner_positive.rs: a slide at rest within 0.5 stop of Pro on both machines and no more clipped (twin: the former entry sits +0.9 stop and fails); negatives and B&W on both machines bit for bit against the former settings with clicks and contrast (twin: a slide differs). Real files: Roll #8 frames 6432 and 6433 hash identical before and after on Pro and both machines.

title: Prepare the Roll on slides: one measuring window, each frame's own RGB Auto Levels
detail: Owner's call beyond Swift, positive only: Prepare the Roll on a slide roll walks Film, Flat-Field and the Window step again, the negative's component and gesture. The one window is laid on every frame as geometry.measure_window, in the scan's fractions as roll::start lays a negative's, so each frame sees it in its own crop. The final key, MEASURE N FRAMES, runs on each ticked frame the positive AUTO LEVELS key through that window (key::slide_levelled): one black and white on the frame's RGB composite, gains at rest, three equal per-channel levels, no roll reference; off the interface thread, counted and stoppable, landed as one gallery step through land_roll, so undo restores every frame's levels and window and a second run re-levels each frame. The measuring copies come from the measurer's decode cache. Base and Flags stay skipped: no roll vote, so a flag would keep nothing out; a flag a negative draft left counts for nothing on a slide roll. #706 holds: a slide never prepared opens with no window. Window step help, Film Type and Auto Levels help in English, French and Spanish. Negative and B&W paths untouched.
outcome: oni-measure/tests/slide_roll.rs: three synthetic slides of different exposures each get their own RGB black and white through the window, all three different, gains 0, per-channel equal; the same frames without their near-white border read the same (twin: a window over the whole scan moves the white); a negative roll of the same frames still combines into one reference with aligned gains; the window is the same absolute rect on frames of different crops (twin: their in-crop windows differ). Window check slides: the slide roll walks Film then Window, MEASURE 3 FRAMES lays one window and three different levels, the Crop tab shows the window unarmed, one gallery undo restores every frame and redo lays them again; an unprepared slide opens with no window. Real slides (temp copy of three test Positif sidecars, Swift's window): 326 black 1.0346 white 2.8871, 329 0.8195 / 2.4974, 331 0.9734 / 2.9755, about 0.2 s a frame.

title: The Auto levels key on a prepared slide finds Prepare's levels, press after press
detail: Measured before any change: on the owner's own frames (four Lumix DC-S1R RW2 of Photos Digitales, his camera table installed) and twelve T7 ARW slides, Prepare's per-frame levels then the key, and the key three times, land the same levels to the last digit, through oni-measure and through the real window (open folder, PREPARE, MEASURE, the key pressed four times). Both read the same pre-levels image (truncated lays the graduation on the windows), through the same window and decode, and write absolute ends. The owner's sidecars show why another result came: at 12:58:38 one write laid rest levels (0.90309/3) on every frame not touched since, as a step undone does, so the key then read from rest, not from Prepare's levels. The negative's two steps creep by about 5e-4 a press (recentred from the gains in place), as Swift's AutoLevels.balance does: left as is.
outcome: oni-measure/tests/slide_roll.rs: on three synthetic slides the key after Prepare returns Prepare's settings whole, and a second press the same (twin: the window moved over the bright border, the white moves past 0.05). Window check slides: two presses on the prepared open slide leave its settings equal (twin: the key moves an unprepared slide's levels, earlier in the check). A key reading after the levels (Stage::GlobalLevels) fails both.

title: The canvas is colour-matched on macOS: the drawable is tagged Display P3 and the canvas encodes for it
detail: The window's CAMetalLayer had no colorspace, so macOS showed the canvas's sRGB numbers as the panel's own Display P3: +17 % mean chroma on roll #8's DSC_6432 (C* 14.9 against the export's 12.7, skin ΔE 7.1). Swift tags its drawable with the screen's space; the vendored femtovg renderer now asks wgpu for Display P3 on macOS and the app's canvas, histogram and thumbnails encode for it (display::WINDOW), so the canvas proofed to the export's space matches the file. Check: three patches exported as Display P3 JPEG and read through the embedded ICC sit within ΔE 2 of the canvas read through the drawable's tag; the twin, sRGB numbers on an untagged P3 panel, is caught above ΔE 4.

title: A Swift user's upgrade, checked on the owner's own rolls and support folder
detail: Headless example `upgrade_check` (every sidecar under a scans folder read; a copy of rolls rendered against the Swift thumbnails and written back; a copy of the support folder loaded) and the window check `upgrade` (ONI_UPGRADE_ROLLS mirrored, each roll opened, its first frame double-clicked and left: no sidecar edited, only this app's own keys added beside a current one; the twin, a notch, is seen). On the owner's data: 1589 sidecars (v11 to v19) and 46 roll markers read, 28 frames from 14 rolls rendered and round-tripped, presets, masks, projects, favourites, roots, library, index, transition table and journal loaded; nothing broke.

title: What's new for the release: everything the Rust app brings
detail: The welcome sheet's points rewritten as one list, a few words each and one line at most: the rebuild, colours kept, faster export beside the editor, instant Auto White Balance, the steadier roll measure, slides, Scanner fixes, the roll guide, dyes from the stock, stock icons, help demos, big folders, project walking, hover submenus, safety. English, French and Spanish. The sheet checks' tall window grows to hold it.

title: The app stamped 1.4.0, above the Swift app's 1.3.1
detail: oni-app's version 1.4.0, so the splash, the What's new heading, the Windows installer and the update feed name the Rust build after the last Swift release. Built for macOS by scripts/release-build and for Windows by the manual package workflow; nothing published.

title: The Windows build is stamped as the Mac one
detail: The package workflow fetches the whole history and builds with ONI_VERSION from oni-app's version and ONI_BUILD = 10000 + the commit count, as scripts/release-build does, so a Windows build compares with the update feed as the Mac build does.

title: A slide's white point mirrors its saturation
detail: The white point's saturation (Print.pointsCurve) took a negative's sense on a slide, where it moves the print the other way: on a positive the high end now loses saturation as the white point rises; the black point keeps the negative's sense. Owner's call, beyond Swift. Check in finishing's points test, its twin the black end unchanged.
